- There are exactly two foreground colors: fixed barrier pixels and moving pixels.
- In every row where the moving color appears, it forms one contiguous horizontal run ending at the right edge.

Rule
- Process each occupied row independently.
- Clear the moving run from the right edge.
- Repaint that run starting immediately to the right of the row's rightmost barrier pixel, or at column 0 when no barrier is present.
- Keep the barrier pixels and all rows without moving pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The fixed pixels are row-wise stoppers; each moving run simply slides left as far as possible without crossing the nearest stopper.

annotation.src: right-edge horizontal runs of the moving color, one run per occupied row
annotation.path: left along the same row through background cells, stopping immediately to the right of the nearest fixed barrier pixel or at the left edge if no barrier is present
annotation.trajectory: translate each whole run horizontally, preserving its length and color; rows are independent
annotation.transform: clear each run's original right-edge cells; keep fixed barrier pixels and rows without moving runs unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor each maximal solid 3x3 foreground region marked by red pixels, making its center yellow and its other grey cells orange.

Input structure
- The grid contains black empty cells plus grey foreground material with red
  marker pixels embedded in some solid 3x3 foreground windows.
- A candidate window is a 3x3 region with no black cells, at least one red
  pixel, and a grey center.
- Overlapping candidate windows may exist when one sees only part of the red
  marker; the intended marker window has the maximal set of red pixels.

Rule
- Select the candidate 3x3 windows whose red pixel set is not a strict subset
  of another candidate's red pixel set.
- In each selected window, recolor the grey center pixel to yellow.
- Recolor every other grey pixel in the selected window to orange, leaving
  red pixels and the rest of the grid unchanged.

Key insight
- The red pixels identify local 3x3 foreground blocks; maximal red-set
  containment removes the overlapping partial views of the same marked block.

annotation.src: solid 3x3 foreground regions with no black cells, a grey center, and at least one red marker pixel
annotation.transform: keep only candidate regions whose red marker mask is not a strict subset of another candidate's red marker mask; recolor each selected region's grey center yellow and its other grey pixels orange, preserving red pixels and everything outside

tags: condition:最大标记集去重叠, max_marker_no_overlap

references.docstring:
Complete the separated array of one-hole tiles.

Input structure
A square grid has one background color and one foreground color. Its side
length is n*n+n-1, partitioning it into an n by n array of n by n tiles
separated by single background rows and columns. Some tiles are already
present; each present tile is filled with foreground except for one
background pixel at the local coordinate matching the tile's array position.

Rule
Keep the separator rows and columns background. For every tile position
(tile row, tile column), fill that n by n tile with the foreground color and
leave only the local pixel at (tile row, tile column) as background.

Key insight
The hole inside each tile is a coordinate label for that tile's position in
the larger tile array, so the sparse input samples define the complete
position-coded pattern.

annotation.src: partial n by n array of n by n foreground tiles separated by one background row and column; each visible tile has one background pixel at the local coordinate matching its array coordinate
annotation.dst: empty tile slots in the same separated array
annotation.transform: complete every tile as foreground except for its coordinate-label background pixel, and keep separator rows and columns background

tags: condition:孔洞位置等于坐标, hole_equals_coordinate

references.docstring:
Extend a solid rectangle into side stripes, leaving blank the rows or columns marked by control pixels.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- The foreground contains one unique largest 4-connected solid rectangle and singleton marker pixels of one other color.
- Every marker lies in one of the four side strips aligned with the rectangle, not in a diagonal quadrant.

Rule:
- Keep the original rectangle and markers unchanged.
- Above and below the rectangle, fill each rectangle column that has no marker on that side.
- Left and right of the rectangle, fill each rectangle row that has no marker on that side.

Key insight:
- The markers encode the excluded projected rows or columns for their side of the rectangle; the unmarked positions become rectangle-colored extension stripes.

annotation.src: largest solid foreground rectangle and singleton marker pixels aligned with its four side strips
annotation.transform: extend the rectangle color through every unmarked projected row or column on each side; marker-aligned rows or columns stay bg and the markers are preserved

tags: condition:标记排除对应行列, marker_excludes_row_col

references.docstring:
Fill the black target rectangle with a left-right mirror of the colored source motif.

Input structure:
- A dominant background surrounds one fully occupied colored rectangular motif.
- A single black rectangular region is the same shape as the colored motif.

Rule:
- Crop the colored motif from its tight bounding box.
- Reflect that crop horizontally and paste it over the black rectangle.

Key insight:
- The black region is not erased by a fill color; it is a destination slot for the mirrored motif.

annotation.src: fully occupied colored rectangular motif s
annotation.dst: black rectangular slot d
annotation.match_cond: unique s maps to unique d; s.bbox.shape == d.bbox.shape
annotation.transform: paste a left-right mirror of s into d; preserve the rest of the grid

references.docstring:
Paint a blue 3x3 hollow neighborhood around each red marker inside a green object's bounding rectangle.

Input structure
- The input contains a black background, green 4-connected objects, and red marker pixels.
- Each green object forms an almost-rectangular region; its bounding box identifies the region it controls.
- The active red markers are exactly the red pixels lying inside one of those green-object bounding boxes.
Rule
- Preserve the input grid, including every active red marker itself.
- For each active red marker, recolor all in-bounds 8-neighbor cells to blue.
- If two active markers touch, their marker centers remain red rather than being overwritten by the other's blue stamp.
Key insight
- Red pixels outside the green rectangles are distractors; containment in a green component's bbox selects the markers to stamp.

annotation.src: red marker pixels inside the bbox of a 4-connected green object; red pixels outside all such bboxes are distractors
annotation.transform: paint each selected marker's in-bounds 8-neighborhood blue, except selected marker centers remain red; pixels outside all stamps stay unchanged

tags: condition:仅处理区域内标记, markers_inside_only

references.docstring:
Complete same-color marker segments inside a regular lattice of framed tiles.

Input structure
- The grid is partitioned by separator rows and columns into 4x4 framed tiles.
- All tile borders have one frame color, and each 2x2 tile interior has a dominant fill color.
- Other interior colors are endpoint markers, with their exact 2x2 subcell position preserved.

Rule
- Group endpoint markers by marker color and by their relative interior subcell.
- When two or more endpoints in a group share a tile row, fill every intervening tile at that same subcell with the marker color.
- When two or more endpoints in a group share a tile column, fill every intervening tile at that same subcell with the marker color.

Key insight
- The colored endpoints are not connected in pixel space; they are connected on the coarser tile lattice, and the chosen interior subcell identifies which lane to paint.

annotation.src: non-structural marker pixels in the 2x2 interiors of framed 4x4 tiles, grouped by color and relative interior subcell
annotation.match_cond: markers connect only when they have the same color and the same relative interior subcell
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical segment on the tile lattice between matching markers that share a tile row or tile column
annotation.trajectory: paint that same relative interior subcell of every intervening tile with the marker color
annotation.transform: keep separator lines, tile frames, structural interior fill cells, and original markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Fill a hollow grey square frame with nested square shells cycling grey, red, grey, and black.

Input structure
- The grid contains black background and one complete one-cell-thick grey square frame.
- The frame interior and any exterior padding are black.

Rule
- Preserve the frame bbox and recolor every cell in it by its distance from the frame border.
- Shell depths repeat the color cycle grey, red, grey, black while moving inward.
- In the 9x9 small-frame case, the lone center cell remains in the black center left by the first blank shell.

Key insight
- The output is a distance-shell rewrite of the single square frame, not a movement or matching task.

annotation.src: single one-cell-thick grey square frame enclosing black interior pixels
annotation.dst: same frame bbox partitioned into concentric square shells by distance from the frame
annotation.transform: preserve exterior pixels; paint shells outside-to-inside with repeating cycle grey, red, grey, black, with the 9x9 frame's final singleton remaining black

references.docstring:
Fill each interior cell whose row label and column label have the same color.

Input structure
- The background fills the interior rectangle excluding the bottom row and rightmost column.
- The right edge gives a non-background color label for each interior row.
- The bottom edge gives a non-background color label for each interior column.

Rule
- Keep the bottom row and rightmost column unchanged.
- For every interior cell, compare its row's right-edge label with its column's bottom-edge label.
- Recolor the cell to that label color exactly when the two labels match; otherwise keep it background.

Key insight
- The border colors are row and column headers, so the output is the equality table of those two header sequences.

annotation.src: background cells in the interior rectangle, with right-edge row labels and bottom-edge column labels
annotation.transform: recolor each interior cell to the shared label color when its row label equals its column label; otherwise leave it background; keep the border labels unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: the right edge gives the row color sequence and the bottom edge gives the column color sequence

references.docstring:
Tile each rectangular non-wall cavity with the colored seed pattern it already contains.

Input structure
- The dominant color forms solid walls around one or more rectangular cavities.
- A unique most common non-wall color is the empty cavity color.
- Each cavity contains exactly one other color, arranged as one copy of a repeat tile.

Rule
- For each 4-connected non-wall cavity, take the bbox of its seed color as the tile.
- Repeat that tile across the entire cavity, preserving the phase set by the seed's current position.
- Leave wall cells unchanged and leave tile-empty positions as the empty cavity color.

Key insight
- The colored pixels are not moved objects; they are one visible instance of a periodic mask that fills its containing rectangle.

annotation.summary: Repeat each colored seed mask across its rectangular cavity while preserving wall pixels and mask gaps.
annotation.src: rectangular non-wall cavities, each containing empty pixels and one colored seed mask
annotation.transform: use each seed-color bbox as the periodic tile for its cavity; repeat it in both directions with the seed's phase, leaving tile gaps empty

references.docstring:
Repeat the input tile in both directions once for each distinct input color.

Input structure
A non-empty 2D color grid; the examples are 3x3 tiles containing two to four
distinct colors.

Rule
Count the number of distinct colors in the input. Tile the entire input grid
that many times vertically and that many times horizontally.

Key insight
The output size is controlled by the palette size of the input, and the unit
being repeated is the whole grid rather than individual pixels.

annotation.src: entire input grid as one periodic tile
annotation.dst: k x k array of original-size tile slots, where k is the number of distinct input colors
annotation.transform: copy the input tile unchanged into every slot
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by k

tags: condition:色数决定重复次数, color_count_repetition

references.docstring:
Pack the hollow square frames into a contiguous strip ordered by their original positions.

Input structure
- A black-background scene of separated monochrome 4x4 objects: hollow square frames and solid square distractors.
Rule
- Keep only the hollow frames and paste them edge-to-edge into one strip.
- If the hollow-frame positions spread more by column than row, pack left-to-right ordered by column; otherwise pack top-to-bottom ordered by row.
Key insight
- The solid blocks are distractors; the hollow frames are the retained sprites, and their dominant layout axis determines the output strip.

annotation.src: hollow 4x4 foreground frame sprites s, ignoring solid 4x4 blocks
annotation.dst: contiguous output sprite slots d along the hollow-frame dominant axis
annotation.match_cond: rank(s by position on the chosen axis) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: crop each frame to its bbox and paste the crops edge-to-edge without recoloring
annotation.multi_step: choose horizontal packing when frame column span exceeds row span; choose vertical packing when row span exceeds column span
annotation.grid_shape: common 4x4 frame crop size multiplied by number of hollow frames along the chosen packing axis

references.docstring:
Recolor each foreground pixel by whether its horizontally reflected counterpart is also foreground.

Input structure:
- The grid has black background pixels and exactly one non-black foreground color.
- Foreground pixels may or may not have a matching foreground pixel in the reflected row at the same column.

Rule:
- Preserve black background pixels.
- Recolor a foreground pixel red if the pixel at the same column in the opposite row is also foreground.
- Recolor every other foreground pixel grey.

Key insight:
- The red pixels are the horizontally symmetric intersection of the foreground mask with its top-bottom reflection.

annotation.src: single non-black foreground color mask on black background
annotation.transform: recolor foreground pixels whose top-bottom reflected counterpart is also foreground to red; recolor all other foreground pixels to grey

tags: condition:交集差集分别着色, intersection_diff_colored

references.docstring:
Erase each foreground object that contains more than one sparse marker-color pixel.

Input structure
- A dominant background surrounds separated 4-connected foreground objects.
- The foreground uses one dense object color and one sparse marker color.
Rule
- Infer the marker as the unique less frequent foreground color.
- Keep objects with zero or one marker pixel.
- Recolor every pixel of an object to background when it contains two or more marker pixels.
Key insight
- The marker count inside each whole object, not the object's size or position, decides whether that object remains.

annotation.src: 4-connected non-bg objects; marker color is the unique less frequent foreground color
annotation.transform: erase to bg each object with two or more marker-color pixels; preserve objects with zero or one marker pixel

tags: condition:标记超阈值则擦除, erase_above_threshold

references.docstring:
Fill each horizontal span enclosed by consecutive outline pixels with red.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- All non-background pixels share one outline color and form diagonal boundary strokes.
- Rows contain one or more outline pixels; consecutive outline pixels bound horizontal gaps.

Rule
- Preserve the original background and outline pixels.
- In each row, find consecutive outline pixels from left to right.
- Recolor every background pixel strictly between each consecutive pair to red.

Key insight
- The diagonal outline becomes a filled shape one scanline at a time: each row's outline pixels mark the span endpoints.

annotation.src: single-color diagonal outline pixels on a background grid
annotation.transform: preserve outline pixels; in each row recolor background pixels between consecutive outline pixels to red

references.docstring:
Paint the longest black diagonal segment teal, choosing the middle segment when the longest run is an odd-width parallel band.

Input structure
A 10x10 grid containing black pixels embedded in a grey field/frame.

Rule
Find every maximal contiguous black segment along both diagonal directions. Select the maximum-length segment; if the maximum-length candidates form adjacent parallel diagonals, select the central diagonal of that band. Recolor the selected black pixels to teal.

Key insight
The output marks the hidden straight diagonal stroke inside the black mask; the only ambiguous training case is a three-diagonal band, where the centered parallel run is the marked stroke.

annotation.src: maximal contiguous black runs in either 45-degree diagonal orientation inside the grey frame
annotation.transform: recolor the longest run teal and preserve all other pixels
annotation.multi_step: if multiple longest runs are adjacent parallel diagonals, choose the central run of the band

references.docstring:
Extract and stack the contents between each row-aligned pair of 2x2 marker blocks.

Input structure
- The grid contains noise plus one marker color whose components are all 2x2 blocks.
- The marker blocks occur as left/right pairs sharing the same two-row span.

Rule
- For each paired marker span in top-to-bottom order, copy the rectangle strictly between the two marker blocks.
- Stack those copied rectangles vertically, discarding the markers and all cells outside the copied rectangles.

Key insight
- The extraction markers are identifiable as the unique color made only of 2x2 components arranged in row-aligned pairs.

annotation.src: two-row interior rectangles s between each left/right pair of 2x2 blocks of the unique marker color, ordered top-to-bottom
annotation.dst: stacked two-row output bands d, ordered top-to-bottom
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: copy each interior rectangle unchanged and discard the marker blocks and surrounding noise
annotation.grid_shape: height is twice the number of marker pairs; width is the common gap between paired marker blocks

references.docstring:
Copy the existing foreground sprite into every three-marker corner frame, reflecting it to the frame's missing corner.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One non-background color forms singleton marker pixels; every three markers are three corners of a same-size square.
- The other non-background color forms one sprite mask already placed at the missing corner of one marker square.

Rule
- Find the source marker square whose missing corner touches the corresponding corner of the sprite bbox.
- For every marker square with the same side length, place a copy of that sprite outside the square at its missing corner.
- Reflect the sprite vertically and/or horizontally when the target missing corner lies in a different quadrant from the source missing corner.
- If the source bbox is a complete hollow square border, keep the corner-bracket motif selected by the source anchor.

Key insight
- The yellow three-corner squares are control frames: their absent fourth corner gives both the anchor point and the quadrant for the red sprite copy.

annotation.src: foreground sprite s already anchored at one three-marker square frame
annotation.dst: three-marker square frame d with one missing corner
annotation.match_cond: d.side == source frame side; d.missing_corner gives the anchor corner and quadrant
annotation.transform: clear s from its source bbox and stamp s at every d; reflect s horizontally or vertically when d's missing-corner quadrant differs from the source quadrant

references.docstring:
Slide closed foreground objects upward and open foreground objects downward, keeping their columns and stacking on collision.

Input structure
- The grid has a single background color and several monochromatic 4-connected foreground objects.
- Some objects are closed frames with at least one enclosed background hole inside their bounding box.
- The remaining objects are open line-like sprites with no enclosed hole.

Rule
- Redraw every object on an empty background canvas without changing its color, shape, or horizontal position.
- Closed frame objects slide vertically upward to the first non-colliding position.
- Open objects slide vertically downward to the first non-colliding position.
- Within each direction, preserve the original vertical order so overlapping columns stack instead of crossing.

Key insight
- The only role distinction is whether an object encloses a hole: hole objects pack against the top edge, while non-hole objects pack against the bottom edge.

annotation.src: monochromatic 4-connected foreground objects, classified by whether their bbox encloses a background hole
annotation.path: closed objects slide straight upward in their original columns; no-hole objects slide straight downward in their original columns, stopping at the edge or the nearest settled object
annotation.trajectory: move each whole object without changing its shape or color
annotation.transform: redraw the settled objects on an empty background canvas, erasing their original positions
annotation.multi_step: settle upward movers from top to bottom and downward movers from bottom to top so same-column overlaps stack without crossing

tags: condition:有孔者升无孔者降, hole_up_holeless_down

references.docstring:
Emit blue perpendicular guide lines from each green marker and stamp blue rings where they cross the red guide lines.

Input structure
- The background is dominant, with full-span parallel red guide lines.
- Each source marker is a green 3x3 ring centered on a red guide-line pixel.
- All guide lines are horizontal or all guide lines are vertical.

Rule
- A marker on a horizontal red line emits a vertical blue line through its center column; a marker on a vertical red line emits a horizontal blue line through its center row.
- The emitted line paints only background cells blue.
- At each crossing with a red guide line, stamp a blue 3x3 ring with the red center preserved; keep the original green source marker unchanged.

Key insight
- The green ring is not copied along the red line; it defines the perpendicular projection, and every red-line crossing on that projection receives the same ring shape in blue.

annotation.src: green 3x3 marker rings centered on full-span red guide lines
annotation.path: full row or column through each marker center, perpendicular to the orientation of the red guide lines
annotation.trajectory: paint background cells on the path blue
annotation.transform: at every red guide-line crossing on the path, paint a blue 3x3 ring with the red center preserved; keep original green marker rings unchanged

references.docstring:
Draw each colored marker's fixed trail, then turn red/vertical trail crossings into yellow down-left diagonals.

Input structure
- A black background contains one pixel of each present marker color drawn from blue, red, green, and pink.
- The grey and yellow colors are absent from the input and are used only in the output trail drawing.

Rule
- Blue paints two grey pixels to the right and places a blue endpoint one row above the second grey pixel.
- Red paints three grey pixels to the left and places a red endpoint four columns left.
- Green paints two grey pixels downward and places a green endpoint three rows down.
- Pink paints five grey pixels upward and places a pink endpoint six rows up.
- Where a red horizontal segment crosses a green or pink vertical segment, paint yellow there and continue yellow diagonally down-left to the grid edge.

Key insight
- Marker color identifies a fixed motion/trail, and yellow is the collision effect between the red westward trail and a vertical trail.

annotation.src: single colored marker pixels on the black background
annotation.path: color-coded fixed routes: blue goes two cells right then one up, red goes four left, green goes three down, and pink goes six up
annotation.trajectory: paint intermediate route pixels grey and place a same-color marker at each endpoint, preserving the original markers
annotation.transform: where a red horizontal segment crosses a green or pink vertical segment, recolor the crossing yellow and extend yellow diagonally down-left to the grid edge

tags: condition:颜色决定运动方向, color_determines_motion

references.docstring:
Stamp the whole input pattern into output block slots selected by grey pixels.

Input structure
- The input is a non-empty 2D grid containing grey control pixels.
- The output is divided into blocks with the same height and width as the input.

Rule
- Treat the input grid as both the source pattern and a placement mask.
- For each grey input pixel, copy the entire input grid into the corresponding
  output block.
- For each non-grey input pixel, leave the corresponding output block black.

Key insight
- Grey pixels do not expand as solid grey blocks; they select where full
  copies of the original pattern are stamped.

annotation.src: input pixel grid, with grey pixels acting as a placement mask
annotation.transform: copy the whole input grid into each corresponding input-sized output block whose source pixel is grey; leave all other blocks black
annotation.grid_shape: H x W input -> (H*H) x (W*W) output

tags: condition:控制色选中则印章, stamp_where_control

references.docstring:
Recolor every red foreground object of area at least four to pink.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and a single red foreground color.
- The foreground is split into one or more 4-connected red objects.
- Pink is absent from the input and is used only for selected output objects.

Rule
- Preserve black background pixels and red objects with area one, two, or three.
- Recolor every 4-connected red object with area at least four to pink.

Key insight
- The changed objects are exactly the connected red objects that are large
  enough; their position and shape do not otherwise matter.

annotation.src: 4-connected red foreground objects on a black background
annotation.transform: recolor each object with area at least 4 to pink; preserve smaller red objects and the background

tags: condition:面积超阈值则变色, recolor_above_threshold

references.docstring:
Extract the largest clean framed sprite whose foreground pattern is not duplicated.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and two foreground colors.
- The foreground contains several same-size rectangular sprites with a one-cell frame.
- Extra foreground clutter may touch the outside of a sprite, and smaller framed subpatterns may occur inside repeated sprites.

Rule
- Find clean rectangles whose border is one foreground color and whose interior contains no background.
- Keep only the largest such rectangles; these are the full source sprites.
- Among those sprites, return the single full sprite pattern that occurs exactly once.

Key insight
The surrounding clutter is irrelevant once the maximal intact frames are detected; the task is an odd-one-out selection among the clean sprite patterns.

annotation.src: maximal clean one-cell framed rectangular sprites on the dominant background, ignoring attached foreground clutter and smaller nested frames
annotation.transform: select the single maximal sprite pattern that occurs exactly once among the same-size framed sprites and output that sprite unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: height and width of the selected framed sprite crop

references.docstring:
Fill black gaps with the unique known color from each cell's horizontal/vertical mirror orbit.

Input structure
The grid is an otherwise nonblack pattern with color 0 marking missing pixels. Nonblack cells reveal a horizontal reflection over the lower row band and a vertical reflection over the right column band.

Rule
Infer the row-reflection and column-reflection constants whose reflected nonblack pairs agree. For each black pixel, collect its row mirror, column mirror, and combined row+column mirror positions that stay in bounds; the known colors in that orbit must be unique, and every black pixel in the orbit is recolored to it.

Key insight
A gap can face another gap across one mirror axis, so the fill must use the full two-axis reflection orbit rather than a single reflected cell.

annotation.src: grid with black mask pixels over a pattern symmetric by row reflection after a two-row prefix and by column reflection after a two-column prefix
annotation.transform: replace each black mask pixel with the unique nonblack color in its horizontal/vertical reflection orbit; preserve all visible pixels

tags: condition:轨道内已知色唯一, unique_known_in_orbit

references.docstring:
Collapse each foreground block in a background-separated lattice to its unique majority color, then add a background border.

Input structure
- The dominant background color forms complete separator rows and columns,
  including the outer border.
- The separator lines divide the foreground into a rectangular lattice of
  same-sized filled blocks.
- Every block has one unique majority color and contains no background cells.

Rule
- Find the contiguous non-separator row bands and column bands.
- For each band intersection, write the unique majority color of that input
  block to the corresponding interior cell of the output.
- Leave a one-cell background border around the summarized lattice.

Key insight
- The output is a coarse color map of the block lattice; the internal shape
  noise inside each block is discarded by taking the block majority.

annotation.src: foreground blocks in a lattice divided by complete background separator rows and columns
annotation.transform: collapse each block to its unique majority color and place those colors in the corresponding cells of a background-bordered summary grid
annotation.grid_shape: number of non-separator row bands + 2 by number of non-separator column bands + 2

tags: condition:每块取唯一多数色, majority_color_per_block

references.docstring:
Use the matching pair of tiles in each band as a color-substitution example and apply it to the remaining tile.

Input structure:
- Background rows separate horizontal bands of small same-size colored tiles.
- Each band contains exactly three non-background tile regions in the same columns.
- Within a band, exactly two tiles have the same equality pattern up to color renaming.

Rule:
- For each band, find the ordered pair of same-pattern tiles whose source colors cover the third tile.
- Learn the color mapping from that source tile to the matching destination tile.
- Recolor the third tile by that mapping and place it in the corresponding output band.

Key insight:
The duplicated tile pattern is a miniature example pair that defines how to translate colors for the odd tile out.

annotation.src: remaining tile s in each horizontal band
annotation.dst: ordered same-pattern tile pair d0->d1 in the same band
annotation.match_cond: d0 and d1 have identical equality pattern, and s.colors are all present in d0
annotation.transform: recolor s by the d0.color -> d1.color mapping
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input, one tile-column wide
annotation.symbol_instructions: within each band, the matched tile pair is an example that defines the color substitution for the third tile

references.docstring:
Stretch the compact colored line prototype onto the sparse yellow skeleton canvas.

Input structure
- The grid has black background with grey separator/filler cells.
- One panel contains only a sparse yellow skeleton; its bounding box is the output canvas.
- The other panel is a compact colored prototype made from horizontal and vertical line segments.

Rule
- Treat endpoints, corners, and crossings of the prototype foreground as graph vertices.
- The yellow pixels are the same vertex pattern after independently stretching rows and columns.
- Map sorted prototype vertex rows/columns to sorted yellow rows/columns.
- Paint every prototype foreground cell and adjacent foreground edge through the mapped row/column spans.

Key insight
- The yellow pixels are anchors for the prototype's graph vertices, while the compact prototype supplies the colors for the stretched line segments.

annotation.src: compact colored line prototype plus sparse yellow skeleton of its graph vertices
annotation.dst: yellow skeleton bbox used as the stretched canvas
annotation.transform: match prototype vertex rows/columns to yellow anchor rows/columns in order; stretch each colored horizontal and vertical prototype segment through the mapped intervals, dropping yellow and grey cells
annotation.grid_shape: same height and width as the yellow skeleton bbox

references.docstring:
Paint the unique shortest background path between the two red endpoints yellow.

Input structure
- The grid contains black background cells, blue blocker cells, and exactly two red endpoint pixels.
- The endpoints are connected by one shortest 4-neighbor route through non-blue cells.

Rule
- Keep every original cell unchanged.
- Find the unique shortest 4-neighbor path from one red endpoint to the other while treating blue cells as blocked.
- Recolor only the black interior cells of that path to yellow.

Key insight
- The blue cells form maze walls, and the output is the single shortest corridor between the two red endpoints.

annotation.src: red endpoint pixel s
annotation.dst: the other red endpoint d
annotation.path: unique shortest 4-neighbor route from s to d through background cells, treating blue cells as blockers
annotation.trajectory: paint each background pixel on the route yellow
annotation.transform: preserve the red endpoints, blue blockers, and off-path background

references.docstring:
Separate four overlapping-looking copies of one 2x2 sprite into the four corners of a 5x5 canvas.

Input structure
A 6x6 grid has one background color and one foreground color.  The foreground
pixels are exactly coverable by four translated copies of one 2x2 sprite mask.

Rule
Infer the unique 2x2 sprite mask whose four translated copies cover all
foreground pixels without overlap, then stamp that mask into the upper-left,
upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right 2x2 regions of a 5x5 output.

Key insight
The tangled input arrangement is only a compact packing of four identical
small sprites; the output regularizes the packing by inserting a blank middle
row and column between the copies.

annotation.src: foreground pixels exactly covered by four translated copies of one 2x2 sprite mask s
annotation.dst: four separated 2x2 corner slots in a 5x5 output
annotation.match_cond: s is the unique 2x2 mask whose four translated copies cover all foreground pixels without overlap
annotation.transform: stamp s into every output corner slot with the foreground color; leave the middle row and column as bg
annotation.grid_shape: 6x6 input -> 5x5 output

references.docstring:
Translate between colored legend shapes and 5x5 encoded pattern blocks.

Input structure
- A large teal-colored panel contains one 8-connected shape for each legend color.
- Outside the panel are 5x5 non-background blocks, either solid color blocks or a shared two-color pattern.

Rule
- A solid color block is replaced by the common two-color pattern whose centered marker cells are that color's legend shape.
- A two-color pattern block has its marker shape matched to a legend shape up to rotation/reflection, then the whole block is filled with the matched legend color.

Key insight
The panel is a color/shape dictionary; the 5x5 blocks are either encoded dictionary entries or decoded color swatches.

annotation.src: 5x5 work blocks s outside the teal legend panel
annotation.dst: colored legend shape entries d inside the teal panel
annotation.match_cond: pattern block marker mask matches d.shape up to rotation/reflection; solid block color equals d.color
annotation.transform: rewrite s in place: matched pattern blocks become solid d.color; matched solid blocks become the common two-color 5x5 pattern with d.shape centered as marker cells
annotation.symbol_instructions: teal panel maps each colored shape to its color; common pattern uses the shared border/base color and marker color from two-color blocks

tags: condition:旋转镜像等价匹配, rotation_reflection_match

references.docstring:
Recolor each grey diagonal band by extending the horizontal marker palette through its diagonal layers.

Input structure
- The background is dominant, with one contiguous horizontal row of colored
  marker pixels and one or more grey diagonal bands.
- Each grey band has a slanted rectangular-ribbon shape with a flat top cap
  at the end nearest the marker row.

Rule
- Keep the background and marker pixels unchanged.
- For each grey band, normalize its slant so the top cap begins at local
  column zero, then use the layer min(row_offset, col_offset), clipped to
  the final layer at the far cap.
- Recolor each grey pixel with the marker palette at layer modulo palette
  length.

Key insight
- The visible grey bands are diagonal ribbons; their color pattern is not
  row-wise but layered from the seed end, with the far cap clipped so the
  last layer continues to the end.

annotation.src: grey diagonal ribbon bands on the background
annotation.transform: normalize each band's slant from its top cap; recolor each grey pixel by the marker color at min(row offset, normalized column offset), capped at the far end
annotation.symbol_instructions: the contiguous marker row gives the cyclic color order for band layers

references.docstring:
Stamp the compact upper template into every marked lower mask cell as an expanded block image.

Input structure
- The grid has one solid grey separator row.
- Above it is a template region made of monochrome 2x2 blocks.
- Below it is a same-size mask containing only background and red marker pixels.

Rule
- Compress each 2x2 block in the upper region to one color, giving a small tile.
- Build a blank output whose coarse cell grid is the lower mask and whose cell size is the tile size.
- For every red marker pixel in the lower mask, paste the tile into the corresponding output block.

Key insight
The top half encodes the motif at half resolution, while the lower red mask encodes which coarse cells receive that motif.

annotation.src: upper 6x6 template region and lower red marker mask separated by a grey row
annotation.transform: compress each 2x2 block of the template to one cell; expand each lower mask pixel to a 3x3 output block, stamping the compressed tile only at red marker positions and leaving other blocks background
annotation.grid_shape: 13x6 input -> 18x18 output
annotation.symbol_instructions: upper template region encodes the 3x3 tile; lower red mask encodes the coarse output positions that receive the tile

tags: condition:标记位置接收模板, marker_receive_template

references.docstring:
Summarize each foreground color as a top-aligned vertical bar ordered by bbox height.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background color and several foreground color masks.
The foreground colors have distinct bounding-box heights.

Rule
Measure the bounding-box height of each foreground color mask. Sort the
colors from tallest to shortest, make one output column per color, and fill
the top cells of that column with the color for its measured height.

Key insight
The input positions and horizontal extents are discarded; only each color's
vertical span determines the histogram height and column order.

annotation.src: foreground color masks s ordered by decreasing bounding-box height
annotation.dst: top-aligned histogram columns d ordered left to right
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: fill each column with s.color for s.bbox.height cells from the top, leaving the rest as background
annotation.grid_shape: height is the largest foreground color bbox height; width is the number of foreground colors

tags: condition:包围盒高决定柱高, bbox_height_bar_height

references.docstring:
Pack all foreground fragments into a solid compact rectangle while preserving their colors.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- The foreground is split into monochromatic 4-connected polyomino fragments.
- The total foreground area is exactly the area of the compact output rectangle.

Rule
- Sort fragments by decreasing area, with equal-area fragments ordered left-to-right in the input.
- For each fragment, try its identity/reflected/rotated orientations in that order and scan placements from top-left to bottom-right.
- Keep the first set of non-overlapping placements that fills the whole compact rectangle.

Key insight
The scattered objects are jigsaw fragments; the output is their canonical top-left packing into the smallest near-square rectangle.

annotation.src: monochromatic 4-connected foreground fragments s ordered by decreasing area, breaking equal areas left-to-right
annotation.dst: compact 3x4 rectangle packed from top-left to bottom-right
annotation.transform: discard background spacing; preserve each fragment color; rotate or reflect fragments as needed so all foreground cells tile the rectangle without overlap
annotation.multi_step: for each ordered fragment, try identity/reflected/rotated orientations and top-left scan positions; keep the first complete tiling

references.docstring:
Draw same-colored rectangular connector bands through background channels between four matching marker blocks.

Input structure
- A background lattice of separated framed tiles; the frame color is the unique most frequent non-background color.
- Each tile region contains one solid non-frame interior block.
- The unique most common interior color is the default; every other interior color marks four rectangle corners.

Rule
- For each marker color, find its two row bands and two column bands.
- Paint that color through background cells along the two horizontal and two vertical sides of the implied rectangle.
- Preserve all original frame, default interior, marker, and off-path background pixels.

Key insight
- The repeated tile frames define which cells are obstacles and which cells are background channels; matching interior colors supply rectangle corners independent of tile and marker size.

annotation.src: non-default interior marker blocks inside framed tile regions, grouped by color
annotation.dst: same-color marker blocks sharing a marker row band or column band
annotation.path: for each marker color, connect the four corner blocks along the two horizontal and two vertical sides of their implied rectangle, crossing only background channel cells
annotation.trajectory: paint every background cell on each rectangle side with the marker color
annotation.transform: keep all framed tiles, default interiors, marker blocks, and off-path background unchanged

tags: condition:沿通道绘制矩形边, draw_rect_via_channel

references.docstring:
Fill the inside of a rectangular frame with alternating red and yellow square rings around its inner control pixel.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color and one foreground color.
- The foreground forms a rectangular one-pixel-thick frame.
- Exactly one foreground control pixel lies inside the frame.

Rule
- Preserve the frame and the control pixel.
- For each background pixel inside the frame, compute its Chebyshev distance
  from the control pixel.
- Odd distances become yellow; even distances become red.

Key insight
- The added colors are concentric square rings centered on the lone interior
  control pixel, with ring color determined by distance parity.

annotation.src: background pixels inside the foreground rectangular frame, with a single foreground control pixel inside the frame
annotation.transform: preserve the frame and control pixel; recolor each background interior pixel by Chebyshev-distance parity from the control pixel, odd to yellow and even to red

tags: condition:奇偶距离决定颜色, parity_distance_color

references.docstring:
Extend the red start pixel into a recursive rectilinear ray network that turns at colored marker pixels.

Input structure
- The canvas has black background, one red start pixel on the left edge, and isolated colored marker pixels.
- Original non-red, non-background marker pixels are blockers and are preserved.
- Marker colors are green, pink, orange, and teal; orange markers on the lower border are terminal when hit from above.

Rule
- Start with a horizontal red ray from the red edge pixel.
- A ray paints background cells red until it reaches the first original marker in each direction of its row or column.
- The first time a marker opens, emit the perpendicular row or column from the red cell immediately before that marker; later hits on the same marker only stop the ray.
- Process emitted rows/columns depth-first, with right/down emissions taking priority over left/up emissions when both are discovered together.
- If a downward vertical ray reaches an orange marker on the lower border, stop there without opening a new horizontal ray.

Key insight
- The output is not a global fill: it is the depth-first closure of marker-triggered perpendicular ray turns, with marker pixels acting as one-time controls.

annotation.src: single red start pixel on the left edge
annotation.path: start horizontally; each ray paints until the first original colored marker in each direction, then emits the perpendicular row or column from the cell just before that marker
annotation.trajectory: paint traversed background pixels red while preserving all original markers
annotation.multi_step: process emitted rows/columns depth-first; each marker opens at most once, later hits only stop, and a lower-edge orange marker hit from above is terminal

references.docstring:
Connect hollow rectangular frames into one shortest visible corridor network.

Input structure
- A single foreground color forms disconnected hollow rectangular frames on the background.
- A visible candidate gap is horizontal or vertical, has overlapping frame interiors, and is clear background between the two frames.

Rule
- Select the minimum-length spanning set of visible frame-to-frame gaps.
- For a horizontal selected gap, paint the two boundary rows of the overlapping interiors across the gap, then erase the facing wall cells strictly between those rows.
- For a vertical selected gap, do the transposed operation with boundary columns and the facing top/bottom wall cells.

Key insight
- The connector is determined by the overlap of the rooms' interiors, and longer redundant visible gaps are ignored once the shortest spanning network connects all frames.

annotation.src: pair of hollow rectangular frames s
annotation.dst: clear horizontal or vertical gap d between the frames
annotation.match_cond: s.interiors overlap across d and d contains only background cells
annotation.transform: paint d on the two boundary rows or columns of the interior overlap; erase facing wall cells strictly inside the connector opening
annotation.multi_step: choose visible gaps by increasing gap length as a spanning tree until all frames are one 4-connected object

tags: condition:重叠决定走廊宽度, overlap_corridor_width

references.docstring:
Carve an alternating background checkerboard through the interior of each solid colored rectangle.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- Every non-background object is a monochrome 4-connected filled rectangle.
- Each rectangle is at least 3x3, so it has a border and a nonempty interior.

Rule:
- Preserve each rectangle border unchanged.
- Within each rectangle interior, replace cells whose row-plus-column parity is
  even relative to the interior's top-left cell with the background color.
- Leave the other interior cells and all background cells unchanged.

Key insight:
- The output is not moving the rectangles; it applies the same top-left-anchored
  checkerboard mask independently inside every solid rectangular object.

annotation.src: solid monochrome foreground rectangles on the background
annotation.transform: preserve each rectangle border; inside each rectangle, recolor cells at even parity from the interior top-left to background and leave the alternating cells colored

tags: condition:行列奇偶决定填充, parity_fill

references.docstring:
Stretch a rectilinear foreground line drawing so its outside edges sit next to the control markers.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One foreground color forms a connected rectilinear line drawing made exactly from full horizontal and vertical bars.
- The other foreground color consists of isolated control pixels outside the drawing.
Rule
- Find the unique rectangle that contains the original line drawing and has every control pixel one cell outside one of its sides.
- Move the original outer bars to the corresponding sides of that rectangle, keeping interior bars fixed.
- Redraw the bars across the new rectangle and preserve the control pixels.
Key insight
- The markers do not get connected; they specify the final bounding sides of a stretched line drawing.

annotation.src: rectilinear foreground line drawing made of full horizontal and vertical bars, plus isolated control pixels outside the drawing
annotation.transform: find the unique rectangle containing the drawing with every control pixel one cell outside a side; move only the outer boundary bars to that rectangle, keep interior bars fixed, redraw the bars, and preserve control pixels

references.docstring:
Complete each partial copy of the yellow-marked 3x3 template by adding the template's yellow cells.

Input structure
- A black background contains scattered blue/teal distractors and one full 3x3 sprite whose yellow pixels mark the cells to add.
- The yellow pixels' bounding box is the full template window.
- Partial copies elsewhere already contain the template's non-yellow pixels in the same relative positions.

Rule
- Use the yellow bounding box as the 3x3 template.
- Search every 3x3 window for an exact match to the template's non-yellow pixels.
- At each matching window, paint yellow into the positions that are yellow in the template.

Key insight
- Yellow is not a target marker; it identifies the missing-cell mask to transfer onto every same-layout partial copy.

annotation.src: yellow-marked 3x3 template sprite s
annotation.dst: 3x3 grid windows d
annotation.match_cond: d matches s on every non-yellow cell and has bg/yellow at s.yellow-mask cells
annotation.transform: paint s.yellow-mask cells yellow in each matched d; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Overlay the right side-panel mask onto the left panel only when the two masks do not overlap.

Input structure:
- The input is split by a solid non-background separator column into two equal-size panels.
- The side panels share one background color.
- Each side panel contains exactly one foreground color, forming a positional mask.

Rule:
- Remove the separator column and use the left panel as the output canvas.
- If any foreground cell in the right panel coincides with a foreground cell in the left panel, ignore the right panel.
- Otherwise, copy the right panel foreground cells into their corresponding positions on the left panel.

Key insight:
- The right mask is accepted only when it fits entirely into the empty cells of the left mask.

annotation.src: two equal-size side-panel masks separated by a solid vertical bar
annotation.transform: use the left panel as the output; if the right foreground overlaps any left foreground cell, leave the left panel unchanged, otherwise overlay the right foreground into matching positions
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one side panel

references.docstring:
Build a five-block horizontal strip by alternating the input tile with its left-right reflection.

Input structure
- A nonempty 2D color grid; all cells are part of the source tile.
- The examples use a 4x4 tile and produce a same-height strip five tiles wide.

Rule
- Concatenate five whole-tile blocks across columns.
- Use the original tile in blocks 1, 3, and 5.
- Use the left-right mirror of the tile in blocks 2 and 4.

Key insight
The output is mirrored horizontal wallpaper, not pixel scaling: whole-grid copies alternate orientation.

annotation.src: entire input grid as the source tile
annotation.dst: five horizontal tile slots in the output strip
annotation.transform: fill the slots left to right with [src, left-right reflection of src, src, left-right reflection of src, src]
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input; width multiplied by 5

references.docstring:
Draw the straight segment between the two red markers, turning crossed blue pixels green and crossed empty pixels red.

Input structure
- The input contains only black background, blue foreground pixels, and exactly two red marker pixels.
- The two red markers lie on one horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree diagonal line.

Rule
- Copy the input grid.
- Walk the inclusive straight segment from one red marker to the other.
- Each path cell that was blue becomes green; each path cell that was black or red becomes red.

Key insight
- The red marker pair defines a queen-move path, and the output records which original cells on that path were blue versus not blue.

annotation.src: two red marker pixels
annotation.path: inclusive horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree diagonal segment connecting the markers
annotation.trajectory: paint every cell on the segment according to its input color
annotation.transform: black or red path cells become red; blue path cells become green; all off-path cells remain unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor every candidate object whose run-compressed shape matches the single prototype object, allowing rotation and reflection.
Input structure
A black-background grid contains exactly two foreground colors: one color forms a single prototype object, and the other forms multiple candidate objects.
Rule
Crop each object to its bbox, collapse adjacent identical rows and columns to remove stretch, and recolor every candidate whose collapsed mask is a rotation or reflection of the prototype's collapsed mask.
Key insight
The prototype is a line-drawing symbol; candidate symbols can be stretched in row/column runs, so matching must compare the compressed topology rather than raw size.

annotation.src: candidate objects s in the multi-object foreground color
annotation.dst: single prototype object d in the other foreground color
annotation.match_cond: run-compressed s.shape == run-compressed d.shape up to rotation/reflection
annotation.transform: recolor matched s to d.color; leave nonmatching objects unchanged

references.docstring:
Return the corner tile mask that is missing from the rotation family shown in the input.

Input structure
- The grid is an odd-sized square split by a one-pixel background cross into four square corner tiles.
- Three corner tiles contain masks made from one source color on the background.
- The remaining corner tile is a solid non-background placeholder color.

Rule
- Read the three source masks from the corner tiles.
- Generate the four rotations of that mask family.
- Output the unique rotated mask that is not one of the three source masks, using the source color on the background.

Key insight
The placeholder marks the missing fourth member of a rotation set; the answer is that absent tile, not the placeholder itself.

annotation.src: three source-color masks in the corner tiles around a background cross
annotation.dst: the tile-size output for the solid placeholder corner
annotation.transform: complete the rotation family by outputting the unique rotated mask not already shown, using the source color on the background
annotation.grid_shape: input (2n+1) x (2n+1) -> n x n corner tile

references.docstring:
Fill the interior implied by a left half-outline and its horizontal mirror.

Input structure
A 2D grid contains one background color and one foreground color. The
foreground is the left half of a horizontally symmetric closed outline, with
its global right edge immediately left of the vertical symmetry axis.

Rule
Clear the outline. For each row containing foreground, take the foreground
pixel closest to the axis as the left boundary, mirror it across the
half-column axis just to the right of the global right edge, and fill only
the cells strictly between those two boundary pixels.

Key insight
Row segments near the top and bottom are outline, not fill; the row's
rightmost foreground pixel is the inner boundary that determines that row's
hidden symmetric interior span.

annotation.src: single-color left half-outline; the global rightmost foreground column sits immediately left of the horizontal mirror axis
annotation.dst: interior of the completed horizontally symmetric outline on the same canvas
annotation.transform: erase the visible outline; for each foreground row, mirror the row's rightmost foreground pixel across the half-column axis and fill the cells strictly between the boundary pair with the same color

references.docstring:
Return the hollow 3x3 sprite that is enclosed by the sparse guide mask.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Several monochrome 3x3 hollow-square sprites sit on the background.
- The remaining foreground pixels are a single-color sparse guide mask whose bbox frames one sprite.

Rule
- Find every hollow 3x3 square sprite.
- Build the guide mask from all non-background pixels that are not part of those sprites.
- Return the tight bbox crop of the unique sprite fully contained in the guide mask bbox.

Key insight
- The guide pixels do not draw the output; their bounding rectangle selects which existing hollow-square sprite to crop.

annotation.src: hollow 3x3 square sprite s
annotation.dst: sparse guide-mask bbox d
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox is fully contained in d.bbox
annotation.transform: return the tight bbox crop of matched s
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 crop

references.docstring:
Connect all red control pixels by drawing green orthogonal segments to the unique red spine.

Input structure
- A black background contains only red control pixels.
- Exactly two red pixels share one row or one column; this aligned pair defines the spine segment.
- Every other red pixel lies within the span of that spine along the perpendicular direction.

Rule
- Paint the background cells between the aligned red pair green, preserving the red endpoints.
- If the spine is horizontal, draw a vertical green segment from each other red pixel to the spine.
- If the spine is vertical, draw a horizontal green segment from each other red pixel to the spine.

Key insight
- The only repeated row or column among the red pixels is the connector trunk; all remaining pixels attach to it perpendicularly.

annotation.src: red control pixels on the black background; the only pair sharing a row or column defines the spine
annotation.path: paint the spine between the aligned red pair, then cast each remaining red pixel perpendicularly to the spine along its row or column
annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel on these straight connector segments green
annotation.transform: preserve all red control pixels and leave other background cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Rotate the red segment one quarter-turn clockwise around the grey marker, recoloring its original cells green.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background, exactly one grey marker, and one red
  4-connected segment.
- The red segment is a straight horizontal or vertical bar attached to the
  grey marker at exactly one end.
- The clockwise-rotated red segment fits on the same canvas.

Rule:
- Locate the grey marker and the adjacent red cell, which gives the bar's
  direction away from the marker.
- Recolor every input red cell green.
- Draw a red segment of the same length from the marker in the direction
  obtained by rotating the original direction clockwise.

Key insight:
- The grey marker is the pivot, and the side occupied by the red bar tells
  which perpendicular side receives the new red bar.

annotation.src: straight red bar attached to a single grey pivot on a dominant background
annotation.transform: recolor the original red bar green; from the grey pivot paint an equal-length red bar in the direction 90 degrees clockwise from the original bar

tags: condition:顺时针四分之一圈, clockwise_quarter

references.docstring:
Expand the centered red pixel into a square red V with a periodic blue diagonal fill.

Input structure
- The input is a single odd-length row with black background.
- Exactly one foreground pixel is present, and it is red at the center column.

Rule
- Create an N x N background canvas, where N is the input width.
- Draw red diagonals from the top-center marker down-left and down-right until they hit the side edges.
- Paint blue on the NW-SE diagonal lattice with the marker column's modulo-4 phase, clipped to the strict interior of the red V above the midpoint and unclipped below it.

Key insight
- The lone red pixel is the apex of a triangular pattern; the blue cells are one repeated diagonal family inside and below that triangle.

annotation.src: single centered red marker in a one-row black input
annotation.transform: expand to an N x N black canvas; draw a red V from the top-center marker to both side edges; paint blue on the modulo-4 NW-SE diagonal lattice inside the V and on all rows below it
annotation.grid_shape: N x N square, where N is the input width

references.docstring:
Extract the unique partition cell whose foreground pixels are all one color.

Input structure
- A black-background square grid is divided by full horizontal and vertical
  separator lines of one non-black color into equal square cells.
- Most cells contain scattered foreground noise of several colors.
- Exactly one cell has non-background pixels of a single color only.

Rule
- Ignore the separator lines and split the grid into its equal cells.
- Return the unique cell whose non-background pixels are monochromatic,
  preserving its black pixels and foreground color.

Key insight
- The answer is not built from the whole grid; it is the only separator-free
  cell that is internally color-consistent, while the other cells mix colors.

annotation.src: black-background grid divided into equal square cells by complete one-color separator rows and columns
annotation.transform: crop the unique separator-free cell whose non-background pixels are all the same color; preserve that cell exactly
annotation.grid_shape: one separator-free cell

references.docstring:
Complete the dominant-color object by adding its left-right mirror image.

Input structure
A rectangular grid contains one uniquely most frequent color forming the main
foreground object, with other colors acting as clutter/noise.

Rule
Reflect every pixel of the dominant color across the vertical centerline of
the grid and recolor the reflected cells with that same dominant color.

Key insight
The noisy cells are exactly the missing counterpart pixels needed to make the
dominant-color mask horizontally symmetric.

annotation.summary: Complete the dominant-color mask by adding its horizontal mirror image.
annotation.src: mask of the uniquely most frequent color
annotation.dst: mirror cells across the grid's vertical centerline
annotation.transform: paint each mirrored cell with the source color; preserve all existing pixels elsewhere

references.docstring:
Build a 3x3 mosaic of whole-grid mirror reflections around the original tile.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 color grid; every cell belongs to the source tile.

Rule
- Produce a 9x9 grid split into nine 3x3 tile slots.
- The center slot is the original tile.
- Slots above or below the center reverse source rows.
- Slots left or right of the center reverse source columns.
- Corner slots reverse both rows and columns.

Key insight
The output is reflection wallpaper of the entire small grid, not per-pixel scaling or color-specific processing.

annotation.src: entire 3x3 input grid used as the source tile
annotation.dst: 3x3 array of 3x3 tile slots in the output
annotation.transform: place src in the center; use vertical reflections above/below, horizontal reflections left/right, and 180-degree reflections in the corners
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 3

references.docstring:
Erase the control bars and tile each matched sprite toward its bar.

Input structure
- The background contains colored non-line sprites plus one-cell-thick control
  bars.
- A horizontal bar has the same column span as a sprite; a vertical bar has
  the same row span as a sprite.

Rule
- Remove every control bar.
- For each bar, find the nearest sprite aligned with the bar's span on the
  perpendicular axis.
- Repeat that sprite periodically from its original position toward the bar,
  clipping at the grid boundary and leaving sprite-background cells empty.

Key insight
- The bar is not copied itself; it gives the direction and terminal line for
  repeating the aligned sprite motif.

annotation.src: colored non-line sprite s matched to a one-cell-thick control bar sharing s's row span or column span
annotation.path: straight cardinal path from s toward the matching bar: vertical for a horizontal bar with the same columns, horizontal for a vertical bar with the same rows; stop after the repeated sprite covers the bar line
annotation.trajectory: copy s every full sprite height/width along the path, clipping at grid edges and treating background cells inside s as transparent
annotation.dst: aligned control bar marking the terminal row or column
annotation.transform: erase the control bars; keep original sprites and all copied sprite pixels

references.docstring:
Render the lower grey slot array by replacing each colored control pixel with the matching legend template.

Input structure
A background grid has a top legend: each colored marker sits one row above and one column left of a
2x2 template drawn in a shared template ink color.  Below it is a rectangular array of 2x2 grey slots,
where a slot may contain one colored control pixel in place of grey.

Rule
Read the legend as color -> 2x2 template mask.  Convert the lower slot array into a compact array with
the same row/column layout and one background separator row/column between neighboring tiles.  Empty
grey slots become blank tiles; a colored slot becomes that color's legend mask recolored with the
control color.

Key insight
The colored pixel in a grey slot names which top legend template to stamp; its position inside the slot
is irrelevant.

annotation.src: colored control pixels inside lower 2x2 grey slots s
annotation.dst: top legend 2x2 template masks d
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.marker_color
annotation.transform: replace each lower slot with d.mask recolored to s.color in the compact output lattice; slots without a control pixel become background
annotation.grid_shape: lower R x C slot array -> (2R+R-1) x (2C+C-1) output with one background separator row/column
annotation.symbol_instructions: top legend maps each colored marker to the adjacent 2x2 template mask

references.docstring:
Rebuild the visible frame fragments as centered concentric square rings.

Input structure
The input has a dominant background and several non-background colors. Each
foreground color marks one square frame or center block, possibly with gaps
caused by overlap with other frames. The intended side length of a color is
the larger side of the bbox of all pixels of that color.

Rule
Sort the colors by intended side length from largest to smallest. Create a
square output whose side is the largest length, then draw each color as the
border of the centered square with that side length.

Key insight
Positions in the input are only a scrambled/overlapped display of the
nested frames; the bbox side lengths provide the layer order and output
ring sizes.

annotation.src: foreground color masks s, each with side length max bbox height/width, ordered largest to smallest
annotation.dst: centered square frame layers d ordered from outermost to innermost
annotation.match_cond: rank(s by decreasing side length) == rank(d from outside inward)
annotation.transform: draw each s.color as the one-cell border of its matched centered square
annotation.grid_shape: square side length is the largest source bbox side length

references.docstring:
Complete the wallpaper by replacing black holes with the colors from the inferred repeating tile.

Input structure
- The input is a two-dimensional grid containing a repeated rectangular color tile.
- Black pixels are holes in that wallpaper, not part of the tile.
- Every tile phase is visible at least once in a non-black cell.

Rule
- Find the unique smallest row and column period whose non-black cells agree by repeated phase.
- Reconstruct the full grid by writing the tile color at each cell's phase.

Key insight
- The corrupted cells are exactly the black pixels; their colors are determined by the repeated phase shared with non-black copies elsewhere.

annotation.src: non-black cells of a repeated rectangular tile, with black cells as missing holes
annotation.transform: infer the smallest fully observed row and column period, then fill every black cell with the color at the same tile phase

tags: condition:非缺损像素一致性, non_corrupted_consistency

references.docstring:
Slide each solid rectangular body by the length and direction of its one-cell-thick tail, then redraw the scene with sliders on top.

Input structure
- The background is black.
- Each foreground color represents one object: either a filled rectangle, possibly partly hidden by another color, or a filled rectangle with a straight one-cell-thick tail of length at least two.
- Slider tails extend in one cardinal direction from one side of their rectangle; shifted slider rectangles remain in bounds and do not overlap one another.

Rule
- Restore every non-slider object as the filled rectangle of its input bounding box.
- For every slider, discard the tail and translate only the rectangular body by the tail length in the tail direction.
- Draw the translated slider rectangles over the restored static rectangles.

Key insight
- A thin tail is a displacement vector for its rectangle, while wider missing areas inside another color's bounding box are occlusion that should be restored.

annotation.src: colored slider objects, each a solid rectangular body with a one-pixel-thick tail
annotation.path: straight in the cardinal direction of the tail for exactly the tail length
annotation.trajectory: move only the solid rectangular body to its final translated bbox; do not leave a trail
