references.docstring:
Recolor each grey placeholder pixel with the visible control color in its row.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background, grey placeholder pixels, and colored row control pixels in one marker column.
- Every row containing grey pixels contains exactly one non-background, non-grey control pixel; rows without grey contain no other foreground.

Rule
- Preserve background and control pixels.
- For each row, replace all grey pixels with that row's control color.

Key insight
- The grey shape is not filled as a connected object; the row-aligned control marker supplies the replacement color independently for every grey pixel in that row.

annotation.src: grey placeholder pixels and same-row control pixels in the marker column
annotation.transform: replace each grey pixel with the color of the control pixel in the same row; preserve background and control pixels
annotation.symbol_instructions: marker-column control pixels give the replacement color for grey pixels in their row

references.docstring:
Extend the top colored columns downward, routing blocked columns around horizontal obstacle segments.

Input structure
The background is the dominant color.  Row 0 contains a single non-background
source color forming vertical columns at the top.  The remaining foreground
color appears only as one row of horizontal obstacle segments below those
columns.

Rule
Copy the input, then extend every source column to the bottom of the grid.
If a source column hits an obstacle segment, paint a horizontal run on the
row just above the obstacle from the source column to the nearest outside
side of that segment, then continue vertically downward in that outside
column.  Exact midpoint ties detour to the right side.

Key insight
The red segments do not move or change color; they only redirect the falling
teal columns to the closest free side before the columns continue downward.

annotation.src: vertical teal source columns at the top edge
annotation.path: drop each source column downward; if it reaches a red horizontal segment, slide on the row above that segment to the nearest outside column, using the right side on exact ties, then continue downward there
annotation.trajectory: paint the falling and sliding trail with teal
annotation.transform: preserve the red obstacle segments and existing teal pixels

references.docstring:
Count the marker pixels inside the rectangular frame and render that count as a 3x3 row-major tally.
Input structure
A background grid contains one one-cell-thick rectangular frame color and one marker color scattered both inside and outside the frame.
Rule
Return a 3x3 background grid with the first N cells in row-major order set to the marker color, where N is the number of marker pixels strictly inside the frame.
Key insight
The rectangular frame defines the only region to summarize; same-colored markers outside it are distractors.

annotation.src: marker-color pixels strictly inside the one-pixel rectangular frame
annotation.transform: count those marker pixels and fill that many cells of a 3x3 background grid in row-major order with the marker color
annotation.grid_shape: fixed 3x3 count tally

references.docstring:
Tile the input 3 by 3, draw blue across each repeated foreground row, and draw green on nearby northwest-southeast diagonals.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and exactly one non-background foreground color.
- The foreground color may appear in one or more cells.
- Blue and green are reserved trace colors, not source foreground colors.

Rule
- Repeat the whole input three times vertically and horizontally.
- In the tiled canvas, every background cell in a row containing a repeated foreground pixel becomes blue.
- Every still-background cell one step northwest or southeast of a repeated foreground pixel becomes green.

Key insight
The repeated foreground pixels define the output scaffold; horizontal row traces have priority, and diagonal marks only fill cells that remain background.

annotation.src: input grid as a tile, with its non-background foreground mask
annotation.dst: 3-by-3 array of input-sized tile slots
annotation.transform: copy the input into every tile slot; in the tiled canvas, recolor background cells in rows containing foreground to blue, then recolor still-background cells one step northwest or southeast of a foreground pixel to green
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width tripled

references.docstring:
Paint a teal diamond envelope around each straight foreground bar.

Input structure
- The grid has a single background color and one non-background foreground color.
- Every foreground object is a solid horizontal or vertical one-cell-thick bar.
- Teal is absent from the input and is reserved for the added envelope pixels.

Rule
- Keep every original foreground bar unchanged.
- For a horizontal bar, paint teal rows above and below it; each step away from the bar shortens the interval by one pixel at both ends.
- For a vertical bar, apply the same shrinking construction rotated ninety degrees.

Key insight
- A bar of length L defines a centered diamond of radius floor((L - 1) / 2), with the original bar forming the middle line and teal filling only the surrounding background cells.

annotation.src: solid horizontal or vertical one-cell-thick foreground bars on a background
annotation.transform: around each bar, paint background pixels teal in the centered diamond envelope: each step away from the bar shortens the interval by one pixel from both ends; preserve the original bars

references.docstring:
Compress the colored pixels on a 5x5 X into the corresponding 3x3 square outline.

Input structure
- The input is a 5x5 grid with a dominant background color.
- Every non-background pixel lies on one of the two diagonals, forming an X.
- All diagonal positions are colored foreground pixels.

Rule
- Keep the center pixel at the center of the 3x3 output.
- Project the northwest diagonal arm onto the top edge from left to center.
- Project the northeast arm onto the right edge from top to center.
- Project the southwest arm onto the left edge from center to bottom.
- Project the southeast arm onto the bottom edge from center to right.

Key insight
- The output is not a crop; it is the same X-shaped set of nine colored pixels
  folded into the perimeter and center of a 3x3 grid.

annotation.src: 5x5 grid whose non-background pixels form an X
annotation.transform: fold the four diagonal arms into the corresponding edges of a 3x3 square and keep the center pixel centered

references.docstring:
Restore the black-erased cells by tiling the smallest repeating pattern visible in the remaining cells.

Input structure
A same-size grid contains an otherwise regular two-dimensional color lattice, with black rectangles masking some cells.
Rule
Treat black pixels as unknown, infer the unique smallest rectangular period that agrees with every non-black pixel, and tile it across the full grid.
Key insight
The visible cells still include every residue of the repeating tile, so the black pixels are occlusions rather than objects to preserve.

annotation.src: the visible non-black cells of the repeating two-dimensional color lattice
annotation.transform: treat black pixels as occlusions; infer the unique smallest rectangular repeating tile consistent with the visible cells and tile it over the full grid

tags: condition:可见像素约束推断, infer_from_visible

references.docstring:
Extend the input's diagonal color band onto a canvas with doubled height and width.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Foreground cells form a narrow row-periodic band along one diagonal direction.
- If the band slopes up-right/down-left, a horizontal flip makes it a down-right band in the top-left quadrant.

Rule:
- Canonicalize the band so the input is the top-left quadrant of the larger pattern.
- Learn the occupied diagonal offsets and the smallest row period of colors, including background gaps within the band.
- Paint the same offset/period rule onto a 2H x 2W background canvas, then undo the horizontal flip if needed.

Key insight:
The input is a corner crop of a larger periodic diagonal pattern, not a pixel-scaled image.

annotation.src: top-left or top-right corner crop of a narrow row-periodic diagonal color band
annotation.transform: extend the same diagonal offsets and periodic color/background gaps through the larger canvas
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Draw the green perimeter of the parallelogram whose opposite corners are the two marker pixels.

Input structure
- The input is a same-size canvas with a dominant background and exactly two foreground marker pixels of one color.
- The marker-to-marker offset has both row and column components, with unequal magnitudes.

Rule
- Decompose the vector between markers into a 45-degree diagonal vector plus the remaining horizontal/vertical vector.
- Treat those two vectors as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, with the markers as opposite corners.
- Paint the four sides green while preserving the marker pixels.

Key insight
- The outline is not a direct line interpolation; it is the perimeter of the parallelogram induced by the diagonal and axis-aligned parts of the marker offset.

annotation.src: two same-color marker pixels on the background, used as opposite corners of an implied parallelogram
annotation.transform: decompose the marker-to-marker offset into a 45-degree diagonal side and the remaining horizontal/vertical side; paint green on the parallelogram perimeter and keep the markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Repeat the whole square input tile once per input row and column.

Input structure
- A nonempty square 2D color grid.
- The entire grid is the motif to be repeated; individual pixels are not enlarged.

Rule
- Let N be the side length of the input grid.
- Tile the full input grid N times vertically and N times horizontally.

Key insight
The output size grows from N x N to N^2 x N^2 because the unit of repetition is the complete input tile.

annotation.src: entire square input grid as one periodic tile
annotation.dst: N x N array of original-size tile slots, where N is the input side length
annotation.transform: copy the input tile unchanged into every slot
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by N

references.docstring:
Crop the 4-connected foreground sprite whose colored pattern occurs only once among otherwise duplicated sprites.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Foreground pixels form several separated 4-connected sprites.
- Every distractor sprite has an identical colored bounding-box crop elsewhere in the grid.

Rule
- Crop each 4-connected foreground sprite to its bounding box.
- Compare the exact colored crops, including background pixels inside each crop.
- Return the only crop whose exact pattern occurs once.

Key insight
- The answer is the outlier sprite by repetition count, not by position, color id, or size alone.

annotation.src: 4-connected foreground sprites on the background; all distractor sprite crops repeat elsewhere
annotation.transform: crop and return the single sprite whose exact colored bounding-box crop occurs once
annotation.grid_shape: bounding-box crop of the singleton sprite

references.docstring:
Recolor each grey pixel that has a same-row horizontal mirror partner to blue.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background and one grey foreground mask.
- The grid width is even, so horizontal mirror partners are distinct cells.
- Blue is absent from the input and is introduced only in the output.

Rule:
- For each grey pixel, look at the cell reflected across the vertical midline.
- If the reflected cell is also grey, recolor the original pixel blue.
- Leave unpaired grey pixels and all background pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The output marks the horizontally symmetric grey pairs in each row; grey pixels without a matching mirror partner are noise.

annotation.src: grey foreground pixels on a black even-width grid
annotation.transform: recolor a grey pixel to blue iff the grey mask also contains its same-row horizontal mirror pixel; preserve unpaired grey pixels and background

references.docstring:
Collapse each run of identical neighboring rows and columns to one representative.

Input structure:
- The grid is a stretched small pattern: foreground bars make some rows and columns
  distinctive, while the blank bands between them duplicate adjacent row or column
  vectors.
- Repeated bands are contiguous; the colors themselves do not define special cases.

Rule:
- Scan rows from top to bottom and keep the first row of each consecutive run of
  identical rows.
- Scan columns from left to right and keep the first column of each consecutive run of
  identical columns.
- The output is the intersection of those kept row and column representatives.

Key insight:
- The large image is just a run-length-expanded version of the target pattern along
  both axes, so removing adjacent duplicate row and column vectors recovers it.

annotation.src: grid with consecutive runs of identical row vectors and consecutive runs of identical column vectors
annotation.transform: keep the first row of each identical-row run and the first column of each identical-column run
annotation.grid_shape: number of row runs x number of column runs

references.docstring:
Extend broken horizontal bars vertically through their gap columns.

Input structure
- The background is empty color, and each control cell is a one-pixel gap
  inside a horizontal bar: its immediate left and right neighbors have the
  same non-background color.
- Gap cells in the same column form a top-to-bottom stack, with a
  non-background vertical marker color somewhere below the last gap.
Rule
- For each gap column, sort its gaps by row. Paint from the top through each
  gap row with that row's horizontal-bar color, then paint the remaining
  lower part of the column with the marker color found below the last gap.
Key insight
- A gap column is an implicit vertical color ruler: horizontal bars provide
  the upper breakpoints, and the lower marker provides the final segment.

annotation.src: background pixels whose left and right neighbors are the same non-bg color, grouped by column, plus the unique non-bg marker color below each column
annotation.transform: fill each selected column top-to-bottom: each gap row's bar color applies from the previous breakpoint through that gap, and the lower marker color applies after the last gap; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Complete the four inner quadrants as flipped, recolored copies of the top-left template.

Input structure:
- A one-cell background border surrounds a square interior split into a 2x2 block grid.
- The upper-left block is a complete two-color template.
- The other blocks contain sparse control pixels placed where their corresponding
  flipped template symbols should take those colors.

Rule:
- Use the upper-left block unchanged for the first quadrant.
- Horizontally flip the template for the upper-right quadrant, vertically flip it
  for the lower-left quadrant, and flip both axes for the lower-right quadrant.
- In each quadrant, every non-background input pixel maps the transformed
  template symbol under it to that pixel's color; symbols without a control
  pixel become background.

Key insight: The control pixels are not objects to move; they are a local
recoloring legend for the transformed template underneath each quadrant.

annotation.src: complete two-color template in the upper-left interior block plus sparse control pixels in the other interior blocks
annotation.dst: the four equal blocks of the bordered interior
annotation.transform: fill the upper-left block with the template, upper-right with its horizontal reflection, lower-left with its vertical reflection, and lower-right with both reflections; recolor each transformed template by the local control pixels, leaving unmapped template symbols as background
annotation.symbol_instructions: within each target block, a control pixel gives the output color for the transformed template symbol at that same relative position

references.docstring:
Remove blank separator columns and slide each vertical object group so adjacent connector endpoints touch.

Input structure
A short strip contains monochrome path-like object groups, each occupying a contiguous run of non-background columns; runs are separated by all-background columns. Each group has a unique degree-1 foreground endpoint on both its left and right outer edge.

Rule
Delete the all-background separator columns. Keep the first group in its original vertical position, then process the remaining groups from left to right: shift each group vertically, without rotation or recoloring, so its left endpoint is on the same row as the previous placed group's right endpoint, and paste it immediately to the right.

Key insight
The intended contacts are the degree-1 edge endpoints, not every possible foreground edge overlap, which makes the packed strip a single connected chain.

annotation.src: monochrome path-like column groups s separated by all-background columns, ordered left to right
annotation.dst: adjacent packed column slots d in the same left-to-right order
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: remove separator columns; keep the first group at its original vertical offset, then paste each later group shifted vertically so its left degree-1 edge endpoint touches the previous placed group's right degree-1 edge endpoint
annotation.multi_step: after each placement, that group's right endpoint row becomes the connector row for the next group
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input; width is the sum of the non-background column-group widths

references.docstring:
Overlay two stacked foreground masks and recolor their union yellow.

Input structure
- The input is a 2D grid with black background.
- The grid has even height and splits into two equal-size panels.
- The top panel contains a green mask and the bottom panel contains a grey mask.
Rule
- Align the two panels cell by cell.
- Output one panel-sized black grid.
- Paint a yellow pixel wherever either aligned input cell is foreground.
Key insight
- The output is the union of the two foreground masks after vertical alignment.

annotation.src: two same-size foreground/background panels stacked vertically, green above grey
annotation.transform: replace each aligned pixel pair with yellow iff at least one source pixel is foreground, otherwise black
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one panel

references.docstring:
Slide every foreground object horizontally to the right until it settles against the border or another settled object.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color and several separate 4-connected foreground objects.
- Each foreground object is a small multicolor rectangle-like sprite on the same canvas.
- Objects may overlap in their row ranges, so rightward movement can make a left object stop behind a right object.

Rule
- Treat each 4-connected foreground object as a rigid sprite.
- Simultaneously move every sprite one column right whenever its next cells are inside the grid and not blocked by a sprite that cannot move.
- Repeat the simultaneous move until no sprite can move; preserve each sprite's internal colors and shape.

Key insight
- The output is the terminal state of eastward gravity on the foreground sprites, not a recoloring or per-row sort.

annotation.src: each 4-connected foreground sprite s
annotation.path: straight eastward slide until a one-column shift would leave the grid or collide with a sprite that can no longer move
annotation.trajectory: move s rigidly to its terminal position, preserving its internal color pattern
annotation.transform: old sprite cells become background
annotation.multi_step: All unblocked sprites shift one column east together each step; chains of overlapping row ranges settle from the right border or rightmost stopped sprite back to the left.

references.docstring:
Toggle the colors on straight row or column segments bracketed by opposite-edge yellow markers.

Input structure
- Yellow marker pixels appear in aligned pairs on one pair of opposite grid edges.
- A left-edge/right-edge marker pair selects that full row segment; a top-edge/bottom-edge marker pair selects that column segment.
- The strict interior cells of selected segments use only black, teal, pink, and orange.

Rule
- Keep the yellow endpoint markers unchanged.
- For every selected segment, recolor each strict interior cell by toggling black <-> teal and pink <-> orange.
- Leave all cells outside the selected segments unchanged.

Key insight
- The marker pair orientation selects the path; the path cells are not filled with a constant color but have their two color pairs inverted in place.

annotation.src: rows or columns selected by yellow marker pairs on opposite grid edges
annotation.transform: toggle each strict interior pixel between paired markers: black <-> teal and pink <-> orange; keep the yellow markers and all other cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Stamp the input sprite in a periodic right-and-down pattern where every third horizontal copy is pink.

Input structure
- A black/dominant background contains exactly one 8-connected foreground sprite.
- The sprite has a tight bounding box; its mask, height, and width define the repeated tile.
- Repeated copies are separated by one background row or column.

Rule
- Starting at the sprite's original upper-left bbox corner, place slots every sprite_width+1 columns.
- On the original sprite row, fill the horizontal slots with the sprite mask; slots 0,1,3,4,... keep the source color, while slots 2,5,8,... become pink.
- Starting at each pink horizontal slot, repeat pink copies downward every sprite_height+1 rows.
- Clip any copy that extends beyond the grid edge.

Key insight
- The first row establishes a repeating two-source-color then one-pink rhythm, and only the pink columns continue vertically.

annotation.src: single foreground sprite mask and bbox dimensions
annotation.dst: same-grid slots spaced one blank row/column apart from the source bbox upper-left
annotation.transform: stamp the sprite across the first slot row, keeping the source color except every third horizontal slot is pink; repeat only the pink slots downward and clip at grid edges

tags: condition:周期内指定位变色, cyclic_pos_recolored

references.docstring:
Fill the frame interior with the frame color except for the rectangle spanned by the marker pixels.

Input structure
- A background, a one-cell-thick rectangular foreground frame, and marker
  pixels of the other foreground color inside the frame.
Rule
- Use the frame bbox and marker bbox.
- Recolor background cells strictly inside the frame to the frame color unless
  they lie inside the marker bbox; keep frame and marker cells unchanged.
Key insight
- The marker pixels define a protected rectangular window, not paths to draw.

annotation.src: one-cell rectangular frame with background interior and marker pixels inside
annotation.transform: fill background cells inside the frame with the frame color except within the marker-pixel bbox; keep the frame and markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Compare the two separated panels, keeping shared pixels and marking pixels that appear in only one panel.

Input structure
- The input has two equal-width panels separated by one solid non-background divider column.
- Background is the dominant color, and the divider color appears only in the divider.

Rule
- Remove the divider and compare the left and right panels cell by cell.
- If both panels have the same value at a cell, copy that value.
- If only the left panel has foreground at a cell, write red.
- If only the right panel has foreground at a cell, write blue.

Key insight
- The output is a per-position comparison map of two aligned panels, not a crop of either panel.

annotation.src: aligned cell pairs from two equal-size side panels separated by a solid vertical divider
annotation.transform: remove the divider; copy the shared color when both cells match, output red for left-only foreground, blue for right-only foreground, and background for background/background
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one side panel

references.docstring:
Paint every background cell on the same row/column parity lattice as the single colored marker.

Input structure
- A 2D grid containing black background pixels, grey fixed pixels, and exactly one non-grey/non-black colored marker pixel.

Rule
- The marker's row parity and column parity define the selected lattice.
- Recolor each black background pixel with the marker color iff both its row parity and column parity match the marker.
- Leave grey pixels and all background pixels on the other three parity lattices unchanged.

Key insight
- The marker is copied by coordinate parity, not by connectivity through the grey layout.

annotation.src: black background pixels plus the unique non-black non-grey marker pixel
annotation.transform: copy the marker color to every black pixel with the same row parity and column parity as the marker; keep grey pixels and other black pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Enlarge the whole 3x3 grid by the number of distinct colors present.

Input structure
The input is a 3x3 color grid, and every pixel belongs to the source pattern.

Rule
Count all distinct colors in the input. Replace each input pixel by a solid
square block with side length equal to that count.

Key insight
The output scale factor is encoded by palette diversity, not by any specific
color identity.

annotation.src: all pixels of the 3x3 input grid, summarized by the number of distinct colors
annotation.transform: count all distinct input colors and replace each pixel by a same-color square block of that side length
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by the number of distinct colors

references.docstring:
Summarize each colored frame as a row whose length is the number of gray markers it contains.

Input structure
The input has a dominant background, several 4-connected colored frame
objects, and gray marker pixels placed inside those frames. Gray is not a
frame color, and every marker lies inside exactly one colored frame bbox.

Rule
For each colored frame, count the gray marker pixels inside its bounding
box. Sort the frames by this count from smallest to largest, then create
one output row per frame: the frame color repeated for its marker count,
padded on the right with background to the largest count.

Key insight
The output is not a spatial crop of the scene; it is a count summary where
the gray marker population inside each frame determines both row length and
row order.

annotation.src: colored 4-connected frame objects, each with gray marker pixels inside its bbox
annotation.dst: output rows ordered top-to-bottom by increasing gray-marker count
annotation.match_cond: rank(s.gray_marker_count ascending) == rank(d.row_order top-to-bottom)
annotation.transform: paint each row with s.color repeated s.gray_marker_count times, then right-pad with background
annotation.grid_shape: number of rows is the number of frames; width is the largest gray-marker count

references.docstring:
Extract the unique foreground color mask whose cropped shape is symmetric across a vertical axis.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background and several colored masks.
- Each non-background color forms one candidate mask, possibly split into multiple 4-connected objects.
- Exactly one candidate's bounding-box crop is invariant under left-right reflection.

Rule:
- For each non-background color, crop all pixels of that color to their bounding box.
- Select the unique crop that equals its left-right mirror image.
- Return that crop, with non-selected cells in the crop set to the background color.

Key insight:
- The target is not identified by its color or size; it is the only color mask with vertical mirror symmetry.

annotation.summary: Extract the only color mask whose cropped shape has vertical mirror symmetry.
annotation.src: non-background color masks, each cropped to its own bounding box
annotation.transform: select the unique crop invariant under left-right reflection and return it with background holes preserved
annotation.grid_shape: bbox of the selected color mask

references.docstring:
Count the upward and downward red T tetrominoes into fixed green and blue tally panels.

Input structure
- A black background containing only red 4-connected T tetromino objects.
- Each object is a 2x3 T, either with its stem above the horizontal bar or below it.

Rule
- Make a 3x6 black output split into two 3x3 panels.
- For each upward T, fill the next corner slot in the left panel with green.
- For each downward T, fill the next corner slot in the right panel with blue.
- The slot order inside each panel is top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right.

Key insight
- The red objects' positions are irrelevant; only the count of each T orientation is summarized.

annotation.src: 4-connected red T tetromino objects on black, classified by whether the stem is above or below the horizontal bar
annotation.transform: count upward T objects and paint that many green corner slots in the left 3x3 panel; count downward T objects and paint that many blue corner slots in the right 3x3 panel; slot order is top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right
annotation.grid_shape: fixed 3x6 tally grid

references.docstring:
Outline every closed blue rim by painting its outside boundary red and its hole-side boundary green.

Input structure:
- The canvas background is black and all foreground pixels are blue.
- Blue pixels form one or more 4-connected objects; some objects enclose black holes.
- A hole is a 4-connected black component that does not touch the grid edge and is adjacent to exactly one blue object.

Rule:
- Leave blue pixels unchanged.
- For each hole-enclosing blue object, color edge-connected black cells red when they touch that object in the 8-neighborhood.
- Color black hole cells green when they touch their enclosing blue object in the 8-neighborhood.
- Complete the red outline at one-cell top-left diagonal closures of the filled rim.

Key insight:
- The task is not filling whole regions; it labels the two sides of each closed rim, while open blue objects have no enclosed hole and stay unchanged.

annotation.src: 4-connected blue objects on a black background; some objects enclose 4-connected black holes
annotation.transform: preserve blue pixels; for each object that encloses a hole, paint its outside one-cell outline red and its hole-side one-cell outline green, including diagonal corner cells; leave open objects unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor all copies of the teal prototype symbol and the straight symbol-slot runs between aligned copies.

Input structure
- The grid is a table of 3x3 symbol slots separated and bordered by one-pixel background lines.
- Each occupied slot contains a single-color symbol mask.
- Exactly one slot is teal; its 3x3 mask is the prototype.

Rule
- Every slot whose symbol mask matches the teal prototype is recolored teal.
- In each table row or column, slots strictly between consecutive matching prototype slots are recolored orange.
- The symbol masks and all background separator pixels are preserved.

Key insight
- The visible colors mark roles, but the matching relation is the 3x3 shape mask; orange marks the row/column intervals connecting repeated prototype masks.

annotation.src: unique teal 3x3 symbol slot s in the separated table
annotation.dst: all 3x3 symbol slots d in the table
annotation.match_cond: d.mask == s.mask
annotation.transform: recolor every matching d teal; recolor nonmatching symbol slots strictly between consecutive matching slots in the same row or column orange

references.docstring:
Paint the blank separator row or column inside the foreground bounding box green across the whole grid.

Input structure
A background grid contains one colored foreground mask whose bounding box has exactly one completely empty interior row or column.

Rule
Find the foreground bounding box and locate the all-background row or column strictly inside it; recolor that entire grid row or column green.

Key insight
The blank interior line is the separation axis between the colored subregions, and the output marks this axis over the full canvas.

annotation.src: single-color foreground mask on bg with one all-background interior row or column through its bbox
annotation.transform: paint that separator row/column green across the entire grid; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Sort the separated 3x3 tiles by their number of blue pixels and repack them from bottom-left to top-right.

Input structure
The grid is an 11x11 canvas divided by two full black rows and two full
black columns into a 3x3 array of 3x3 tiles. Each tile contains only blue
and red pixels.

Rule
Count the blue pixels in each tile. Sort the nine tiles by that count in
increasing order, then place them unchanged into the tile slots starting at
the bottom-left, moving left-to-right across each row, and continuing upward.

Key insight
The internal tile patterns are not edited; the puzzle is an ordering task
where blue-pixel density determines each tile's rank.

annotation.src: 3x3 blue/red tiles s separated by black grid lines, ordered by increasing count of blue pixels
annotation.dst: 3x3 tile slots d ordered from bottom-left to top-right, left-to-right within each row
annotation.match_cond: rank(s.blue_pixel_count) == rank(d.bottom_to_top_row_major_order)
annotation.transform: copy each tile unchanged into its ranked slot and keep the black separator lines

references.docstring:
Add a mirrored colored copy of each green tabbed outline on the side opposite its one-pixel tab.

Input structure
- The black background contains one or more 4-connected green outline objects.
- Each green object has a bounding box with exactly one side containing a single green tab pixel.
- The intended reflected copy is separated from the original bounding box by one background row or column and may be clipped by the grid edge.

Rule
- If the tab is on the left or right, mirror the object horizontally and place it on the opposite side in blue.
- If the tab is on the top or bottom, mirror the object vertically and place it on the opposite side in teal.
- Keep every original green pixel unchanged and paint only background cells reached by the reflected copy.

Key insight
- The lone boundary pixel identifies both the mirror axis and the side to avoid; the copy appears across the object's opposite bbox side with a one-cell gap.

annotation.src: 4-connected green outline objects on the background, each with one bbox side containing a single tab pixel
annotation.transform: mirror each object to the opposite side of its tab with a one-cell gap; color horizontal mirrors blue and vertical mirrors teal, clip off-grid pixels, and preserve the green originals

references.docstring:
Move the grey divider to the far edge of the left-hand mirror slot and recolor matching red markers blue.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one full-height grey vertical divider.
- Blue marker pixels are to the left of the divider; red marker pixels are to the right.

Rule
- Let the divider be at column k; erase it and draw it at column 2*k+1.
- Reflect the horizontal span of the left blue markers across the original divider.
- If red markers between the old and new divider occupy exactly that reflected column span, recolor those red pixels blue.

Key insight
- The new divider creates a mirror slot with the same width as the left partition; only the red mask whose column span matches the reflected blue span is converted.

annotation.src: blue marker mask s left of the full-height grey divider
annotation.dst: red marker mask d in the mirror slot between the old and shifted divider
annotation.match_cond: d.column_span == reflection of s.column_span across the old divider
annotation.transform: move the grey divider from column k to column 2*k+1; recolor matched d from red to blue and preserve all other markers

tags: condition:反射跨度匹配重涂, recolor_reflect_match

references.docstring:
Recover the solid marker rectangle from a virtually centered two-axis mirror pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a square crop of a larger pattern mirrored across both center axes.
- One color is structurally unique because all of its pixels form one solid rectangular marker.
- The mirror coordinate is two cells outside the visible crop, so each known pixel matches positions with row or column index `shape + 1 - index`.

Rule:
- Locate the marker rectangle and make an output grid with the same height and width.
- For each marker pixel, copy the single visible color from its horizontal, vertical, or 180-degree mirror orbit.
- If the whole orbit is hidden or outside the crop, use the transposed upper-left representative of that orbit.

Key insight:
- The rectangle is an occlusion mask, not an object to preserve; the answer is the missing crop of the virtual mirror pattern.

annotation.src: visible crop of a larger pattern mirrored across both center axes, with one solid rectangular marker hiding a region
annotation.transform: return the marker-sized hidden region; each marker pixel is recovered from its horizontal, vertical, or 180-degree mirror orbit using virtual coordinate shape+1-index, and cropped-edge orbits use the transposed upper-left representative
annotation.grid_shape: output height and width equal the solid marker rectangle

references.docstring:
Move each scattered color into the rectangular frame whose interior checkerboard has the same cell count.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- Foreground contains one or more one-cell-thick rectangular frames.
- All non-frame foreground pixels are isolated markers grouped by color.

Rule:
- For each frame, count the cells of the checkerboard pattern inside its border,
  starting at the upper-left interior cell.
- Match that frame to the unique outside marker color with the same number of pixels.
- Erase all outside markers and paint the matched color into the frame interior's
  upper-left-starting checkerboard cells.

Key insight:
- The scattered pixels are not placed by their coordinates; their color populations
  are counts that select which frame interior they should fill.

annotation.src: outside monochromatic marker mask s
annotation.dst: hollow rectangular frame interior d
annotation.match_cond: |s| == number of upper-left-starting checkerboard cells in d
annotation.transform: erase s from original cells and fill those checkerboard cells of d with s.color

references.docstring:
Recolor every non-isolated black object in the blue field to teal.

Input structure:
- The grid contains only blue background pixels and black foreground pixels.
- Black pixels form 4-connected objects, including singleton noise pixels.

Rule:
- Keep all blue pixels unchanged.
- Keep every singleton black object unchanged.
- Recolor every black object with area greater than one to teal.

Key insight:
- The distinction is 4-connectivity among black pixels: touching black pixels are
  real objects to mark, while isolated black pixels are preserved as noise.

annotation.src: 4-connected black objects on a blue background
annotation.transform: recolor each black object with area greater than one to teal; preserve singleton black pixels and all blue pixels

references.docstring:
Overlay the two side masks split by the separator column and recolor their union red.

Input structure

- The separator divides the remaining columns into equal left and right regions.
- Each side region contains background plus one foreground mask color.

Rule
- Pair cells by their position in the left and right regions.
- Mark an output cell when either paired input cell is foreground.

- The separator is only a partition marker; the output is the union of the two aligned side masks.

annotation.grid_shape: same height as input and half the non-separator width

references.docstring:
Collapse a grid made by stretching a smaller color matrix into duplicate row and column runs.

Input structure
The input is a 2-D color grid with no empty background; each answer row has been expanded into
one or more identical adjacent rows, and each answer column into one or more identical adjacent
columns.

Rule
Keep the first row from each maximal run of identical neighboring rows, and keep the first
column from each maximal run of identical neighboring columns.

Key insight
The visible colors already form the answer matrix; the only operation is removing redundant
row and column repetitions from the expanded blocks.

references.docstring:
Move aligned singleton markers along straight sightlines until they touch the nearest 2x2 block, leaving non-sightline and lower-left distractor markers fixed.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One foreground color forms filled 2x2 blocks.
- The other foreground color forms singleton marker pixels.

Rule
- For each marker, find clear horizontal or vertical sightlines to any 2x2 block and choose the unique nearest block by travel distance.
- Move that marker to the adjacent ring cell on the same row or column of the chosen block.
- Markers with no clear sightline stay in place; a lower-row marker to the left of a block also stays fixed when that block already has chosen vertical markers both above and below it.

Key insight
- The red 2x2 blocks act as magnets, so each direct marker ray is compressed to the one-cell ring around its nearest block while unrelated singleton markers remain noise.

annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical sightline toward the unique nearest aligned red 2x2 block, stopping at the adjacent ring cell; markers with no clear sightline do not move
annotation.trajectory: move each selected marker pixel to its stopping cell
annotation.dst: one-cell ring around the matched red 2x2 block
annotation.transform: clear moved marker sources and keep red 2x2 blocks and unmoved marker pixels unchanged
annotation.multi_step: choose nearest clear aligned blocks before moving; a lower-row marker left of a block stays fixed when that block already has selected vertical markers above and below

references.docstring:
Find the duplicate of the 3x3 sample marked by a grey L-stencil and draw a grey frame around it.

Input structure:
- A 3x3 sample region is marked by grey pixels immediately to its right and below, forming an L-stencil.
- The same 3x3 color pattern appears exactly once elsewhere in the grid.
- The duplicate has a one-cell margin available on every side.

Rule:
- Read the 3x3 sample from the upper-left side of the grey L-stencil.
- Locate the unique other exact occurrence of that 3x3 sample.
- Paint a one-cell-thick grey rectangular frame around the duplicate sample, preserving its interior.

Key insight:
The grey L is not the target frame itself; it identifies the small sample whose matching copy should be framed.

annotation.src: 3x3 sample region s marked by a grey L-stencil
annotation.dst: other 3x3 region d in the grid
annotation.match_cond: d has exactly the same 3x3 color pattern as s
annotation.transform: paint a one-cell-thick grey rectangular frame around d; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Reverse the top-to-bottom order of the colored sprites while preserving each sprite's shape and columns.

Input structure
A background canvas contains one sprite mask for each foreground color; the sprites' bboxes form a contiguous vertical stack.

Rule
Read the foreground color masks by bbox top row, then paste those same sprite masks from the original stack top in reverse order.

Key insight
The sprites are defined by color masks and bbox rows, so connectivity is irrelevant; only the vertical stack order changes.

annotation.dst: contiguous vertical output slots d covering the original foreground stack rows, ordered top-to-bottom
annotation.match_cond: rank(s in top-to-bottom order) == rank(d in bottom-to-top order)
annotation.transform: paste each sprite with its bbox-relative shape and original columns; background elsewhere

references.docstring:
Split two side-by-side masks and mark the cells that are empty in both.

Input structure
- The input is a 2D grid with black background.
- The grid has even width and splits into two equal-size panels.
- The left panel contains a pink mask and the right panel contains a grey mask.
Rule
- Align the two panels cell by cell.
- Output one panel-sized black grid.
- Paint a yellow pixel wherever both aligned input cells are background.
Key insight
- The output is the intersection of the two background masks after horizontal alignment.

annotation.src: two same-size foreground/background panels placed side by side, pink on the left and grey on the right
annotation.transform: replace each aligned pixel pair with yellow iff both source pixels are background, otherwise black
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one panel

references.docstring:
Draw the colored rectangle defined by four control pixels and connect its interior to the red pivot with a grey cross.

Input structure
- The background grid contains exactly one red pivot pixel.
- Four other single-pixel controls have unique topmost, bottommost, leftmost, and rightmost positions.
- The red pivot lies strictly inside the rectangle bounded by those extreme row and column positions.

Rule
- Use the topmost control's row and color for the rectangle top side, the bottommost for the bottom side, the leftmost for the left side, and the rightmost for the right side.
- Paint the top and bottom sides across the full left-to-right span, then paint the left and right sides only between them.
- Paint grey from the pivot to each side along the pivot's row and column, preserving the red pivot itself.

Key insight
- The four controls are not directly joined to each other; their row and column extrema define a rectangular frame around the pivot.

annotation.src: one red pivot pixel and four other colored control pixels on the background, with unique top/bottom row and left/right column extrema
annotation.transform: draw the rectangle defined by the control extrema, using each side control's color; inside it draw grey horizontal and vertical segments through the red pivot, preserving the pivot

references.docstring:
Vertically align all repeated colored sprites to the teal sprite's top row.

Input structure
The grid has a uniform background and several foreground colors. Each
foreground color forms exactly one 4-connected sprite, and all sprites have
the same normalized mask. The teal sprite is the vertical alignment anchor.

Rule
Clear the canvas to background. For every colored sprite, keep its original
left column and shape, but paste it with its top row equal to the teal
sprite's original top row.

Key insight
The sprites are already horizontally separated copies of the same mask; the
only missing structure is their common vertical alignment to the teal copy.

annotation.src: monochromatic repeated sprite s
annotation.dst: teal-row aligned slot d with the same left column as s
annotation.match_cond: d.top == teal_sprite.top and d.left == s.left
annotation.transform: clear original sprite locations and paste each s unchanged into d

references.docstring:
Compress the enlarged uniform grid into a 3x3 map showing which coarse blocks contain sparse marker pixels.

Input structure
- The input is a nonempty two-dimensional grid whose height and width are
  each divisible into three equal bands.
- Exactly two colors are present: a unique dominant fill color and a unique
  sparse marker color.

Rule
- Split the input into a 3x3 array of equal rectangular blocks.
- For each block, write the marker color in the corresponding output cell if
  that block contains any marker pixel; otherwise write the fill color.

Key insight
- The large grid is a scaled-up 3x3 code: marker location within a block is
  irrelevant, only the occupied coarse block matters.

annotation.src: 3x3 equal block partition of a two-color grid with sparse marker pixels
annotation.transform: collapse each block to the marker color if it contains any marker pixel; otherwise use the dominant fill color
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 coarse occupancy map

references.docstring:
Trace a green path from the start, turning right at pink controls and left at teal controls until it exits the grid.

Input structure
- A black-background grid contains exactly one green start pixel.
- The remaining foreground pixels are pink and teal one-pixel turn controls.
- The green start has exactly one cardinal sightline whose first non-background pixel is a turn control.

Rule
- Begin moving from the green start toward that visible control.
- Paint green through background cells in a straight line.
- When the next cell is a pink control, turn right without overwriting it; when it is a teal control, turn left without overwriting it.
- Stop when the next step would leave the grid.

Key insight
- The colored control pixels are not targets to fill; they are turn instructions for a single ray that leaves a continuous green trail.

annotation.src: single green start pixel with pink and teal turn-control pixels
annotation.path: begin along the unique cardinal sightline from the start to a control; travel straight through background cells, turning right immediately before each pink control and left immediately before each teal control, stopping at the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint every visited background pixel green
annotation.transform: preserve the original green start and all pink/teal controls

references.docstring:
Extend the single seed pixel into a clipped square spiral, stopping before the first blocker on that spiral.

Input structure
- The dominant background contains exactly one single-pixel foreground seed.
- There may also be foreground blocker pixels of one other color.
- The output keeps the same shape and preserves all original non-background pixels.

Rule
- Starting at the seed, follow directions up, right, down, left, with leg lengths 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, and so on.
- Paint in-bounds background cells on the spiral with the seed color; out-of-bounds steps are skipped but still count.
- If the next in-bounds spiral cell is a blocker, stop before painting it.

Key insight
- The spiral is traced in the unbounded plane and clipped to the grid, which is why separate visible segments can appear when later legs re-enter the canvas.

annotation.src: single foreground seed pixel
annotation.path: unbounded square spiral starting upward from the seed; directions repeat up, right, down, left with leg lengths 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, and so on, clipping out-of-bounds steps and stopping before the first blocker pixel
annotation.trajectory: paint every in-bounds background pixel along the spiral with the seed color
annotation.transform: preserve the original seed and blocker pixels

references.docstring:
Copy every solid foreground rectangle repeatedly along both downward diagonal directions, clipping copies at the grid edge.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- There is one foreground color.
- Each 4-connected foreground object is a filled axis-aligned rectangle.

Rule
- Keep the original rectangles.
- For a rectangle of height h and width w, stamp the same rectangle at offsets (h, -w), (2h, -2w), ... and (h, w), (2h, 2w), ...
- Drop only the out-of-bounds part of any stamped rectangle and stop once a trajectory is fully outside the grid.

Key insight
- Each rectangle is both the sprite and the stride: its height controls the downward step and its width controls the sideways step.

annotation.src: each filled foreground rectangle s
annotation.path: two downward diagonal paths from s, stepping by s.height rows and by +/-s.width columns until the stamped rectangle is fully outside the grid
annotation.trajectory: copy s at every step, dropping any cells that fall outside the grid
annotation.transform: keep the original rectangles and union all copied foreground pixels on the background

references.docstring:
Expand a 3x3 color grid to 5x5 by copying its border pixels outward one cell.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 grid of ARC colors.

Rule
- Place the input at the center of a 5x5 output.
- Copy the top and bottom input rows into the adjacent outer rows, and the
  left and right input columns into the adjacent outer columns.
- The corner pixels are copied outward in both directions, forming 2x2 corner blocks.

Key insight
- This is a one-cell edge padding of the entire grid, not a per-color or
  object-specific transformation.

annotation.src: 3x3 input pixel grid
annotation.transform: copy the grid into the center and fill the one-cell border by extending the nearest edge pixels outward
annotation.grid_shape: 5x5 edge-padded grid

references.docstring:
Return the missing rectangular patch by completing the square's full reflection symmetry.

Input structure:
- A square patterned grid has one solid rectangular region of black missing pixels.
- Outside that missing rectangle, the pattern obeys the same value under all eight square symmetries.

Rule:
- Find the bounding box of the black missing region.
- For each missing pixel, inspect its D4 symmetry orbit across horizontal, vertical, and diagonal reflections.
- Copy the unique non-black value found elsewhere in that orbit into the corresponding output cell.

Key insight:
- The output is not the repaired full grid; it is exactly the hidden rectangle, and every hidden value is determined by its symmetric copies.

annotation.src: square color pattern with one solid black rectangular missing region; visible cells obey all D4 square symmetries
annotation.transform: replace each black missing pixel with the unique non-black color in its horizontal, vertical, and diagonal reflection orbit; output only the repaired rectangle
annotation.grid_shape: bbox of the black missing rectangle

references.docstring:
Recolor each isolated blue dot by the majority-colored marker bordering its open region.

Input structure
- Black is the background.
- Blue cells form two roles: multi-cell horizontal/vertical wall segments and isolated one-cell dots.
- Non-blue foreground colors are marker cells sitting on the walls, endpoints, or region corners.

Rule
- Treat multi-cell blue components and all colored marker cells as barriers.
- Flood-fill the remaining black cells plus isolated blue dots into 4-connected open regions.
- For each region containing isolated blue dots, count the distinct colored marker cells that touch
  the region in the 8-neighborhood; recolor every isolated blue dot in that region to the unique
  majority marker color.

Key insight
- The colored wall/corner markers label compartments by vote; the scattered blue dots are the
  only cells to rewrite, while the blue wall network and marker cells stay fixed.

annotation.src: isolated blue pixels inside 4-connected open regions separated by multi-cell blue wall segments and colored marker pixels
annotation.transform: for each region containing isolated blue pixels, count distinct colored markers touching the region in the 8-neighborhood; recolor those blue pixels to the unique majority marker color while preserving walls, markers, and bg

references.docstring:
Flood-fill each marked chamber bounded by walls with its marker color.

Input structure
A same-size grid has a dominant background/open color, one repeated wall color,
and one-cell colored markers sitting inside some wall-bounded open chambers.

Rule
Infer the wall as the unique non-background color that appears more than once.
Treat wall pixels as barriers. For every 4-connected non-wall component, leave
it unchanged if it has no marker; otherwise assert it has exactly one marker and
recolor the whole component with that marker's color.

Key insight
The repeated color is a maze wall that partitions the background into chambers;
the singleton marker inside a chamber supplies the fill color for that chamber.

annotation.src: 4-connected non-wall regions made of background pixels and singleton colored markers, separated by the repeated wall color
annotation.transform: for each region containing a marker, recolor all non-wall pixels in that region to the marker color; leave unmarked regions and wall pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Decode the two-row red glyph strip into a downward red trace starting from a centered green marker.

Input structure
- The input is a black 2-row strip containing 4-connected red glyphs, read left to right.
- Each glyph spans both rows and has exactly one top red entry cell; its bottom row is either the same cell only or a two-cell elbow.
Rule
- Make a black output whose width is one more than half the input width and whose height is one marker row plus one row for each elbow and two rows for each vertical glyph.
- Put a green marker in the center of the top row, then trace the glyphs downward: a vertical glyph paints two red cells in the current column; an elbow paints the two bottom cells as a horizontal red segment and moves the current column left or right.
Key insight
- The missing top cell of each 2x2 elbow tells whether the trace exits left or right; the glyphs are pipe instructions rather than shapes to copy literally.

annotation.src: implicit trace head initialized at the centered green output marker
annotation.path: read the red input glyphs left to right; a vertical glyph advances two rows in the same column, and a 2x2 elbow advances one row while stepping to the bottom cell not under the entry cell
annotation.trajectory: paint the decoded vertical or horizontal red segment for each glyph
annotation.transform: build a black output canvas with the green marker at top center; do not copy the input strip itself
annotation.grid_shape: height is one marker row plus decoded path rows; width is input_width/2 + 1
annotation.symbol_instructions: each red glyph's single top cell is the entry; its bottom row defines the segment to paint and the next trace-head column

references.docstring:
Reflect each foreground color mask vertically inside its own bounding box.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains several monochrome foreground masks.
- Each foreground color is a glyph-like mask; it may be split under
  4-connectivity but is treated as one mask by color.

Rule
- For each non-background color independently, find the mask's bounding box.
- Keep every pixel's column and replace its row r by r0 + r1 - r, where
  r0 and r1 are the top and bottom rows of that color mask's bounding box.

Key insight
- The scene is not globally flipped; each colored mask is mirrored within its
  own vertical extent, so one-row and vertically symmetric masks stay fixed.

annotation.src: each non-background color mask
annotation.transform: for each mask, reflect its pixels top-to-bottom within its own bbox; keep columns and colors, redraw on the background

references.docstring:
Fill whole lattice cells along straight red and green marker runs, coloring red/green intersections pink.

Input structure
- A teal lattice divides the canvas into rectangular background cells.
- Red and green marker pixels sit inside some cells of that lattice.
- Markers of the same color are paired by sharing a lattice row or a lattice column.

Rule
- For each color, any lattice row with at least two same-color markers is filled between the leftmost and rightmost marker cells.
- Likewise, any lattice column with at least two same-color markers is filled between the topmost and bottommost marker cells.
- Fill entire cells, preserve the teal lattice, and color cells reached by both red and green runs pink.

Key insight
- The marker pixels are not expanded locally; they are endpoints in a coarser grid whose rows and columns are the lattice cells.

annotation.src: red and green marker pixels inside cells of the teal lattice
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical lattice-cell run from a marker cell to a same-color marker cell sharing its lattice row or column
annotation.dst: the aligned same-color marker cell at the other end of the run
annotation.trajectory: fill every whole lattice cell on the inclusive run with the marker color
annotation.transform: preserve the teal lattice; cells covered by both red and green runs become pink

references.docstring:
Draw the blue rectangular border spanned by the three marker pixels while preserving the markers.

Input structure
- The grid has a uniform background and exactly three same-color foreground marker pixels.
- The marker pixels lie on the boundary of their shared bounding box.
- Blue is absent from the input and is the output border color.

Rule
- Compute the bounding box of the three marker pixels.
- Paint the top, bottom, left, and right sides of that box blue.
- Restore the original marker pixels on top of the blue border.

Key insight
- The sparse marker pixels are control points for the missing rectangle; their bounding box is the frame to complete.

annotation.src: three same-color marker pixels on a uniform background
annotation.transform: draw a blue rectangular border along the bbox of the marker pixels, then preserve the marker pixels

references.docstring:
Emit the next 3-row band in a cyclic table of colored 3x3 sprite masks.

Input structure
The input is a 3x3 sprite lattice: sprite rows are separated by full
background rows, and sprite columns are separated by full background
columns.  Each column keeps one color across all sprite rows.

Ignoring color, each sprite row is the previous sprite row shifted one slot
left.  The output is the next shifted sprite row, recolored by the fixed
colors of the output columns.

The colors mark the columns, while the uncolored 3x3 masks form the cyclic
sequence; after m input sprite rows, column j receives mask (j + m) modulo
the number of columns.

annotation.dst: next 3-row band of the same column slots
annotation.transform: ignore color to read the cyclic mask sequence: each lower band shifts masks one slot left; emit the next shifted band and recolor each mask with its column color
annotation.grid_shape: 3 rows by input width

references.docstring:
Crop to the rectangular frame and replace its interior with the doubled enclosed color pattern.

Input structure:
- A background canvas contains one single-color rectangular frame.
- Inside the frame, a smaller non-background, non-frame color pattern occupies a tight sub-bbox of the interior.

Rule:
- Crop the output to the frame bbox.
- Take the tight bbox of the interior pattern, excluding background and frame color.
- Scale that pattern by a factor of two and write it into the frame interior.

Key insight:
- The frame determines the output size, while the colored seed pattern inside it is a compact half-scale version of the final frame interior.

annotation.transform: crop to the frame bbox, scale the interior pattern bbox by 2, and replace the frame interior with that scaled pattern while preserving the frame border
annotation.grid_shape: same height and width as the rectangular frame bbox

references.docstring:
Collapse the right-edge palette into one vertical coded bar using the grey marker height as the per-color run length.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, one top-aligned vertical grey marker
segment, and a contiguous set of full-height non-background palette columns
at the right edge. The column immediately to the left of the palette is
background.

Read the palette columns left-to-right. Erase those palette columns, then
fill the adjacent background column with the palette colors from top to
bottom, repeating each palette color for as many rows as the grey marker
segment is tall and cycling through the palette until the grid ends.

The grey segment is not copied; its height is the run-length instruction
for expanding the ordered right-edge palette into the new vertical bar.

annotation.dst: runs in the single background column immediately left of the palette, ordered top-to-bottom
annotation.match_cond: s at palette rank k fills each destination run whose run index mod palette length is k

annotation.symbol_instructions: top-aligned grey marker height gives the run length for every palette color

references.docstring:
Recolor the lower half of the foreground shape red.

references.docstring:
Count the 4-connected background regions and return one background pixel per region as a single column.

references.docstring:
Fill the center of the largest solid empty rectangle with teal.

rectangle; its height and width are at least three cells.

The target is the largest axis-aligned solid rectangle, not the whole
connected black component around it.

references.docstring:
Fill the black gaps by continuing the smallest rectangular periodic color tile.

Input structure
A grid contains a non-black rectangular periodic pattern with some black pixels
removed from it.

Rule
Find the unique smallest-area period rectangle whose residue classes are
consistent across all non-black pixels and all observed at least once, then
replace each black pixel by the color at the same row/column residue.

annotation.src: non-template color mask s, possibly split into multiple fragments
annotation.dst: translated copies d of the unique largest foreground template mask
annotation.match_cond: d contains the observed s pixels; choose the unique minimum non-overlapping set of d per color
annotation.transform: paint every cell of each matched d with s.color; leave the template unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend the single rectangular bar into two diagonal zigzag chains, alternating the bar with its 90-degree rotated copy in the paired color.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color and exactly one 4-connected monochrome foreground object.
- That foreground object is a solid non-square rectangle, either green or pink.
- The foreground rectangle's height and width define the alternating step period.

Rule
- Keep copies of the original rectangle on both diagonals through the seed, with row and column offsets of height + width.
- Between every adjacent pair of same-diagonal original copies, place a 90-degree rotated rectangle in the other color.
- Continue the pattern across the whole canvas and clip any rectangle that crosses an edge.

Key insight
- The two visible colors encode alternating orientations of the same bar along two crossing 45-degree zigzag paths; boundary fragments are just clipped copies.

annotation.src: single solid green/pink rectangular sprite s
annotation.path: two 45-degree zigzag paths crossing at s; original-orientation copies recur every s.height + s.width cells on both diagonals, with rotated copies bridging adjacent originals
annotation.trajectory: stamp clipped solid rectangles across the canvas: original-orientation copies keep s.color and rotated copies use the other green/pink color
annotation.transform: output contains the generated zigzag bars on the background

references.docstring:
Extend the red plus into an eight-direction star with blue diagonal rays and repeating teal-teal-yellow cardinal rays.

Input structure
- The canvas background is black.
- The only foreground object is one 4-connected five-pixel red plus.
- The plus supplies a center, four diagonal gaps, and four cardinal arms.

Rule
- Preserve the red plus.
- From each diagonal neighbor of the plus center, paint a blue ray to the grid edge.
- From each cardinal arm, continue outward to the grid edge with the repeating color pattern teal, teal, yellow.

Key insight
- The red plus is a compact ray emitter: its diagonal gaps start the uniform blue diagonals, while each arm starts the same three-cell cardinal stripe pattern.

annotation.src: single 5-pixel red plus
annotation.path: diagonal rays start from the four diagonal neighbors of the plus center and continue to the grid edge; cardinal rays start just beyond each red arm and continue outward to the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint diagonal ray cells blue; paint cardinal ray cells with the repeating outward pattern teal, teal, yellow
annotation.transform: keep the red plus unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor the two sprite masks whose pixelwise union equals a third sprite mask.

Input structure
- The grid has black background and red foreground arranged as six 4x4
  sprite regions in a 3-by-2 array, separated by blank rows and columns.
- Each sprite region contains a non-empty red mask.
- Exactly one sprite is the pixelwise OR of two other sprite masks, except
  that duplicate operand copies are resolved by row-major position.

Rule
- Find two operand sprites whose foreground masks each contribute at least
  one unique pixel and whose union exactly matches a destination sprite.
- Recolor the operand sprite pixels teal and recolor the destination sprite
  pixels green; leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The three changed sprites are identified by a mask-union relation; position
  matters only when identical operand copies create the same relation.

annotation.src: red 4x4 sprite masks s in the 3-by-2 array
annotation.dst: red sprite mask d in the same array
annotation.match_cond: two distinct s masks have pixelwise union equal to d, and each contributes at least one pixel
annotation.transform: recolor the two matched operand sprites teal and d green; leave all other pixels unchanged
annotation.multi_step: if duplicate operand copies make the same relation, use the row-major earliest copy

references.docstring:
Paint a red square around each yellow marker, sized to stop just before the nearest grey marker.

Input structure
- A black background contains one or more yellow marker pixels and one or more grey blocker pixels.
- The output has the same shape as the input and preserves the yellow and grey pixels.

Rule
- For each yellow marker, find the minimum Chebyshev distance to any grey blocker.
- Fill the centered square of radius one less than that distance with red, changing only background pixels.

Key insight
- Grey pixels define the first forbidden Chebyshev ring around each yellow marker, so the red square is the
  largest centered square that remains one cell short of every grey blocker.

annotation.src: yellow marker pixels and grey blocker pixels on a black background
annotation.transform: around each yellow marker, fill background pixels in the centered red square whose radius is one less than the nearest grey pixel's Chebyshev distance; preserve yellow and grey pixels

references.docstring:
Expand a small sprite into a block grid by stamping the whole sprite wherever the original has a non-black pixel.

Input structure:
- The input is a small rectangular sprite on a black background.
- Non-black pixels mark which output blocks should receive a copy of the sprite.
- The output dimensions are the input height squared by the input width squared.

Rule:
- Partition the output into input-sized blocks, one block per input cell.
- For each non-black input cell, copy the full input sprite into the corresponding output block.
- Leave blocks corresponding to black input cells entirely black.

Key insight:
- The input acts as both the stencil and the stamp: colored cells select block positions,
  and the same sprite is pasted into each selected block.

Fill black regions enclosed by green boundaries with yellow while preserving the original boundary.

Input structure:
- The input is a square black grid containing one or more green closed shapes.
- Green pixels form the visible boundaries of enclosed regions.
- Black pixels may appear both inside and outside those boundaries.

Rule:
- Detect the interior of the green objects.
- Exclude the green boundary pixels themselves.
- Recolor enclosed black interior pixels yellow and leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The transformation depends on topology rather than shape identity: only black cells
  trapped inside a green boundary are changed.

Extend a repeated blue sprite pattern to a 9-cell span and recolor the repeated foreground red.

Input structure:
- The input is a black-background grid containing a blue sprite repeated by translation.
- The repetition may run horizontally or vertically.
- The visible grid is shorter than the required completed span.

Rule:
- Infer the dominant translation period from matching blue pixels.
- Tile the corresponding base slice until the repeated axis reaches length 9.
- Recolor all blue foreground pixels red in the completed pattern.

Key insight:
- The repeated sprite supplies its own period; once the period is inferred, completion is just
  tiling along that axis followed by a color change.

Shift each object pixel one step right unless it is on the object's lower-right frontier.

Input structure:
- The input contains one or more same-color objects on a black background.
- Objects are connected components and may have diagonal or slanted edges.
- Each object is processed independently in its original position.

Rule:
- For every non-black pixel in an object, look for any other object pixel down and to the right.
- If such a pixel exists, move the current pixel one column to the right.
- If not, leave the pixel in place.

Key insight:
- The local move is controlled by the object's southeast support: pixels with something beyond
  them down-right slide, while the terminal southeast contour stays fixed.

Project the central sprite through each surrounding partial copy, recoloring each ray to match its guide.

Input structure:
- The input contains one largest central sprite and several smaller partial sprites around it.
- Each surrounding sprite is a same-shape subset of the central sprite in its own color.
- All objects sit on a black background.

Rule:
- Find the largest displacement that makes the central sprite cover each surrounding sprite.
- Recolor the central sprite to the surrounding sprite's color.
- Repeat that displacement from the center until the copies leave the canvas.

Key insight:
- Each partial outer object is a direction-and-color guide: aligning the central sprite to it
  reveals the vector that should be extended repeatedly.
tags: condition:副本指示方向与色, copy_dir_and_color

references.docstring:
Convert two blue bitmasks separated by a gray bar into their pixelwise overlap.

Input structure:
- The input contains two same-sized blue/black masks.
- A full-height gray vertical bar separates the left and right masks.
- Blue marks active cells and black marks inactive cells.

Rule:
- Locate the gray separator column.
- Compare the masks cell by cell.
- Output red exactly where both corresponding mask cells are blue; output black elsewhere.

Key insight:
- The gray bar is only a layout delimiter; after splitting on it, the task is a logical AND
  between the two aligned masks.

Repeat each colored diagonal every three offsets to fill the 7x7 grid with an interlaced pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a 7x7 black grid containing three full diagonals.
- Each diagonal has a distinct non-black color.
- The diagonals run in the same slope direction.

Rule:
- For every non-black input cell, draw its full diagonal in the output.
- Redraw that same diagonal color at offsets spaced by three rows.
- Clip the repeated diagonals to the 7x7 canvas.

Key insight:
- A single colored diagonal defines a whole congruence class modulo three; repeating all three
  classes creates the final interlacing.

Slide the red object in a cardinal direction until it first touches the fixed teal square.

Input structure:
- The input contains one teal 2x2 square and one red object on a black background.
- The red object is aligned so a horizontal or vertical slide can make contact.
- The teal square remains fixed in the output.

Rule:
- Keep only the teal square as the starting output.
- Try cardinal translations of the red object from shortest to longest.
- Return the first translation where the red object touches the teal square by 4-connectivity.

Key insight:
- The task is a minimal-contact slide: the red shape moves straight toward the teal anchor and
  stops as soon as their edges touch.

Connect matching colored cells across the divider grid by filling the black cells between them.

Input structure:
- The input is partitioned by full horizontal and vertical bars of one divider color.
- Rectangular cells are mostly black, with some cells filled by non-divider colors.
- Matching colored cells may appear in the same row or column of the partition.

Rule:
- Identify the divider color from full rows or columns.
- For each non-black, non-divider colored cell, search rightward and downward for the next same color.
- Fill intervening black cells along that row or column with the matching color.

Key insight:
- Same-colored cells act like endpoints on the partition lattice; only the black gaps between
  aligned matching endpoints are recolored.

Recolor four gray bars by height rank from tallest to shortest.

Input structure:
- The input contains exactly four separated gray bars on a black background.
- The bars have distinct heights and are connected components.
- Their positions are irrelevant except for locating their pixels.

Rule:
- Extract the four gray bar components.
- Sort them by foreground pixel count in descending order.
- Recolor them blue, red, green, and yellow from tallest to shortest.

Key insight:
- The output color encodes relative size, not location: bar height order determines the palette.
tags: condition:高度排名映射颜色, height_rank_to_color

references.docstring:
Use the uniquely sparse 3x3 cell as a color key for all cells in the divided grid.

Input structure:
- The input is a 3-by-3 arrangement of cells separated by one divider color.
- Each cell contains black plus several colored pixels.
- Exactly one cell has four non-black, non-divider pixels; the others have five.

Rule:
- Split the grid into its divider-separated cells.
- Find the cell with exactly four colored pixels and crop it as the guide sprite.
- Fill every cell uniformly with the guide sprite color at the corresponding cell position.

Key insight:
- The special sparse cell is a miniature 3-by-3 lookup table: its position-indexed colors
  determine the color assigned to every region.
tags: condition:稀疏单元色查找表, sparse_cell_color_lookup

references.docstring:
Expand each two-color cross into a larger cross-and-diagonal motif.

Input structure:
- The input contains small 3x3 cross objects on a black background.
- Each cross has one arm color and a different center color.
- Crosses are independent connected components.

Rule:
- Locate the center and bounding box of each cross.
- Extend the arm color one step farther north, south, east, and west.
- Extend the center color along all four diagonals within the expanded 5x5 footprint.

Key insight:
- The two colors have different growth roles: the arm color grows orthogonally, while the
  center color grows diagonally.

Turn two seed pixels into alternating full-length bars repeated at twice their separation.

Input structure:
- The input contains exactly two non-black pixels on a black grid.
- Their placement determines whether the bars run across rows or columns.
- The two seed colors are preserved as the alternating bar colors.

Rule:
- If either seed lies on a side edge, draw full row bars through the two seed rows.
- Otherwise, draw full column bars through the two seed columns.
- Repeat both bars along the perpendicular axis using a stride of twice their separation.

Key insight:
- The two seeds define both the orientation and period of a two-color stripe pattern.

Extract the only quadrant whose foreground color differs from the other three.

Input structure:
