annotation.src: non-cross foreground mask in the upper-left quadrant; the central full cross supplies the output color
annotation.dst: four quadrants of the canvas formed after removing the cross row and column
annotation.transform: recolor the upper-left mask to the cross color; copy it to the upper-left quadrant and mirror it horizontally, vertically, and both ways into the other quadrants
annotation.grid_shape: input height - 1 by input width - 1

references.docstring:
Fill black gaps by propagating the maximally supported repeating translation.

Input structure
A same-size colored periodic field contains black pixels that mark missing cells.
All non-black pixels are already correct and provide many repeated-color pairs.

Rule
Find the nonzero translation vector whose overlapping visible cells have the
largest support with no color disagreements.  Cells connected by this vector
and its inverse are one periodic equivalence class; replace each black cell by
the unique visible color in its class.

Key insight
The occlusions hide a repeated lattice, and the strongest self-translation of
the visible pixels identifies exactly how to copy colors through the gaps.

annotation.src: non-black pixels of a periodic color field with black missing-cell masks
annotation.transform: infer the maximally supported self-translation whose overlapping visible pixels agree, then fill every black pixel from the unique color in its translation-equivalence class

tags: condition:平移向量决定填充, translation_sets_fill

references.docstring:
Select and output the object that touches the gray indicator pixel.

Input structure:
- Several same-colored objects sit on a black background.
- A single gray pixel touches exactly one of those objects.
- The object color is the only non-black, non-gray color in the grid.

Rule:
- Detect all objects of the shared non-gray color.
- Detect the gray indicator pixel.
- Return the cropped object that has 4-connected contact with the indicator.

Key insight:
- The gray pixel is an external selector and is not included in the returned pattern.

Complete the foreground shape by mirroring it across the 2x2 marker square.

Input structure
- A dominant background, one source foreground color, and one marker color.
- The marker color appears exactly as a solid 2x2 square.
- Source pixels lie in one or more quadrants around that marker square.

Rule
- Use the center of the 2x2 marker square as both a horizontal and vertical
  mirror axis.
- For every source pixel, paint its vertical reflection, horizontal
  reflection, and 180-degree reflection in the same source color.

Key insight
- The green 2x2 square is not copied; it defines the mirror center for a
  four-way reflection closure of the red mask.

annotation.src: source-color mask and the solid 2x2 marker square
annotation.dst: the missing mirror copies around the marker square
annotation.transform: reflect every source pixel across the horizontal and vertical center lines of the marker square, preserving the marker and all existing source pixels

tags: condition:标记定义双轴镜像, marker_biaxial_mirror

references.docstring:
Mirror the full-width colored top band into the bottom rows while leaving the original band and middle background unchanged.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- All foreground pixels form a contiguous band of complete rows starting at the top edge.
- Every row below that top band is background.

Rule
- Copy the top band into the same-width bottom rows, reversing the row order vertically.
- Preserve the original top band and the background gap between the two bands.

Key insight
- The output is a vertical edge reflection of the input's top colored row band, not a recoloring or resizing.

annotation.src: contiguous full-width foreground row band touching the top edge
annotation.dst: same-width row slots touching the bottom edge
annotation.transform: copy the top band to the bottom slots in vertically reversed row order, leaving the original band and intervening background unchanged

references.docstring:
Add a one-cell border by extending each input edge outward while keeping the new corners black.

Input structure:
- A nonempty 2D grid of ARC colors.
- The whole input is the source region; its outer rows and columns define the border to add.

Rule:
- Place the input in the center of an output with two extra rows and two extra columns.
- Copy the top, bottom, left, and right input edges into the adjacent new border cells.
- Leave the four new corner cells black.

Key insight:
- The output is not a scale-up; it is the original grid surrounded by a one-pixel extrusion of its boundary.

annotation.src: entire input grid, with its outer rows and columns defining the added border
annotation.transform: embed the input one cell inside a larger black canvas; copy each input edge outward into the adjacent border cells and leave the four new corners black
annotation.grid_shape: input height+2 by input width+2

tags: condition:边缘延伸角落留黑, edge_extrude_corner_black

references.docstring:
Summarize the jagged color bands as a one-pixel sequence in their spatial order.

Input structure:
- The grid is fully covered by a small set of colors with no separate background.
- Along exactly one axis, line-majority colors form consecutive broad bands.
- The compressed band sequence contains every input color exactly once.

Rule:
- Find the unique band axis by compressing row-majorities and column-majorities.
- Keep one pixel for each band color, ordered top-to-bottom for row bands or
  left-to-right for column bands.
- Return a column vector for horizontal bands and a row vector for vertical bands.

Key insight:
- The irregular boundaries are noise; the line-majority run sequence reveals the
  coarse color order that the output preserves.

annotation.src: jagged full-grid color bands with no separate background; along one axis, line-majority runs contain each color once
annotation.transform: collapse each majority band to one pixel in spatial order: left-to-right bands become a 1-row sequence, top-to-bottom bands become a 1-column sequence
annotation.grid_shape: 1 x number of colors for vertical bands, or number of colors x 1 for horizontal bands

tags: condition:行主色压缩单像素, row_majority_to_pixel

references.docstring:
Stack a vertical reflection of the whole input grid above the original grid.

Input structure:
- A nonempty rectangular grid whose complete contents form the source tile.

Rule:
- Build an output with the same width and twice the height.
- Put the vertically flipped input in the top half.
- Put the unchanged input in the bottom half.

Key insight:
- The transformation is not object- or color-based; the whole input grid is
  the tile, and the output completes a vertical mirror pattern around the
  join between the two copies.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as a tile
annotation.dst: vertical two-tile stack
annotation.transform: place the vertically mirrored tile above the original tile
annotation.grid_shape: input height doubled; input width unchanged

tags: condition:翻转副本堆叠拼接, flip_copy_stacked

references.docstring:
Reflect the non-symmetric object across the horizontal and vertical symmetry axes of the separate symmetric marker.

Input structure:
- The grid contains exactly two monochromatic non-black objects.
- One object has both horizontal and vertical mirror symmetry.
- The other object sits in one quadrant relative to those symmetry axes.

Rule:
- Detect both objects and identify the one with both mirror axes.
- Use those axes as symmetries for the whole output grid.
- For every pixel of the other object, paint all reflected orbit positions with its color.

Key insight:
- The symmetric object defines the reflection axes; the non-symmetric object supplies
  the pixels to replicate.
tags: condition:借轴复制非对称体, axis_replicates_asym

references.docstring:
Recolor the grey cells that complete each partially red equal-arm plus sign.

Input structure
The grid contains black background, grey distractor/substrate cells, and red marker pixels.
The red pixels lie on one or more incomplete axis-aligned plus signs with one shared radius.

Rule
Infer the shared radius from the largest odd red span inside a non-black horizontal or vertical run.
Find radius-sized plus masks whose in-bounds cells are all non-black and whose row/column both contain red evidence.
Select the masks that cover all red pixels, strongest new red evidence first, and recolor only their grey cells teal.

Key insight
Black cells break candidate spans; within the noisy grey field, the valid pluses are the crosses that explain the red markers.

annotation.src: red marker pixels embedded in grey/black noise, forming partial equal-arm plus-sign masks
annotation.transform: infer the shared plus radius from the widest odd red span within a non-black run; for each supported plus mask, recolor its grey cells teal and leave red markers, black background, and other grey cells unchanged

tags: condition:标记推断十字涂底, marker_cross_recolor

references.docstring:
Shoot green rays from both ends of a teal diagonal line and reflect them off the red rectangle.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one short teal diagonal line on a black background.
- A single red rectangle or bar lies in the ray path.
- The scene may be rotated.

Rule:
- Detect the teal line endpoints and the red rectangle.
- Draw green in both outward diagonal directions from the teal line.
- When a ray hits red, flip the appropriate direction component and keep drawing.

Key insight:
- The teal line gives the initial ray direction, and the red object acts as a reflecting
  obstacle for the green path.

Recolor the one-pixel-inset interior of every solid foreground rectangle to teal.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- Non-background pixels form separated 4-connected monochrome objects.
- Each foreground object is a filled axis-aligned rectangle at least 3 cells tall and wide.

Rule
- Preserve every original pixel except the strict interior of each rectangle.
- For every foreground rectangle, replace all cells not on its one-pixel border with teal.

Key insight
- The output marks rectangle interiors, not whole objects: the original colors remain only as borders.

annotation.src: 4-connected solid monochrome foreground rectangles on the background
annotation.transform: recolor each rectangle's strict one-pixel-inset interior to teal; preserve the original rectangle border colors and background

references.docstring:
Extract the teal-marked sprite as a 3x3 mask recolored to that sprite's color.

Input structure
- A background grid contains several small foreground sprites.
- Exactly one teal control pixel is 4-connected into one sprite.
- The marked multicolor component has a 3x3 bounding box and exactly one
  non-teal foreground color.

Rule
- Find the 4-connected foreground component containing the teal marker.
- Crop that component's bounding box.
- Output the component mask inside the crop, replacing both the marker and
  the sprite pixels with the component's non-teal color.

Key insight
- The teal pixel selects the sprite to summarize; the other sprites are
  distractors.

annotation.src: 4-connected foreground object containing the teal control pixel
annotation.transform: crop its 3x3 bbox and recolor every object pixel, including the control pixel, to the object's single non-teal color; keep other crop cells bg
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 marked object bbox

references.docstring:
Move the red object forward one slot along the green-dot track.

Input structure:
- A red object overlaps one position on a straight track of green dots.
- The green dots are evenly spaced in a row or column.
- The background is black.

Rule:
- Detect the red object and all green dot objects.
- Determine the track direction from the green dot centers.
- Redraw the green dots, then translate the red object along the track to the next non-colliding slot.

Key insight:
- The green dots are discrete alignment slots, and the first collision-free translation
  places the red object one step forward on that track.

Expand a diagonal-index color table by cycling its non-black header sequence.

Input structure
- The input is a nonempty square grid.
- The top row and left column are the same header sequence.
- Every cell is the header color at index max(row, column); black header cells
  appear only as a trailing blank suffix.

Rule
- Drop the trailing black blanks from the header.
- Repeat the remaining header colors until it is twice as long as the input side.
- Fill the doubled square so each cell again takes the repeated header color
  at index max(row, column).

Key insight
- The visible pattern is not a 2D tile; it is a one-dimensional header sequence
  projected through the max(row, column) diagonal-index rule.

annotation.src: top row/left column header sequence of the diagonal-index table, ignoring trailing black blanks
annotation.transform: cycle the active header to twice the input side length and fill each output cell with header[max(row, column)]
annotation.grid_shape: square with input side length multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Extend the top-aligned foreground row pattern downward to a ten-row grid.

Input structure:
- The input is a width-10 grid with height below 10.
- Background is the dominant color, and the foreground uses one color.
- Rows form a translated periodic sequence: after a fixed vertical period,
  the row mask reappears shifted horizontally by a fixed offset.

Rule:
- Copy the input rows into the top of a 10-row background canvas.
- Infer the minimal vertical period and its unique horizontal shift from the
  observed rows.
- Continue each missing row from the row one period above it, applying the
  same horizontal shift and clipping cells that move outside the grid.

Key insight:
- The partial drawing is the top of a periodic row sequence, so the missing
  bottom rows are determined by the matching earlier row in the period.

annotation.src: top-aligned partial row pattern on a 10-column grid, using one foreground color on the background
annotation.dst: the missing rows of the fixed 10x10 output grid
annotation.transform: infer the minimal vertical row period and horizontal shift; copy the input rows at the top, then continue rows by shifting the row one period above, clipping off-grid foreground cells

references.docstring:
Add a green outside outline around the foreground shapes and fill their enclosed holes yellow.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color and exactly one foreground color.
- The foreground pixels form blocky objects that may enclose background holes.
- Green and yellow are absent from the input and are reserved for the added marks.

Rule:
- Keep all foreground pixels unchanged.
- Recolor every background pixel in an enclosed hole to yellow.
- Recolor every exterior background pixel that 8-touches the foreground to green.

Key insight:
- The two new colors separate background by region: unreachable-from-border background is hole fill, while border-reachable background adjacent to the foreground is the outside outline.

annotation.src: single-color foreground objects on a background; some objects enclose background holes
annotation.transform: draw a one-cell 8-neighborhood green outline on exterior background pixels around the foreground; recolor enclosed background holes to yellow; preserve foreground pixels

tags: condition:孔洞填色轮廓描色, holes_fill_outline

references.docstring:
Drop a yellow marker to the bottom row under each object's horizontal center.

Input structure:
- The grid contains separated monochromatic objects on a black background.
- Each object has a bounding box with a well-defined center column.
- The bottom row is available for the dropped markers.

Rule:
- Detect each foreground object.
- Compute the center column of its bounding box.
- Paint a yellow pixel in the last row at that center column.

Key insight:
- Only the object's horizontal center matters; the marker falls all the way to the
  canvas bottom rather than stopping at other objects.
tags: condition:对象中心在边行标, center_marked_edge_row

references.docstring:
Fill each grey-separated 3x3 window with the paired color of its center marker.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color, and grey full rows/columns form separator lines.
- The non-separator regions are 3x3 windows.
- Each 3x3 window contains exactly one foreground marker at its center.

Rule
- Keep every grey separator line unchanged.
- Replace each 3x3 window by a solid block using the marker's paired fill color:
  blue->pink, red->orange, green->teal, yellow->maroon.

Key insight
- The grey grid is only a partition; the center marker inside each cell chooses the
  solid color that fills that cell.

annotation.src: grey separator grid partitioning the canvas into 3x3 regions, each with one center marker pixel
annotation.transform: preserve the grey separators; fill each 3x3 region solidly with the marker's paired color (blue->pink, red->orange, green->teal, yellow->maroon)

tags: condition:标记色定窗口填充, marker_sets_window_fill

references.docstring:
Move each solid colored rectangle upward by exactly its own height.

Input structure
A black-background grid contains one or more separated monochromatic
foreground objects. Each object is a solid axis-aligned rectangle, with an
equally sized empty region immediately above it.

Rule
Clear every rectangle from its original position, then paste the same
rectangle directly above that position, offset upward by the rectangle's
height.

Key insight
The vertical displacement is not shared globally: each rectangle jumps by
its own bbox height, so its new bottom edge is just above its old top edge.

annotation.summary: Move each solid colored rectangle directly upward by its own height.
annotation.src: solid monochromatic foreground rectangles s
annotation.path: vertical path upward from s by s.bbox.height cells
annotation.trajectory: paint only the final moved rectangle at the shifted position
annotation.transform: erase each original rectangle; keep all other background cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Fill the whole grid with the unique most frequent input color.

Input structure
- The input is a nonempty 2D grid.
- Exactly one color appears more often than every other color.

Rule
- Find the unique most frequent color in the input.
- Replace every pixel with that color, preserving the input shape.

Key insight
- The scattered colors are reduced to a single consensus color determined only by frequency.

annotation.src: all pixels grouped by input color frequency
annotation.transform: recolor every pixel to the unique most frequent input color

tags: condition:最高频色覆盖全图, top_freq_fills_grid

references.docstring:
Summarize each 3x3 input block as one output pixel, ignoring grey marks.
Input structure
- The grid dimensions are multiples of 3, forming a lattice of 3x3 blocks.
- Background is the dominant color, and grey pixels are marker/noise cells.
- Each real block contains one non-background, non-grey color in at least
  eight of its nine cells.
Rule
- Replace each 3x3 block by background if it contains only background and grey.
- Otherwise replace it by the unique non-background, non-grey color in that block.
Key insight
- The large grid is an enlarged low-resolution picture; grey cells are defects
  within or between blocks and should not become output colors.

annotation.src: 3x3 blocks in the input block lattice, with grey marker/noise pixels ignored
annotation.transform: collapse each block to background if it contains only background/grey; otherwise collapse it to its unique non-background, non-grey block color
annotation.grid_shape: one output cell per 3x3 input block

references.docstring:
Move the green object until it touches the red bar, then place a teal copy of the bar beyond it.

Input structure:
- The grid contains exactly one red bar and exactly one green object.
- Both objects sit on a black background.
- The scene may be rotated.

Rule:
- Find the shortest cardinal displacement that makes the green object touch the red bar.
- Paste the green object at that touching position.
- Recolor a copy of the red bar teal and translate it opposite the movement direction until clear.

Key insight:
- The red bar is both the contact target and the template for the teal bar placed on
  the far side of the moved green object.
tags: condition:碰触后对侧放副本, touch_copy_opposite

references.docstring:
Fill each two-pixel foreground color into the axis-aligned rectangle whose opposite corners those pixels mark.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- Every foreground color appears exactly twice, as two isolated corner markers.
- The rectangles spanned by different colors do not overlap.

Rule
- For each foreground color, take the inclusive bounding box of its two pixels.
- Recolor every pixel inside that bounding box to the same foreground color.
- Leave all pixels outside those rectangles as background.

Key insight
- The two equal-colored pixels are not separate objects; together they specify the opposite corners of a filled rectangle.

annotation.src: foreground color masks, each consisting of exactly two same-color marker pixels on the background
annotation.transform: fill the inclusive axis-aligned bounding rectangle spanned by each marker pair with that pair's color; leave background elsewhere unchanged

references.docstring:
Complete each partial object by scaling and recoloring the largest template so its indicator aligns with the partial indicator.

Input structure:
- The grid contains several two-color objects on a black background.
- One indicator color appears in every object.
- One object is the full template; the others are partial scaled objects with their own colors.

Rule:
- Find the common indicator color across all objects.
- Choose the template by largest object size normalized by indicator size.
- Scale and recolor the template for each other object, then paste it with indicators aligned.

Key insight:
- The indicator region supplies both correspondence and scale, while the template supplies
  the missing shape around each partial object.
tags: condition:指示色定缩放对位, indicator_scale_align

references.docstring:
Summarize the large square-tile mosaic as a 3x3 mask colored by the sparse marker color.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly two foreground colors appear.
- One foreground color forms equal solid square tiles on a 3x3 lattice; the
  other foreground color is sparse marker noise.

Rule:
- Find the unique foreground color whose mask bbox divides into 3x3 equal
  square regions, each either completely filled or empty.
- Output a 3x3 grid with the other foreground color at filled tile positions
  and background elsewhere.

Key insight:
- The noisy marker color is only the output paint color; the large tiled
  object encodes the output pattern by which coarse lattice cells are filled.

annotation.src: large foreground-color square-tile mosaic whose bbox partitions into a 3x3 lattice, plus a sparse marker color
annotation.transform: collapse the lattice to a 3x3 mask; write the marker color where a square tile is present and background elsewhere
annotation.grid_shape: input -> 3x3 coarse occupancy mask

references.docstring:
Crop the 3x3 block from the upper-right corner of the 9x9 input.

Input structure:
- The input is a 9x9 grid arranged as a 3x3 array of 3x3 blocks.
- The desired block is located at the top row and rightmost column of that block layout.

Rule:
- Return rows 0 through 2 and columns 6 through 8 unchanged as the 3x3 output.

Key insight:
- The output is not computed from color statistics; it is the fixed upper-right block of the partitioned input.

annotation.src: 9x9 grid partitioned into a 3x3 lattice of 3x3 blocks
annotation.transform: crop the upper-right 3x3 block unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend the blue square up-left and the red square down-right along their diagonals to the grid edge.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background.
- There is exactly one blue 2x2 square and exactly one red 2x2 square.
- The diagonal ray beyond each active corner is clear background until it leaves the grid.

Rule
- Keep the input pixels unchanged.
- From the blue square's top-left corner, paint a blue diagonal ray in the up-left direction.
- From the red square's bottom-right corner, paint a red diagonal ray in the down-right direction.
- Each ray stops only when the next step would leave the grid.

Key insight
- The colored 2x2 squares are fixed emitters: blue uses its northwest corner and red uses its southeast corner, so the missing pixels are the two outward diagonal continuations.

annotation.src: blue 2x2 square and red 2x2 square
annotation.path: blue emits from its top-left corner up-left; red emits from its bottom-right corner down-right; each diagonal ray stops at the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint every visited background pixel with the emitting square's color
annotation.transform: preserve the original squares and all off-path background pixels

tags: condition:各色从角对角至边, color_diag_corner_edge

references.docstring:
Grow concentric square borders from three equally spaced diagonal seed pixels.

Input structure:
- The grid is black except for exactly three same-colored pixels.
- The pixels lie on a 45-degree diagonal with equal spacing.
- The middle pixel is the center for the square borders.

Rule:
- Sort the three seed pixels and measure the spacing to the center pixel.
- Draw a square border centered on the middle pixel using that spacing.
- Repeat outward at integer multiples of the spacing until no new cells are added.

Key insight:
- The outer seed pixels define the first square's diagonal corners, and the same spacing
  drives the repeating larger borders.
tags: condition:间距决定同心重复, spacing_concentric_repeat

references.docstring:
Crop the colored rectangle frame and connect scattered pixels to the same-colored frame side.

Input structure:
- Four full non-black lines form a rectangle on a black background.
- Each frame side has a distinct color.
- Extra scattered pixels share the color of exactly one frame side.

Rule:
- Locate the two full horizontal and two full vertical frame lines.
- Identify the scattered pixel color outside those lines.
- Crop to the frame and draw straight connections from each scattered pixel to the matching-colored side.

Key insight:
- The scattered pixel color selects which frame side to connect to after the rectangle
  is cropped out of the larger grid.
tags: condition:散落连接同色框边, scatter_connect_side

references.docstring:
Complete each incomplete 3x3 yellow object by coloring the missing cells in its bounding box orange.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one or more 8-connected yellow objects.
- Each yellow object fits in a 3x3 bounding box and has black gaps inside that box.

Rule
- Find each 8-connected yellow object.
- For the object's 3x3 bounding box, recolor every black cell in that box to orange.
- Keep the existing yellow pixels and all background outside those boxes unchanged.

Key insight
- The yellow pixels mark partial 3x3 blocks; orange fills the missing pixels needed to make each block solid.

annotation.src: 8-connected yellow objects on a black background, each with a 3x3 bbox
annotation.transform: within each object's bbox, recolor bg pixels to orange; preserve the yellow pixels and all bg outside the bboxes

references.docstring:
Rotate the entire input grid 180 degrees around its center.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 grid whose pixels form one complete pattern.

Rule
- Move each pixel to the cell opposite it through the grid center.

Key insight
- The output preserves all colors and positions relative to each other, but the global orientation is reversed.

annotation.src: entire 3x3 input grid
annotation.transform: rotate the whole grid 180 degrees

references.docstring:
Draw both diagonals through the single colored pixel using that pixel's color.

Input structure:
- The grid is black except for exactly one non-black pixel.
- The input grid is square or rectangular.
- The lone pixel's color is the output line color.

Rule:
- Locate the single non-black pixel.
- Draw in all four diagonal directions from that location.
- Keep drawing to the canvas edge with clipping.

Key insight:
- The lone pixel provides both the intersection point and the color for the two full
  diagonal lines.
tags: condition:过像素画双对角线, both_diags_through_pixel

references.docstring:
Expand the grid by reflecting it rightward and then downward.

Input structure
The input is a small rectangular color grid.

Rule
Form the top half of the output by placing the original grid next to its
left-right mirror. Form the bottom half by reflecting that top half
top-to-bottom.

Key insight
The output is not a nearest-neighbor scale-up; it is a four-quadrant mirror
tile whose upper-left quadrant is the original input.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as the upper-left quadrant
annotation.dst: 2x2 mirror tile of input-size quadrants
annotation.transform: copy the input unchanged to the upper-left, mirror it left-right into the upper-right, then mirror the full top half top-bottom into the lower half
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 2

tags: condition:翻转形成对称铺展, mirror_symmetric_expand

references.docstring:
Recolor the object whose shape matches the colored template inside the grey L-frame.

Input structure:
- The black background contains one grey L-frame, with its vertical leg on
  the right and horizontal leg on the bottom of the frame bbox.
- A single colored template object lies in the area enclosed above-left by
  that L-frame.
- Other colored objects are scattered outside the framed template region.

Rule:
- Extract the normalized mask of the colored template inside the grey
  L-frame bbox.
- Find the unique outside object with the same normalized mask, ignoring
  its color.
- Recolor that matched outside object to grey and leave all other pixels
  unchanged.

Key insight:
The grey L-frame is a shape selector: it marks the template to search for
elsewhere in the scene.

annotation.src: colored objects s outside the grey L-frame
annotation.dst: match to the colored template object d enclosed by the grey L-frame
annotation.match_cond: s.normalized_mask == d.normalized_mask
annotation.transform: recolor matched s to grey; leave the framed template and all other objects unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: grey L-frame marks the template shape and output color

references.docstring:
Reduce two same-sized masks separated by a solid divider into the cells empty in both masks.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- A single full-width separator row has a non-background color that appears only in that row.
- The separator splits the grid into two equal rectangular masks, each with one foreground color.
Rule
- Remove the separator row and align the upper and lower masks cell by cell.
- Output the same shape as one mask.
- Paint green where both aligned cells are background; paint background everywhere else.
Key insight
- The output is the complement of the union of the two foreground masks.

annotation.src: two equal 4x4 masks above and below a solid one-pixel separator row
annotation.transform: for each aligned pixel, output green iff both source pixels are background; otherwise output background
annotation.grid_shape: 4x4 mask

references.docstring:
Fill smallest red-bounded black rectangles teal and largest ones blue.

Input structure:
- Red divider lines partition a black grid into rectangular black regions.
- The red lines remain as separators.
- There may be multiple regions tied for smallest or largest area.

Rule:
- Treat red as the background and find the black rectangular components.
- Compute each component's black area.
- Recolor smallest-area regions teal and largest-area regions blue, leaving red dividers intact.

Key insight:
- The output depends only on relative region area within the red partition, not on
  the regions' positions.
tags: condition:极值区域分别涂色, extreme_regions_recolor

references.docstring:
Select the unique stacked tile that breaks the diagonal symmetry shared by the other tiles.

Input structure
- A 9x3 grid made of three vertically stacked 3x3 two-color tiles.
- Exactly two tiles are symmetric across the main diagonal, and exactly one is not.

Rule
- Split the input into its three 3x3 tiles.
- Return the only tile whose cells are not equal to their transposed positions.

Key insight
- The desired tile is identified by structural asymmetry, not by its colors or by its position.

annotation.src: three vertically stacked 3x3 two-color tiles
annotation.transform: return the unique tile that is not symmetric across its main diagonal; discard the two diagonally symmetric tiles
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 selected tile

tags: condition:选无对角对称瓦片, select_asym_tile

references.docstring:
Recolor every non-isolated green object on the black canvas to teal.

Input structure
- The grid is a black background containing green foreground pixels.
- Green pixels form one or more 4-connected objects; some objects may be single pixels.

Rule
- Keep black pixels unchanged.
- Keep each single-pixel green object unchanged.
- Recolor every green object with area greater than one to teal.

Key insight
- The deciding property is 4-connected object size: isolated green pixels are markers to preserve, while larger green objects are recolored.

annotation.src: green 4-connected foreground objects on the black background
annotation.transform: recolor each green object with area greater than one to teal; leave single-pixel green objects and black bg unchanged

references.docstring:
Draw horizontal teal rays from paired red edge bars on rows selected by teal markers, turning each marker yellow.

Input structure
- The black background contains exactly two equal-height solid vertical red bars, one on each side edge.
- Teal marker pixels are isolated single cells whose rows overlap exactly one of the two red bars.
- All teal markers are aligned with the same red bar.

Rule
- For each teal marker, paint teal background cells horizontally between that marker and its red bar, then recolor the marker yellow.
- Use the marker's vertical offset within the source red bar to select the same offset row of the opposite red bar.
- On that paired row, paint a full teal ray from the opposite red bar to the far edge, preserving the red bar cell.

Key insight
- The teal markers do not move; they choose relative rows in a pair of equal-height edge bars, and the opposite bar emits the same row selections as complete rays.

annotation.src: teal marker pixel s aligned with one row of a red edge bar
annotation.dst: row slot d in the opposite equal-height red edge bar
annotation.match_cond: s.row offset within its source bar == d.row offset within the opposite bar
annotation.transform: on s.row, paint teal from the source red bar to s and recolor s yellow; on d.row, paint a full teal ray from d's red bar to the far edge; preserve red bar pixels

tags: condition:标记偏移映射对侧, marker_maps_opposite

references.docstring:
Convert the separator-delimited board into a summary grid marking cells with two marker pixels.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the empty background.
- One non-background color forms all full separator rows and all full
  separator columns.
- The remaining non-background color is the marker color; every separated
  region contains either one or two marker pixels.

Rule
- Find the separator rows and columns, and use them to partition the input
  into rectangular regions.
- For each region, output blue if it contains two marker pixels; otherwise
  output the background color.

Key insight
- The large grid is a 3x3 table of tiny marker counts, and the output records
  only which table cells have the doubled marker.

annotation.src: 3x3 table of regions separated by solid one-pixel rows and columns, each region containing one or two marker pixels
annotation.transform: collapse each region to blue if it contains two marker pixels, otherwise to the background color
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 summary grid

tags: condition:双标记区域出前景, dual_marker_foreground

references.docstring:
Mirror the entire grid left-to-right.

Input structure
- A non-empty rectangular grid of ARC colors.

Rule
- Reverse the column order of every row, preserving all colors and row positions.

Key insight
- The output has the same shape and color counts as the input because it is the horizontal reflection of the full grid.

annotation.src: entire input grid
annotation.transform: reflect the grid left-to-right by reversing each row

references.docstring:
Paint a yellow 3x3 ring around the crossing of the full foreground row and column.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and two one-cell-wide foreground bars.
- One bar fills a complete row and the other fills a complete column.
- Their crossing pixel lies away from the border.

Rule
- Locate the unique row and unique column that are entirely non-background.
- Paint the 3x3 neighborhood centered on their crossing yellow.
- Restore the original crossing pixel, leaving only the eight surrounding cells changed.

Key insight
- The row/column crossing is the center of a local marker that replaces both nearby bar pixels and nearby background pixels.

annotation.src: unique full foreground row and unique full foreground column crossing on bg
annotation.transform: paint the eight pixels around their crossing yellow, preserving the crossing pixel and all other cells

references.docstring:
Create a four-quadrant mirror pattern from the whole input grid.

Input structure:
- The entire rectangular input grid is the seed tile.

Rule:
- Place the input tile in the upper-left quadrant.
- Place its left-to-right reflection in the upper-right quadrant.
- Reflect that full top strip top-to-bottom to make the lower half.

Key insight:
- The output is a 2x2 reflection tiling, not a pixelwise scale-up.

annotation.src: entire input grid as the seed tile
annotation.transform: copy the seed to the upper-left, place its horizontal reflection to the right, then place a vertical reflection of that top strip below
annotation.grid_shape: twice the input height by twice the input width

references.docstring:
Fit two monochromatic puzzle pieces together into the tightest rectangular assembly.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid containing exactly two non-black monochromatic objects.
- Each object is a puzzle piece that may be translated but not rotated.
- The pieces come from a compact two-color object.

Rule:
- Crop the two pieces from the input.
- Try all non-overlapping translations on a canvas large enough to hold both pieces.
- Return the placement whose cropped bounding box leaves the fewest black cells.

Key insight:
- The reconstruction is the densest translation-only packing of the two pieces.

Mirror gray objects across their nearest red frame so the reflected copies land inside the frames.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with red frame objects and gray objects outside them.
- All objects are aligned along one row or one column.
- Each gray object belongs to the closest red frame.

Rule:
- Detect the red frames and gray objects.
- Infer whether the reflection axis is horizontal or vertical from object alignment.
- Reflect each gray object across the center line of its closest frame and redraw the frame.

Key insight:
- The red frames define local mirror axes; each gray object moves by reflection, not by free translation.
tags: condition:跨框中线反射入内, reflect_centerline_in

references.docstring:
Reflect the grid across its horizontal midline by reversing the row order.

Input structure:
- A non-empty 2D grid of colored pixels.

Rule:
- Preserve every row exactly as-is.
- Place input row r at output row H - 1 - r.

Key insight:
- Only the vertical order of rows changes; colors and left-to-right row
  contents are unchanged.

annotation.src: entire input grid
annotation.transform: reflect across the horizontal midline; row r becomes row H - 1 - r

references.docstring:
Recolor the interior of the smaller yellow rectangle blue and the larger yellow rectangle red.

Input structure:
- The grid is a black canvas containing exactly two solid rectangles of one
  non-black foreground color.
- Each rectangle is at least 3 cells tall and 3 cells wide, so it has a
  one-cell border and a nonempty interior.
- The two rectangles have different areas.

Rule:
- Leave the black background and each foreground rectangle's one-cell border
  unchanged.
- Fill the smaller rectangle's interior with blue.
- Fill the larger rectangle's interior with red.

Key insight:
- The output colors are assigned by rectangle area rank, while the rewritten
  region is simply each rectangle's bbox interior.

annotation.src: two solid yellow rectangles on a black background, each with a nonempty bbox interior
annotation.transform: fill each rectangle's bbox interior by area rank: smaller rectangle blue, larger rectangle red; preserve yellow borders and background

references.docstring:
Move gray puzzle pieces into holes in a red shape and recolor the placed pieces blue.

Input structure:
- The input has one red object on a black background.
- Gray puzzle pieces are separate from the red object.
- Black gaps inside the red object's bounding area are holes to be plugged.

Rule:
- Crop each gray puzzle piece.
- Greedily place pieces where they do not collide with the red object and cover the most hole cells.
- Paste all placed pieces and then recolor gray pixels to blue.

Key insight:
- The red object's bounding area identifies the target holes, so the best placements maximize plugged black cells.
tags: condition:拼块填孔洞后变色, pieces_fill_holes_recolor

references.docstring:
Reconstruct scattered fragments by placing scaled and rotated copies of the multicolor template.

Input structure:
- The background is a non-black color.
- One object is the multicolor template with the largest variety of colors.
- Other objects are partial scaled and rotated fragments of that template.

Rule:
- Treat the most common non-black color as the background.
- Try rotations and scale factors of the template against the remaining fragments.
- Iteratively paste the best color-compatible placement and erase the matched fragment pixels.

Key insight:
- The complete template is distinguished by color variety, while fragments are partial observations of transformed copies.
tags: condition:缩放旋转对齐碎片, scale_rotate_align_frag

references.docstring:
Scale a small pattern to fill the interior of the red square frame and return that frame.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with a red square frame.
- A separate non-red 3x3 pattern object appears elsewhere.
- The frame interior is an integer scale of the small pattern.

Rule:
- Detect the red frame object and the separate pattern object.
- Compute the scale from the red frame's interior size.
- Scale the pattern and paste it inside the frame, returning only the framed result.

Key insight:
- The red square supplies both the target scale and the output extent.
tags: condition:框内尺寸决定缩放, frame_size_sets_scale

references.docstring:
Replace each hollow 3x3 foreground square with a red plus sign in the same window.

Input structure:
- A background grid containing one foreground color.
- Exactly two target motifs are 3x3 hollow squares: a background center surrounded by eight foreground pixels.

Rule:
- For each target motif, erase the four corner pixels to background.
- Recolor the four edge-neighbor pixels and fill the center pixel red.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
The changing regions are local masks: each square outline is rewritten in place as a plus mask.

annotation.src: the two 3x3 hollow foreground-square motifs with a background center
annotation.transform: replace each motif in place: corner pixels -> background, center and orthogonal-neighbor pixels -> red; keep all other pixels unchanged

tags: condition:方框换为十字掩模, square_to_cross_mask

references.docstring:
Draw full grid-spanning lines through the special color's boundary marker pairs.

Input structure:
- The input contains scattered pixels of several colors.
- One color appears only as four pixels on the grid boundary.
- Those boundary pixels mark the rows or columns of the output lines.

Rule:
- Find the color whose pixels all lie on the boundary.
- For markers on the top or bottom edge, draw a full vertical line through that column.
- For markers on the left or right edge, draw a full horizontal line through that row.

Key insight:
- Boundary-only pixels are line endpoints; all other scattered colors are noise.
tags: condition:边界标记定贯穿线, boundary_marker_span

references.docstring:
Replace every fully black 3x3 gap in a noisy colored field with a blue 3x3 square.

Input structure:
- The input is a fixed-size grid with many scattered non-blue colored pixels.
- One or more fully black 3x3 squares are embedded in the pattern.
- Existing colored pixels should remain unchanged.

Rule:
- Scan all 3x3 windows in the input.
- Select windows that are entirely black.
- Fill each still-black matching window with blue.

Key insight:
- The targets are uniform black square voids amid the colored scatter.
tags: condition:全黑窗口换前景色, black_to_foreground

references.docstring:
Copy the yellow-marked tile to the larger-grid slot named by the yellow pixel's local position.

Input structure
The input is a square canvas partitioned by full grey separator rows and
columns into a 3x3 array of equal 3x3 tiles.  Non-separator cells are black
background or colored foreground, with exactly one yellow marker pixel.

Rule
Find the tile containing the yellow marker.  Copy that entire 3x3 tile to
the tile whose macro row and column are the marker's local row and column
inside the source tile.  Clear all other non-separator cells to black and
preserve the grey separator grid.

Key insight
The yellow pixel has two roles: it identifies the source sprite and, by its
local coordinate within that sprite, encodes the destination slot.

annotation.src: 3x3 tile s containing the singleton yellow marker in the grey-separated 3x3 tile grid
annotation.dst: 3x3 tile slot d in the same grey-separated grid
annotation.match_cond: d.macro_row == yellow_marker.local_row_in_s and d.macro_col == yellow_marker.local_col_in_s
annotation.transform: clear all non-separator cells, preserve the grey separator grid, and stamp s into d

tags: condition:标记坐标编码槽位, marker_encodes_slot

references.docstring:
Extend the grid to the right with a left-right mirror copy of the whole input.

Input structure
- The input is a non-empty 2D grid that forms the complete left half of the output.
Rule
- Keep the original grid unchanged as the left half.
- Append the same rows in reverse column order as the right half.
Key insight
- The transformation is global horizontal reflection completion over the whole grid.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as the left tile
annotation.dst: horizontal two-tile strip
annotation.transform: copy the input tile on the left and append its left-right reflection on the right
annotation.grid_shape: input height unchanged; input width doubled

references.docstring:
Extend colored pixels downward from the underside of a chevron when the chevron is above them.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with one large chevron-shaped object.
- A second color appears as scattered pixels.
- Only scattered pixels in columns beneath the chevron affect the output.

Rule:
- Identify the chevron as the largest object and find its color.
- For each pixel of the other color, search upward in its column for the chevron.
- If found, fill that column from just below the chevron to the bottom with the pixel color.

Key insight:
- The chevron acts as an overhead boundary that activates vertical fills only in covered columns.

Complete the bounding rectangle around an incomplete teal shape by filling its missing cells red.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid containing an incomplete teal rectangle.
- The teal pixels define the intended rectangle's bounding box.
- Black pixels inside that bounding box are missing rectangle cells.

Rule:
- Find the bounding box of all non-black pixels.
- Replace black cells inside that box with red while preserving teal cells.
- Paste the completed rectangle back into the original grid.

Key insight:
- The non-black bounding box gives the full rectangle extent; interior black cells are gaps to complete.

Encode the number of distinct input colors as one of three grey lines on black.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 grid with one, two, or three distinct colors and no
  explicit background.

Rule
- One distinct color becomes a grey top row.
- Two distinct colors become a grey main diagonal.
- Three distinct colors become a grey anti-diagonal.
- All non-line pixels become black.

Key insight
- The visible color identities do not matter; only the distinct-color count
  selects which 3-cell line to draw.

annotation.src: 3x3 input grid summarized by its number of distinct colors
annotation.transform: replace the grid with black except for a grey 3-cell line: one color -> top row, two colors -> main diagonal, three colors -> anti-diagonal

references.docstring:
Extend each small arrowhead with a line in the direction it points.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with several same-colored arrowhead objects.
- Each arrowhead is a small shape whose missing corner indicates its direction.
- Lines should use the arrowhead color.

Rule:
- Crop each arrowhead and compare the mean positions of colored and black cells.
- Use that offset to infer the pointing direction.
- Draw a line from the matching outer corner of the arrowhead's bounding box to the grid edge.

Key insight:
- The arrowhead asymmetry identifies both the direction of travel and the corner where the path begins.

Recolor each gray object according to its pixel count.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with separate gray objects.
- Objects are detected using 4-connectivity.
- The generated objects have two, three, or four gray pixels.

Rule:
- Count the gray pixels in each object.
- Recolor two-pixel objects green, three-pixel objects red, and four-pixel objects blue.
- Leave any other gray object unchanged.

Key insight:
- Object area, not shape or position, determines the replacement color.

Use a downscaled monochrome pattern as a mask on the multicolor square.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with one large single-color pattern object.
- A smaller dense multicolor square appears elsewhere.
- The pattern is an integer scale-up of a square mask.

Rule:
- Separate the monochrome pattern from the multicolor square.
- Crop both objects and downsample the pattern to the square's size.
- Keep square pixels where the downsampled pattern is non-black and set the rest to black.

Key insight:
- The large object is a binary stencil that aligns with the square after integer downscaling.

Draw a one-pixel teal border around an otherwise black input canvas.

Input structure:
- The input is a rectangular black grid.
- No object content needs to be preserved.
- The output has the same dimensions as the input.

Rule:
- Create a black output grid with the input shape.
- Color the first and last rows teal.
- Color the first and last columns teal.

Key insight:
- The transformation depends only on the canvas dimensions.

Append a vertical reflection of the input pattern below the original.

Input structure:
- The input is a dense square pattern of non-black colors.
- The full input pattern is preserved in the output.
- The output is twice as tall as the input.

Rule:
- Treat the entire input as the source pattern.
- Flip the pattern top-to-bottom.
- Concatenate the original pattern above the reflected copy.

Key insight:
- The lower half is a mirror image across the input's bottom edge.

Complete every partial centered motif using the complete motifs visible in the same grid.

Input structure:
- The background contains one or more complete 3x3 motifs, each with a center color and a symmetric same-color shell mask.
- Other copies of those motifs are partial: either the center pixel is present without its shell, or the shell is present without its center.
- For each center color, the complete motif uniquely determines the shell color and shell offsets.

Rule:
- Infer every complete motif as center color -> (shell color, shell offsets).
- Around every pixel with a known center color, fill missing shell-offset background pixels with the shell color.
- At every background pixel whose surrounding offsets already contain a complete shell, fill the center with that motif's center color.

Key insight:
The complete motifs are templates that make center-only and shell-only partial copies two views of the same local sprite.

annotation.src: complete centered 3x3 motif template s with center color, shell color, and symmetric shell offsets
annotation.dst: partial motif copy d: either a center pixel alone or a matching shell mask around an empty center
annotation.match_cond: d.center_color == s.center_color, or d.shell_color == s.shell_color and d.shell_offsets == s.shell_offsets
annotation.transform: paint d's missing shell pixels or missing center pixel to complete the matched motif

tags: condition:完整图案推断缺失, motif_infers_missing

references.docstring:
Return the one sprite among several objects that has a symmetry.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid containing several monochromatic sprites.
- One sprite is symmetric under a rotation, reflection, or diagonal symmetry.
- The other sprites are non-symmetric distractors.

Rule:
- Detect and crop each object into its sprite.
- Test each sprite for radial, vertical, horizontal, and diagonal symmetry.
- Return the first sprite that satisfies one of those symmetry tests.

Key insight:
- Shape symmetry, not color or position, identifies the target sprite.

Fill black gaps by reconstructing the cyclic symmetric coordinate table visible in the non-black cells.

Input structure:
- The grid is square, with black pixels marking missing cells in an otherwise complete symmetric table.
- The first row is complete: it shows the diagonal color, the previous cycle color, then paired runs of the palette cycle.
- Every non-black input pixel already agrees with the hidden table.

Rule:
- Read the palette cycle from every other first-row cell starting at column 2, stopping when the diagonal color repeats.
- For a cell, let near = min(row, column) and dist = abs(row - column).
- Use the diagonal color when dist is 0, the previous cycle color when dist <= near + 1, otherwise cycle through blocks of width near + 2.

Key insight:
The missing pixels are not locally interpolated; they are entries of a global symmetric table indexed by distance from the main diagonal.

annotation.src: square grid with black gaps in a symmetric diagonal-index table; the complete first row gives the cyclic palette order
annotation.transform: reconstruct the full table from row and column coordinates: main diagonal uses the first palette color, cells within near+1 of the diagonal use the previous cycle color, and farther cells cycle in blocks of width near+2; fill the black gaps

tags: condition:已有推断缺失像素, existing_infer_missing

references.docstring:
Color every third black region between a red bouncing divider line yellow.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid split by a red line.
- The red line acts as a boundary between connected black regions.
- Regions are ordered from left to right by their bounding boxes.

Rule:
- Find connected regions using red as the separating background.
- Sort the regions from left to right.
- Flood-fill regions with indices 0, 3, 6, and so on with yellow.

Key insight:
- The red path partitions the grid; the fill pattern is determined by region order.

Crop the non-background rectangle and mirror it left-to-right.

Input structure
A mostly background grid contains one filled rectangular foreground region,
made from two non-background colors.

Rule
Find the tight bounding box of all non-background pixels, crop that region,
and return the crop with its columns reversed.

Key insight
The outer placement in the input is irrelevant; the output is the foreground
rectangle viewed in a horizontal mirror.

annotation.src: filled foreground rectangle inside a mostly background grid
annotation.transform: crop to the foreground bbox and mirror the crop horizontally; discard surrounding background
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop to the foreground bbox

references.docstring:
Compress uniform horizontal or vertical color stripes into a one-pixel-wide color sequence.

Input structure:
- The input is made of full-width horizontal stripes or full-height vertical stripes.
- Stripes may have thickness greater than one cell.
- Stripe colors appear in order across rows or columns.

Rule:
- Detect whether rows or columns are constant.
- Collapse consecutive duplicate row or column colors into one entry per stripe.
- Return a column for horizontal stripes or a row for vertical stripes.

Key insight:
- Stripe thickness is redundant; only orientation and ordered colors remain.

Reflect the square grid across its main diagonal.

Input structure:
- The input is a nonempty square grid.
- The colors are arbitrary visible categories and are preserved as a multiset.

Rule:
- Move each pixel at row r and column c to row c and column r.
- Return the transposed square grid.

Key insight:
- Every training output is the input read by columns instead of rows, which is
  exactly a main-diagonal reflection.

annotation.src: entire square input grid
annotation.transform: reflect across the main diagonal: output[row, col] = input[col, row]

references.docstring:
Overlay the four monochrome quadrant masks onto their common half-size canvas.

Input structure
The input is a 2x2 arrangement of equal-size regions on a uniform background.
Each region contains foreground pixels of exactly one color, forming one mask
at the output scale.

Rule
Start with a background output the size of one region. Stamp the masks from
back to front by quadrant position: top-left, bottom-right, bottom-left,
then top-right. Later masks overwrite earlier masks where they overlap.

Key insight
Folding all four quadrants onto the same coordinates gives the output
canvas; the quadrant positions encode the visible layer stack.

annotation.src: monochrome foreground masks s in the 2x2 quadrants, ordered back-to-front by quadrant position: top-left, bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right
annotation.dst: layers d of the half-size output canvas ordered back-to-front
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: fold each mask onto its local coordinates and stamp it with its quadrant color; later layers overwrite earlier overlaps
annotation.grid_shape: output is one quadrant: input height/2 by input width/2

tags: condition:四象限折叠同画布, quadrants_fold_one

references.docstring:
Copy the upper sprite into the adjacent side selected by the lower marker, reflecting it horizontally.

Input structure:
- The background contains two non-background color masks in vertically separated, aligned bboxes.
- The upper mask is the source sprite.
- The lower mask is a marker with one pixel on either the left or right end of its top row.

Rule:
- If the marker's top-row pixel is on the left end, use the same-size block immediately left of the source bbox.
- If it is on the right end, use the same-size block immediately right of the source bbox.
- Horizontally reflect the source mask and paint it into that destination block with the source color.

Key insight:
The lower marker is a direction code for which side should receive the reflected copy of the upper sprite.

annotation.src: upper non-background sprite mask and lower aligned marker mask
annotation.dst: same-size block immediately left or right of the upper sprite
annotation.transform: copy a horizontal reflection of the upper sprite into the selected adjacent block, leaving the original pixels unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: the marker's single top-row pixel on the left/right end selects the left/right destination block

references.docstring:
Recolor unboxed shape copies to match the same-shaped object enclosed by a gray box.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with gray outline boxes and colored sprites.
- Some colored sprites are contained inside gray boxes.
- Other sprites outside the boxes may share the same shape in different colors.

Rule:
- Separate gray box objects from non-gray sprite objects.
- Identify sprites contained inside gray interiors.
- Recolor outside sprites with matching shape masks to the contained sprite's color.

Key insight:
- Gray boxes mark reference examples whose colors transfer to same-shaped free copies.
tags: condition:框内参考色传同形, boxed_color_to_match

references.docstring:
Crop the framed mask and recolor each mask pixel with the legend color from its quadrant.

Input structure:
- A one-color frame is encoded by two full horizontal lines and two full vertical
  lines of the same color.
- The four diagonal pixels outside the frame corners are the quadrant legend colors.
- The framed interior contains one background color and one mask color.

Rule:
- Output only the rectangular interior of the frame.
- Split that interior into four equal quadrants.
- Replace each mask pixel by the corresponding outside-corner legend color and
  leave background pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The four corner pixels are not part of the output; they are a color legend
  for the mask cells in the matching quadrant of the cropped interior.

annotation.src: interior mask inside a same-color frame with four outside-corner control pixels
annotation.symbol_instructions: each outside corner color gives the fill color for the matching quadrant of the frame interior
annotation.transform: crop to the frame interior, split it into four equal quadrants, recolor mask pixels by their quadrant control color, and leave background pixels unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: frame interior

tags: condition:角标色定象限涂色, corner_sets_quadrant

references.docstring:
Downscale a black-line grid of colored partitions to one color pixel per region.

Input structure:
- The input is divided into rectangular regions by full black rows and columns.
- Each region contains scattered pixels of one non-black color.
- Region layout determines the output grid layout.

Rule:
- Locate the horizontal and vertical black divider lines.
- Iterate the rectangular intervals between dividers.
- Put each region's non-black color into the corresponding output cell.

Key insight:
- Divider geometry maps large colored regions directly to output pixel coordinates.
tags: condition:每区域折叠单像素, region_to_pixel

references.docstring:
Convert marked divider-grid cells into pixels colored by matching corner markers.

Input structure:
- The input has divider bars of one color forming rectangular regions.
- Some region vertices are single pixels in colors different from the divider.
- A valid marked region has all four diagonal corner markers in the same color.

Rule:
- Identify the divider color and crop to the area spanned by special vertex pixels.
- Find black regions bounded by the divider color.
- Emit the shared corner color for regions with four matching non-divider markers, otherwise black.

Key insight:
- Colored vertices label regions, while the divider color only defines the grid structure.
tags: condition:四角同色定区域色, corners_set_region

references.docstring:
Replace scattered blue pixels with an upper-left red tally of the same size.

Input structure
- The grid is a 3x3 black-background mask.
- Blue pixels are the only foreground pixels, with a count from one to four.
Rule
- Ignore the source positions and count the blue pixels.
- Clear the grid and paint that many red pixels in the canonical tally order:
  top row from left to right, then the center cell.
Key insight
- The blue mask is summarized by pixel count rather than moved as a shape.

annotation.src: 3x3 black-bg mask containing one to four blue foreground pixels
annotation.transform: replace the mask by a red count tally: paint the first n cells in order top-left, top-middle, top-right, center, where n is the number of blue pixels; all other cells become bg

references.docstring:
Color exterior background green and enclosed background regions red around the line object.

Input structure
- The grid has black background and one non-background color.
- The non-background pixels form one 4-connected orthogonal line object.

Rule
- Preserve the colored line object.
- Treat the line object as a wall: background connected to the grid border is exterior and becomes green.
- Background not 4-connected to the border is enclosed by the line object and becomes red.

Key insight
- This is a wall flood-fill task: flood from the boundary to identify exterior background, then the remaining background cells are holes.

annotation.src: single-color 4-connected foreground line object on black background
annotation.transform: preserve the line object; flood-fill border-connected background green and recolor the remaining enclosed background regions red

references.docstring:
Return the single repeated tile from a grid made of two identical adjacent copies.

Input structure
- The grid is a rectangular pattern duplicated exactly once, either side-by-side
  or top-to-bottom.
- The two copies occupy equal-sized halves along the duplication axis.

Rule
- Find the only axis whose two equal halves are identical.
- Output the first half along that axis.

Key insight
- The output is not recolored or otherwise transformed; it is the source tile
  before the duplicate copy was appended.

annotation.src: entire input grid as two identical adjacent tile copies
annotation.transform: find the unique horizontal or vertical equal-half split whose halves match; output the first tile half
annotation.grid_shape: one repeated tile block

references.docstring:
Use a 2x2 color guide to recolor the four quadrants of a 6x6 green mask.

Input structure:
- The input is a 9x9 grid split by one teal row and one teal column.
- One region contains a 2x2 guide with four non-black, non-green colors.
- The opposite region contains a 6x6 green sprite on black.

Rule:
- Separate the teal-divided regions and identify the color guide and green sprite.
- Split the green sprite into four equal quadrants.
- Recolor green pixels in each quadrant with the corresponding guide color in the same relative position.

Key insight:
- The teal cross only organizes the two artifacts; the 2x2 guide is a miniature color map for
  the 6x6 sprite's four 3x3 quadrants.

annotation.src: 9x9 grid divided by a solid one-pixel cross into one 2x2 color legend, one opposite 6x6 single-color mask, and two empty side regions
annotation.transform: replace the input with the 6x6 mask; split it into four 3x3 quadrants and recolor each mask pixel from the corresponding legend cell while preserving background pixels
annotation.grid_shape: 6x6 mask region
annotation.symbol_instructions: 2x2 color legend maps its cells in reading order to the four 3x3 mask quadrants

references.docstring:
Extend each diagonal control pixel attached to a foreground 2x2 square into a ray to the grid edge.

Input structure
- The dominant background surrounds one monochrome foreground object.
- The object contains a unique solid 2x2 square.
- Any extra foreground pixels are single diagonal neighbors of the square's corners.

Rule
- Preserve the input grid.
- For each extra foreground pixel diagonally attached to a square corner, continue in the same diagonal direction away from the square.
- Paint every background cell on that ray with the foreground color until the ray leaves the grid.

Key insight
- The 2x2 square is the anchor; its diagonal corner pixels are ray seeds that point outward from the square.

annotation.src: diagonal foreground control pixels adjacent to corners of the unique foreground 2x2 square
annotation.path: straight diagonal ray continuing from each control pixel away from the square until the grid boundary
annotation.trajectory: paint every visited background pixel with the foreground color
annotation.transform: preserve the square, control pixels, and all off-path background pixels

tags: condition:锚角对角射线至边, anchor_diag_to_edge

references.docstring:
Fill each empty rectangle whose marker pixels match a transformed copy of the source sprite's marker mask.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains one solid rectangular source sprite made from a fill color and embedded marker-color pixels.
- Additional marker-color pixels are scattered elsewhere, and some groups form transformed copies of the source marker mask.

Rule
- Find the source rectangle as the unique fill-color component whose bbox is fully occupied by fill and marker colors.
- Consider all unique rotations and reflections of the source rectangle's marker mask.
- Wherever a transformed marker mask exactly overlays marker-color pixels and every other in-bounds cell of that rectangle is background, paint those background cells with the fill color.

Key insight
The scattered marker pixels identify empty stamp locations by reproducing the source sprite's internal marker pattern.

annotation.src: source rectangular sprite s with fill-color cells and an embedded marker-color mask
annotation.dst: empty rectangular slot d containing marker-color pixels
annotation.match_cond: d.marker_mask equals a rotation/reflection of s.marker_mask; every non-marker in-bounds cell of d is bg
annotation.transform: paint d's bg cells with s.fill_color; preserve marker pixels and the original source sprite

tags: condition:掩码变换匹配则补, transform_match_fill

references.docstring:
Remove noise pixels from colored rectangles, restoring attached noise to rectangle color when needed.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with large same-colored rectangles.
- A different noise color appears as small objects on or away from the rectangles.
- Noise that touches a rectangle strongly represents an occluded rectangle cell.

Rule:
- Split objects into small noise objects and larger rectangle objects.
- For each noise object, count its 4-neighbor contact with each rectangle.
- Recolor noise to the rectangle color if it has at least two rectangle neighbors; otherwise delete it.

Key insight:
- Neighbor support distinguishes rectangle-covered noise from background noise.
tags: condition:邻接够归并否则删, merge_or_delete

references.docstring:
Remove isolated same-color noise pixels while leaving large rectangles intact.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with large rectangles.
- Rectangles and noise pixels share the same non-black color.
- Noise pixels have weak local support compared with rectangle pixels.

Rule:
- Visit every non-black pixel.
- Count its non-black 4-neighbors.
- Keep pixels with at least two colored neighbors and turn the rest black.

Key insight:
- Rectangle pixels have enough adjacent support, while isolated random noise does not.

Build a 2x2 mosaic from the input grid and its three quarter-turn rotations.

Input structure:
- A square 2D grid.

Rule:
- Put the original grid in the upper-left block.
- Put the 90-degree clockwise rotation in the upper-right block.
- Put the 90-degree counterclockwise rotation in the lower-left block.
- Put the 180-degree rotation in the lower-right block.

Key insight:
- Each output quadrant is the entire input seen from one of the four square rotations.

annotation.src: entire square input grid
annotation.transform: make a 2x2 mosaic with the original grid at upper-left, 90-degree clockwise rotation at upper-right, 90-degree counterclockwise rotation at lower-left, and 180-degree rotation at lower-right
annotation.grid_shape: input side length doubled in both dimensions

references.docstring:
Decode a 3x3 mask made from solid 3x3 blocks and stamp that mask into each active output block.

Input structure:
- The input has one background color and one foreground color.
- The foreground bounding box is a 9x9 square divided into nine uniform 3x3 tiles.
- Each tile is either entirely foreground or entirely background, forming a 3x3 mask.

Rule:
- Compress the 9x9 source region to its 3x3 on/off mask.
- Build a 9x9 output by replacing every on cell of that mask with a copy of the whole mask.
- Replace every off cell of the mask with a blank 3x3 block.

Key insight:
- The input is a block-enlarged binary symbol, and the output is the Kronecker product of that symbol with itself.

annotation.src: on cells s of the 3x3 mask decoded from the uniform 3x3 input tiles
annotation.dst: 3x3 output blocks d in the corresponding 3x3 block grid
annotation.match_cond: s.pos == d.block_grid_position
annotation.transform: paint the full decoded 3x3 mask inside each matched block; leave unmatched blocks background
annotation.grid_shape: 9x9 output

tags: condition:掩码克罗内克自积, kronecker_self

references.docstring:
Recolor hollow blue objects green while preserving non-hollow blue objects.

Input structure:
- The input contains multiple blue objects on a black background.
- Some objects fully enclose one or more black interior cells.
- Other blue objects are incomplete or open and do not enclose an interior region.

Rule:
- Find each blue connected component.
- Test whether the component has black cells inside its enclosed interior.
- Recolor hollow components green and paste all other objects unchanged.

Key insight:
- The decision is topological: a closed boundary that traps background cells is the feature
  that distinguishes objects to recolor.

annotation.src: 4-connected blue foreground objects
annotation.transform: recolor each complete one-cell-thick rectangular frame with bg interior to green; preserve incomplete or non-rectangular blue objects and bg

references.docstring:
Complete each partial row by applying its left-prefix color mapping to the full template row pattern.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly one row is fully non-background; this row is the two-color template pattern.
- Every other nonempty foreground row starts at column 0, has a contiguous
  non-background prefix, and then background cells to the right.

Rule
- For each partial row, pair each prefix cell with the template color in the
  same column to decode that row's color mapping.
- The prefix must define exactly one output color for each of the two template colors.
- Fill the entire row by replacing each template color with its decoded row color.

Key insight
- The complete row supplies only the sequence of roles; each shorter row's
  prefix gives the row-specific colors for those roles.

annotation.src: one complete two-color template row plus partial foreground rows whose left prefixes encode row-specific color maps
annotation.transform: for each partial row, decode template-color to row-color assignments from the prefix and fill the row by replaying the template sequence with that mapping
annotation.symbol_instructions: the complete row supplies the role sequence; each partial row's prefix gives the colors for those roles

tags: condition:前缀色映射补全行, prefix_map_complete

references.docstring:
Fill each background region of the broken lattice green if it is one intact rectangular cell, otherwise yellow.

Input structure
- The grid has a single background color and one non-background color forming a broken rectangular lattice.
- Background pixels form 4-connected regions: some are single intact cell interiors, others pass through gaps in the lattice.
Rule
- Preserve all non-background lattice pixels.
- For each 4-connected background region, compare its area with its inclusive bounding-box area.
- Recolor a region green when it exactly fills that rectangle; recolor it yellow when gaps connect multiple cells and leave lattice pixels inside its bounding box.
Key insight
- A single isolated cell is exactly a solid rectangle, while any open multi-cell area is a non-rectangular background component.

annotation.src: 4-connected background regions inside a broken single-color rectangular lattice
annotation.transform: preserve lattice pixels; recolor each background region green if it exactly fills its bbox, otherwise yellow

tags: condition:完整与缺损区异色, intact_broken_differ

references.docstring:
Move the single colored marker down one row and draw alternating yellow columns above it.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with exactly one non-black, non-yellow marker pixel.
- The marker is not on the bottom row.
- The marker's column defines the parity of the stripe pattern.

Rule:
- Move the marker color one row downward and clear its original cell.
- From the top through the marker's original row, color yellow every other column aligned with the marker column.
- Leave all other cells black.

Key insight:
- The marker supplies both a dropped object and a phase reference for the repeated vertical
  yellow stripe pattern.

annotation.src: single non-background marker pixel; its row and column select the affected region
annotation.transform: move the marker one row down; recolor to yellow all cells above and including its original row in every other column aligned with the marker column

references.docstring:
Grow a periodic vertical-bar pattern rightward from the lone colored pixel and add alternating gray markers.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with exactly one non-black pixel.
- The lone pixel supplies the bar color and starting column.
- Gray is reserved for the alternating marker pixels.

Rule:
- Draw vertical bars upward from the seed row every two columns to the right.
- Place gray pixels in the intervening columns.
- Alternate the gray marker row between the top and bottom edge.

Key insight:
- The seed pixel determines the color and phase of a periodic pattern across the remaining columns.
tags: condition:种子周期生成竖线, seed_periodic_bars

references.docstring:
Move the external two-color motif into the marked frame, mirroring it when needed so its side colors match the frame sides.

Input structure:
- The background contains four equal marker pixels at the corners of an empty
  rectangle.
- The two vertical sides of that rectangle are uniform foreground bars with
  different colors.
- A separate two-color motif has the same height and width as the rectangle's
  interior, and uses exactly the two side-bar colors.

Rule:
- Crop the marked rectangle to form the output canvas.
- Insert the separate motif into the rectangle interior.
- If the motif's left and right edge colors are reversed relative to the
  frame side colors, mirror the motif horizontally before insertion.

Key insight:
- The side bars are color labels for the motif orientation: the motif is
  placed in the only horizontal orientation whose visible side colors agree
  with the frame.

annotation.src: two-color motif s outside the marked rectangle
annotation.dst: interior d of the rectangle whose corners are marker pixels and whose side bars have the motif colors
annotation.match_cond: s.left_edge_color == d.left_side_color and s.right_edge_color == d.right_side_color after optional horizontal reflection
annotation.transform: crop the marked rectangle; copy s into d, mirroring s horizontally first if its side colors are reversed
annotation.grid_shape: bbox of the four marker pixels

references.docstring:
Extend each black marker into a full divider line through its colored rectangle.

Input structure
- The grid is partitioned into non-square monochrome rectangular regions.
