- A unique rare marker color appears as isolated pixels inside those regions.
- Each region is otherwise filled with exactly one non-marker color.

Rule
- For each wide region, replace the full region-height column through every
  marker with the marker color.
- For each tall region, replace the full region-width row through every
  marker with the marker color.
- Preserve colored regions that contain no marker.

Key insight
- The marker does not spread globally; the aspect ratio of its own rectangle
  chooses the perpendicular divider direction and the rectangle bounds stop it.

annotation.src: non-square monochrome rectangular regions containing black marker pixels
annotation.transform: in each wide region, recolor the full column through each marker to black; in each tall region, recolor the full row through each marker to black; leave regions without markers unchanged

tags: condition:标记沿短轴展分割, marker_short_axis_div

references.docstring:
Reverse the colors of the nested rectangular rings while preserving their positions.

Input structure
The grid is made of concentric one-cell-thick rectangular layers.  Every cell
at the same distance from the nearest edge has the same color.

Rule
Find the ordered color sequence from the outermost layer to the innermost
layer, reverse that sequence, and recolor each layer at its original depth
with the corresponding reversed color.

Key insight
The geometry is already correct; only the depth-indexed color sequence of the
nested rings is mirrored from outside to inside.

annotation.src: monochrome rectangular ring layers s ordered from outermost to innermost
annotation.dst: same ring-layer slots d ordered from outermost to innermost
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) + rank(d) == layer_count - 1
annotation.transform: preserve every layer mask and recolor each d with the color of its matched opposite-depth s

references.docstring:
Fill each hollow blue rectangular frame with red for even interior area and orange for odd interior area.

Input structure
- A black background contains one or more one-cell-thick blue rectangular frames.
- Each frame encloses a black rectangular interior.
- Frames may be separate or touch along their outside borders.

Rule
- Detect every blue rectangular border in the original input.
- Compute each frame's interior area.
- Fill the interior red when that area is even, or orange when it is odd.
- Leave the blue borders and all exterior background unchanged.

Key insight
- The fill color encodes the parity of the empty rectangular interior, so
  frames must be detected as rectangles rather than foreground components.

annotation.src: one-cell-thick blue rectangular frames on a black background, each enclosing black interior pixels; frames may touch externally
annotation.transform: fill each frame interior red if its interior area is even and orange if it is odd; preserve frame borders and exterior background

tags: condition:面积奇偶定填充色, parity_sets_fill

references.docstring:
Expand each sparse marker inside the dense rectangle into a full marker-color row and column.

Input structure
- A noisy grid contains one largest rectangle using exactly two colors.
- Within that rectangle, one color is the dominant base and the other appears only as sparse interior marker pixels.

Rule
- Crop to the marked rectangle's shape.
- Start with the rectangle's base color everywhere, then for every marker pixel paint its whole row and whole column with the marker color.

Key insight
- The small marker pixels are row/column controls; the surrounding noisy cells are distractors and the output keeps only the expanded marked rectangle.

annotation.src: largest two-color rectangle in the noisy grid: a dominant base color with sparse interior marker pixels
annotation.transform: crop to that rectangle, fill with the base color, and paint every row and column containing a marker pixel in the marker color
annotation.grid_shape: same height and width as the marked rectangle

tags: condition:标记展为整行整列, marker_to_row_col

references.docstring:
Copy the single colored sprite so its bounding-box center lands on the gray marker.

Input structure:
- A background grid containing one non-gray foreground sprite.
- Exactly one gray marker pixel sits in an otherwise empty region.
- The sprite's bounding box has odd height and odd width, so it has a center cell.

Rule:
- Keep the original sprite unchanged.
- Extract the full bounding box of the non-gray sprite, treating background cells inside the box as transparent.
- Paste that sprite box centered on the gray marker, replacing the marker.

Key insight:
The gray pixel is not a color to preserve; it marks the center of a second copy of the existing sprite.

annotation.src: single non-gray foreground sprite s
annotation.dst: empty same-size window d centered on the gray marker pixel
annotation.match_cond: unique s maps to unique d; s.bbox_center aligns with d.gray_marker
annotation.transform: stamp s into d with background transparent; remove the gray marker and preserve the original sprite

tags: condition:精灵对准标记复制, sprite_at_marker

references.docstring:
Return the one quadrant pattern that is not repeated among the four separated quadrants.

Input structure:
- The grid has odd height and width.
- The middle row and middle column are the background color, forming a separator cross.
- The separator cross divides the grid into four same-sized rectangular quadrant regions.

Rule:
- Compare the four quadrant regions as complete arrays.
- Exactly one quadrant pattern occurs once while the other three share another pattern.
- Output a copy of the uniquely occurring quadrant region.

Key insight:
- The large grid is a four-choice set of small patterns; the answer is the odd one out.

annotation.src: four same-sized quadrant regions separated by a background row and column
annotation.transform: compare the four quadrant arrays and output the one complete quadrant pattern that occurs only once
annotation.grid_shape: the quadrant region size (2x2 for the given inputs)

references.docstring:
Copy the color of the unique complete rectangular frame onto the matching empty rectangle elsewhere.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one complete monochrome rectangular frame.
- That frame's interior is a single empty color.
- Elsewhere, exactly one same-size rectangle has the same empty-colored interior
  but a non-frame-colored perimeter.

Rule:
- Find the complete source frame and infer its color, size, and empty interior color.
- Find the unique same-size non-source window whose interior is entirely the
  empty color.
- Recolor that window's perimeter to the source frame color, preserving every
  other pixel.

Key insight:
- The source frame is a template for completing the camouflaged rectangle:
  its interior identifies the empty color, while its bbox gives the destination
  size and perimeter shape.

annotation.src: complete monochrome rectangular frame s with a single empty interior color
annotation.dst: same-size rectangular window d elsewhere whose interior has that same empty color
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox.shape == d.bbox.shape and s.interior.color == d.interior.color; unique s maps to unique d
annotation.transform: paint d.perimeter with s.color; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Scale and place the external multicolor object into the yellow-cornered region where it matches existing colors.

Input structure:
- The input contains one small multicolor object outside a larger region.
- Four yellow singleton pixels mark the corners of the larger output region.
- The marked region contains partial colored evidence from a scaled version of the small object.

Rule:
- Use the four yellow pixels to crop the target region.
- Generate scaled versions of the small object and try all placements inside that crop.
- Choose a placement whose colored cells cover every existing non-black, non-yellow cell in the target region, then paste it.

Key insight:
- The partial colored cells inside the frame are alignment constraints for the scaled miniature;
  the yellow corners define the output crop.

annotation.src: external multicolor miniature pattern s
annotation.dst: scaled block slots inside the corner-marked frame d
annotation.match_cond: d.scale is the common in-frame square size; choose the unique offset where every existing square block in d aligns to a same-colored cell of s
annotation.transform: crop to the frame and paint each non-bg cell of s as a solid scale-by-scale block, preserving the frame corners
annotation.grid_shape: crop to the rectangle marked by the four corner pixels
annotation.symbol_instructions: external miniature pattern encodes the full block layout and colors

references.docstring:
Build a vertically symmetric output by appending the input rows in reverse order.

Input structure:
- The input is a non-empty 2D ARC grid.
- The whole input grid is the source pattern.

Rule:
- Keep the input grid as the top half.
- Place a vertical reflection of the entire input directly below it.

Key insight:
The output is not recolored or edited cell-by-cell; it is the original pattern followed by the same rows read bottom-to-top.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as the top-half pattern
annotation.transform: append a vertical reflection of the input grid underneath, preserving all colors
annotation.grid_shape: input height multiplied by 2, width unchanged

references.docstring:
Tile the input with horizontal and vertical reflections into a 3-by-2 mirrored canvas.

Input structure:
- The input is a monochromatic sprite on a black background.
- The full input pattern is used as the source tile.
- The output is three times taller and twice as wide as the input.

Rule:
- Build the middle band by concatenating a left-right reflection beside the original.
- Flip that middle band top-to-bottom.
- Stack the flipped band above and below the middle band.

Key insight:
- The output is generated by reflecting the source across the left and horizontal band edges.

Draw red segments toward the gray divider and blue segments away from it.

Input structure:
- The input is a black grid with one straight gray row or column.
- Red and blue pixels appear on both sides of the gray divider.
- The gray divider stops lines that are drawn toward it.

Rule:
- Detect whether the gray divider is horizontal or vertical.
- Draw red lines from red pixels toward the divider.
- Draw blue lines from blue pixels away from the divider toward the edge.

Key insight:
- The gray line is an axis of attraction for red and repulsion for blue.
tags: condition:颜色决定射线方向, color_determines_ray_direction

references.docstring:
Fill the gray square with stripe colors in the order and orientation they appear.

Input structure:
- The grid contains colored stripes and one gray square.
- The gray square side length matches the number of stripe color entries.
- Stripes are all vertical or all horizontal.

Rule:
- Extract the gray square as the output canvas.
- Sort non-gray stripes by column for vertical stripes or row for horizontal stripes.
- Fill each output column or row with the corresponding stripe color in order.

Key insight:
- Stripe orientation determines whether the ordered colors become output columns or rows.

Rotate the filled template region into each following empty region.

Input structure:
- Gray divider lines split the grid into same-sized regions.
- Exactly one region contains a non-black, non-gray template.
- Later regions are black slots for rotated copies.

Rule:
- Locate full gray row or column dividers and derive the region slices.
- Find the first region containing template pixels.
- Fill each subsequent region with the next 90-degree clockwise rotation.

Key insight:
- The dividers define ordered slots; the template supplies the repeated rotation sequence.

Repeat the foreground row band vertically to fill the whole grid.

Input structure
- The input is a 2D grid with a background color and one contiguous horizontal
  band of rows containing all non-background pixels.
- Rows outside that band are entirely background.

Rule
- Use the full-width foreground band as a vertical tile.
- Repeat that tile upward and downward over the original canvas, keeping the
  original band row aligned with its input row position.

Key insight
- The sparse input is a phase marker for a vertical row pattern, not a set of
  separate objects to move or recolor.

annotation.src: full-width foreground row band used as a vertical tile
annotation.dst: all rows of the original canvas
annotation.transform: repeat the band rows upward and downward with modulo phase anchored at the band's input row position, preserving background cells inside the tile

tags: condition:前景行带铺满画布, foreground_band_tiles_to_fill_canvas

references.docstring:
Crop out the foreground rectangle that contains the most marker pixels.

Input structure
- The upper-left cell is background.
- The foreground consists of multiple 4-connected solid rectangles made from
  a common fill color, with a rarer marker color replacing some cells.

Rule
- Treat the rarer of the two foreground colors as the marker color.
- Count marker pixels inside each foreground rectangle.
- Return the exact bounding-box crop of the unique rectangle with the largest
  marker count.

Key insight
- The output is not redrawn or recolored; it is one existing input rectangle
  selected by the count of its marker pixels.

annotation.src: solid foreground rectangles containing sparse marker pixels
annotation.transform: select the rectangle with the largest marker-pixel count and return it unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop to the selected rectangle bbox

references.docstring:
Replace each foreground cell of the compact motif with a full copy of that motif in the corresponding output block.

Input structure
- The grid contains a single non-background color forming a compact square-bbox motif.
- The full grid dimensions are the motif dimensions squared.

Rule
- Crop the foreground motif from its bounding box.
- For each foreground pixel in the motif at local position (r, c), paste the whole motif into output block (r, c).
- Leave all other blocks as background.

Key insight
- The sparse input is a self-expansion: the motif is both the block-placement mask and the stamp copied into every selected block.

annotation.src: cropped single-color foreground motif s
annotation.dst: motif-sized output block d in the full canvas
annotation.match_cond: d.block_grid_position is a foreground pixel position in s
annotation.transform: stamp s into each matched block; leave unmatched blocks as background
annotation.grid_shape: same as input; full grid dimensions are motif dimensions squared

tags: condition:前景位置决定印章, foreground_positions_determine_stamp

references.docstring:
Downscale a colored rectangular partition grid to one pixel per partition.

Input structure:
- A multicolored chessboard-like sprite sits on a black background.
- Each cell is a monochromatic rectangle and cell sizes may vary.
- Component upper-left corners define the row and column partition positions.

Rule:
- Detect the non-black rectangular components.
- Collect sorted unique top-left row and column positions.
- Sample the input color at each position to build the compact output grid.

Key insight:
- The output is the partition coordinate skeleton, not a proportional resize.
tags: condition:每分区缩为单像素, each_partition_reduced_to_one_pixel

references.docstring:
Complete each lower foreground prefix by continuing the top complete column pattern in blue.

Input structure
A black-background grid has one foreground color arranged in separated row-groups. The top row-group spans every column and is the complete reference pattern; each lower row-group starts at the left edge and contains a shorter prefix of the same column-state pattern.

Rule
Keep all existing foreground pixels. For every lower row-group, compare its compressed sequence of nonempty row-offset states by column to the top pattern, then paint the missing suffix columns with blue using the remaining top states; if the lower group already reaches the top pattern's final state, continue that final state to the right edge.

Key insight
The exact run lengths before a state change can vary, but the compressed order of column states is shared: horizontal bars, zigzags, and multi-row stripes are all completed by extending that state sequence.

annotation.src: top full-width foreground row-group and lower left-edge row-group prefixes
annotation.dst: missing right-side suffix columns of each lower row-group
annotation.transform: compress consecutive equal column states in the top group; each lower group matches a prefix of those states, then extends the remaining states to the right edge in blue, repeating the final state when the prefix has reached it

tags: condition:完整模式续写缺失, missing_suffix_continued_from_pattern

references.docstring:
Expand each isolated colored marker into a centered 3x3 hollow outline whose color is paired with the marker color.

Input structure:
- A black background contains one or more isolated single-pixel markers.
- Marker colors are red, green, and/or teal.
- Each marker has an empty one-cell neighborhood, so a centered 3x3 outline
  fits without hitting other foreground.

Rule:
- Keep each marker unchanged.
- Around each green marker, paint the surrounding 3x3 outline pink.
- Around each teal marker, paint the surrounding 3x3 outline yellow.
- Around each red marker, paint the surrounding 3x3 outline blue.

Key insight:
- The marker pixel is the center; its color selects the outline color, while
  the geometry is always the same 3x3 hollow square.

annotation.src: isolated red, green, and teal marker pixels on black background
annotation.transform: keep each marker; paint the centered 3x3 hollow outline around green in pink, teal in yellow, and red in blue

tags: condition:标记色决定描边色, marker_color_determines_outline

references.docstring:
Repeat the 3x3 input sprite into the first foreground-count slots of a black block grid.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 sprite containing black background and exactly one non-black foreground color.
- The number of black pixels determines the square block-grid side length.
- The number of non-black pixels determines how many copies of the sprite are emitted.

Rule
- Build a black output canvas with black-pixel-count slots per side, where each slot is 3x3.
- Copy the entire input sprite into the first non-black-pixel-count slots in row-major order.
- Leave all remaining slots black.

Key insight
- The colors are not changed; the two pixel counts control the output size and the number of repeated input sprites.

annotation.src: entire 3x3 input grid used as a sprite; black-pixel count b and foreground-pixel count f
annotation.dst: b x b grid of 3x3 sprite slots
annotation.transform: copy the input sprite into the first f slots in row-major order and leave the remaining slots black
annotation.grid_shape: square with side length 3b

references.docstring:
Keep only the unique largest solid monochrome rectangle and erase the surrounding noise.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background with scattered non-background noise pixels.
- One non-background color contains a unique large solid axis-aligned rectangle,
  possibly with extra same-color protrusions outside the rectangle.
Rule
- Find the largest-area solid rectangle whose cells all share one non-background
  color and whose height and width are both at least two.
- Return a blank background grid with only that rectangle redrawn in its
  original position and color.
Key insight
- The retained color is identified by the large filled rectangular support,
  not by its color id or by total color frequency.

annotation.src: non-background pixels on a black background, including one unique largest solid monochrome rectangle
annotation.transform: erase all pixels except that largest solid rectangle; preserve the rectangle's original color and position

references.docstring:
Expand each input pixel into a solid 3x3 block of the same color.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 color grid.

Rule
- Replace every pixel at input position (r, c) with a 3x3 block in output
  rows 3*r..3*r+2 and columns 3*c..3*c+2.
- Preserve the original pixel color, including the background color.

Key insight
- The output is a fixed nearest-neighbor scale-up of the entire 3x3 grid,
  not a foreground-only object transformation.

annotation.src: 3x3 input pixel grid
annotation.transform: replace each pixel by a solid 3x3 block of the same color at the corresponding block-grid position
annotation.grid_shape: 9x9 nearest-neighbor scale-up

tags: condition:每像素扩展为色块, each_pixel_expanded_to_block

references.docstring:
Draw a foreground-color rectangular frame just inside the four marker pixels.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background color, one foreground drawing color, and one marker color.
- The marker color appears exactly four times, with unique top, bottom, left, and right extrema.
- The foreground drawing color is the only non-background, non-marker color.

Rule:
- Use the min/max marker rows and columns as outside guides.
- Paint the rectangle border from one row/column inside those marker extrema in the foreground color.
- Preserve all existing pixels, including the markers and the original foreground object.

Key insight:
- The four markers are control pixels for the frame sides; the existing foreground object supplies the color to draw with.

annotation.src: four marker pixels that define the outside bounds of a frame plus the existing foreground color
annotation.transform: draw a rectangular border one cell inside the marker extrema in the foreground color; preserve the markers and original foreground pixels

references.docstring:
Expand each color in the 2x2 marker block into the diagonally opposite clipped rectangle around that block.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color and exactly one 2x2 foreground block.

Rule
- Keep the marker block unchanged.
- Each marker pixel fills the outside rectangle diagonally opposite its position in the block.
- Each painted rectangle is adjacent to the marker block and extends at most two rows and two columns, clipped by the grid edge.

Key insight
- The 2x2 block is a local quadrant legend: each cell names the color for the opposite quadrant-like region around the block.

annotation.src: single 2x2 foreground marker block on the background
annotation.transform: keep the marker block unchanged; fill each adjacent outside rectangle diagonally opposite a marker pixel with that pixel's color, extending at most two rows and two columns and clipping at the grid edge
annotation.symbol_instructions: the 2x2 marker block maps each cell color to the diagonally opposite surrounding region

references.docstring:
Color selected divider-bounded regions by their relative positions.

Input structure:
- Gray lines partition a black canvas into multiple regions.
- At least three non-gray regions are present.
- Regions are selected by upper-left, middle, and lower-right position.

Rule:
- Treat gray as the divider color and find connected regions between dividers.
- Fill the upper-left region blue and the lower-right region green.
- Fill the middle positional candidate red while leaving dividers unchanged.

Key insight:
- The regions are not identified by shape; their sorted positions determine their colors.

Overlay the two equal-size input masks and mark cells that are background in both.

Input structure
The grid is a vertical stack of two same-width rectangular masks.  Each half
contains the same background color plus exactly one foreground color.

Rule
Return one half's shape, filled with the background color, and recolor a
cell red when the corresponding cell is background in both input halves.

Key insight
The output is the common empty-space mask of the two stacked patterns, not
a crop or a transformation of either foreground object.

annotation.src: two equal-size masks stacked vertically, sharing one background color
annotation.transform: collapse each pair of corresponding cells to one output cell: paint red where both source cells are background, otherwise background
annotation.grid_shape: height halved, same width

references.docstring:
Move the four interior-corner markers to the opposite corners just outside the rectangular frame.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- The foreground contains a unique one-pixel-thick monochrome rectangular frame.
- The only other foreground pixels are four markers at the frame interior's four corners.
Rule
- Keep the frame unchanged and clear the four marker pixels to the background color.
- Place each marker at the opposite corner of the frame's one-cell-expanded bounding box.
Key insight
- The frame defines both the source marker slots just inside it and the destination slots just outside it.

annotation.src: colored marker pixel s at an interior corner of the rectangular frame
annotation.dst: outside corner slot d of the frame's one-cell-expanded bbox
annotation.match_cond: s and d occupy diagonally opposite corners relative to the frame
annotation.transform: clear s to bg and paint d with s.color; keep the frame unchanged

references.docstring:
Preserve the uniquely most frequent input color and recolor all other pixels gray.

Input structure:
- The grid contains at least two colors.
- Gray is absent from the input and is used only as the output replacement color.
- Exactly one input color has the largest pixel count.

Rule:
- Find the unique most frequent color in the whole grid.
- Keep pixels of that color in their original locations.
- Replace every other pixel with gray.

Key insight:
- The visible role of the preserved object is its population: the majority
  color remains, while all minority colors are merged into the same gray fill.

annotation.src: all pixels grouped by input color frequency
annotation.transform: preserve pixels of the unique most frequent color; recolor every pixel of all other colors to gray

references.docstring:
Add the four colored diagonal corner markers around every grey 2x2 square.

Input structure
- The grid has black background pixels and one or more 4-connected grey
  foreground objects.
- Every grey object is a solid 2x2 square with a one-cell black margin at
  each diagonal outside corner.

Rule
- Preserve the input grid.
- For each grey square, paint blue at the northwest outside corner, red at
  the northeast outside corner, green at the southwest outside corner, and
  yellow at the southeast outside corner.

Key insight
- The grey squares are fixed anchors; the output is a local decoration of
  each square's bounding box, not a movement or matching problem.

annotation.src: solid grey 2x2 square objects on a black background
annotation.transform: preserve each grey square and paint blue, red, green, and yellow pixels at its northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast diagonal outside corners

tags: condition:四角固定配色装饰, fixed_color_diagonal_corner_decoration

references.docstring:
Extend the existing horizontal color pattern to twice the input width.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one or more non-background rows.
- Every column belongs to a repeating horizontal period that may be truncated
  at the right edge of the input.
Rule
- Find the shortest horizontal period that explains all input rows.
- Keep the height fixed and continue that period until the grid is twice as
  wide as the input.
Key insight
- The output is not a copy of the input appended to itself; it is the next
  columns of the underlying periodic tile.

annotation.src: the input grid as the visible prefix of a horizontally periodic tile
annotation.transform: find the shortest column period that explains all rows, then continue that period to twice the input width
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input; width doubled

tags: condition:宽度加倍延续周期, double_width_continuing_period

references.docstring:
Extend each colored marker pixel into a rightward alternating marker/grey stripe ending at the grid edge.

Input structure
- A dominant background with single-cell non-background marker pixels.
- Each marker row contains exactly one marker pixel.
- The marker pixels are not grey; grey is reserved for the alternating separator cells in the output.

Rule
- Preserve all cells to the left of each marker.
- From each marker through the right edge of its row, write the marker color on even offsets from the marker and grey on odd offsets.
- Rows with no marker remain unchanged.

Key insight
- The marker is the start of a horizontal ray; distance parity from the marker determines whether a cell receives the marker color or grey.

annotation.src: single-cell non-background marker pixels, one per active row
annotation.path: horizontal ray from each marker to the right edge of its row
annotation.trajectory: paint the ray continuously, alternating marker color on even offsets from the marker and grey on odd offsets
annotation.transform: keep rows without markers and cells left of each marker unchanged

references.docstring:
Crop the red object and fit each multicolor puzzle piece into its matching red-shaped hole.

Input structure:
- The input contains one fully red object with black holes.
- It also contains several multicolor puzzle pieces on the black background.
- Puzzle pieces may include red cells that act as the hole-fitting stencil.

Rule:
- Crop the red object to form the output canvas.
- Sort puzzle pieces by the number of red cells so larger stencils are placed first.
- Try rotations and translations, placing each piece where its red cells land only on black holes.

Key insight:
- Red cells inside a piece are not paint for the red object; they are the stencil that tells
  which hole shape the piece can occupy.

annotation.src: outside two-color motif s whose carrier-color cells form a stencil
annotation.dst: 8-connected background hole component d inside the large carrier-color rectangle
annotation.match_cond: some rotation of s has carrier-color cells exactly equal to d
annotation.transform: crop to the rectangle bbox, fill it with carrier color, and stamp the rotated s paint-color cells over it
annotation.grid_shape: crop to the large carrier-color rectangle bbox

references.docstring:
Slide the rectangular body of the non-rectangular foreground object along its straight stem until it touches the rectangular anchor.

Input structure
- A black-background grid with exactly two foreground colors.
- One foreground color is a solid rectangular anchor object.
- The other foreground color is one connected object made from a unique largest
  solid rectangular body plus a straight one-cell-wide connector stem.
Rule
- Erase the whole non-rectangular object.
- Translate only its rectangular body along the connector direction by the
  connector length, so the body lands next to the anchor.
Key insight
- The connector is not kept; it is a path telling how far and in which
  direction the solid body should slide.

annotation.src: unique largest solid rectangular body inside the non-rectangular foreground object
annotation.path: straight one-cell-wide connector stem toward the separate solid rectangular anchor; move by the stem length
annotation.dst: slot adjacent to the anchor at the stem end
annotation.trajectory: paint only the final translated rectangle
annotation.transform: erase the original moving-color object including the stem; keep the anchor unchanged

references.docstring:
Decode three fixed gray glyphs into colored rows ordered from left to right.

Input structure:
- The input is three 4x4 gray/black glyphs separated horizontally by black columns.
- Each glyph is one of four known black-mask patterns.
- The left-to-right glyph order determines the top-to-bottom output row order.

Rule:
- Crop and sort the three glyph components by column position.
- Map each glyph pattern to its associated color: red, teal, yellow, or green.
- Create a square output with one solid row per decoded glyph color.

Key insight:
- The position of black cells within each 4x4 gray block is a symbolic code for an output color.

annotation.src: three black/grey 4x4 glyph regions separated by black columns
annotation.transform: decode each glyph from the position of its black mask and replace it by one solid output row: solid -> red, centered hole -> teal, side gaps -> green, lower centered hole -> yellow
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3, one row per input glyph from left to right

references.docstring:
Collapse two separator-stacked masks into a green mask of their foreground disagreements.

Input structure
- A single full-width separator row has a color that appears only in that row.
- The separator splits the grid into equal-height upper and lower masks.
- The two masks share exactly one color, the background, and each has one non-background foreground color.
Rule
- Remove the separator row and align the upper and lower masks cell by cell.
- Paint green where exactly one of the two aligned cells is foreground.
- Paint the shared background color everywhere the two aligned cells agree.
Key insight
- The output is the symmetric difference (xor) of the two aligned foreground masks.

annotation.src: two equal-size foreground masks above and below a solid one-pixel separator row
annotation.transform: collapse each aligned pair of cells to one output cell: paint green iff exactly one source cell is foreground; otherwise background
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one source mask

tags: condition:前景不一致处涂色, disagreement_cells_painted

references.docstring:
Extend each colored marker rightward to the grid edge, then downward on the right edge until the next marker row.

Input structure
- The grid is a non-empty rectangle with a dominant background color.
- Every foreground cell is a single colored marker pixel.
- Each active row contains exactly one marker.

Rule
- Sort the marker pixels from top to bottom.
- For each marker, paint its row from the marker column through the right edge with the marker color.
- Then paint the rightmost column from that marker row down to one row before the next lower marker, or to the bottom for the last marker.

Key insight
- The markers are row-start controls for right-turning paths, and the next marker below is the stopping boundary for the vertical edge segment.

annotation.src: foreground marker pixels, one per active row
annotation.path: from each marker, go horizontally right to the last column, then downward along the last column until one row before the next lower marker or the bottom edge
annotation.trajectory: paint every visited background pixel with the marker color while keeping the original marker
annotation.multi_step: process markers in top-to-bottom row order so each marker's vertical segment ends before the next marker row

tags: condition:转折至下一标记行, turning_path_to_next_marker_row

references.docstring:
Rebuild the colored frame around the mask, recoloring each mask pixel by its unique nearest side.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Four same-length solid bars form the top, bottom, left, and right sides of
  a rectangular frame, with the frame corners left as background.
- All remaining foreground components share one mask color and occupy an
  n by n bbox, matching the frame interior size.

Rule
- Output the compact n+2 by n+2 frame with the four bars on the border.
- Normalize the mask bbox into the frame interior.
- For each mask pixel, compare its distances to the top, left, bottom, and
  right edges of the mask bbox; recolor it with the corresponding side color
  only when the nearest side is unique.
- Keep tied mask pixels in the original mask color and leave all other
  interior cells as background.

Key insight
- The mask is not simply copied: side colors claim exactly the pixels whose
  nearest frame side is unambiguous, while equidistant pixels remain mask-colored.

annotation.src: four colored same-length frame bars and a separate same-size foreground mask bbox
annotation.transform: compact the bars into the output border; place the normalized mask inside it; recolor each mask pixel by the color of its unique nearest border side, leaving tied pixels as the mask color
annotation.grid_shape: n+2 by n+2, where n is the side-bar length and mask bbox size

references.docstring:
Convert color frequencies into a top-aligned histogram ordered from most to least common.

Input structure:
- The input is a small grid fully filled with non-black colors.
- Each color may appear multiple times.
- Original pixel positions are irrelevant after counting.

Rule:
- Count how many cells each color occupies.
- Sort colors by descending count.
- Build a black output with one column per color and fill each column from the top for that color's count.

Key insight:
- The output is a frequency chart: color order is determined by population, and column height is
  the count itself.

annotation.src: input colors s ordered from most frequent to least frequent by pixel count
annotation.dst: left-to-right top-aligned histogram columns d
annotation.match_cond: rank(s by pixel count descending) == rank(d left-to-right)
annotation.transform: discard original positions; fill each matched column from the top with its color for exactly its input pixel count, leaving remaining cells black
annotation.grid_shape: height is the largest color pixel count; width is the number of input colors

references.docstring:
Complete a corner-coded set of concentric square frames by reflecting it to all four sides.
Input structure
- The grid is an odd-sized square with black/empty background and foreground pixels only on the odd-coordinate lattice.
- The foreground pixels form a compact code near one corner of the lattice.
Rule
- Choose the unique corner closest to all foreground pixels and read pixels as local coordinates from that corner.
- A diagonal local pixel gives the color of the four corners of that ring.
- A local pixel on the horizontal or vertical side of a ring gives the color for both opposite sides of that ring.
Key insight
- The sparse input is one corner's description of nested square frames, not the frames themselves; the missing cells are filled by bilateral symmetry and side expansion.

annotation.src: foreground pixels in the nearest-corner code on the odd-coordinate lattice
annotation.dst: completed concentric square frames on the same odd-coordinate lattice
annotation.transform: read the nearest corner as the local origin; diagonal code pixels color the four corners of their ring, while horizontal and vertical side code pixels fill the two opposite sides of that ring

references.docstring:
Reflect the square grid across its uniform foreground main diagonal.

Input structure
- The input is a square grid with a dominant background color.
- The main diagonal is a complete one-color foreground line.
- The diagonal color appears only on that line; other foreground colors are off the line.

Rule
- Keep the diagonal fixed and move every off-diagonal pixel to the cell with swapped row/column coordinates.
- Equivalently, return the matrix transpose of the input grid.

Key insight
- The one-color diagonal is the reflection axis, so color values are preserved while coordinates are transposed.

annotation.src: square grid with a complete one-color main diagonal as the mirror axis
annotation.transform: transpose the grid across that diagonal: each cell at (r,c) moves to (c,r), preserving colors

references.docstring:
Return the 3x3 patch that completes the grid's left-right mirror symmetry.

Input structure
- The input is a horizontally mirrored pattern with one compact 3x3 black missing patch.
- The missing patch's reflected counterpart across the vertical axis is fully colored.

Rule
- Find the black 3x3 patch.
- For each patch cell, copy the color from the same row and mirror-reflected column.
- Output only the recovered 3x3 patch, not the full repaired input grid.

Key insight
- The black cells are not background; they mark a cropped hole whose values are determined by left-right reflection.

annotation.src: left-right mirror-symmetric color pattern with one compact 3x3 black missing patch
annotation.transform: copy the colors from the missing patch's same-row mirror-reflected columns, reverse their column order, and output that recovered 3x3 patch
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 cropped missing patch

references.docstring:
Flood-fill black background regions connected to original blue pixels, turning them blue while leaving blockers unchanged.

Input structure:
- A rectangular grid has black background cells, one or more blue seed pixels, and other non-black colors acting as blockers.
Rule:
- Starting from every original blue pixel, traverse 4-neighbor black cells and recolor each reached black cell blue.
- Leave every non-black pixel unchanged.
Key insight:
- Black cells remain black exactly when no orthogonal path of black cells connects them to an original blue seed.

annotation.src: original blue pixels
annotation.path: 4-neighbor flood through black background cells, blocked by any other foreground color and stopping when no adjacent black cells remain
annotation.trajectory: paint every reached black pixel blue
annotation.transform: preserve all original non-black pixels and leave black regions not reached by the flood unchanged

tags: condition:种子沿连通域扩散, spread_from_seed_through_connected

references.docstring:
Collapse a separator grid into one color per region, then mirror the compact grid left-to-right.

Input structure:
- The input is divided into uniformly colored cells by horizontal and vertical separator bars.
- Each region between separators has a single color.
- The separator color forms a connected partition spanning the full canvas.

Rule:
- Identify the separator color and extract all separator-delimited regions.
- Replace each region with one pixel of its region color, preserving row and column order.
- Mirror the compact region-color grid horizontally.

Key insight:
- The large chessboard-like image is an enlarged region map; the final step is a left-right
  reflection of that compressed map.

annotation.src: equal square regions separated by one-pixel full horizontal and vertical separator lines; each region is uniform
annotation.transform: collapse each separator-free region to its single color, then mirror the coarse color map left-to-right
annotation.grid_shape: one output pixel per separator-free region

references.docstring:
Move the foreground object so its bounding box fits exactly inside the four corner markers.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, one foreground color forming exactly the
four corners of a rectangle, and one 4-connected foreground object whose
bounding box is the same size as that rectangle's interior.

Rule
Clear the moving object from its original position, then translate every one
of its pixels so the object's bbox upper-left corner becomes the upper-left
cell inside the marker rectangle.

Key insight
The corner markers are not copied or filled; they define a target interior
window for the unchanged object mask.

annotation.src: single 4-connected foreground object s of the non-marker color
annotation.dst: interior d of the rectangle defined by the four same-color corner markers
annotation.match_cond: unique s maps to unique d; s.bbox size equals d.size and s.bbox upper-left aligns to d upper-left
annotation.transform: erase s from its original location and translate its mask unchanged into d; keep the corner markers fixed

tags: condition:对象移入标记矩形, object_moved_into_marker_rectangle

references.docstring:
Draw a teal L-shaped path from the red pixel to the green pixel, moving horizontally first and then vertically.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color, exactly one red marker, and exactly one green marker.
- The red and green markers are in different rows and different columns.
- Every other input cell is background.

Rule
- Start from a copy of the input.
- Paint teal background cells across the red marker's row until reaching the green marker's column.
- From that elbow, paint teal background cells along the green marker's column until just before the green marker.

Key insight
- The red marker supplies the starting row, and the green marker supplies the target column for a horizontal-then-vertical Manhattan path.

annotation.src: red marker pixel s
annotation.path: horizontal segment from s along s.row to the green marker column, then vertical segment along that column toward the green marker, stopping before the marker
annotation.dst: green marker pixel d
annotation.trajectory: paint every background cell on the L path teal
annotation.transform: keep the red and green marker pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Summarize the largest foreground object-size class as solid vertical color bars.

Input structure:
- The input has a dominant background color and several monochromatic
  4-connected foreground objects.
- Each foreground color appears as exactly one object.
- The largest objects have distinct left edges, giving a unique left-to-right
  ordering.

Rule:
- Find the maximum foreground object area.
- Keep exactly the objects with that area.
- Build an output whose height is that maximum area and whose columns are
  filled with the kept object colors in left-to-right input order.

Key insight:
- The original shapes are distractors; only object area and horizontal order
  survive, so each selected object collapses to a same-color vertical bar.

annotation.src: largest-area monochromatic foreground objects, ordered left-to-right by bbox left edge
annotation.dst: output columns in the same left-to-right order
annotation.match_cond: s.left_edge.order == d.column.order
annotation.transform: replace each selected object by a solid same-color column whose height is the object area
annotation.grid_shape: height is largest object area; width is number of largest objects

references.docstring:
Trace the blue pixel diagonally upward while bouncing off side walls.

Input structure:
- The grid is black except for one blue pixel.
- The blue pixel is the starting point of the path.
- The grid boundaries act as the reflecting walls.

Rule:
- Move diagonally up and right from the start pixel.
- Paint every visited cell blue.
- Reverse horizontal direction at the left or right edge and stop when exiting the top.

Key insight:
- Only the horizontal direction changes on a bounce; the path always moves upward.

Tile the whole input grid once to the right to make two identical horizontal copies.

Input structure:
- A nonempty 2D color grid; all colors, including background, are part of the tile.

Rule:
- Preserve the input as the left half of the output.
- Copy the same full grid into the right half without changing colors or orientation.

Key insight:
- The output is a width-doubling repetition of the entire grid, not a per-object
  recolor or local edit.

annotation.src: entire input grid used as a tile
annotation.dst: two side-by-side original-size blocks
annotation.transform: copy the input unchanged into both the left and right blocks
annotation.grid_shape: same height as input and twice the input width

references.docstring:
Move each marker pixel straight inward until it touches the one-cell ring around the solid 2x2 block.

Input structure
- The background contains exactly two foreground colors.
- One foreground color forms a unique filled 2x2 block.
- The other foreground color appears as marker pixels aligned with the block by row, column, or 45-degree diagonal.

Rule
- Keep the 2x2 block fixed.
- Clear every marker from its original position.
- Project each marker along its row, column, or diagonal toward the block, stopping in the adjacent ring cell on the same side/corner of the 2x2 block.

Key insight
- The 2x2 block is the anchor, and every marker is already on one of the eight rays extending from the block's surrounding ring.

annotation.src: marker pixels outside the solid 2x2 foreground block
annotation.path: straight row, column, or 45-degree diagonal path inward toward the 2x2 block, stopping at the adjacent ring cell on the same side or corner
annotation.trajectory: move each marker pixel to its stopping cell
annotation.dst: one-cell ring around the solid 2x2 block
annotation.transform: clear the original marker positions and keep the 2x2 block fixed

references.docstring:
Fill every fully enclosed background region inside red outlines with blue.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and red one-cell-thick outline/barrier pixels.
- Red outlines may touch each other or the grid boundary, and some red shapes
  may be incomplete.
- Blue is absent from the input and appears only as the fill color.

Rule
- Treat red pixels as walls and trace all background pixels connected to the
  grid boundary by 4-neighbor steps.
- Recolor each remaining background pixel to blue.
- Leave red pixels and exterior background unchanged.

Key insight
- The blue cells are exactly the background holes: black regions that cannot
  escape to the outer boundary without crossing a red wall.

annotation.src: red 4-connected outline/barrier pixels on black background, with some barriers enclosing background holes
annotation.transform: preserve red pixels; flood-fill border-connected background as background and recolor the remaining enclosed background regions blue

tags: condition:孤立背景区域填充, unreachable_background_filled

references.docstring:
Recolor every second pixel in each down-right foreground diagonal run to yellow.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background and exactly one non-background foreground color.
- The foreground pixels form one-cell-wide runs using down-right diagonal adjacency.

Rule:
- For each maximal down-right diagonal run, keep the first pixel in its original color.
- Walking down-right, recolor the odd-indexed pixels of that run to yellow.
- Leave the background and even-indexed foreground pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- Alternation restarts at each top/left endpoint of a diagonal run; rows with
  multiple foreground pixels belong to different runs, not one global sequence.

annotation.src: maximal one-cell-wide foreground diagonal runs with down-right adjacency
annotation.transform: from each run's top/left endpoint, recolor every second foreground pixel yellow and preserve the other pixels

references.docstring:
Pack the four colored 2x2 L sprites into a compact 4x4 frame around a central hole.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- There are exactly four monochrome 4-connected foreground objects.
- Each object is a three-pixel L shape occupying a 2x2 bounding box with one background corner.

Rule
- Crop each L sprite to its 2x2 bounding box.
- Place it in the 4x4 output quadrant opposite its missing corner, preserving its orientation and color.
- The missing corner of each sprite becomes one cell of the central 2x2 background hole.

Key insight
- The object orientation, not its absolute input position or color id, determines which output quadrant it occupies.

annotation.src: monochrome 2x2 L sprite s
annotation.dst: one of four 2x2 quadrants d in the 4x4 output around the central hole
annotation.match_cond: s.missing_corner is the inner corner of d facing the central 2x2 hole
annotation.transform: crop s to its 2x2 bbox and copy it into d without rotation
annotation.grid_shape: 13x13 input -> 4x4 output

tags: condition:缺角决定目标象限, missing_corner_determines_quadrant

references.docstring:
Keep only the tallest and shortest vertical bars, recoloring them blue and red.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color and one foreground color forming
  separated one-cell-wide vertical bars.
- The tallest and shortest bars have unique heights.

Rule
- Clear the grid to background.
- Repaint the tallest input bar at its original location in blue.
- Repaint the shortest input bar at its original location in red.

Key insight
- The grey bars behave like a height ranking: only the maximum and minimum
  ranks survive, and their original columns and vertical extents are preserved.

annotation.src: foreground vertical bars ranked by height
annotation.transform: clear all bars except the unique tallest and shortest; recolor the tallest bar blue and the shortest bar red

tags: condition:保留极值高度分色, keep_extremes_and_recolor

references.docstring:
Paint the long hidden blank corridors green while preserving the colored clutter.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background color and one visible clutter color.
- Green is absent from the input and is used as the output fill color.
- The intended hidden corridors are long all-background rectangular bars, but
  random background gaps can touch them or create small blank pockets.

Rule:
- First keep only background pixels whose whole in-grid 3x3 neighborhood is background.
- Enumerate maximal rectangles inside that clear-background mask.
- In descending rectangle area, accept rectangles whose major axis spans at least
  half a grid side and add only newly exposed 4-connected portions at least one
  third of a grid side in area.
- Recolor the accepted background mask green.

Key insight:
- The object to reveal is negative space: true corridors survive a one-pixel
  clearance test and contribute long new rectangular growth, while incidental
  gaps are either short or add only tiny disconnected fragments.

annotation.src: background pixels in long clear-background rectangular bars hidden among one-color clutter
annotation.transform: recolor the selected background mask to green; preserve all clutter pixels
annotation.multi_step: use the 3x3-clear background mask, process maximal long rectangles largest first, and keep only substantial new 4-connected bar growth

references.docstring:
Fill triangular green and blue wedges around a left-anchored red horizontal segment.

Input structure:
- The grid has an empty background and exactly one foreground object.
- The foreground object is a red horizontal segment starting at the left edge.

Rule:
- Preserve the red segment.
- Above the red segment, fill left-aligned rows green with width equal to the segment length plus distance above.
- Below the red segment, fill left-aligned rows blue with width equal to the segment length minus distance below.

Key insight:
- The red segment is the shared base width; moving upward expands the fill by one cell per row, while moving downward shrinks it by one cell per row.

annotation.src: left-anchored red horizontal segment on an empty background
annotation.transform: preserve the red segment; paint rows above as a left-aligned green wedge whose width grows by one per row away from the segment, and rows below as a left-aligned blue wedge whose width shrinks by one per row

tags: condition:逐行宽度递变成楔, row_width_increments_form_wedge

references.docstring:
Overlay the four quadrant masks split by a separator cross into one smaller grid.

Input structure:
- A 2D grid has one solid separator row and one solid separator column of the
  same non-background color.
- The cross divides the grid into four equal-size regions.
- Each region is a mask made from background plus one distinct foreground color.

Rule:
- Compare corresponding pixels of the four regions.
- For each output pixel, keep the first non-background pixel in row-major
  region order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
- If all four corresponding pixels are background, output background.

Key insight:
- The separator cross is not part of the answer; it presents four aligned
  layers whose visible top layer is determined by quadrant position.

annotation.src: four same-size quadrant masks s ordered top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right around the separator cross
annotation.dst: aligned output layer slots d on one canvas, ordered from top visible layer to bottom hidden layer
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: stamp each mask at its relative coordinates; earlier layers keep their color at overlaps and uncovered cells remain background
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one quadrant; separator row and column are removed

references.docstring:
Fill the one-cell black gaps inside dashed horizontal blue bars with red.

Input structure
- The grid is a black canvas containing only blue foreground pixels.
- Every blue pixel belongs to a horizontal dashed bar whose blue pixels are separated by one black gap.

Rule
- Preserve all input pixels.
- Recolor each black pixel to red exactly when its immediate left and right neighbors are blue.

Key insight
- The output completes each dashed blue row segment locally; the only changed cells are horizontal 1-0-1 gaps.

references.docstring:
Crop to the tight foreground bounding box and replace retained background pixels with black.

Input structure
- A single dominant background color surrounds one foreground mask made from one or more non-background colors.
- The output keeps only the rectangular bounding box of that foreground mask.

Rule
- Find all pixels whose color is not the input background color.
- Crop the input to the tight bounding box of those foreground pixels.
- Inside that crop, replace the input background color with black and preserve every foreground color.

Key insight
- The output is not a connected-object extraction; it is the foreground mask's rectangular crop, so background gaps inside the crop become the output blank color.

references.docstring:
Extend the colored diagonal through gray triangle tips and remove the guides.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one colored diagonal line on black background.
- Gray right-triangle objects touch that diagonal.
- The diagonal color is the only non-gray foreground color.

Rule:
- Determine the diagonal color and orientation.
- For each gray object, find the bordering tip farthest from the original diagonal.
- Draw a same-colored diagonal through that tip in both directions, then erase gray pixels.

Key insight:
- Gray triangles are construction guides whose remote tips seed the new parallel diagonals.

references.docstring:
Move the single teal object down one row and recolor it red.

Input structure:
- One teal object appears on a black background.
- The object has room to move down one pixel.
- No other foreground objects are expected.

Rule:
- Extract the single foreground object.
- Recolor every foreground cell red.
- Translate the object one row downward on a black output canvas.

Key insight:
- The object shape is preserved exactly; only color and vertical position change.

Fill each row with the color selected by that row's grey marker column.

Input structure:
- The grid is a 3x3 black background with grey marker pixels.
- Each row contains exactly one grey marker and two black pixels.

Rule:
- Read the grey marker column in each row.
- Replace the whole row by the color assigned to that column: left -> red, middle -> yellow, right -> green.

Key insight:
- The grey pixels are row-wise control pixels; their horizontal position, not their connected shape, determines the output row color.

annotation.src: 3x3 black grid rows, each with one grey marker
annotation.transform: fill each row with the color determined by its marker column: left red, middle yellow, right green

references.docstring:
Select the 3x3 sprite with the largest foreground-pixel count and return that sprite.

Input structure
The input is a one-dimensional strip of 3x3 tiles, either horizontal or vertical.
Black is the background color. Each tile contains exactly one non-black color.

Rule
Partition the strip into its 3x3 tiles. Count non-black pixels in each tile,
require a unique maximum count, and output that winning tile unchanged.

Key insight
The selected sprite is determined by filled area, not by color or by its position
in the strip.

annotation.src: monochrome 3x3 sprites arranged as a horizontal or vertical strip on black background

annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 selected sprite tile

references.docstring:
Arrange the nine small gray squares into a 9x9 layout by their internal colored directions.

Input structure:
- The input contains nine 3x3 gray squares, one of them blank.
- The other squares contain colored cells attached near one side or corner.
- Squares may touch in the input and are detected by their fixed 3x3 size.

Rule:
- Start from a 9x9 gray output.
- Ignore the all-gray square.
- Slide each nonblank square from the center to the output edge indicated by its colored cells and paste it there.

Key insight:
- Each small square encodes its destination by the direction of its colored patch relative to the gray center.
tags: condition:色块决定输出位置, color_direction_determines_placement

references.docstring:
Recolor the largest rectangular black pocket(s) in each black component red.

Input structure
- The input is a grey field with black empty regions; no red pixels are
  present initially.
- Black regions are interpreted as 4-connected components.
- Some black components contain a solid rectangular subregion with both
  height and width at least 2.

Rule
- For each 4-connected black component, enumerate all solid all-black
  rectangles with height >= 2 and width >= 2.
- If a component contains such rectangles, recolor every maximum-area
  rectangle in that component to red.
- Leave grey pixels and black cells outside those selected rectangles
  unchanged.

Key insight
- The output is not the union of every black 2x2 square; within each black
  component, smaller overlapping rectangles are ignored unless they tie for
  the largest area.

annotation.src: 4-connected black components on a grey field
annotation.transform: within each component, find all solid black rectangles with height and width at least 2; recolor every maximum-area rectangle red, including ties, and leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Replace the red anchor pixel with a fixed four-corner color pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is black except for one red pixel.
- The red pixel marks the center of the output pattern.
- The output keeps the input shape.

Rule:
- Locate the red pixel.
- Create a blank black output canvas.
- Paste a 3x3 pattern with colored diagonal corners centered on the red pixel.

Key insight:
- The red pixel is only an anchor and is not copied into the output.
tags: condition:锚点粘贴固定图案, paste_fixed_pattern_at_anchor

references.docstring:
Use the bottom-left guide pixel to recolor the central object.

Input structure:
- A colored object appears away from the bottom-left corner.
- The bottom-left cell contains a single guide color.
- Black is the background and the guide color differs from the object color.

Rule:
- Read the guide color from the bottom-left cell.
- Clear that guide pixel to black.
- Recolor every remaining foreground cell with the guide color.

Key insight:
- The corner pixel is a color key that transfers its color and then disappears.

Fill the cup interior with yellow and emit yellow rays from its opening.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one non-black cup shape on black background.
- The cup encloses black interior cells and has an opening on one side.
- The cup may be rotated to face any direction.

Rule:
- Find the cup bounding box and the black cells inside it.
- Fill those interior cells yellow.
- Draw yellow straight out through the opening and diagonally from the opening endpoints until blocked.

Key insight:
- The opening position relative to the cup center determines the outward direction of the fill.

Scale the whole input so each cell becomes a square block whose side length is the number of foreground pixels.

Input structure
A small grid with a uniquely dominant background color and at least one non-background pixel.

Rule
Count the non-background pixels, then replace every input pixel by a solid square block of that side length.

Key insight
The colored pixels are not moved independently; their count sets the uniform magnification factor for the entire grid.

annotation.src: 3x3 grid with n non-background pixels
annotation.transform: replace every input pixel with an n-by-n block of the same color
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by n

tags: condition:前景数为放大系数, foreground_count_as_scale_factor

references.docstring:
Move each colored ray endpoint inward to touch the singleton marker it points at.

Input structure
- The background contains exactly two singleton marker colors.
- Every other foreground pixel is on the same row or column as exactly one marker.
- The landing cells adjacent to those markers are empty and do not conflict.

Rule
- Keep the two singleton markers fixed.
- For each non-marker foreground pixel, find the unique marker sharing its row or column.
- Clear the original pixel and repaint it in the cell immediately next to that marker along the same ray.

Key insight
- The scattered pixels are already directional endpoints of cardinal rays; the output compresses each ray to its nearest cell around the ray's marker.

annotation.src: non-marker foreground pixels on cardinal rays from one of the two singleton marker pixels
annotation.path: straight row/column path inward toward the unique aligned singleton marker, stopping at the cell adjacent to that marker

annotation.dst: adjacent cell around the aligned singleton marker
annotation.transform: clear each original endpoint and keep the marker pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Select the 3x3 sprite with the most pixels of the rare foreground color.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains several separated 4-connected foreground sprites.
- Exactly two foreground colors fill each sprite, and every sprite is a solid 3x3 rectangle.
- One foreground color is globally rarer; it acts as the marked color.

Rule
- Infer the marked color as the unique least frequent non-background color.
- Extract each foreground component as its 3x3 sprite.
- Return the unique sprite with the largest count of marked-color pixels.

Key insight
- The output is a crop of one existing sprite, selected by marker density rather than by location.

annotation.src: separated 4-connected 3x3 sprites filled by two foreground colors on a dominant background
annotation.transform: select the unique sprite with the most pixels of the globally rarer foreground color and output that sprite unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: 3x3 crop of the selected sprite

tags: condition:标记色最多者选中, max_marker_count_selected

references.docstring:
Recolor isolated 1x1 red components blue while leaving larger red components alone.

Input structure:
- The grid contains red components on a black background.
- Components are detected with 4-connectivity.
- Some red components may be single isolated pixels.

Rule:
- Detect all red components.
- For each component with a 1x1 bounding box, recolor that pixel blue.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- Object size, not location or surrounding shape, determines which red pixels change.

Fill red rectangles whose corners are marked by groups of four yellow pixels.

Input structure:
- Yellow pixels mark outside corners of one or more hidden rectangles.
- Rectangle interiors are black in the input.
- The four yellow markers share two rows and two columns.

Rule:
- Search yellow pairs that can form opposite rectangle corners.
- Confirm the other two yellow corners by row and column alignment.
- Fill the open interior of each such rectangle red.

Key insight:
- Yellow pixels are geometric corner constraints; the red output is the implied interior.
tags: condition:四角标记围定内部, four_corners_define_interior

references.docstring:
Summarize the empty space above liquid in a U-shaped frame as a 3x3 clockwise gauge.
Input structure
- The grid has a background, one U-shaped frame color, and one fill color inside the frame.
- The fill color forms a solid bottom-aligned rectangle in the frame interior.
Rule
- Count the empty interior rows above the first filled row.
- Output a 3x3 background grid and paint that many cells with the fill color along a clockwise spiral from the top-left.
Key insight
- The output is not a scaled copy of the liquid; it is a compact gauge of the headspace height.

annotation.src: U-shaped frame with a solid bottom-aligned fill mask in its interior
