tags: condition:空行数映射填充量, empty_rows_map_to_fill_amount

references.docstring:
Expand each colored source pixel into a recolored copy of the companion mask template.

Input structure:
- The input is two equal square panels, either side-by-side or stacked.
- The two panels share exactly one background color.
- One panel is a source grid with colored foreground pixels; the other is a mask template using one marker color.

Rule:
- Make an N^2 x N^2 output for N x N panels, initialized to the background.
- For each non-background source pixel at source position (r, c), recolor the template marker mask with that pixel's color.
- Stamp that recolored mask into the corresponding N x N output block at block position (r, c).

Key insight:
- The source grid supplies the block positions and colors, while the separate one-color panel supplies the repeated sprite shape.

annotation.src: two equal square panels: a colored source grid and a one-color mask template
annotation.transform: for each non-background source pixel, stamp the mask template recolored to that pixel color into the corresponding output block; leave source-background blocks empty
annotation.grid_shape: N x N panels -> N^2 x N^2 output
annotation.symbol_instructions: the one-color mask panel defines the sprite shape copied for each source pixel

tags: condition:源色决定模板涂色, source_color_determines_template_recolor

references.docstring:
Recolor every pink pixel red while preserving every orange pixel.

Input structure:
- The grid is a non-empty 2D array containing exactly pink and orange pixels.
- Pink pixels are the source mask to rewrite; orange pixels are preserved.

Rule:
- Copy the grid.
- Replace every pink pixel with red.
- Leave every orange pixel unchanged.

Key insight:
- The changed cells are exactly the pink mask, so the task is a direct
  in-place color normalization.

annotation.src: pink pixel mask among orange pixels
annotation.transform: recolor every pink pixel to red; leave orange pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor each 8-connected foreground object by whether its normalized shape is repeated or unique.

Input structure
- The dominant background contains several same-color foreground objects.
- Objects are 8-connected; diagonal contact joins pixels into the same object.
- Up to translation within each bbox, exactly one object shape appears once
  and exactly one other object shape appears multiple times.

Rule
- Group foreground objects by their normalized bbox mask.
- Recolor the singleton-shape object red.
- Recolor every repeated-shape object blue.
- Keep the background unchanged.

Key insight
- The recolor is determined by object-shape frequency, not by position or size alone.

annotation.src: same-color foreground objects on bg, grouped by 8-connected normalized bbox shape
annotation.transform: recolor the singleton object shape to red; recolor every repeated object shape to blue; preserve bg

references.docstring:
Draw a green one-cell border around every adjacent red pair while leaving isolated red pixels unchanged.

Input structure
- The grid is a black background containing only red foreground pixels.
- Each 4-connected red object is either a single pixel or a two-pixel horizontal/vertical domino.

Rule
- Preserve all input pixels.
- For each red domino, expand its bounding box by one cell in all directions, clipped to the grid.
- Paint the perimeter of that expanded box green wherever it is currently black.

Key insight
- The green marks are not drawn around all red pixels, only around the 4-connected red objects of area two.

annotation.src: 4-connected red foreground objects on a black background
annotation.transform: preserve all pixels; for each two-pixel horizontal/vertical red object, paint green on the perimeter of its bbox expanded by one cell and clipped to the grid; leave single red pixels unframed

references.docstring:
Recolor every foreground object that encloses a background hole to teal.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and exactly one foreground color.
- The foreground pixels form separate 4-connected objects.
- Teal is absent from the input and is reserved as the output mark.

Rule
- Keep objects whose bbox contains no enclosed background region unchanged.
- For each foreground object with a 4-connected background hole inside its bbox, recolor all of that object's pixels to teal.
- Leave background pixels unchanged, including the holes themselves.

Key insight
- The changed objects are selected by topology, not by size or position: they are precisely the objects whose mask has an interior hole.

annotation.src: single-color 4-connected foreground objects on a background; some objects enclose background holes
annotation.transform: recolor each object that encloses a 4-connected background hole to teal; preserve objects without holes and all background pixels

references.docstring:
Grow each green rectangle outward from its red border indicator to the canvas edge.

Input structure:
- Each foreground object is a green rectangle with one red pixel on its border.
- Objects sit on a black background.
- The red pixel indicates the side from which growth should extend.

Rule:
- Find each rectangle-and-indicator component.
- Extend a green band from the rectangle toward the canvas edge on the indicator side.
- Draw a red line from the indicator pixel to that same edge.

Key insight:
- The indicator side controls direction, while the rectangle thickness controls the grown band.
tags: condition:指示侧扩展至边界, extend_from_indicator_to_edge

references.docstring:
Stretch the colored rectangular frame outward until its far edge reaches the lone marker pixel.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- A single marker pixel is the only foreground color that appears once.
- All other foreground pixels form one solid rectangular frame with one border color and one interior color.

Rule
- If the marker is above or below the frame and its column lies within the frame, extend the frame vertically to the marker row.
- If the marker is left or right of the frame and its row lies within the frame, extend the frame horizontally to the marker column.
- Redraw the expanded rectangle with the same border and interior colors; everything outside remains background.

Key insight
The marker selects which side of the rectangle moves and where the new outer border lies; it is consumed by that border.

annotation.src: one two-color rectangular frame on the background plus a singleton marker pixel aligned with one side span
annotation.transform: erase the marker and redraw the frame expanded in the marker direction so the marker row or column becomes the new outer border; preserve the frame border and interior colors

tags: condition:标记决定拉伸终点, marker_determines_stretch_endpoint

references.docstring:
Replace each isolated grey control pixel with a centered 3x3 grey-and-blue motif.

Input structure
- The grid background is the dominant color, and every foreground pixel is grey.
- Each grey pixel is isolated with a full 3x3 background neighborhood around it.
Rule
- Erase each grey center to background.
- Paint the four diagonal neighbors grey and the four orthogonal neighbors blue.
Key insight
- The sparse grey pixels are not final objects; they are centers for a fixed 3x3 stencil.

annotation.src: isolated grey control pixels on the background
annotation.transform: replace each control pixel's 3x3 neighborhood with grey corners, blue edge-midpoints, and a background center

references.docstring:
Recolor each solid gray rectangle by marking its corners blue, border yellow, and interior red.

Input structure
- The grid contains black background cells and one or more gray foreground objects.
- Each gray object is a 4-connected solid rectangle with height and width at
  least 2.

Rule
- For every gray rectangle, recolor its four corner cells blue.
- Recolor its remaining border cells yellow.
- Recolor all strict interior cells red.
- Leave black background cells unchanged.

Key insight
- The output colors encode each rectangle's local geometry, not its position
  or size: corners, edges, and interiors receive fixed roles independently
  for every gray component.

annotation.src: 4-connected solid grey rectangular objects on a black background
annotation.transform: within each rectangle, recolor corner pixels blue, remaining border pixels yellow, and strict interior pixels red; leave black background unchanged

tags: condition:角边内部分别涂色, corner_border_interior_recolored

references.docstring:
Connect two aligned colored pixels through a centered split-color hollow rectangle.

Input structure:
- Two single pixels of different colors are aligned horizontally or vertically.
- The background is black.
- There is enough space between the pixels for the hollow rectangle bridge.

Rule:
- Rotate vertical cases into a horizontal canonical form.
- Build a hollow rectangle whose left half uses the left color and right half uses the right color.
- Paste it midway between the pixels and connect each pixel to the nearest side.

Key insight:
- After canonical rotation, the task is a symmetric bridge between left and right color anchors.

Mirror each primary object across its attached indicator pixel and recolor the mirror copy.

Input structure:
- Larger primary-color objects sit on a black background.
- One-pixel indicators of other colors touch the primary objects.
- Indicators may touch sides or corners of the primary object.

Rule:
- Pair each indicator with every primary object it touches.
- Recolor a copy of the primary object to the indicator color.
- Mirror that copy across the side or corner axis implied by the indicator position.

Key insight:
- Attached single pixels provide both the mirror axis and the color for the reflected copy.

Fill reachable maze corridors from two colored seeds with alternating colors.

Input structure:
- Teal cells form the maze structure.
- Two non-teal, non-black indicator colors seed black corridor cells.
- Black cells connected to the seeds are the fill targets.

Rule:
- Identify the two indicator colors excluding teal and black.
- From each seed, recursively fill adjacent black cells.
- Alternate between the two indicator colors at every step.

Key insight:
- Corridor color is determined by path parity from a seed, while teal maze cells stay fixed.
tags: condition:路径奇偶交替涂色, alternating_color_by_path_parity

references.docstring:
Replace the missing-marker cells so the whole grid has matching horizontal and vertical reflections.

Input structure:
- The grid is a complete reflection-symmetric pattern except for cells of one marker color.
- Under reflection across the horizontal and vertical center lines, each orbit has exactly one non-marker color.
- The marker color is structurally unique: treating any other color as missing breaks at least one orbit.

Rule:
- Group cells by their four-way reflection orbit: original, vertical mirror, horizontal mirror, and 180-degree mirror.
- Infer the unique marker color whose removal leaves one known color in every orbit.
- Fill every cell in each orbit with that known color.

Key insight:
- The yellow cells are not objects to move; they are holes in a two-axis mirror pattern, and their values are copied from the visible cells in the same reflection orbit.

annotation.src: non-yellow pixels of a full-grid pattern with horizontal and vertical reflection symmetry
annotation.transform: group cells into four-way reflection orbits; infer yellow as the unique missing-cell marker, then fill each yellow pixel from the single visible color in its orbit

tags: condition:标记处填入轨道色, fill_marker_with_orbit_color

references.docstring:
Extend the central bottom bar color into the flanking columns as an upward stepped outline.

Input structure
- The grid has a background and exactly two foreground colors.
- The bottom row is all foreground: one color forms a single interior contiguous bar, and the other color flanks it.
- The interior bottom bar color is the color that gets extended; the flanking color remains unchanged.

Rule
- Keep the input unchanged, then add one bottom-bar-colored pixel in every bottom-row flanking column.
- For each flanking column, compute its horizontal distance to the nearest end of the interior bar.
- Place the new pixel in that same column, one row above the bottom for each distance step, with an additional one-row gap above the bottom row.

Key insight
- The bottom row is a ruler: distance from the central bar determines how high the matching color is lifted in each side column.

annotation.src: two-color bottom-row pattern: one interior contiguous bar color flanked by the other foreground color
annotation.transform: keep the input unchanged; in each flanking bottom-row column, add the interior bar color at the same column, with row height determined by horizontal distance from the nearest end of the bar

tags: condition:距离决定阶梯高度, distance_determines_step_height

references.docstring:
Enlarge the whole 3x3 grid by the number of distinct foreground colors.

Input structure
The input is a 3x3 grid with one unique dominant background color and at
least one foreground color.

Rule
Count the distinct non-background colors. Replace every input pixel with a
square block of that side length, preserving the pixel's color.

Key insight
The output scale is not fixed; it is encoded by the number of different
foreground colors in the small input pattern.

annotation.src: all pixels of the 3x3 input grid, with background as the unique dominant color
annotation.transform: count distinct non-background colors and replace each input pixel by a same-color square block of that side length
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by the number of distinct non-background colors

references.docstring:
Crop the single foreground rectangle and swap its two non-background colors.

Input structure:
- A dominant background surrounds one fully occupied rectangular foreground region.
- The foreground rectangle contains exactly two non-background colors and no background holes.

Rule:
- Crop to the bounding box of all non-background pixels.
- In that crop, replace each foreground color with the other foreground color.

Key insight:
- The output is the compact foreground rectangle after a two-color inversion, not the original canvas.

annotation.src: single fully occupied two-color foreground rectangle on bg
annotation.transform: crop to the foreground bbox, then swap the two foreground colors inside the crop
annotation.grid_shape: same height and width as the foreground bbox

references.docstring:
Return the color of the unique rectangular foreground object that encloses a background hole.

Input structure
- The input has a dominant background and several separated single-color rectangular foreground objects.
- Exactly one foreground object is a complete rectangular frame around one or more background pixels.

Rule
- Find all monochrome 4-connected foreground objects.
- For each object's bbox, require a complete border in that object's color.
- Select the unique object whose bbox contains a 4-connected background component that does not touch the bbox border.
- Output a 1x1 grid containing the selected object's color.

Key insight
- The answer is not determined by object size, position, or color identity; it is the only object with an enclosed background hole.

annotation.src: single-color rectangular foreground objects on a background; exactly one object encloses a 4-connected background hole
annotation.transform: replace the grid with the color of the object whose bbox contains an enclosed background component
annotation.grid_shape: 1x1 label cell

references.docstring:
Recolor the yellow pixels in every third column of the three-row alternating lattice to pink.

Input structure
- A 3-row grid containing only black bg and yellow foreground.
- The middle row is solid yellow.
- The top row alternates black/yellow, and the bottom row is its color complement.

Rule
- Keep the grid shape and all black pixels unchanged.
- In columns 0, 3, 6, ..., recolor any yellow pixel to pink.

Key insight
- The pink marks are not new objects; they are a regular column-period highlight applied only where the yellow lattice already has pixels.

annotation.src: three-row black/yellow lattice with a solid yellow middle row and complementary alternating edge rows
annotation.transform: recolor yellow pixels in columns 0, 3, 6, ... to pink; keep all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Swap the visible color of the crossing area between two perpendicular full-span bars.

Input structure:
- The dominant background surrounds two non-background colors.
- One horizontal bar occupies a contiguous band of rows with no background cells.
- One vertical bar occupies a contiguous band of columns with no background cells.
- Their rectangular crossing is uniformly one of the two foreground colors.

Rule:
- Preserve the grid except for the crossing rectangle.
- Recolor every crossing pixel to the other foreground color, making the hidden bar visible there.

Key insight:
- The crossing is exactly the intersection of all-foreground rows and all-foreground columns; its current color identifies the bar on top, so the output flips it to the other bar color.

annotation.src: two perpendicular full-span foreground bars on the dominant background
annotation.transform: recolor the rectangular crossing of the all-foreground rows and all-foreground columns to the other foreground color; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Recolor the interior of each solid grey rectangle red while leaving its border unchanged.

Input structure
- The grid has black background and one or more 4-connected grey foreground objects.
- Each grey object is a filled axis-aligned rectangle with height and width at least 3.

Rule
- Preserve the black background and the one-cell grey border of every rectangle.
- Recolor every grey cell strictly inside a rectangle's border to red.

Key insight
- The selected cells are not based on absolute position; they are exactly the non-border cells of each filled rectangle.

annotation.src: solid 4-connected grey rectangular objects on a black background
annotation.transform: recolor each rectangle's non-border interior pixels to red; preserve the grey one-cell border and black background

references.docstring:
Build successive rows by extending a left-to-right color run one cell at a time.

Input structure:
- The input is a single row with one non-black color run and black remainder.
- The row length is even.
- The run starts at the left and grows rightward.

Rule:
- Copy the input row as the first output row.
- For each following row up to half the row length, add one colored cell to the right if possible.
- Stack the generated rows into the output grid.

Key insight:
- Each row represents the previous count incremented by one, capped by the row width.

Copy the four corner patterns into a minimal square output frame.

Input structure:
- Same-color patterns occupy square regions in the four input corners.
- Black cells separate the corner regions.
- At least one foreground pixel is present.

Rule:
- Assign foreground pixels to their nearest input corner.
- Infer the largest needed corner square side length.
- Copy each corner square into the corresponding corner of an output one cell larger.

Key insight:
- The task preserves each pattern's corner-relative offsets while shrinking the canvas.

Repeat the top-row color sequence as full rows below the gray separator.

Input structure:
- The top row contains the color sequence.
- A full gray row separates the sequence from the fill area.
- Rows below the separator are the target area.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Locate the first full gray row.
- Fill every row below it with the top-row colors cycling from left to right.

Key insight:
- The gray row marks where expansion starts; the top row is the repeating row-color schedule.

Recolor the concentric rectangular rings by cycling the outside-to-inside color order one step outward.

Input structure:
- The whole grid is partitioned into one-cell-thick concentric rectangular rings.
- Each ring is monochromatic.
- Reading rings from outside to inside gives at least two distinct colors; a color may reappear on a later ring.

Rule:
- Record the distinct colors in their first outside-to-inside ring order.
- Replace every pixel of each recorded color with the previous color in that cyclic order.

Key insight:
- The transformation is a color-cycle over nesting order, not over numeric color ids or ring sizes.

annotation.src: concentric monochrome rectangular rings, read from outside inward
annotation.transform: record distinct ring colors in first outside-in order; cyclically recolor every pixel of each color to the previous color in that order

references.docstring:
Extend the two perpendicular colored bars across the grid and mark their crossing.

Input structure
- A single background color fills the canvas.

- The short segments define the row and column of the completed cross; the only new color marks their intersection.

Key insight:
- The desired crop is identified by connected foreground area, while the smaller objects are distractors.

references.docstring:
Stack all colored horizontal segments by increasing length, right-aligned above the solid bottom stripe.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, one full-width non-background stripe on

above it. Each non-stripe object is a one-cell-thick horizontal segment.

Rule
Clear the segment objects from their original positions. Sort the segments
by length from shortest to longest, then place them in consecutive rows
immediately above the bottom stripe, with each segment right-aligned to the

Key insight
The scattered segments are not moved by their original row or color; their
lengths define a stack order against the fixed bottom stripe.

references.docstring:
Fill each enclosed square hole in the gray outlines with the color assigned to that hole size.

Input structure
- The grid is a black canvas containing gray outline objects.
- Each relevant interior is a 4-connected black component fully enclosed by gray pixels.
- Enclosed interiors are solid squares of side length 1, 2, or 3.

Rule
- Keep the gray outlines and the exterior black background unchanged.
- Fill a 1x1 enclosed square with pink, a 2x2 enclosed square with orange, and a 3x3 enclosed square with teal.

Key insight
- The fill color is determined by the size of the enclosed background region, not by the outline's position or full shape.

references.docstring:
Paint every completely blank row and column red while preserving the foreground pattern.

Input structure
- The grid contains one background color and one foreground color.
- The background color is the only color that forms at least one full row or full column.
- Red is absent from the input and is reserved for the output guide lines.

Rule
- Find all rows and columns made entirely of the background color.
- Recolor every cell in those full blank rows and columns red.
- Leave all other cells unchanged.

Key insight
- The blank rows and columns are missing guide lines; because they contain no foreground pixels, they can be detected directly as full same-color lines.

annotation.src: background rows and columns that are completely empty in a one-color foreground grid
annotation.transform: recolor every complete background row and column red; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Stamp the whole input pattern into output block slots marked by its unique most frequent color.

Input structure
- The input is a 3x3 grid of non-black colors.
- Exactly one color appears more often than every other color.

Rule
- Treat the input as both a source sprite and a 3x3 placement mask.
- Create a 9x9 black output divided into 3x3 block slots.
- For each input cell whose color is the unique most frequent color, copy
  the entire input grid into the corresponding output block slot.

Key insight
- The dominant color does not get expanded by itself; its positions select
  where full copies of the original 3x3 pattern are stamped.

references.docstring:
Fill black holes by restoring the diagonal cyclic color pattern they interrupt.

Input structure
- The grid is a rectangular cyclic pattern of non-black colors with some
  black pixels removed.
- All non-black colors in the cycle remain visible somewhere in the input.
- Each diagonal residue modulo the number of non-black colors has one color.

Rule
- Infer the diagonal direction and residue-to-color cycle from the visible
  non-black pixels.
- Replace every black pixel with the color assigned to its diagonal residue.
- Preserve every non-black pixel.

Key insight
- The blanks are not objects; they are missing cells in a global repeating
  diagonal tile, so their colors are determined by row + column modulo the
  cycle length.

annotation.src: visible non-black cells of a diagonal cyclic color tile with black holes
annotation.transform: infer each color from its diagonal residue modulo the non-black palette size, then fill every black pixel with the missing tile color

references.docstring:
Repeat the populated tile pattern into every cell of a separator grid.

- The canvas has one background color and a single non-background separator color.
- Solid separator rows and/or columns divide the canvas into equal-sized rectangular cells.

Rule
- Find the separator color from the solid full-width rows or full-height columns.
- Use the separator lines to split the canvas into cells.
- Copy the unique populated cell pattern into every cell, preserving the separator lines.

Key insight
The separators define a coarse tiled board; the visible foreground pattern is the missing tile to repeat everywhere.

references.docstring:
Expand the whole grid by replacing each input pixel with a same-color 2x2 block.

Input structure
A two-dimensional color grid; every pixel is part of the source pattern.

Rule
Double the grid height and width by copying each pixel to the corresponding
2x2 block in the output.

Key insight
The transformation preserves all colors and positions at pixel level, applying
only a uniform scale factor of two.

references.docstring:
Recenter each four-pixel color mask in a shared compact canvas.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- Every non-background color appears as exactly four pixels.
- Each color's four-pixel mask has an odd-compatible row and column center
  when compared with the widest/tallest foreground mask.

Rule:
- For each non-background color, take its four pixels relative to that color's bbox.
- Make the output background-colored with size equal to the maximum foreground

- Paste every relative color mask centered in that common output canvas.

Key insight:
- The large input only separates the colored masks spatially; the desired image
  is their center-aligned overlay after removing the surrounding background.

references.docstring:
Recolor every orange pixel gray while preserving the blue and teal pixels.

Input structure:
- The grid is a non-empty 2D canvas using only blue, orange, and teal pixels.
- Orange is present and gray is absent from the input.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Replace every orange pixel with gray.
- Leave every blue and teal pixel unchanged.

Key insight:
- The orange mask is selected and rewritten in place; there is no movement,

references.docstring:
Crop out the unique region marked by a complete monochrome rectangular frame.

Input structure
The input is a larger patterned grid containing exactly one color whose pixels
form the full perimeter of a rectangle and appear nowhere else.

Rule
Find that complete rectangular frame and return the input cells inside its
bounding box, including the frame itself.

Key insight
The wanted output is not rebuilt from the repeated background pattern; it is
the exact subgrid selected by the only color that forms a complete frame.

references.docstring:
Extend the grid to the right with a left-right mirror copy of the whole input.

Input structure
- The input is a non-empty 2D grid that forms the complete left half of the output.

Rule
- Keep the original grid unchanged as the left half.
- Append the same rows in reverse column order as the right half.

Key insight
- The transformation is global horizontal reflection completion over the whole grid.

references.docstring:
Recolor every grey placeholder pixel by the control color at the left edge of its row.

Input structure
- The grid has a background color, grey placeholder pixels, and colored row control pixels.
- Each row containing grey pixels has exactly one non-background, non-grey control pixel in column 0.

Rule
- Preserve the background and all non-grey control pixels.
- For each row, replace every grey pixel by the color of that row's column-0 control pixel.

- The connected grey shapes are not filled object by object; each row is independently keyed by its left-edge marker.

references.docstring:
Continue the translational pattern across the canvas and shift its phase one column right.

Input structure:
- The background is a non-black color inferred from the border.
- Foreground pixels form a partially tiled translational pattern.
- The pattern does not cover the full canvas in the input.

Rule:
- Infer the background color from the most common border color.
- Detect translational symmetries of the foreground pattern.
- Fill a one-column-wider canvas by symmetry orbits, then drop the first column.

Key insight:
- Extending before cropping creates the rightward phase shift without wraparound artifacts.

Complete straight same-color marker segments across the tiled lattice.

Input structure
The grid is a 3x3 array of equal 2x2 tiles separated by full-width and
full-height separator lines.  Each tile is mostly the same base color, with
a few non-base marker pixels at fixed local offsets inside their tiles.

Rule
For each marker color and local tile offset, connect any pair of markers
that lie in the same tile row or same tile column by recoloring the base
cells between them to that marker color at the same local offset.

Key insight
The colored pixels are endpoints in tile coordinates, not free cells in the
raw grid; the missing pixels are found by completing axis-aligned segments
in the 3x3 tile lattice while preserving the endpoint's local position.

annotation.trajectory: recolor each base-color cell on the inclusive interval with the marker color
annotation.transform: keep separator lines, original marker pixels, and off-path base cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Replace each red pixel with a copy of the whole input pattern in the corresponding enlarged block.

Input structure
A small grid uses black as empty space, with red pixels acting as control cells inside a colored motif.

Rule
Create an output whose block grid has one block for each input pixel, where each block is the same shape as the input. For every red input pixel, fill its corresponding output block with an exact copy of the input; every non-red pixel contributes an all-black block.

Key insight
The red pixels mark the macro-locations where the entire input pattern is recursively stamped, not just where red itself should be enlarged.

annotation.transform: copy the whole input grid into each corresponding 3x3 output block whose source pixel is red; leave all other blocks black

references.docstring:
Pack scattered colored singleton pixels into a 3x3 snake summary ordered by input column.

Input structure
A grid has a dominant background color and up to nine non-background
singleton pixels. The foreground markers occupy distinct columns.

Rule
Sort the foreground pixels from left to right by their input column. Write
them into a 3x3 background canvas in groups of three, reversing every odd
output row: row 0 left-to-right, row 1 right-to-left, row 2 left-to-right.

Key insight
The output is not a spatial crop; it is the column order of the scattered
markers folded into a boustrophedon 3x3 reading pattern.

annotation.dst: 3x3 output cells d ordered in snake order: row 0 left-to-right, row 1 right-to-left, row 2 left-to-right

annotation.grid_shape: fixed 3x3 output

references.docstring:
Replace each grey center marker with a solid blue 3x3 block on the 3x3 macro-grid.

Input structure
- The grid is a black-background canvas whose dimensions are multiples of 3.
- Foreground pixels are grey markers, each centered inside a 3x3 macro block.

Rule
- Start with a blank output of the same shape.
- For every grey marker, fill its containing 3x3 macro block with blue.

Key insight
- The grey pixels are control markers for block activation; they are not preserved as output objects.

annotation.transform: replace each marked macro block with a solid blue 3x3 block; leave unmarked macro blocks black

references.docstring:
Collapse two separator-stacked masks into a green mask of their foreground union.

Input structure
- A single full-width separator row has a color that appears only in that row.
- The separator splits the grid into equal-height upper and lower masks.
- The two masks share exactly one color, the background, and each has one non-background foreground color.
Rule
- Remove the separator row and align the upper and lower masks cell by cell.
- Paint green where either of the two aligned cells is foreground.
- Paint the shared background color where both aligned cells are background.
Key insight
- The output is the union of the two aligned foreground masks.

references.docstring:
Return the smaller object from the pair that has the same shape at different scales.

Input structure:
- The grid has a most-common background color.
- Three colored objects are present, one of them a distractor.
- Two objects share shape but differ in color and scale, and the larger may be clipped.

Rule:
- Split candidate objects by color against the background.
- Compare object masks after scaling smaller candidates by factors of 2 or 3.
- Crop and return the unique smaller object that matches a larger scaled object.

Key insight:
- Shape matching ignores color and allows the scaled larger object to be partially outside the canvas.

Split each vertical red bar by recoloring its lower half teal.

Input structure:
- The background is black.
- The only foreground color is red, arranged as one or more contiguous vertical bars.
- Empty columns contain only background pixels.

Rule:
- For each red vertical bar, leave the upper ceil(height/2) cells red.
- Recolor the lower floor(height/2) cells of that same bar to teal.
- Preserve all background cells.

Key insight:
- Each occupied column is an independent height marker; the transformation is a
  per-bar bottom-half recolor, not a global shape or path operation.

annotation.src: contiguous vertical red bars on a black background
annotation.transform: within each bar, preserve the upper ceil(height/2) red pixels and recolor the lower floor(height/2) pixels to teal

references.docstring:
Composite the three separated color layers from back to front.

Input structure:
- Three pattern panels are separated by red vertical bars.
- The left panel is yellow, the middle panel is maroon, and the right panel is blue.
- Black cells are transparent within each panel.

Rule:
- Split the input at the red divider columns.
- Use the right blue panel as the base output.
- Overlay non-black maroon cells, then non-black yellow cells.

Key insight:
- Panel order encodes occlusion: blue is back, maroon is middle, and yellow is front.

Extend every foreground pixel straight downward, filling its column to the bottom with that pixel's color.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Each non-background pixel is a source in a distinct column.
- Cells below each source in the same column are background.

Rule
- Copy the input grid.
- For each foreground source at (r, c), color every cell from row r through
  the bottom of column c with the source color.
- Preserve all cells outside those downward vertical rays.

Key insight
- Each colored pixel defines both the color and the column of a vertical
  downward fill.

annotation.src: each non-background source pixel s
annotation.path: straight downward in s.column through background cells to the bottom edge
annotation.trajectory: paint every cell on the downward vertical ray with s.color
annotation.transform: preserve all cells outside the painted rays

references.docstring:
Draw mirrored gray staircases of step length two from the teal anchor pixel.

Input structure:
- The grid is black except for one teal pixel.
- The teal pixel is away from the border.
- The output keeps the input dimensions.

Rule:
- From the teal pixel, draw gray steps upward then rightward with length two.
- Also draw gray steps downward then leftward with length two.
- Restore the teal pixel after drawing the staircases.

Key insight:
- The single teal pixel is the shared center of two opposite staircase arms.

Activate both diagonals through each marker pixel and recolor activated base-color cells to that base color's paired marker color.

Input structure
- The canvas is filled by two large base colors.
- The other colors occur as marker pixels placed in those base-color regions.
- A marker's surrounding base-color neighborhood identifies which base color the marker color represents.

Rule
- For every marker pixel, activate the full NW-SE and NE-SW diagonals through that pixel, all the way to the grid edges.
- Starting from the original grid, every activated cell whose color is one of the two base colors changes to that base color's paired marker color.
- Original marker pixels remain unchanged, including where diagonal paths cross them.

Key insight
- The markers do not paint only their own color; they define diagonal paths, and the color written on each path cell is chosen by the cell's original base color.

annotation.src: marker pixels in the two large base-color regions; each marker color is paired with the neighboring base color it replaces
annotation.path: both full diagonals through every marker pixel, extending to the grid edges
annotation.trajectory: paint the union of those diagonal cells according to the original base color at each cell
annotation.transform: base-color cells on active diagonals become their paired marker color; marker pixels and off-path cells remain unchanged

references.docstring:
Replace the sparse scene with a square diagonal marker grid whose side length is the number of foreground objects.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color and exactly one foreground color.
- The foreground pixels form one or more separated 4-connected objects.

Rule:
- Count the 4-connected foreground objects.
- Return a square grid, filled with the background color, with side length equal to that count.
- Place the foreground color on the main diagonal from upper left to lower right.

Key insight:
- The large foreground shapes are tokens to count; their detailed shapes and positions do not affect the output beyond the object count.

references.docstring:
Extract the upper-left 2x2 seed tile from the larger patterned grid.

Input structure
- The input is a two-dimensional grid with even height and width.
- The compact seed pattern is located in the upper-left 2x2 region.

Rule
- Return the first two rows and first two columns unchanged.

Key insight
- The surrounding cells are shifted/permuted repetitions of the seed, so the
  unshifted representation is already present in the upper-left corner.

annotation.src: patterned input grid made from a 2x2 seed tile and shifted/permuted copies
annotation.transform: extract the exposed seed tile from the upper-left 2x2 region

references.docstring:
Copy the foreground pixels of the input across a doubled canvas along the down-right diagonal.

Input structure:
- The input is a nonempty 2D grid with a unique dominant background color.
- The non-background pixels form the sparse motif to be repeated.

Rule:
- Create an output canvas with twice the input height and twice the input width, filled with background.
- For each foreground pixel at input position (r, c), paint that color at every output position (r+k, c+k) while it remains in bounds.
- If two painted diagonal traces meet, they must agree in color.

Key insight:
- The input is stamped with transparent background at every one-cell down-right offset; it is not enlarged by scaling individual cells.

annotation.path: one-cell down-right diagonal offsets on a doubled canvas, stopping when the shifted sprite no longer intersects the canvas
annotation.trajectory: stamp the foreground pixels of s at every offset; clipped pixels outside the canvas are dropped
annotation.transform: fill all unstamped cells with the input background

references.docstring:
Paint alternating square rings from each colored corner marker, clipped to cells uniquely nearest to that marker.

Input structure
- The grid is background except for colored marker pixels in two or more corners.

Rule
- For every cell, compare squared Euclidean distance to each corner marker.

- A uniquely owned cell takes its marker color exactly when its Chebyshev distance

Key insight
- The output is not made from lines between corners; it is the set of even
  square-distance rings around each active corner, cut by nearest-marker
  boundaries.

- The examples preserve every value in the vertical center column and delete all off-center foreground pixels.

references.docstring:
Recolor gray objects red when their area is six and blue otherwise.

Input structure:
- The input is a 10x10 black grid containing gray objects.
- Objects are 4-connected gray components.
- Some components have area exactly six.

Rule:
- Detect all gray components on the black background.
- Recolor each component with area six red.
- Recolor every other component blue on a black output canvas.

Key insight:
- Component area alone controls the output color; each object's shape is preserved.

Add a clipped direction-colored four-neighbor cross around each blue marker pixel.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one foreground color: blue marker pixels.
- Marker pixels are isolated enough that their four-neighbor stamps do not overlap or touch another marker.

Rule
- Keep every original blue marker pixel unchanged.
- For each marker, recolor its in-bounds background neighbor above to red, left to orange, right to pink, and below to teal.
- Clip the stamp at the grid boundary.

Key insight
- The marker position is an anchor; the added color is determined solely by compass direction from that anchor.

annotation.transform: preserve each marker; paint each in-bounds background neighbor by direction: above -> red, left -> orange, right -> pink, below -> teal

references.docstring:
Recolor every second grey marker from the right edge to green.

Input structure
The grid has three rows, black background, and exactly one grey foreground
pixel in each column.

Rule
Starting with the rightmost column, recolor the grey foreground pixel in
every other column to green; leave the skipped grey pixels and background
unchanged.

Key insight
The foreground pixels form a left-to-right sequence, and the output marks
alternating sequence positions counted from the right.

annotation.src: grey marker pixels s, one per column, ordered right-to-left by column
annotation.dst: same marker locations
annotation.transform: recolor the 1st, 3rd, 5th, ... markers in that order to green; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend every colored marker that is row- or column-aligned with the 2x2 anchor square until it touches that square.

Input structure
- The background contains one non-background 2x2 square anchor.
- All other foreground objects are single colored marker pixels.
- Some marker pixels share one row or one column with the anchor square.

Rule
- Keep the anchor and all original marker pixels unchanged.
- For each marker on an anchor row, paint horizontally from the marker to the cell next to the anchor.
- For each marker on an anchor column, paint vertically from the marker to the cell next to the anchor.
- Ignore markers that are not aligned with any anchor row or column.

Key insight
- The 2x2 square supplies the only two active rows and two active columns; aligned singleton markers emit straight segments into the nearest side of the square.

annotation.src: single colored marker pixels that share a row or column with the 2x2 foreground anchor square
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical segment from each aligned marker along the shared row/column to the cell adjacent to the anchor
annotation.dst: nearest side of the 2x2 anchor square
annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel on the segment with the marker color
annotation.transform: keep the anchor square and all original marker pixels unchanged; ignore unaligned markers

references.docstring:
Replace the noisy 5x5 single-color mask with the fixed 3x3 grey symbol encoded by its foreground color.

Input structure:
- The input is a 5x5 grid with black background.
- All foreground pixels share one visible color: red, blue, or green.
- The exact foreground pixel positions vary within each color class.

Rule:
- Red emits a grey top-T symbol.
- Blue emits a grey plus symbol.
- Green emits a grey lower-right L symbol.
- The output background is black and the symbol pixels are grey.

Key insight:
- The foreground shape is distractor noise; the single foreground color is the code for the 3x3 output symbol.

annotation.src: 5x5 black-background mask with exactly one foreground color
annotation.transform: ignore foreground positions and replace the grid with the grey symbol encoded by that color: red -> top-T, blue -> plus, green -> lower-right L

references.docstring:
Connect a red pixel to a teal pixel with a yellow right-angle path.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with exactly one red pixel and one teal pixel.
- The red and teal pixels are not in the same row or column.
- The output keeps the original endpoint pixels.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Draw yellow horizontally from the red pixel's row to the teal pixel's column.
- Draw yellow vertically along the teal pixel's column until reaching the teal pixel.

Key insight:
- The teal pixel supplies the destination column first, so the path is an L shape
  with its corner aligned to the red row and teal column.

Fill the inside of a cup and extend teal outward through its opening.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one non-black cup-shaped object on a black background.
- The cup is an almost closed rectangular outline with one boundary opening.
- Black cells inside the cup and at the opening define the fill and exit path.

Rule:
- Find the cup's bounding box and mark the black cells inside it.
- Fill those interior cells with teal.
- Detect the opening side and draw teal straight outward from every opening cell.

Key insight:
- The only boundary gap identifies both the cup interior and the direction for the
  emitted teal line.

Swap every teal pixel with gray and every gray pixel with teal.

Input structure:
- The input is an arbitrary square grid of non-black colors.
- Teal and gray may appear anywhere in the grid.
- Other colors are not part of the swap.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Recolor original gray cells to teal.
- Recolor original teal cells to gray while leaving all other cells unchanged.

Key insight:
- The transformation is a pure color substitution, so positions and all non-target
  colors are preserved exactly.

Expand a vertical colored line into a centered alternating-color pyramid.

- Identify the line color, center column, and lowest occupied row.
- Build a black output grid of the same size.

- The original line is the pyramid axis; moving upward shortens the run, while

- Detect each square object and clear the output background to black.
- Fill blue below each square's original footprint down to the grid bottom.
- Draw a green frame twice the square size around it, then paste the original square back.

Key insight:
- Each square contributes two independent structures: a vertical blue projection from

Connect every horizontally or vertically aligned pair of blue marker pixels with teal segments.

Rule

- In each row, sort the blue marker columns and paint teal on the background cells strictly between adjacent markers.
- In each column, sort the blue marker rows and paint teal on the background cells strictly between adjacent markers.

- The task asks for only the occluded square, not the full repaired scene; every unoccluded mirror counterpart yields the same patch.

Recolor each grey object by the colored top-row marker whose column passes through it.

- Each grey rectangle has exactly one control-pixel column inside its horizontal span.

- Keep the background and top-row control pixels unchanged.

- The markers act as vertical labels for grey regions: horizontal-span

references.docstring:
Return the color of the rectangular region that contains the most rare marker pixels.

Rule:
- Find the unique least frequent color; these cells are the markers.
- Count how many marker pixels belong to each surrounding region color.

- The markers are not output directly; they vote for the region they sit inside,

Complete straight horizontal and vertical connectors between same-color marker pixels that already share a row or column.

- For every row containing at least two original foreground pixels, color the full span from the leftmost to rightmost such pixel.
- For every column containing at least two original foreground pixels, color the full span from the topmost to bottommost such pixel.

Key insight
- The markers define all orthogonal line segments by row/column alignment; spans are computed from the input markers, not from newly drawn pixels.

references.docstring:
Trace a bouncing blue diagonal path upward and recolor the black background teal.

Input structure:
- The grid has a black background with exactly one blue pixel.
- The blue pixel is the start of an upward-right diagonal ray.
- The left and right grid edges act as reflection walls.

Rule:
- Starting from the blue pixel, draw blue one step up and horizontally each move.
- Reverse horizontal direction when the next step would leave the grid.
- Stop when the path exits through the top, then change remaining black cells to teal.

Key insight:
- The path behaves like a diagonal ray reflecting only off vertical walls before the
  final background recoloring.

Extend a multicolor cross across the canvas by repeating its color sequences.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one connected multicolor cross on a black background.
- One full row and one full column of the cropped sprite meet at the cross center.
- The row and column colors form the sequences to repeat.

Rule:
- Crop the cross and locate the row and column that pass through its center.
- Copy the input grid as the output canvas.
- Paste the center column and center row sequences repeatedly in both directions.

Key insight:
- The cross is a seed for periodic extension: its central row and column are reused
  at intervals equal to their own lengths.

Restore a noisy striped grid by repainting each stripe line with its dominant color.

Input structure:
- The grid is a full canvas of either horizontal row stripes or vertical column stripes.
- Sparse noise pixels may use stripe colors or extra colors, but each true stripe line
  still has a unique dominant color.

Rule:
- Score the horizontal-stripe interpretation by summing the dominant-color counts of
  every row, and score the vertical-stripe interpretation the same way over columns.
- Choose the uniquely better orientation.
- Repaint each row or column in that orientation entirely with its unique dominant color.

Key insight:
- The correct stripe direction is the one whose lines are much closer to monochrome;
  the output is the clean striped canvas hidden under the noise.

references.docstring:
Fold the grid across its solid vertical separator, overlaying the reflected right side onto the left side.

Input structure
A non-background vertical separator column spans the full grid height. It

background. Reflected foreground overlaps, when present, have the same color.

Rule
Remove the separator column, mirror the right region horizontally, and
overlay it onto the left region. For each output pixel, keep the foreground
color from whichever folded side is non-background; if both sides are
foreground, their colors must agree.

Key insight
The two sides are complementary halves around the separator, and the output
is the separator-free left-side coordinate system after folding the right
side inward.

references.docstring:
Complete the foreground pattern by rotating it into a square with four-way rotational symmetry.

- The grid has a dominant background and a partial foreground pattern inside one hidden square region.
- The intended square is the unique smallest square containing all foreground pixels whose 90-degree rotation closure has no color conflict.

Rule
- Keep the grid shape and background.
- For each foreground pixel in the inferred square, paint its positions under 0, 90, 180, and 270 degree rotations about the square center.

Key insight
The missing cells are not mirrored; they are exactly the orbit needed to complete quarter-turn rotational symmetry.

references.docstring:
Move a colored cross left and downward by the gray counter value.

Input structure:
- The input is a 10x10 black grid with one solid colored row and one solid colored column.
- The row and column share the same non-black, non-gray color.
- The top of the rightmost column contains gray pixels that encode the shift amount.

Rule:
- Count gray pixels in the rightmost column.
- Find the colored cross row, column, and color.
- Recreate the cross on black after moving the row down and the column left by that count.

Key insight:
- The gray pixels are a numeric instruction only; they disappear after determining
  how far to shift the cross.

Stamp the red sprite into every matching empty slot in the gray-and-black pattern.

Input structure
- The grid uses black empty cells, gray support cells, and one red marker sprite.
- The red sprite bbox defines the stamp mask.
- Gray cells inside the sprite bbox define the support signature; if an enclosed interior gray support exists, it is the anchor signature.

Rule
- Scan candidate bbox positions from top-left to bottom-right.
- A candidate matches when every red-mask position is still black and every support-signature position is gray.
- If the sprite bbox has no gray support cells, only border-touching black slots of the same shape match.
- Paint each matched red-mask position red, preserving all other cells.

Key insight
The red cells are a stamp; gray support inside the stamp window, or the grid border for unsupported solid stamps, identifies the blank copies to complete.

- Object color is determined by topology of the mask, not by position or size.

references.docstring:
Repeat a black template object outward in the color and direction of its touching indicator.

Draw black diagonals from the single black pixel across a non-black background.
