Extend a solid rectangle's color along outward diagonals after they pass through frame corners.
Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, one solid rectangular foreground object, and one one-cell-thick orthogonal frame object in a different color.
Rule
From each outer corner of the solid rectangle, trace the outward diagonal; if the first non-background pixel on that ray is a corner of the frame, continue past that frame pixel and paint every remaining background pixel on the same diagonal with the rectangle color.
Key insight
The frame corner selects which rectangle-corner diagonals are active, and the interior/background part of the ray before the frame is left unchanged.

annotation.src: solid rectangular foreground object s
annotation.path: from each outer corner of s, follow the outward diagonal until the first non-background pixel; the ray is active only if that pixel is an orthogonal corner of the other-color frame, then continues on the same diagonal to the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint only the background pixels beyond the frame corner with s.color
annotation.transform: keep s, the frame, and the interior/background pixels before the frame unchanged

references.docstring:
Extend each control pixel perpendicular to the full bars, marking every bar hit with a 3x3 contact marker.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Exactly one foreground color forms one or more complete parallel rows or complete parallel columns.
- The other foreground color appears as isolated control pixels off those bars.

Rule
- For each control pixel, cast rays in both directions perpendicular to the bars.
- Stop each ray at the first bar cell it reaches and color the control-to-hit segment with the control color.
- After all rays are drawn, stamp a 3x3 block of the bar color centered on each hit, restoring the center to the control color.
- Directions with no bar before the grid edge emit nothing.

Key insight
- The only complete rows or columns identify the bars and their orientation; the contact markers are layered after the rays.

annotation.src: isolated control pixels not on the full bar rows/columns
annotation.path: straight ray in both directions perpendicular to the parallel full bars, stopping at the first bar cell reached in each direction; no ray where no bar is reached
annotation.trajectory: paint the control-to-hit segment with the control color
annotation.transform: after all rays, stamp a 3x3 block of the bar color centered on every hit and restore each center cell to the control color; keep other cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Rotate the entire square grid 90 degrees counterclockwise.

Input structure
The input is a square 2D grid whose cells form a small black-and-one-color
pattern.

Rule
Preserve every cell color and move each cell to its position under a 90-degree
counterclockwise rotation of the whole grid.

Key insight
The foreground shape is not rewritten internally; the complete canvas, including
black cells, is rotated as one pattern.

annotation.src: entire square input grid
annotation.transform: rotate the whole grid 90 degrees counterclockwise, preserving every cell color

references.docstring:
Fill unobstructed horizontal gaps between neighboring foreground objects with maroon.

Input structure
- The grid has one connected background color and one foreground color split into several 4-connected solid rectangles.
- Foreground rectangles can be horizontally separated while overlapping in their row spans.
Rule
- For every pair of foreground rectangles with separated column spans and overlapping row spans, consider the rectangle between their bounding boxes.
- Paint that between-box region maroon when no third foreground rectangle has a bounding box crossing both that horizontal gap and the same shared row span.
- Keep all original pixels unchanged.
Key insight
- The bridges are determined by adjacency of object bounding boxes in horizontal layers, not by scanning each row independently.

annotation.src: black gap regions between horizontally separated 4-connected red rectangular objects
annotation.transform: recolor a gap to maroon across the shared row span of its two red rectangles when no third red bbox crosses both that gap and shared span; preserve all red pixels and other black pixels

references.docstring:
Flow teal pixels across the grid while red edge pixels push the paths aside.

Input structure:
- The black grid has teal pixels on one edge and red pixels on a perpendicular edge.
- Teal starts flow toward the opposite edge.
- Red edge pixels create row or column push effects.

Rule:
- Determine the teal flow direction and red push direction from the occupied edges.
- Start a path from each teal pixel.
- Move along the flow direction, but shift one cell away whenever aligned with any red pixel.

Key insight:
- Red pixels act like directional repellers: they do not move, but their rows or
  columns offset the teal streams.

Extend the inner-color leaf markers into full row and column cuts through the foreground rectangle.

Input structure
- A black background contains one solid rectangular foreground region.
- The rectangle uses exactly two colors: an outer color at all four corners and an inner color mass.
- Single-cell leaf protrusions of the inner color stick into the outer-color margin.

Rule
- A leaf whose only inner-color neighbor is above or below selects its column; a leaf whose neighbor is left or right selects its row.
- Selected rows and columns are recolored to the outer color inside the foreground rectangle.
- The same selected rows and columns are extended through the background outside the rectangle using the inner color.

Key insight
- The protruding leaf pixels are not noise: each is a control marker naming one row or column to cut through the rectangle and continue outward.

annotation.src: single-cell inner-color leaf markers attached to the inner color mass inside the foreground rectangle
annotation.path: a leaf attached vertically selects its column; a leaf attached horizontally selects its row; extend that axis from the rectangle to the canvas edge
annotation.trajectory: paint background cells outside the rectangle on the selected row or column with the inner color
annotation.transform: inside the rectangle, recolor the full selected row or column to the outer corner color

references.docstring:
Crop the foreground shape to its tight bounding box and magnify that crop by a factor of two.

Input structure
A 2D grid with a dominant background color and exactly one non-background color forming a sparse shape.

Rule
Find the tight bounding box of all non-background pixels, crop that rectangular region, and replace each cropped pixel with a 2x2 block of the same color.

Key insight
The output is the entire foreground bounding-box region enlarged, so background gaps inside the shape are scaled along with the colored pixels.

annotation.src: unique non-background foreground mask on a dominant background
annotation.transform: crop to the foreground bbox, then replace each retained pixel by a 2x2 same-color block
annotation.grid_shape: foreground bbox height and width multiplied by 2

references.docstring:
Fill the empty upper half with a vertical mirror of the lower-half pattern.

Input structure
The grid has even height. The upper half is entirely background, and the
lower half contains the foreground pattern to be completed.

Rule
Copy the lower half into the upper half after reversing its row order.
Leave the original lower half unchanged.

Key insight
The blank upper region is the missing reflected counterpart of the visible
lower region.

annotation.src: lower-half foreground pattern below an empty upper half
annotation.dst: empty upper-half region
annotation.transform: fill the upper half with the lower half mirrored vertically; preserve the lower half

references.docstring:
Paint green in each output cell where both side panels are background.

Input structure:
- The grid has a centered solid non-background separator column.
- The separator splits the grid into equal-size left and right panels.
- Each panel is a same-size mask using the shared background and one foreground color.

Rule:
- Remove the separator column.
- Compare the two side panels cell by cell.
- Output background where either panel has foreground, and green where both panels have background.

Key insight:
- The output is the intersection of the two panels' empty space, not a copy of either colored mask.

annotation.src: two equal-size side-panel masks separated by a solid centered vertical bar
annotation.transform: for each corresponding cell, output green iff both side-panel cells are background; otherwise output background
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one side panel

references.docstring:
Expand four diagonal color markers into corner glyphs and add dashed grey sides between them.

Input structure
- The input is a background grid with exactly four foreground pixels.
- The foreground has two colors, each appearing twice, on opposite corners of one
  axis-aligned rectangle.

Rule
- Each marker becomes a centered 3x3 glyph: the center keeps its input color and
  the eight surrounding cells use the other marker color.
- In the open gap between adjacent glyphs on each rectangle side, paint grey dashes.
  A gap cell is grey when its nearest side-end distance is even.

Key insight
- The four pixels are rectangle corners; their diagonal color pairing defines the
  corner glyphs, and the sides are dashed symmetrically inward from both ends.

annotation.src: four colored marker pixels at the corners of an axis-aligned rectangle, with two colors paired on opposite corners
annotation.path: from each corner marker, follow the rectangle side gap toward adjacent corner markers on the same row or column, excluding the cells occupied by the 3x3 corner glyphs
annotation.trajectory: paint grey dashes on side-gap cells whose nearest side-end distance is even
annotation.transform: replace each marker with a centered 3x3 glyph whose center keeps the marker color and whose border uses the other marker color; keep background elsewhere

references.docstring:
Mark background cells in foreground-bearing columns with teal, then repeat the marked grid as a 2x2 tile.

Input structure
- The input is a nonempty 2D grid with one dominant background color.
- Exactly one non-background foreground color appears, and it is not teal.

Rule
- Preserve every original foreground pixel.
- In any column containing at least one foreground pixel, recolor background
  cells to teal.
- Repeat the resulting grid twice vertically and twice horizontally.

Key insight
- The foreground pixels select whole columns of the tile; the output is a
  repeated copy of that completed tile, not a nearest-neighbor scale-up.

annotation.src: entire input grid, with foreground pixels selecting their columns
annotation.dst: 2x2 grid of input-size tile slots
annotation.transform: complete the tile by recoloring background pixels in foreground-bearing columns to teal, then copy that tile into all four slots
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 2

tags: condition:含前景列整列涂色, fg_col_full_recolor

references.docstring:
Use the grey pixels as a mask for the only other input color and turn everything else black.

Input structure
- The grid contains exactly two colors.
- Grey marks the pixels that survive into the output.
- The other input color is the paint color and is not black.

Rule
- Create a black output grid with the same shape as the input.
- Recolor every grey input pixel to the unique non-grey input color.
- Recolor every non-grey input pixel to black.

Key insight
- Grey is not a background here; it is the mask showing where the colored
  shape should appear after the original colored cells are removed.

annotation.src: two-color grid where grey pixels form a mask and the other non-black color is the paint color
annotation.transform: recolor grey mask pixels to the paint color; recolor all original paint-color pixels to black

references.docstring:
Mirror the inner pattern pieces outward across the two red frame halves.

Input structure:
- The grid contains two red frame halves enclosing gray pattern pieces.
- The frame pair may be horizontal or vertical after rotation.
- The inner pattern lies between the red frame halves.

Rule:
- Detect the red frame components and paste them into a blank output.
- Crop the full inner pattern and split it into two halves along the frame axis.
- Mirror each half across its corresponding frame line and paste it outside the frame.

Key insight:
- The red frame halves are symmetry axes; the enclosed gray pattern is split and
  reflected outward rather than copied in place.

Output a vertical list of rectangle colors ordered by frequency after skipping the most common.

Input structure:
- The grid contains separated monochromatic rectangle objects on a black background.
- Rectangles are arranged in an array and colored from several non-black colors.
- Color frequency is measured by object count, not pixel count.

Rule:
- Detect each rectangle object and record its non-black color.
- Sort colors by how many rectangles have that color.
- Drop the most frequent color and write the remaining colors top to bottom in a one-column grid.

Key insight:
- The output is a rank summary of object colors, so rectangle positions and dimensions
  are discarded after counting.

Complete the arithmetic sequence of rectangular side-strokes and turn all remaining background grey.

Input structure
A zero-background 2D grid contains one non-background color. Its 4-connected
objects are clipped rectangular side-strokes: each object occupies the same
set of bbox sides, such as top+right, left+bottom, or a three-sided U.

Rule
Sort the observed stroke bboxes by increasing bbox area. Consecutive bboxes
differ by a constant coordinate delta, so extend that bbox sequence in both
directions until the corresponding clipped side-stroke has no visible pixels.
Paint every visible side-stroke with the input foreground color and paint
all other cells grey.

Key insight
The missing output pixels are not filled from local adjacency; the visible
objects are consecutive members of one larger arithmetic family of rectangular
side-strokes, with larger members clipped by the canvas boundaries.

annotation.src: foreground 4-connected rectangular side-strokes with the same bbox-side pattern
annotation.dst: missing members of the same arithmetic bbox sequence
annotation.transform: sort stroke bboxes by size, extend the constant bbox delta in both directions, clip each generated side-stroke to the grid, paint those pixels with the foreground color, and paint all other cells grey

references.docstring:
Return the three foreground colors as a vertical list ordered by decreasing pixel count.

Input structure
A dominant background contains exactly three foreground color masks.

Rule
Count the pixels of each foreground color, sort the colors from largest mask
to smallest mask, and emit those colors as a 3x1 column.

Key insight
The input positions and mask shapes are distractors; the output is the size
ranking of the color masks.

annotation.src: foreground color masks s ordered by descending pixel count
annotation.dst: rows d of the 3x1 output column from top to bottom
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: emit each mask color as one pixel in its assigned row
annotation.grid_shape: 3x1 column

references.docstring:
Recover the black occluded rectangle from a translationally symmetric pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a repeated color pattern with no true background color.
- A black rectangle masks part of the pattern.
- Non-black cells elsewhere reveal the translational symmetry.

Rule:
- Treat black cells as the occlusion mask.
- Detect translational symmetries while ignoring black.
- Fill each black cell from a non-black cell in its symmetry orbit, then crop the filled rectangle.

Key insight:
- Symmetry orbits provide equivalent unoccluded samples for each missing cell, and
  the answer is only the reconstructed occluded region.

Compress two stacked masks into one mask marking positions empty in both.

Input structure:
- The grid is two same-size square masks stacked vertically.
- Each half contains the same background color plus one distinct foreground color.
- Red is absent from the input and is used as the output marker color.

Rule:
- Compare the two halves cell by cell.
- Output red where both cells are the shared background color.
- Output the shared background color everywhere else.

Key insight:
- The output is the intersection of the background masks, not a transformation
  of either colored foreground object alone.

annotation.src: two same-size square masks stacked vertically, each with one foreground color and the same background color
annotation.transform: for each cell position, write red when both corresponding input cells are background; otherwise write background
annotation.grid_shape: same size as one input half

references.docstring:
Extract the largest rectangular foreground frame and recolor its cropped contents to the marker color.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- There are exactly two foreground colors: one forms complete rectangular
  one-pixel-thick frames, and the other appears as marker pixels/noise.
- The intended frame is the unique largest rectangular frame by bounding-box area.

Rule
- Find the foreground color that forms rectangular frames.
- Crop the bounding box of the unique largest frame of that color.
- In the crop, replace every non-background pixel with the other foreground color.

Key insight
- The marker color supplies the output color; only the largest frame's bbox
  decides which marker pixels are kept and which outside pixels are discarded.

annotation.src: largest complete rectangular frame, including marker-color pixels inside its bounding box
annotation.transform: crop to that frame bbox and recolor every non-background pixel in the crop to the marker color
annotation.grid_shape: bounding box of the largest rectangular frame

references.docstring:
Draw a green marker rectangle below each 2x2 square sized by its color count.

Input structure:
- The input is a 10x10 black grid with separated 2x2 colored squares.
- Each square may contain one to four non-black colors.
- The generated placement leaves room around squares for added markers.

Rule:
- Detect each multicolor square object.
- Count the distinct non-black colors inside it.
- Paste a green rectangle directly below the square with height equal to that count and matching square width.

Key insight:
- The added green shape encodes diversity inside each square: more distinct colors
  produce a taller marker.

Sweep a colored input line diagonally upward-right to form a large square pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a one-cell-wide line containing black and colored pixels.
- Non-black colors appear in the line and determine the output scale.
- The output is a black square canvas.

Rule:
- Set the square size to input line length times the number of distinct non-black colors.
- Place the original line at the bottom-left of the output.
- Repeatedly paste the same line one row up and one column right with clipping.

Key insight:
- Diagonal rays are produced by translating the whole sparse line, so every colored
  input pixel leaves a parallel diagonal trace.

Count red 2x2 squares and mark that count in a fixed blue 3x3 pattern.

Input structure:
- The input is a square black grid containing separated 2x2 red squares.
- Up to five red squares may be present.
- The output is always a 3x3 black grid.

Rule:
- Detect all connected red square objects.
- Count how many red squares are present.
- Fill that many positions in the fixed blue order: corners by alternating columns with the center between them.

Key insight:
- The output ignores the locations of the red squares and encodes only their count
  along a predetermined sparse 3x3 sequence.

Recover the hidden 5x5 patch by rotating the scene 180 degrees and cropping the blue-mask location.

Input structure
A scene contains exactly one solid 5x5 blue mask over a larger rotationally symmetric pattern.

Rule
Locate the blue mask, rotate the whole input grid 180 degrees, and return the 5x5 patch at the mask's original bbox.

Key insight
The blue block is an occluder; the hidden pixels are supplied by the opposite 180-degree-corresponding part of the same pattern.

annotation.src: visible 180-degree rotationally symmetric pattern outside the solid 5x5 blue mask
annotation.dst: region covered by the blue mask
annotation.transform: rotate the whole input grid 180 degrees and output the crop at the blue mask bbox
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as the blue mask

references.docstring:
Complete a sparse grid by casting occluding diagonal rays from the longest run and filling the remaining diagonal-connected regions from the short bars.

Input structure
- Black-background grid with one unique longest 4-connected foreground object.
- The longest object is a horizontal or vertical multicolor run; all other foreground objects are shorter monochrome bars.

Rule
- On a blank canvas, process the longest run from left to right or top to bottom; each pixel emits four 45-degree rays that stop at the first already-painted pixel.
- Each remaining monochrome bar fills every still-blank pixel reachable from it by diagonal steps.

Key insight
- Earlier pixels in the long run occlude later diagonal rays, and those ray barriers partition the background into diagonal-connected regions for the short bars.

annotation.src: unique longest multicolor run; shorter monochrome bars
annotation.path: long-run pixels cast four diagonal rays in left/top order, stopping at earlier painted rays; short bars flood through still-bg cells by diagonal adjacency
annotation.trajectory: paint each visited pixel with the source pixel or bar color
annotation.transform: preserve input foreground and fill only the diagonal ray paths and diagonal-connected regions
annotation.multi_step: draw occluding rays from the longest run first, then fill each short bar's remaining diagonal-connected region

tags: condition:处理顺序决定遮挡, order_determines_block

references.docstring:
Slide the non-square sprite to the square anchor and replace the anchor with the sprite's mirror image.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- There is one 8-connected non-background sprite that is not a solid 2x2 square.
- There is one solid 2x2 square anchor in another non-background color.

Rule:
- Move the sprite straight toward the anchor along their unique cardinal separation until it touches the anchor's near edge.
- Reflect the moved sprite across that near edge and draw the reflected copy in the anchor color.
- Clear the original locations; the output keeps only the moved sprite and reflected anchor-color copy.

Key insight:
- The 2x2 square marks the mirror line: its side facing the sprite becomes the contact edge for a two-color reflected pair.

annotation.src: 8-connected non-square foreground sprite s
annotation.dst: solid 2x2 square anchor d
annotation.match_cond: s faces d by cardinal separation with overlapping span
annotation.transform: translate s to touch d's facing edge, mirror s across that edge in d.color, and clear originals

references.docstring:
Extend each colored marker from its directional sprite to a grid edge, painting a dotted ray and the whole edge side.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- One repeated body color forms small 8-connected directional sprites.
- Each marker is a singleton non-background, non-body color embedded in one sprite.

Rule:
- The body pixels around a marker lie mostly behind it; the opposite direction is the marker's ray direction.
- Paint every second pixel from the marker along that ray, then paint the entire boundary side reached by the ray.
- If two painted boundary sides meet at a corner, make that shared corner black.

Key insight:
- The same seven-pixel body sprite rotates to encode the direction; its local center-of-mass bias points away from the ray.

annotation.src: singleton colored markers embedded in seven-pixel directional body-color sprites
annotation.path: cast from each marker in the direction opposite the sprite body bias to a grid boundary side
annotation.trajectory: paint every second pixel along the ray, then paint the full reached boundary side in the marker color
annotation.transform: shared corners where two painted boundary sides meet -> black; original sprites remain unchanged

references.docstring:
Paint the teal outline of the right triangle determined by the missing corner of the grey-marker square.

Input structure
The grid is an orange background with exactly four foreground marker pixels of one color. The markers have a square bounding box: three markers are bbox corners, and the fourth marker is inside that square.
Rule
Find the one corner of the marker bounding square that has no marker. That missing corner is the right-angle vertex of a right isosceles triangle; paint its two axis-aligned legs and the opposite diagonal in teal, leaving existing marker pixels unchanged.
Key insight
The present corner marker opposite the missing corner is a decoy; the three triangle vertices are the missing corner and the two marker corners adjacent to it.

annotation.src: four grey marker pixels whose bbox is a square with exactly one missing corner
annotation.transform: paint teal on the outline of the right triangle inside the square: the missing bbox corner is the right-angle vertex, the two adjacent marker corners are the other vertices; keep grey markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Mark every complete square object with red pixels just outside its corners.

Input structure:
- A uniform background contains one or more monochrome 4-connected foreground objects.
- The relevant objects are square frames or filled squares: their bbox is square
  and all cells on the bbox border have the object's color.
- Non-square bars and incomplete fragments may also appear and are ignored.

Rule:
- Keep the input unchanged.
- For each complete square object, paint red on the two outside background
  pixels orthogonally adjacent to each of the square's four corners.

Key insight: The transformation is not based on size or color; it selects
objects whose bounding box is a complete square border and labels only their
exposed outer corner-adjacent cells.

annotation.src: monochrome 4-connected foreground objects on the background; some objects have a complete square bbox border
annotation.transform: for each object whose bbox is square and whose bbox border is fully foreground, paint red on the two outside background pixels orthogonally adjacent to each of its four corners; leave bars and incomplete fragments unchanged

references.docstring:
Combine each column's repeated template mask with its single solid color swatch.

Input structure:
- The grid is a table of framed panels separated by background rows/columns.
- The leftmost column gives one solid row-label color for each panel row.
- In each panel column, exactly one panel has a solid non-background interior,
  while the other panels share the same mask drawn in one template color on
  the background.

Rule:
- For every panel column, find the row containing the solid interior swatch.
- Rebuild one output panel using that row's left label as the frame color.
- Fill the repeated template mask with the swatch color and leave the mask
  background cells as background; separate rebuilt panels with one
  background column.

Key insight:
The table encodes a colorized stencil per column: the solid panel supplies
the paint color and frame label, while the duplicate template panels supply
the shape mask.

annotation.src: input panel column s with one solid swatch and repeated template masks
annotation.dst: output panel d in the same column order
annotation.match_cond: s.column_index == d.column_index
annotation.transform: use s.swatch color as fill, s.swatch row label as frame color, and s.repeated mask as shape
annotation.grid_shape: one row of panels, same panel size as input, with one bg separator column between panels

references.docstring:
Move each colored object vertically until it touches the matching top or bottom border bar.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- The top row is a full-width bar in one foreground color and the bottom row is a full-width bar in another.
- All other foreground pixels are 8-connected monochrome objects whose color matches one of those bars.

Rule:
- Top-bar-colored objects move upward so their bbox top is row 1.
- Bottom-bar-colored objects move downward so their bbox bottom is the row above the bottom bar.
- A downward-moving one-column segment whose landing overlaps its source becomes the continuous vertical segment swept between them.

Key insight:
The horizontal bars are destination anchors: color determines which border an object slides toward, while columns and object shape are otherwise preserved.

annotation.src: non-border 8-connected foreground objects matching a full-width border bar color
annotation.path: vertical path toward the same-color top or bottom border bar
annotation.dst: touch the same-color border bar
annotation.trajectory: translate each object to the adjacent row of that bar; a downward one-column segment whose landing overlaps its source fills the continuous swept segment
annotation.transform: redraw the border bars and moved objects on the bg

references.docstring:
Move each marker from a lattice corner gap into the adjacent enclosed 12-pixel cavity.

Input structure:
- The grid is a repeated teal lattice around black 12-pixel cavities.
- A marker is a non-black pixel placed at the northwest corner gap of one
  complete 5x5 lattice tile; the marker may itself be teal.

Rule:
- For every marked northwest corner gap, clear that marker to black.
- Fill the 12 black pixels in the tile immediately down-right of the marker
  with the marker color.
- Leave the rest of the lattice unchanged.

Key insight:
- The apparent isolated markers are control pixels for the adjacent cavity;
  teal markers are recognized as extra teal pixels occupying a gap that the
  periodic lattice template says should be black.

annotation.src: non-black marker pixels at northwest corner gaps of 5x5 teal lattice tiles
annotation.transform: erase each marker; fill the 12 black pixels in the adjacent down-right cavity with marker color
annotation.notes: a teal marker is an extra teal pixel in a gap that the lattice template otherwise leaves black

references.docstring:
Use the pink control pixel to choose where the maroon pixel belongs inside the grey 3x3 region, and turn the control pixel maroon.

Input structure:
- The grid contains one 3x3 region made from eight grey pixels and one maroon pixel.
- There is exactly one pink control pixel outside that region.

Rule:
- Restore the old maroon cell in the 3x3 region to grey.
- Compare the pink pixel to the 3x3 region: above/same band/below selects top/middle/bottom, and left/same band/right selects left/middle/right.
- Paint the selected cell maroon and recolor the pink control pixel maroon.

Key insight:
- The pink pixel acts as a relative-position marker for a 3x3 target inside the grey region.

annotation.src: pink control pixel and grey 3x3 region containing one maroon pixel
annotation.transform: move the maroon pixel to the grey region cell selected by the control pixel's relative position; recolor the control pixel maroon and restore the old maroon cell to grey

references.docstring:
Move each gray marker along its green path until it reaches the cell next to a black-green-black gate, erasing the path behind it.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Foreground components are made from a path color, a paired gate-end color, and single marker pixels.
- A gate is a straight end-center-end motif whose center has the path color and whose two ends share the gate-end color.

Rule:
- In every 4-connected foreground component with exactly one marker and one gate, erase the marker and all path-color pixels except the gate center.
- Place the marker on the unique path-color pixel adjacent to the gate center but not between the two gate ends.
- Components without both a marker and a gate stay unchanged.

Key insight: The black-green-black motif marks the stopping gate; the gray marker consumes the connected green path until it rests on the path cell immediately beside that gate.

annotation.src: grey marker in a 4-connected green path component with one black-green-black gate
annotation.path: continuous green path from the marker toward the gate
annotation.trajectory: move the marker along the green path to dst
annotation.dst: green path pixel adjacent to the gate center and outside the two black gate ends
annotation.transform: erase the old marker and traversed green path except the gate center; leave components without both marker and gate unchanged

references.docstring:
Move each right-side colored shape into the left slot whose template color is its exact complement.

Input structure:
- The grid has two equal-width slots separated by one background column.
- Non-background rows form horizontal bands separated by all-background rows.
- Each band has a shared template color in the left slot and one colored source shape in the right slot.

Rule:
- For each band, define its destination shape as the cells in the left slot not occupied by the template color.
- Normalize every right-side source shape to right-slot coordinates and match it to the unique equal destination shape.
- Clear the original right-side source pixels and paint the matched left-slot complement with the source color.

Key insight:
The right-side objects are not placed by row order; each one completes the unique left template whose missing cells have the same shape.

annotation.src: colored source shape s in a right slot
annotation.dst: left-slot missing-cell complement d of the shared-color template in the same band
annotation.match_cond: normalized shape(s) == normalized shape(d)
annotation.transform: clear s and fill d with s.color

tags: condition:缺口形状唯一配对, unique_complement

references.docstring:
Rotate each magenta source pixel 90 degrees counterclockwise around its matched blue pivot, recoloring the new pixel orange.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- The only foreground colors are blue pivot pixels and magenta source pixels.
- Each magenta source can be paired one-to-one with a blue pivot in the same
  row or column.

Rule:
- Remove all magenta source pixels.
- For each matched source/pivot pair, preserve the source distance from the
  pivot but rotate its offset 90 degrees counterclockwise.
- Paint the rotated in-bounds target orange; if the target is outside the
  grid, the source simply disappears.

Key insight:
The blue pixels are rotation centers, and row/column alignment gives a
unique global matching from each magenta source to its pivot.

annotation.src: magenta source pixel s
annotation.dst: blue pivot pixel d
annotation.match_cond: s and d are uniquely aligned in the same row or same column
annotation.transform: clear s; rotate s.offset around d 90 degrees counterclockwise; paint in-bounds target orange

references.docstring:
Copy each marked sprite to every standalone marker of the same color and erase the original sources.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Each source is an 8-connected component containing a monochrome sprite and one marker pixel of another color.
- Other isolated marker pixels may be destinations; marker colors with no source sprite are distractors.

Rule:
- Clear the grid to background.
- For every source marker color, place the sprite at each other marker of that color using the source marker as the anchor.
- Keep each destination marker pixel in place; do not keep source sprites, source markers, or distractor markers.

Key insight:
- A colored marker is not part of the sprite geometry; it is the anchor that says where same-colored copies of that sprite should be stamped.

annotation.src: 8-connected marked object s containing one marker pixel and a monochrome sprite
annotation.dst: standalone marker pixel d
annotation.match_cond: s.marker.color == d.color
annotation.transform: erase the input; stamp s.sprite at each d using the marker as anchor, keep d, and delete source markers plus distractor markers

references.docstring:
Move each isolated colored pixel into the one-cell frame around a grey 2x2 block.

Input structure:
- Background is the dominant color.
- Grey foreground objects are solid 2x2 anchor blocks.
- Every other non-background, non-grey cell is a colored singleton source.

Rule:
- Keep the grey anchors fixed and clear all colored singleton source pixels.
- For each singleton and each anchor, the normal destination is the cell reached by
  clamping the pixel into the anchor's one-cell outer frame.
- If a diagonally outside singleton has an exact 8-direction sightline into an anchor,
  also allow the cell just before the first grey pixel on that ray.
- Choose distinct destinations that minimize total king-move distance; at equal
  distance prefer exact sightlines, then the shorter Manhattan movement.

Key insight: The grey 2x2 blocks define magnetic frames; conflicts are resolved
structurally by nearest-frame assignment rather than by color identity.

annotation.src: colored singleton pixel s
annotation.dst: candidate cell d in the one-cell frame around a grey 2x2 block
annotation.match_cond: minimize king-move distance from s to d; exact diagonal sightline to the grey block wins equal-distance matches
annotation.transform: move s to d; keep grey blocks fixed and clear old s locations

references.docstring:
Decode the colored slot map inside the marked motif and rebuild the motif lattice with those colors.

Input structure:
- A blank background surrounds a rectangular lattice of identical motifs.
- The motif rows and columns are separated by one background line.
- One motif has colored marker pixels in its internal odd-row/odd-column slots.

Rule:
- The motif size is 2R+1 by 2C+1, where R by C is the motif lattice size.
- Read the marked motif's odd internal slots as the color map for the R by C output motifs.
- Slots that still contain the repeated motif color map to that repeated motif color.
- Rebuild the compact lattice on a canvas filled with the repeated motif color,
  painting each motif mask with its decoded color.

Key insight:
- The holes and filled odd slots inside one motif are a miniature legend for recoloring the entire repeated motif lattice.

annotation.src: odd internal color-map slot s inside the marked motif
annotation.dst: motif-lattice cell d in the compact output
annotation.match_cond: s.logical_slot_position == d.motif_grid_position
annotation.transform: fill the output with the repeated motif color; paint the motif mask at each d with the color decoded from s, treating repeated-color slots as repeated motif color
annotation.grid_shape: crop to the compact motif lattice

references.docstring:
Recolor the two diagonal foreground-bar orientations, assigning teal to the larger orientation and red to the smaller one.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and one foreground color.
- Foreground pixels form one-cell-thick diagonal bars.
- Every foreground pixel belongs to exactly one diagonal orientation.

Rule
- Keep the background unchanged.
- Classify each foreground pixel by whether it has a diagonal neighbor on the NW/SE axis or the NE/SW axis.
- Recolor the orientation with more foreground pixels teal and the other orientation red.

Key insight
- The output colors depend on the relative population of the two diagonal orientations, not on a fixed slash direction or position.

annotation.src: monochrome foreground pixels forming one-cell diagonal bars in the two diagonal orientations
annotation.transform: classify each foreground pixel by its diagonal-neighbor orientation; recolor the orientation with more pixels teal and the other orientation red

references.docstring:
Paint a recolored diagonal copy from each L triomino source object.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- The only foreground objects are 4-connected red and grey L triominoes,
  each occupying three pixels of a 2x2 box.

Rule:
- Grey L objects paint a yellow copy translated one diagonal step toward
  their missing 2x2 corner.
- Red L objects paint a green copy translated one diagonal step away from
  their missing 2x2 corner.
- Copies are clipped by the grid boundary; red-derived green copies are
  painted after grey-derived yellow copies where the projections collide.

Key insight:
- The missing corner of each 2x2 L object identifies its diagonal axis, and
  the source color determines which side of that axis receives the copy.

annotation.src: red and grey 4-connected L-triomino objects
annotation.path: one diagonal step along the missing-corner axis; grey moves toward the missing corner, red moves away from it
annotation.trajectory: paint one clipped copy of the L object
annotation.transform: grey copy -> yellow; red copy -> green; keep source objects unchanged
annotation.notes: red-derived green copy covers grey-derived yellow copy on collisions

references.docstring:
Swap paired marker pixels across the largest foreground-color barrier, placing them just outside the barrier segment.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- One foreground color is the unique most frequent non-background color; its pixels form the stationary barrier.
- Other foreground pixels are single markers, sometimes paired on opposite sides of one contiguous barrier segment in the same row or column.

Rule:
- Scan each row and column that crosses exactly one contiguous barrier segment.
- If the line has exactly one marker on each side of that segment, erase both source markers and place each marker in the cell immediately beyond the opposite side of the segment.
- Lines with markers on only one side are unchanged; the barrier remains unchanged.

Key insight:
- The marker pairing is local to a row or column, and the destination is defined by the nearest cells outside the intervening barrier segment, not by the original distance from the barrier.

annotation.src: single marker pixels that have exactly one marker on the opposite side of the same row or column through the largest foreground-color barrier
annotation.path: move along that row or column across the contiguous barrier segment
annotation.dst: the background cell immediately beyond the opposite side of the barrier segment
annotation.trajectory: paint only the final adjacent cell on each side with the opposite marker color
annotation.transform: erase the original paired marker cells; leave the barrier and unpaired markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Replace each marker below the separator with the mapped top legend square centered on that marker.

Input structure:
- The background surrounds a top legend, one solid non-background separator row, and a lower marker field.
- The legend contains equal-size filled square sprites, with a singleton marker below each sprite and aligned to its center column.
- The lower field contains only background and marker colors from the legend.

Rule:
- Pair legend markers to legend sprites by left-to-right position.
- Discard the legend and separator; keep the grid width and the rows below the separator.
- In the lower field, replace every marker pixel by a filled square of the paired sprite color, centered at the marker location.

Key insight: The top area is a positional color legend, and the actual output is the post-separator marker field expanded by that legend.

annotation.src: filled square sprite s in the top legend
annotation.dst: lower marker d as center anchor
annotation.match_cond: d.color == singleton marker color below s
annotation.symbol_instructions: top legend maps each singleton marker color to its filled square sprite
annotation.grid_shape: rows below the separator, same width

references.docstring:
Move the repeated boundary color's rectangles one block inward while leaving singleton boundary rectangles in place.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- Foreground objects are solid monochrome rectangles touching a grid corner.
- Exactly one foreground color appears as multiple separate 4-connected objects; other colors appear once.

Rule:
- Clear the multiple objects of the repeated color from their original positions.
- For each cleared rectangle, translate it away from the row and column border it touches by exactly its height and width.
- Keep singleton-color objects unchanged; overlapping translated rectangles of the same color merge.

Key insight:
- Multiplicity selects the moving color, and each boundary rectangle's touched edges determine its inward diagonal translation.

annotation.src: the foreground color with multiple 4-connected solid rectangles on grid corners
annotation.path: from each rectangle's corner, move inward away from the touched row and column borders by one rectangle height/width
annotation.trajectory: translate each selected rectangle once; same-color overlaps merge
annotation.transform: clear selected rectangles at their original positions; leave singleton-color rectangles unchanged

references.docstring:
List the colors of overlaid straight lines in their only possible bottom-to-top crossing order.

Input structure
The background is the dominant color. Every foreground color is the visible part
of one full one-cell-thick horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree diagonal line.
Higher lines may hide pixels of lower lines at crossings.

Rule
Recover each full line from its visible collinear pixels. At any cell where
multiple recovered lines cross, the visible color is above every other line
through that cell. Return the unique ordering of all line colors that respects
those above/below constraints and whose consecutive colors are lines that
geometrically cross.

Key insight
The visible crossing colors give a partial layer order, and the intended answer
is the unique Hamiltonian chain through the line-intersection graph from the
bottom layer to the top layer.

annotation.src: overlaid horizontal, vertical, and 45-degree diagonal one-cell-thick line objects
annotation.dst: replace grid with a one-row color sequence
annotation.match_cond: bottom-to-top layer order from crossings: visible color is above every other line through that pixel
annotation.transform: output the unique order that also forms a chain of geometrically crossing consecutive lines
annotation.grid_shape: 1 x number of foreground colors

references.docstring:
Mark the center of each odd-sized solid square with the plus marker color, erasing the marker only when it is outside the marked-center field.

Input structure:
- The dominant color is background.
- Exactly two foreground colors are present: one unique 3x3 plus marker and one color forming separated solid square objects.

Rule:
- For every non-marker 4-connected object, assert it is a solid square.
- If the square side length is odd, recolor its center pixel to the plus marker color; even-sided squares stay unchanged.
- Preserve the plus marker when its center lies inside the bounding box of the odd-square centers; otherwise erase it to background.

Key insight:
- Odd-sided solid squares have a single visible center pixel, and the plus supplies the color used to identify those centers.

annotation.src: a unique 4-connected 5-pixel plus marker and 4-connected solid square objects of the other foreground color
annotation.transform: recolor the center pixel of each odd-sided solid square to the plus marker color; leave even-sided squares unchanged; erase the plus marker when its center is outside the bbox of the recolored centers

references.docstring:
Fold each straight red rod at its black marker, leaving the gray-anchored side fixed.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Each foreground object is a straight horizontal or vertical 4-connected rod.
- Each rod contains many pixels of one line color, one endpoint marker, and one
  interior control marker.

Rule:
- For every rod, keep the segment from the endpoint marker through the control
  marker unchanged.
- Move the line-color tail on the far side of the control marker to a
  perpendicular ray starting next to that marker.
- Choose the perpendicular direction with more space to the grid edge.

Key insight:
- The endpoint marker identifies the fixed side of the rod, while the control
  marker is the hinge; the tail folds into the larger open half-plane.

annotation.src: red tail past the black hinge in each gray-marked rod
annotation.path: perpendicular ray from the black hinge toward the side with more space to the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: continuous, same length as the original tail
annotation.transform: clear the original tail; keep the markers and the gray-to-black segment fixed

references.docstring:
Keep only the center color and redraw it as a diagonal ray to its indicated corner.

Input structure:
- The grid is an odd square with a unique dominant background color.
- The center pixel is foreground.
- Every off-center pixel with the center color lies in the same diagonal
  quadrant relative to the center.

Rule:
- Fill the whole output with the background color.
- Use the quadrant of the center-colored pixels to choose one diagonal
  direction from the center.
- Draw a continuous line of the center color from the center to the grid
  edge in that direction.

Key insight:
The color at the exact center identifies the surviving color, while the
other pixels of that color identify which corner the center should connect to.

annotation.src: the foreground center pixel and the other pixels with the same color
annotation.path: diagonal ray from the center through the quadrant containing the same-color pixels
annotation.trajectory: paint every pixel on the ray with the center color
annotation.transform: clear all other foreground pixels to the dominant background color

references.docstring:
Pack the non-background rows from three separated panels into one panel, scanning panels right-to-left.

Input structure:
- A rectangular grid contains three equal-size panels separated by two full-height divider columns.
- The background is the dominant color; divider pixels use a color that appears only in the divider columns.

Rule:
- Read panels from right to left, and within each panel read rows from top to bottom.
- Keep each row that contains any non-background pixel, discarding all-background rows.
- Place the kept rows at the bottom of a single panel-shaped output, padding above with background rows.

Key insight:
- The task is row packing: the divider columns mark independent panels, and only the occupied rows are moved.

annotation.src: non-background rows in three divider-separated panels
annotation.dst: stack rows into one panel, ordered by panels right-to-left and rows top-to-bottom
annotation.transform: discard all-background rows and top-pad with background to panel height
annotation.grid_shape: output is one panel

references.docstring:
Merge same-sized filled rectangular objects by overlaying their internal marker pixels.

Input structure:
- A dominant background surrounds two or more separated 4-connected foreground objects.
- Every object is a filled rectangle of the same size.
- Each rectangle has the same majority base color plus one or more non-base marker pixels.

Rule:
- Create one output rectangle with the shared object size, filled with the shared base color.
- For each input rectangle, copy every non-base marker pixel to the same relative location
  in the output.
- Marker overlays must either land on base color or agree in color with an existing marker.

Key insight:
The separated rectangles are layers of the same template; their colored marker pixels
combine by local coordinates while the repeated base fill is just the output canvas.

annotation.src: non-base marker pixel s inside a same-sized filled rectangle
annotation.dst: cell d in the shared output rectangle
annotation.match_cond: s.local_position == d.local_position
annotation.transform: fill the output with the shared base color; paint each matched d with s.color
annotation.grid_shape: one shared object bbox

references.docstring:
Rotate each vertical bar's color one slot right and its height one slot left.

Input structure
- A dominant background surrounds several monochrome one-cell-wide vertical bars.
- Every bar is bottom-aligned and occupies a distinct column.
- The ordered bar slots are read from left to right.

Rule
- Keep the grid shape and the bar columns unchanged.
- At slot i, use the color from the previous slot cyclically.
- At slot i, use the height from the next slot cyclically.

Key insight
- Color and height are independent cyclic attributes of the ordered bar slots:
  colors rotate right while heights rotate left.

annotation.src: bottom-aligned one-cell-wide vertical bars ordered left-to-right
annotation.transform: redraw each bar in the same column with the previous bar's color cyclically and the next bar's height cyclically

references.docstring:
Recolor the large mask crop column-by-column using the separate three-row palette strip.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- One large monochrome foreground object is the mask; its bbox is the output region and may contain background holes.
- The remaining foreground is a 3-row palette rectangle with the same width as the mask bbox: two identical color rows and one uniform row.

Rule:
- Crop to the mask object's bbox.
- For each output column, color mask pixels with the corresponding color from the repeated palette rows.
- Replace background holes inside the crop with the palette's uniform third-row color.

Key insight:
The grey object is only a stencil; its columns select colors from the legend, while its holes expose the legend's fill color.

annotation.src: palette column s in the separate 3-row strip
annotation.dst: column d in the mask bbox crop
annotation.match_cond: s.column == d.column_in_crop
annotation.transform: recolor mask pixels in d with s.repeated_row_color; fill background holes with the palette's uniform third-row color
annotation.symbol_instructions: 3-row palette strip maps each mask-crop column to its mask color; the uniform third row gives the hole color
annotation.grid_shape: crop to mask bbox

references.docstring:
Paint each pink control pixel as a teal horizontal bar whose reach equals the foreground counts on that row.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color and one or more pink control pixels.
- Each marker row has exactly one pink pixel; all other non-background pixels
  in that row are counters.
Rule
- Start from an all-background output grid.
- For each pink pixel, count non-background pixels strictly to its left and
  strictly to its right in the same row.
- Paint teal from c - left_count through c + right_count on that row.
Key insight
- The foreground pixels are not copied; only their counts on each side of
  each pink marker encode the teal bar length.

annotation.src: pink control pixels on rows with other non-background counter pixels
annotation.transform: erase all input foreground; for each pink pixel, count non-background pixels strictly left and right on its row and paint a teal horizontal segment extending that many cells from the pink pixel

tags: condition:两侧计数决定长度, side_counts_length

references.docstring:
Move the yellow 3x3 frame by the displacement encoded by the gray path, then draw its diagonal yellow corner rays.

Input structure:
- The background is black.
- One 3x3 yellow frame has a non-yellow control-color center.
- A second control-color pixel is connected through gray path pixels to a lone yellow endpoint.

Rule:
- Use the vector from the second control-color pixel to the lone yellow endpoint as the frame's translation.
- Fill the whole output with the control color.
- Draw the translated yellow frame and extend yellow diagonal rays outward from its four corners to the grid edge.

Key insight: The gray path's turns are irrelevant; its two colored endpoints encode the net displacement to apply to the frame.

annotation.src: 3x3 yellow frame with a control-color center
annotation.path: gray path from the second control-color pixel to the lone yellow endpoint; use only the endpoint displacement
annotation.dst: translate the frame by that displacement
annotation.trajectory: extend yellow diagonal rays from the translated frame's four corners to the grid edge
annotation.transform: fill the canvas with the control color, leaving the translated frame center as that color

references.docstring:
Predict the next panel in a framed sequence by continuing each scheduled colored interval.

Input structure
- The grid is made from three or more equal panels in one row or one column.
- The final input panel is the static target template; every earlier panel differs from it only by dynamic colors absent from the template.
- Each dynamic color appears in a regular temporal schedule across the earlier panels.

Rule
- Keep the final template panel as the output canvas.
- For every dynamic color whose schedule reaches the next panel, compare its last two appearances.
- Extrapolate each one-dimensional interval along the color's changing row or column axis and paint that predicted mask.

Key insight
- The task is not asking for the last visible panel, but for the next frame after the blank/template slot.

annotation.src: sequence of equal rectangular panels ending with a blank/static template panel
annotation.dst: next panel in the sequence
annotation.transform: use the template panel as the output canvas; for each dynamic color absent from the template, follow its regular panel schedule and extrapolate the last two interval changes one more step along the changing row or column axis
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as one panel

references.docstring:
Invert each row's native foreground color against the black background.

Input structure
- A black-background grid whose rows each have one native foreground color plus optional distractor colors.
- The native row color is the most frequent non-bg color in that row; if tied, its run starts leftmost among tied colors.

Rule
- For each row independently, turn pixels of the native row color into bg.
- Turn every other pixel in that row, including bg and distractor colors, into the native row color.

Key insight
- Distractor colors are not preserved objects; they mark cells that participate in the binary complement of the row's native color.

annotation.src: each row's native foreground color on black bg, with optional distractor colors
annotation.transform: replace native-color pixels by bg and replace every other pixel in that row by the native color; choose the native color as the most frequent non-bg row color, breaking ties by leftmost occurrence

references.docstring:
Fill every lattice slot from the color assigned to that slot position by the other lattices.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- The largest foreground color forms several one-pixel-thick rectangular lattice frames.
- The frame lines divide each lattice into the same row-by-column set of rectangular slots; some slots already contain one non-frame color.

Rule:
- Infer a color for each logical slot position from the colored slots across all lattice frames.
- Repaint every slot interior in every lattice with the inferred color for its row/column position.
- Keep the frame lines and all background outside frames unchanged.

Key insight:
- Slot sizes vary by frame, but the complete color pattern is indexed by lattice slot position rather than by absolute pixel size or location.

annotation.src: colored slot s in any lattice frame
annotation.dst: slot interior d in any lattice frame
annotation.match_cond: s.logical_slot_position == d.logical_slot_position
annotation.transform: fill d with s.color, preserving frame lines and outside background

tags: condition:槽位位置决定颜色, slot_position_color

references.docstring:
Erase each target-color object crossed by the ray pointed by the bar-and-control marker.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- There is one three-pixel straight marker bar and one singleton control pixel adjacent to the bar center.
- The remaining non-background color forms multiple 4-connected target objects.

Rule:
- Cast a straight ray from the marker bar center in the direction away from the adjacent control pixel.
- Find every 4-connected target-color object that intersects that ray.
- Recolor all pixels of those hit target objects to the background; all other pixels stay unchanged.

Key insight:
- The whole object is erased when the center ray touches any of its pixels; the full marker bar width is not swept.

annotation.src: three-pixel marker bar with an adjacent singleton control pixel
annotation.path: straight center ray from the bar center going away from the control pixel to the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: ray itself is not painted; it selects each 4-connected target-color object it crosses
annotation.transform: recolor all pixels of selected target objects to background; leave the marker and other target objects unchanged

references.docstring:
Remove each fracture marker line and push the surrounding object pixels one cell away from it.

Input structure
- A background grid with 8-connected foreground objects made from a body color and a rarer marker color.
- Each object has a non-square bbox; the marker pixels form one complete fracture line across the shorter bbox axis.

Rule
- Erase all marker pixels.
- For a wide object, each row has one marker; body pixels left of it shift one cell left and body pixels right of it shift one cell right.
- For a tall object, each column has one marker; body pixels above it shift one cell up and body pixels below it shift one cell down.

Key insight
- The marker line is a crack through the object, so the two sides separate by one pixel perpendicular to the crack.

annotation.src: 8-connected body-color objects on the background, each crossed by a rarer marker-color fracture line
annotation.transform: erase the marker pixels; in each wide object shift body pixels one cell left/right away from the row marker, and in each tall object shift body pixels one cell up/down away from the column marker

references.docstring:
Expand each sparse color object into a filled rectangular region using its legend-paired fill color.

Input structure
A background-color grid has a two-column legend in columns 0 and 1, starting at row 0: each row gives
a source color in the left column and that source color's fill color in the right column.  Outside the
legend, the foreground pixels are sparse dot objects whose colors are exactly the legend source colors.

Rule
Clear the legend.  For each source color, take the bbox of all of its non-legend dots, expand that bbox
by one pixel in every direction, and fill background cells inside the expanded rectangle with the paired
legend fill color while preserving every original non-legend dot.

Key insight
The legend order is also the layer order: earlier legend rows are in front, so fill rectangles are painted
from the last legend row back to the first and higher-priority fills overwrite lower-priority fills.

annotation.src: sparse same-color dot objects and the upper-left source/fill legend
annotation.dst: paint each object's bbox expanded by one pixel
annotation.transform: clear the legend; fill pixels that are not original dots inside each expanded bbox with the paired fill color and preserve the original dots
annotation.multi_step: process legend rows bottom-to-top so earlier rows have priority where expanded bboxes overlap
annotation.symbol_instructions: upper-left source/fill legend maps each dot color to its expanded-bbox fill color

tags: condition:图例顺序决定层级, legend_order_layer

references.docstring:
Repeat the single colored border segment around the rectangular border, leaving one segment-length gap between copies.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- There is exactly one foreground color.
- All foreground pixels form one contiguous segment on the rectangular border, possibly crossing the cycle start.

Rule:
- Unwrap the grid border clockwise into a cyclic path.
- Let n be the length of the foreground segment.
- Copy the segment with the same color every 2*n border positions around the cycle.

Key insight:
- The foreground segment is not extended by rows or columns directly; it is a motif on the perimeter cycle, repeated with an equal-sized gap.

annotation.src: single contiguous foreground segment on the rectangular border
annotation.path: cyclic traversal of the border
annotation.trajectory: copy the segment every two segment lengths around the cycle
annotation.transform: leave non-copied border positions and background unchanged

references.docstring:
Slide each foreground object horizontally to the edge indicated by whether its shape has an open notch.

Input structure:
- Yellow is the background and there is one blue foreground color.
- The foreground is split into separated 4-connected objects.
- Each object keeps its row span and shape in the output.

Rule:
- If an object's bbox border contains a background gap flanked by object pixels along that same border, slide it to the right edge and recolor it green.
- Otherwise slide the object to the left edge and recolor it red.
- Start from a blank background canvas; no moved objects overlap.

Key insight:
- The target side is encoded by the object's shape, not by its original position: open notches go right, while closed or solid shapes go left.

annotation.src: 4-connected blue foreground objects
annotation.path: horizontal slide in the same rows to the selected grid edge
annotation.dst: left edge for closed or solid objects; right edge for objects with a flanked open notch on the bbox border
annotation.trajectory: translate the whole object without changing its shape
annotation.transform: recolor left-moving objects red and right-moving objects green

references.docstring:
Expand the sparse dot lattice into a 26x26 drawing with thick bars between adjacent matching dots.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Foreground pixels lie on logical rows and columns separated by background spacer rows/columns.
- A logical row or column is present when it contains at least one foreground pixel.

Rule
- Expand every background spacer row/column to thickness 2.
- Expand the logical rows/columns equally so the full output is 26x26.
- Paint each foreground logical pixel as a solid rectangle of its color.
- Connect adjacent same-color logical pixels horizontally through the intervening spacer.
- Connect adjacent same-color logical pixels vertically only when neither endpoint is part of a horizontal same-color run.

Key insight
- The input is a sampled line drawing: horizontal same-color runs define the bars first, and only unclaimed same-color vertical neighbors are joined.

annotation.src: foreground pixels on a background-spaced logical lattice
annotation.dst: expanded 26x26 lattice with 2-pixel background spacers
annotation.transform: expand logical rows/columns to equal bands; paint each foreground pixel as a solid rectangle; join adjacent same-color pixels horizontally, and join vertical neighbors only when neither endpoint is part of a horizontal same-color run
annotation.grid_shape: fixed 26x26

references.docstring:
Fill every row from the nearest marked horizontal bar, turning bar rows and color-boundary ties into separator rows.

- Outside the marker column, every row is monochrome: either background or a source bar color.
- Background rows share one marker color in the marker column; source bar rows share the other.

Rule
- Each non-source row takes the color of the nearest source bar, with that row's marker-column pixel set to the source-marker color.
- If a row is exactly midway between nearest bars of different colors, make the whole row the source-marker color.
- Each original source bar row becomes a source-marker row with the marker-column pixel changed to the background-row marker color.

Key insight
- The marked bars are horizontal seeds for a one-dimensional nearest-seed partition over rows; equal-distance rows are separators only when the competing seed colors differ.

annotation.src: marked horizontal bars and the vertical marker column
annotation.transform: recolor each row by the nearest source bar color; each source bar row becomes a marker separator row, and equal-distance rows between different bar colors become plain separator rows

references.docstring:
Keep the larger sprite from each separated panel and overlay those sprites into one 5x5 canvas.

Input structure:
- The input is a 5x17 grid: three 5x5 panels separated by one-cell black columns.
- Each panel has the same background color and exactly one foreground color split into two 4-connected components.

Rule:
- In each panel, discard the smaller foreground component and keep the unique largest component as the sprite.
- Process panels left to right, placing each sprite at its panel coordinates on a 5x5 background canvas.

references.docstring:

references.docstring:
Move every foreground pixel by the fixed offset indicated by its color.

- The foreground is a sparse set of colored pixels.
- Each foreground color is one of the trained motion colors: orange, red,
  maroon, or blue.

- Clear the canvas to the background color.
- Translate orange pixels up 2 cells, red pixels left 2 cells, maroon
  pixels down 2 cells, and blue pixels right 1 cell.
- Preserve each moved pixel's original color.

references.docstring:
Complete a four-corner framed rectangle from one decorated anchor rectangle and its diagonal mate.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Two same-color solid rectangular anchors of the same size sit on opposite
  diagonal corners, with the first anchor above-left of the second.
- The upper-left anchor has two one-cell-thick vertical control bars to its
  right and two one-cell-thick horizontal control bars below it.

Rule:
- Copy the anchor rectangle into the two missing corners of the implied
  larger rectangle.
- Repeat the right-side control bars horizontally between the left and right
  anchors, using their spacing as the period, and draw the outer top and
  bottom borders in the first right-control color.
- Repeat the below-side control bars vertically between the top and bottom
  anchors, using the same period, and draw the outer left and right borders
  in the first below-control color.

frame patterns; the diagonal anchor supplies the opposite corner and the
missing two anchor copies.

annotation.dst: the missing two anchor corners and periodic frame segments between all four anchors

references.docstring:
Compute a grey result bar by adding teal bar heights and subtracting red bar heights.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and several bottom-aligned one-cell-wide vertical bars.
- Teal bars are positive operands; red bars are negative operands.
- The penultimate column is an empty result slot.

- Keep every input bar unchanged.
- Compute result height = total teal bar height - total red bar height.
- Paint that many bottom cells of the penultimate column grey.

Key insight
- The bars encode arithmetic by height, with color providing the sign.

annotation.dst: empty penultimate column result slot
annotation.transform: paint a bottom-aligned grey result bar whose height is total teal bar height minus total red bar height

references.docstring:

- The grid has one dominant background color and exactly two foreground colors.

Rule:

- For each background pixel, if it is diagonally adjacent to the frame color and has no orthogonal adjacency to the frame color, recolor it to the inner color.

Key insight: The inner color marks the color to use, while the frame's diagonal-only background neighbors define the cells to add.

references.docstring:
Paint the maze corridor and framed rooms lying on shortest paths between the two colored endpoint components.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background, one wall color forming thin orthogonal frames, and one endpoint/fill color.

- Treat wall pixels as blocked and every other pixel as passable.
- Find every passable pixel that lies on a shortest 4-connected path between the two endpoint components.
- Also fill any framed square room of an endpoint-derived size that intersects that shortest-path mask.

- Shortest paths identify the route through open connector corridors, while the wall-bordered square rooms need to be expanded from the route centerline to their full interior.

references.docstring:
Recolor wall-separated background regions alternately, starting with grey in the lower-left region.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and one foreground wall color.
- The wall pixels form one or more 4-connected one-cell-thick segments.

- Keep all wall pixels unchanged.
- Label the 4-connected background regions and connect two labels when they

- Color the region containing the lower-left corner grey, then flip between
  grey and green across every wall adjacency.

- The red walls define a bipartite map of regions; the lower-left background

references.docstring:

Input structure
A rectangular grid of colored pixels with no internal empty region to infer.

Rule
Create a black output with the same height and width W + H - 1, then copy
each input row r unchanged starting at column H - 1 - r.

Key insight
The colors and row contents are preserved; only the row offsets change so
the left edge forms a descending diagonal.

annotation.dst: black canvas with the same height and enough columns for the staggered rows

references.docstring:
Replace the active black cutout's tail with background and mark the cutout side facing a colored source region.

Input structure:
- The dominant color is background, with black rectangle-plus-tail cutouts, one gray source region, and colored distractors.
- Non-gray colored regions and single pixels are distractors/blockers, even when they are multi-pixel staircase shapes.

Rule:
- Find each black cutout whose largest solid rectangle leaves exactly a two-pixel tail.
- The active gray source region is visible only by horizontal rays through background from a cutout's left or right side.
- Select the unique cutout side with the most same-source visible rows, erase that cutout's tail to background, and recolor the full selected vertical side pink (6).

Key insight:
- The colored regions do not move; their horizontal line-of-sight identifies which rectangular cutout is being opened and which side receives the pink mark.

annotation.transform: use horizontal line-of-sight from active source regions to choose the unique cutout side with the most visible rows; erase that cutout's tail to background and recolor the full visible vertical side pink

references.docstring:
Move each vertical stream of pixels into a bottom-aligned centered pile.

Input structure
- A mostly background grid contains one or more vertical source columns of
  foreground pixels.
- Each source column has n^2 foreground pixels, and the top-to-bottom color
  sequence splits into monochrome groups of lengths 1, 3, 5, ...

Rule
- Clear the canvas to background.
- For each source column, read the foreground colors from top to bottom and
  rebuild them at the bottom below the same column as odd-width centered
  rows of lengths 1, 3, 5, ...

Key insight
- The scattered vertical pixels are falling grains; a square number of
  grains decomposes into the odd row widths of a centered pyramid.

annotation.dst: bottom-aligned centered pile under the same column

references.docstring:
Infer the background, rotate the whole input 90 degrees counterclockwise, and stack two framed copies vertically.

Input structure:
- Blue is absent from the input.
- One rare marker color appears in exactly two pixels.
- The background is the unique non-marker color whose removal leaves exactly two 4-connected foreground objects, each with one marker pixel and one body color.
- The whole grid, including background and foreground objects, is the sprite to transform.

Rule:
- Rotate the entire input grid 90 degrees counterclockwise.
- Create a blue one-pixel frame around two vertical copies of the rotated grid.
- Use the input background color for the two endpoints of every horizontal frame/separator row.

Key insight: The output is not a crop of the foreground objects; it is two copies of the complete rotated input, separated and enclosed by a newly added blue border.

annotation.dst: two vertical slots inside a new one-pixel blue frame

annotation.grid_shape: rotated input width plus side borders by two rotated input heights plus three frame/separator rows

references.docstring:
Normalize vertical two-color bars between paired marker columns around the marker rows.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- A row of red marker pixels sits directly above a row of gray marker pixels
  in the same alternating columns.
- The columns between adjacent markers contain vertical bars made from a
  contiguous teal run above a contiguous blue run.

- Keep the marker pixels and all non-bar background cells fixed.
- Let h be the maximum teal-run height among the bar columns; paint teal in
  every bar column for h rows ending at the red marker row.
- In each bar column, move its blue run to start at the gray marker row and
  fill all lower cells in that column with maroon.

Key insight
- The marker rows are a baseline: teal is normalized into a common upper
  band, while each blue run keeps its own height below the baseline.

annotation.transform: replace the bar columns with normalized bars: paint a full-width teal band of maximum teal-run height ending on the red marker row, move each blue run to start on the gray marker row, and fill lower cells in that column maroon

references.docstring:
Crop the foreground object whose missing cells match marker shapes, and fill those missing cells with the marker colors.

Input structure
A dominant background surrounds several monochromatic foreground objects. Exactly one object has background gaps inside its bounding box whose component shapes are matched by separate marker objects.
Rule
Find that object, crop its bounding box, and replace each background gap component with the color of the separate marker component or components having the same normalized shape.
Key insight
The marker objects do not mark absolute positions; their shapes identify which gaps in the selected object should be colored, while objects with unmatched gaps are distractors.

annotation.dst: background gap component d inside the selected object's bbox
annotation.match_cond: normalized shape(s) == normalized shape(d), with matching component counts for each gap shape
