annotation.grid_shape: tight crop to the selected object's bbox

references.docstring:
Expand the lower color grid by replacing each pixel with its matching top stencil.

Input structure
The input has a top legend and a lower dense color grid, separated by blank rows.
The legend contains left-to-right 2x2 color swatches and, to their right,
the same number of square neutral-color stencil masks.

Rule
Pair the swatches and stencil masks by left-to-right order. For every pixel in
the lower color grid, paste the paired stencil mask as one output block,
recoloring the mask pixels with that pixel's color and leaving mask holes as bg.

Key insight
The lower grid is not copied directly; it is an index grid whose colors select
the stencil shape from the legend, so each input pixel becomes one square block.

annotation.dst: output block d for a lower-grid pixel
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.input_pixel_color
annotation.transform: recolor s.mask with d.input_pixel_color; stencil holes remain background
annotation.grid_shape: lower grid height and width multiplied by stencil size

references.docstring:
Extract the compact table of solid cells hidden inside a separator lattice.

Input structure
- The grid has full-width and full-height bars of one separator color, dividing it into rectangular cells.

- Split the input into lattice cells using the full separator rows and columns.
- Keep the cells whose full interior is one color, crop to their occupied rectangle, and output those colors.

Key insight
- The periodic pattern is noise; only completely solid lattice cells encode the reduced output grid.

annotation.dst: compact rectangle of solid-cell colors, preserving lattice row and column order

references.docstring:
Move the small colored sprite into the hollow frame by stretching its shape to the frame interior.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- There are exactly two foreground colors: one forms a complete rectangular

- The frame interior is initially background.

Rule:
- Clear the original sprite from its outside location.
- Map the sprite bbox to the frame interior bbox, sending bbox extremes to
  interior extremes.
- Draw straight horizontal or vertical segments between mapped positions of
  adjacent sprite pixels, then fill any enclosed background region inside

Key insight:
The outside sprite is a miniature line/fill diagram for the frame interior,
not a bitmap to scale by block replication.

references.docstring:
Rotate the colors around every 3x3 foreground ring, with corners and side-centers cycling in opposite directions.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color.
- Each 4-connected foreground object is a complete 3x3 ring: eight foreground pixels around a background center.

Rule
- For each ring, move corner colors one step around the four corners.
- Move side-center colors one step around the four side centers in the opposite direction.
- Leave the background center and all other background pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- Corners and side centers form two separate four-cycles on the same 3x3 ring.

annotation.transform: for each ring, cycle the corner colors one step around the corners and cycle the side-center colors one step around the side centers in the opposite direction

references.docstring:
Move each teal-cornered filled rectangle one cell diagonally toward its teal corner.

Input structure:
- Dominant background surrounds several filled rectangular colored objects.
- Each object has exactly one teal control pixel replacing one corner cell of

Rule:
- Treat the teal pixel as the missing corner of its colored rectangle.
- Erase each original rectangle footprint, including the teal pixel.
- Repaint the completed rectangle shifted one cell diagonally in the direction
  of that teal corner.

Key insight:
- The control pixel's corner position gives both the missing cell to restore
  and the diagonal motion vector.

annotation.path: one-cell diagonal shift toward the teal corner
annotation.trajectory: translate each completed rectangle without changing its size or color

references.docstring:
Advance the marker from one half of a vertical bar to the same half of the next longer bar.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and exactly two foreground colors.
- One foreground color forms many vertical one-cell-wide bars; the other appears as a single vertical marker segment.
- The marker segment occupies exactly the top or bottom half of its containing vertical bar.
Rule
- Recolor the current marker segment back to the bar color.
- Find the unique all-bar-color vertical bar whose height is two pixels greater than the marked source bar.
- Recolor the same half of that next longer bar to the marker color.
Key insight
- Each bar's total height encodes an ordered size, and the marker advances from a 2k bar to the corresponding 2(k+1) bar while preserving whether it marks the top or bottom half.

references.docstring:
Slide each blue/teal or yellow/orange row pair together while preserving its left-to-right order.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background.
- Each nonempty row contains exactly two distinct foreground pixels.
- Blue/teal and yellow/orange row pairs are the moving pairs; other color pairs are distractors.

Rule
- For each moving pair, keep the left pixel fixed and move the right pixel left until it touches the left pixel.
- Clear the moved pixel's original location, and leave non-moving rows unchanged.

Key insight
- Only same-hue-family pixel pairs attract horizontally; separated unrelated colors do not compact.

annotation.trajectory: keep only the final pixel immediately right of the other foreground pixel
annotation.transform: erase the original right-pixel location; leave other two-pixel rows unchanged

references.docstring:
Fill the rectangle from the lone foreground pixel to its nearest grid corner.

Input structure
- The grid is a uniform background field with exactly one foreground pixel.
- The foreground pixel's color is the color used for all added pixels.

Rule
- Find the grid corner with the smallest Manhattan distance to the foreground pixel.
- Recolor every pixel in the inclusive axis-aligned rectangle bounded by that
  corner and the foreground pixel to the foreground color.

Key insight
- The single pixel is one corner of the rectangle; the opposite corner is the
  nearest corner of the whole canvas.

annotation.transform: fill the inclusive rectangle between that pixel and its unique nearest grid corner with the pixel color

references.docstring:
Pack the colored sprites along the bottom edge from smallest to largest.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background color and several monochrome 4-connected
foreground sprites; a full-grid one-cell frame may surround the scene.

Rule
Remove any full-grid rectangular frame, sort the remaining sprites by pixel
area from smallest to largest, and paste their bounding-box sprites left to
right with each sprite bottom-aligned.

Key insight
The original locations do not determine the final slots; each sprite's area
gives the packing order, while its shape and color are preserved.

annotation.dst: pack into the bottom-left corner from smallest to largest by pixel area
annotation.transform: clear original positions; preserve each sprite's shape and color; bottom-align bounding-box sprites with no horizontal gaps

references.docstring:
Transform each 9x9 panel by mirroring across its center guide line or filling all four block slots from its lone exemplar.

Input structure
The grid is made of 9x9 panels separated by one-cell-wide grid lines. Each

full non-background center row, a full non-background center column, or no
guide line.

A panel with a full center column is reflected left-to-right, and a panel
with a full center row is reflected top-to-bottom. A panel with no guide line
has exactly one slot color that appears once and one slot color that appears

Key insight
The center guide line encodes the mirror axis, while panels without a guide

annotation.src: 9x9 panel lattice; each panel has four monochrome 3x3 quadrant slots and optionally a full center-row or center-column guide line
annotation.transform: reflect each guided panel across its guide line; for each unguided panel, recolor all four slots to the slot color that appears only once

references.docstring:
Shift each interior pixel whose color matches a frame side one cell toward that matching side.

Input structure
The grid has a one-cell-thick rectangular frame: the four corners are the
background color, and each side between corners is a solid, distinct side
color. The interior is mostly background with sparse foreground pixels.

Rule
Interior pixels with the top-side color move one row up, bottom-side color
move one row down, left-side color move one column left, and right-side color
move one column right. A pixel already adjacent to its matching side stays in
place; colors that do not match a frame side and the frame itself are unchanged.

Key insight
The colored frame sides act as direction labels for matching interior pixels.

annotation.path: one orthogonal step toward the same-colored frame side
annotation.trajectory: translate each pixel one cell; pixels already adjacent to their matching side stay in place

references.docstring:
Move the diagonal foreground segment to the next longer run along the same up-right diagonal.

Input structure
The grid has one background color and one foreground color. The foreground pixels form a
contiguous one-pixel-wide segment on a single anti-diagonal.

Rule
Erase the current segment. If its columns are c0..c1 and its length is L, draw the same
color on columns c1+1..c1+L+1 along the same anti-diagonal.

Key insight
The segment advances past its current upper-right end by one whole segment position, and
the next segment is one pixel longer than the current one.

annotation.trajectory: paint the next contiguous segment one pixel longer than the source

references.docstring:
Cycle each solid odd-sided square to the next smaller centered square, wrapping a single pixel to a 9x9 square.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- Every foreground object is a separated 4-connected monochrome solid square.
- Square side lengths are odd and belong to the cycle 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

Rule:
- Clear the canvas to the background.
- Keep each square's color and center.
- Replace side length n by n - 2 when n > 1; replace side length 1 by side length 9.

Key insight:
- The visible operation is on square size, not color: side lengths cycle 1 -> 9 -> 7 -> 5 -> 3 -> 1.

annotation.transform: clear each original square and repaint a centered square of the same color with side length n - 2 when n > 1; a 1x1 object wraps to a centered 9x9 square

references.docstring:
Erase the two leftmost columns of every foreground object, leaving the rest of each object in place.

Input structure:
- A grid has one dominant background color and several monochromatic 4-connected foreground objects.
- Each foreground object spans at least two columns in its bounding box.

Rule:
- Find each same-color 4-connected foreground object.
- Within each object's own bounding box, set foreground pixels in the two leftmost columns to the background color.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The deletion is measured from each object's local left edge, not from the grid edge or from a shared global column.

annotation.transform: for each object, set foreground pixels in its two leftmost bbox columns to bg

references.docstring:
Complete each partially hidden simple foreground shape by recoloring the occluding pixels in its footprint.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background and several solid foreground shapes.
- Some shapes are partially hidden by other foreground colors, but their full
  footprint is still indicated by a foreground-filled bbox or by a foreground-
  filled 45-degree diagonal line.

Rule
- For each foreground color, complete its full rectangular bbox when that bbox
  contains no background and includes other colors.
- Otherwise, complete its 45-degree diagonal line when all visible pixels lie
  on that line and the hidden line cells are foreground, not background.
- Recolor only those hidden footprint pixels; leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The occluded cells are exactly the non-background cells inside a simple
  shape's implied footprint, so completing shapes is a local recoloring problem.

annotation.transform: recolor foreground pixels inside each implied shape footprint to that shape's color; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Reflect the solid rectangular source objects across the full separator line and color the gap with the separator color.

Input structure:
- A dominant background contains one full-width or full-height one-pixel
  separator line in a non-background color.
- One other foreground color forms solid rectangular objects, all strictly on the same side of that separator.
- Remaining non-background pixels are scattered distractors.

Rule:
- Keep the input grid shape and unchanged pixels outside each affected corridor.
- Mirror each source object across the separator line.
- For every source object, recolor the rectangular strip between the
  original object and its reflection to the separator color, then paint the
  reflected object in the source color.

Key insight:
- The full straight line is a mirror axis; the real objects are identified
  structurally as the only solid rectangles confined to one side, while
  scattered pixels are noise that may be overwritten inside the corridor.

annotation.src: solid rectangular foreground objects all on one side of the full separator row/column
annotation.dst: their mirror positions across the separator line
annotation.transform: copy each source object by reflection; recolor the rectangular strip between each source object and its mirror to the separator color, overwriting background or distractor pixels inside that strip

references.docstring:
Move each marked L-shaped sprite onto the separate pixel matching its marker color.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- Foreground has 4-connected multicolor sprites and isolated one-pixel controls.
- Each sprite has one repeated body color in an L shape plus one embedded marker

- If the embedded marker color also appears as a separate isolated control pixel,
  translate the whole sprite so the body L-bend lands on that control pixel.
- Clear each moved sprite from its old position, clear its consumed control pixel,
  then paste all translated sprites; sprites without a matching control stay put.

Key insight
- The marker color pairs a sprite with its destination control, while the L-bend
  gives the orientation-independent anchor cell to place on that destination.

annotation.dst: isolated control pixel d
annotation.match_cond: s.marker.color == d.color and d lies on the outer diagonal ray from s.L_bend through s.marker
annotation.transform: translate s so s.L_bend lands on d; clear original s and consumed d; keep unmatched sprites and unrelated single pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Redraw foreground objects as nested square rings ordered by object size.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- Every foreground object is a 4-connected monochromatic component.
- Foreground object areas are distinct.

Rule:
- Sort the foreground objects by decreasing pixel count.
- Create a square output with side length 2 * number_of_objects - 1.
- The largest object color fills the outer ring, each next object color fills
  the next inner ring, and the smallest object color fills the center pixel.

Key insight: The objects' original shapes do not get copied; their areas
determine only the outside-to-inside order of the nested square pattern.

annotation.src: monochromatic foreground objects s ordered by decreasing area
annotation.dst: centered square rings d ordered outside-to-inside
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: paint each d with s.color
annotation.grid_shape: square of side 2 * object_count - 1

references.docstring:
Push every colored object touching maroon markers straight outward until it reaches the grid edge.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- Maroon pixels are fixed markers.
- Every other foreground 4-connected object touches the marker pixels on exactly one cardinal side.

Rule:
- Clear each non-background, non-maroon object from its original position.
- Translate it in the direction away from its maroon contact until the object reaches the grid boundary.
- Keep the maroon marker pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The maroon contact side is a launcher: it determines a unique outward ray for the whole object, and the edge of the grid determines the translation distance.

annotation.src: non-background, non-maroon 4-connected objects touching maroon marker pixels
annotation.path: move straight away from the maroon contact side along the matching row or column
annotation.dst: furthest in-bounds position where the object reaches the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: translate each object once, preserving its shape and color
annotation.transform: clear each moving object from its original position; keep maroon markers unchanged

references.docstring:
Complete sparse nested rectangular color layers into solid rectangles.

Input structure
The background is the dominant color, and every foreground color marks one
axis-aligned rectangular layer; the layer bboxes have unique areas and are
nested from outermost to innermost.
Rule
Take each color's bbox as its completed rectangle, except that a child bbox
which already matches at least three sides of its parent's one-pixel inset
expands to that full inset; repaint the rectangles largest to smallest.
Key insight
The scattered pixels are samples of nested rectangular regions, so the
output is a clean redraw of those regions with inner colors overwriting
outer colors.

annotation.src: sparse foreground pixels marking nested axis-aligned rectangular color regions
annotation.dst: same canvas with each nested rectangular region completed
annotation.transform: infer each color's rectangular layer from its bbox; if a child bbox aligns with its parent's one-pixel-inset interior on at least three sides, expand it to that interior; fill layers from largest to smallest so inner colors overwrite outer colors

tags: condition:大层先画小层覆盖, large_first_small_over

references.docstring:
Reverse the sequence of colors along the single 4-connected foreground path while keeping the path shape fixed.

Input structure:
- The background is the dominant color.
- All non-background pixels form one multicolor 4-connected one-pixel-wide path.
- The path has exactly two endpoints and no branches.

Rule:
- Walk the path from one endpoint to the other.
- Replace the colors on those same path cells by the original path colors in reverse order.
- Leave every background pixel unchanged.

Key insight:
- Nothing moves geometrically; only the color string written on the path is reversed between the endpoints.

annotation.src: single multicolor 4-connected foreground path on the background
annotation.transform: read path pixels from one endpoint to the other and reverse that color sequence onto the same pixels; leave background unchanged

tags: condition:形状不变仅反色序, shape_fixed_reversed

references.docstring:
Extract the single plain rectangle and redraw it with the aligned rectangles' border-relative marker pattern.

Input structure:
- The boundary color is the background/separator.
- Foreground objects are dense rectangular regions; exactly one rectangle has only its base color.
- Other rectangles contain their base color plus marker pixels.

Rule:
- Crop the only plain rectangle; this crop is the output canvas.
- Use marked rectangles whose row span overlaps the plain rectangle's row span.
- Transfer their marker pixels by preserving each marker run's distance from the nearest rectangle edges.

Key insight:
- The marked rectangles are examples of an edge-relative pattern, so the missing plain rectangle receives the same pattern resized to its own dimensions.

annotation.src: edge-relative marker run s in a marked rectangle aligned with the plain rectangle row band
annotation.dst: run d in the plain rectangle crop
annotation.match_cond: s.nearest_edge_offsets == d.nearest_edge_offsets
annotation.transform: paint each matched d with the shared marker color; keep base rectangle fill elsewhere
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as the plain rectangle

references.docstring:
Expand the top-left seed mask into a recursive colored pattern and tile it across the full grid.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- All foreground lies in a top-left rectangle whose last row and last column are a solid secondary color.
- Removing that secondary-color row and column leaves a seed region containing background plus one primary color.

Rule
- Use the primary-color pixels in the seed as a binary mask.
- Replace each primary seed cell with a copy of the seed mask in the primary color, and each background seed cell
  with a copy of the seed mask in the secondary color.
- Repeat and crop that expanded tile to the original grid shape.

Key insight
The solid L-shaped secondary-color border is a legend, not output content; it supplies the color used when the
seed's background cells are expanded.

annotation.src: top-left seed region containing background and one primary color, with a solid secondary-color L-shaped legend border
annotation.transform: expand the seed mask once: primary seed cells become primary-color copies of the mask, background seed cells become secondary-color copies, and mask background stays background; tile/crop the expanded pattern to the full grid

tags: condition:前景背景分别替换, fg_bg_separate

references.docstring:
Within each horizontal pair of two-color panels, swap the motif masks and recolor each pasted mask with the source panel's base color.

Input structure:
- A separator color forms full blank rows and at least one full blank column.
- The non-separator area is split into row bands, each containing exactly two same-shaped rectangular panels.
- Each panel has a dominant base color and one minority motif color.

Rule:
- For every row band, clear each panel to its own base color.
- Paste the right panel's motif mask into the left panel using the right base color.
- Paste the left panel's motif mask into the right panel using the left base color.

Key insight:
- The motif colors themselves are distractors; only each motif's shape mask and the two panel base colors are exchanged.

annotation.src: minority-color motif mask s inside a two-color panel
annotation.dst: horizontally paired panel d in the same row band
annotation.match_cond: s.panel and d are paired across the separator columns within the same row band
annotation.transform: clear d to its dominant base color and draw s using s.panel base color

references.docstring:
Connect the innermost mirrored marker pair(s) by filling their horizontal span.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color and one foreground color.
- Each foreground row contains exactly two foreground pixels mirrored across the vertical center.

Rule
- Find the foreground row pair(s) with the smallest horizontal gap between the two markers.
- Fill every pixel between those two markers in each selected row with the foreground color.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- Wider marker pairs are context; the closest marker pair(s) show the unresolved horizontal segment.

annotation.src: rows containing two horizontally mirrored foreground marker pixels
annotation.transform: find the row(s) whose marker pair has the smallest horizontal gap and fill the inclusive segment between those markers with the foreground color

references.docstring:
Use the left-edge color legend to draw a padded rectangular halo around each matching object while preserving enclosed holes.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background color.
- One or more two-row markers sit on the left edge; each marker is a 2x2 block whose left column is an object color and right column is its halo color.
- Away from the markers, every source color from the legend appears as one or more 4-connected monochrome objects.

Rule:
- Keep the input pixels unchanged.
- For each source-color object, take its tight bbox expanded by one cell and clipped to the grid.
- Recolor background pixels in that expanded region to the marker's halo color, except for background holes enclosed by the object.

Key insight:
- The small left-edge bars are a legend: they map object colors to the colors used for the surrounding padded bbox.

annotation.src: 4-connected monochrome objects on the background plus left-edge two-column color legend markers
annotation.transform: for each object whose color appears in the legend, fill background pixels in its one-cell padded bbox with the paired legend color; preserve the object and any enclosed background holes
annotation.symbol_instructions: left-edge two-column legend maps object color to bbox-fill color

references.docstring:
Fill each plus-shaped background notch with the color of the frame side it opens toward.

Input structure
- A one-cell-thick rectangular frame has four solid-colored sides and neutral corner pixels.
- The frame interior contains a dominant background color and one foreground object color.
- Some object boundaries contain five-pixel plus-shaped background notches.

Rule
- Find every background plus whose opposite side is supported by foreground object pixels and whose open side faces one frame side.
- Recolor the five pixels of that plus with the color of the facing frame side.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
The frame side colors are direction labels for the open notches in the foreground object.

annotation.src: solid-color rectangular frame whose four side colors label directions; monochrome 4-connected foreground objects on the dominant background with 5-pixel plus-shaped background notches
annotation.transform: for each plus-shaped background notch, determine its open side from the adjacent foreground support and recolor the five plus pixels to the matching frame side color; leave all other pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Expand the top-left horizontal bar into a wrapped sequence of increasing and decreasing foreground runs.

Input structure:
- The grid has a background color and exactly one foreground color.
- All foreground pixels form one contiguous horizontal bar in the top row.
- The bar starts at the left edge; its length is the control value n.

Rule:
- Build a one-dimensional sequence of foreground runs with lengths
  1, 2, ..., n, n-1, ..., 2, 1.
- Separate adjacent runs by one background pixel.
- Wrap the sequence row-major across the input width and pad the final row
  with background pixels.

Key insight:
The output preserves the input width; the bar length controls the run-length
diamond, and the apparent 2D pattern is just that 1D sequence wrapped into rows.

annotation.src: the top-left horizontal foreground bar; its length n controls the run pattern
annotation.transform: replace the grid with foreground runs of lengths 1, 2, ..., n, n-1, ..., 2, 1 separated by one background pixel and wrapped row-major across the input width
annotation.grid_shape: input width, minimum height needed for the wrapped sequence

references.docstring:
Compact the checkerboard's moving color toward the edge marked by the teal pixel, leaving a maroon swept trail on the marker line.

Input structure
- A blue/black checkerboard with exactly one teal marker replacing a blue pixel on a non-corner edge.
- The marker's checkerboard parity identifies the moving color (blue); the opposite parity is background (black).

Rule
- If the marker is on the left or right edge, compact moving-color pixels in every row toward that side.
- If the marker is on the top or bottom edge, compact moving-color pixels in every column toward that side.
- Preserve the teal marker at its edge cell.
- On the marker's row or column, color cells swept by shifted moving pixels maroon unless the final compacted line occupies them.

Key insight
The marker selects both the compression direction and the checkerboard color class that moves; maroon records the movement trail only along that marked line.

annotation.src: moving-color pixels of the two-color checkerboard; the teal edge marker identifies the moving-color parity
annotation.path: straight along each row toward a left/right marker edge, or along each column toward a top/bottom marker edge
annotation.trajectory: stably compact all moving-color pixels to the marker edge in every parallel line
annotation.transform: preserve the teal marker at its edge cell; on the marker row or column recolor swept vacated cells maroon unless occupied by the final compacted line

references.docstring:
Combine the left, middle, and right ordered objects from three separated panels.

Input structure
- The grid is three HxH panels separated by one-cell vertical separator bars.
- The background is the dominant color, and each panel contains exactly three same-color 4-connected foreground objects.

Rule
- Build a new HxH background canvas.
- From the left panel copy its leftmost object, from the middle panel copy its middle object, and from the right panel copy its rightmost object.

Key insight
- The separator bars create three aligned layers, and the panel's own left-to-right object order selects which object survives in the merged output.

annotation.src: three divider-separated square panels, each with three 4-connected same-color objects ordered left-to-right
annotation.dst: compose the selected objects onto one square output canvas at their original panel coordinates
annotation.transform: copy object 1 from panel 1, object 2 from panel 2, and object 3 from panel 3; discard the other objects and separator columns
annotation.grid_shape: 3 HxH panels with two separator columns -> HxH output

references.docstring:
Complete the sparse colored marker pattern by reflecting it across a full-row/full-column cross.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background and one non-background cross color that
fills exactly one complete row and one complete column. All other foreground
pixels are sparse markers away from that cross.

Rule
Keep the input unchanged, and for each marker pixel copy its color to the
positions obtained by reflecting it across the cross row, across the cross
column, and across both axes. Reflected positions outside the grid are
clipped.

Key insight
The full cross is not a copied object; it is the pair of mirror axes for
completing the quadrant pattern.

annotation.src: sparse non-background marker pixels on one side of a full-row/full-column cross
annotation.dst: their mirror positions across the cross row and cross column
annotation.transform: copy each marker color to its horizontal, vertical, and double-reflection positions; clip reflected positions outside the grid; keep the cross and originals unchanged

references.docstring:
Build a color-labeled shape-equivalence table from the objects listed on the right edge.

Input structure:
- The background contains one main 4-connected object for each foreground color.
- The rightmost column has one singleton pixel of each foreground color, listed top-to-bottom.
- Those singleton pixels define the row and column order of the output table.

Rule:
- Normalize each main object to its tight mask and compare masks up to rotation or reflection.
- Draw 2x2 color labels across the top and down the left, separated by one background row/column.
- For each off-diagonal table cell, paint a 2x2 red block when the two labeled objects have the same shape under rotation/reflection, otherwise paint a 2x2 grey block.
- Leave diagonal cells and all separators as background.

Key insight:
- Object positions and original orientations are distractors; the relation is dihedral shape equivalence, while the right-edge legend fixes the table order.

annotation.src: main colored objects plus right-edge singleton color legend
annotation.dst: 2x2-labeled pairwise relation table in legend order
annotation.transform: normalize each object's mask; red-fill off-diagonal table cells for object pairs with the same shape under rotation/flip, grey-fill all other off-diagonal cells; diagonal cells and separators remain background
annotation.grid_shape: square table with side length 3 * legend length + 2

references.docstring:
Decode a block-grid image by swapping each sprite-coded cell with a solid cell and each blank cell with the sprite.

Input structure
The grid is partitioned by black separator rows and columns into equal-size
square blocks. Each block is either a copy of one two-color sprite or a
uniform blank block of the sprite's minority color; grey pixels are erased
cells that act as wildcards.

Rule
Infer the repeated sprite from fully visible mixed-color blocks. Replace a
block matching that sprite, ignoring grey erasures, with a solid block of
the sprite's majority color. Replace a uniform blank block with the sprite.
Separator rows and columns, including grey erasures on them, become black.

Key insight
The small sprite is a block-level code for one macro-cell state, and the
uniform minority-color block is the other state; the output renders the
opposite code in each macro-cell while cleaning erased pixels.

annotation.src: regular block grid separated by black lines; each block is either a two-color sprite or a uniform blank block, with grey pixels as erasures
annotation.dst: same block grid with the two block states swapped
annotation.transform: infer the sprite from fully visible mixed-color blocks; sprite-coded blocks become solid majority-color blocks, blank blocks become the sprite, and separator/erasure pixels become black

references.docstring:
Recover each partially hidden 6x6 ring sprite and stack complete copies from top layer to bottom layer.

Input structure:
- The dominant color is the background.
- Several non-background colors are visible fragments of the same 12-pixel
  outline ring in a 6x6 box; small off-template marker pixels are noise.
- Ring fragments overlap, so upper rings replace some expected pixels of
  lower rings, and a ring may also be clipped by the input boundary.

Rule:
- Identify every substantial color whose pixels all lie on one translated
  copy of the ring template.
- For each missing in-bounds template pixel, the color currently occupying
  that pixel is above the hidden ring.
- Topologically sort these occlusion relations from top to bottom, then draw
  one complete 6x6 ring for each color in that order on a background canvas.

Key insight:
- The output is not a crop of the scene; it is the layer stack of complete
  ring sprites reconstructed from their visible fragments.

annotation.src: visible fragments of overlapping 6x6 outline-ring sprites; sparse off-template colors are marker noise
annotation.dst: vertical stack of one completed ring sprite per recovered color
annotation.transform: complete every fragment to the 12-pixel ring template using the input background
annotation.multi_step: order sprites from top layer to bottom layer: if a color occupies another sprite's expected ring pixel, it is placed earlier
annotation.grid_shape: 6 columns; height is 6 times the number of recovered ring sprites

references.docstring:
Summarize the foreground line objects as ordered horizontal color stripes.

Input structure:
- A dominant background fills a rectangular grid.
- Each non-background color forms one contiguous one-cell-thick line segment.
- The line segments have distinct topmost rows, and there are at most five of
  them.

Rule:
- Sort the foreground colors by the topmost row occupied by their line
  segment.
- Create a 5x3 output filled with the background color.
- Place one solid 1x3 row for each foreground color, preserving that
  top-to-bottom order and padding any unused rows above with background.

Key insight: The exact line length and slope do not matter; only the
vertical order of the colored line segments is encoded in the output stack.

annotation.src: same-color foreground line segments on the background
annotation.dst: stack as 3-pixel horizontal rows in a 5x3 output, ordered by each segment's topmost row
annotation.transform: replace each segment with a solid row of its color and top-pad unused rows with background
annotation.grid_shape: 16x16 input becomes 5x3 output

references.docstring:
Complete the sparse-color reflected copy of the foreground motif across its matching marker row or column.

Input structure
- The grid has one background color and two foreground colors.
- One foreground color appears only as a sparse marker row or column.
- The other foreground color contains the same sparse marker positions on a parallel row or column, plus the motif on the far side of the sparse markers.

Rule
- Keep the original grid unchanged.
- Reflect every motif pixel of the larger foreground color across the two parallel marker lines.
- Paint the reflected motif pixels with the sparse marker color.

Key insight
- The two equal marker rows or columns are paired landmarks: the sparse-color marker line borders the source motif, and the matching source-color marker line anchors the reflected copy.

annotation.src: larger foreground color: motif on one side of a sparse marker row or column, plus a matching marker line
annotation.dst: background cells beyond the matching source-color marker line
annotation.transform: reflect the motif across the pair of parallel marker lines and recolor it to the sparse marker color; keep all original pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Mark each arrow-like sprite's pointed frame endpoint with its color and the opposite endpoint black.

Input structure:
- The grid has a one-pixel solid rectangular frame around a dominant interior background.
- Inside the frame are monochrome six-pixel sprites shaped as asymmetric T arrows.
- Each sprite has a length-4 bar and a length-3 crossbar one cell closer to the pointed end.

Rule:
- For each sprite, follow its bar axis from the shorter end to the frame.
- Paint that frame endpoint with the sprite color.
- Paint the opposite endpoint on the same row or column black.
- Leave the interior background, sprites, and all other frame pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- The direction is encoded by the crossbar's off-center position: the nearer end is the pointing end.

annotation.src: monochrome six-pixel asymmetric T sprites inside a solid frame
annotation.path: orthogonal ray from each sprite's shorter bar end to the frame, plus the opposite ray on the same row or column
annotation.trajectory: paint the pointed frame endpoint with the sprite color and the opposite frame endpoint black
annotation.transform: leave the sprites, background, and other frame pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Recover the bottom-to-top stacking order of overlaid rectangular color frames.

Input structure:
- The background is one color, and every foreground color is a one-cell-thick rectangular frame.
- Overlapping frame pixels show only the color of the frame that is highest at that location.

Rule:
- Reconstruct each frame as the border of the bounding box of its visible pixels.
- At every cell covered by multiple reconstructed frames, the visible frame color is above the other frames covering that cell.
- Return the unique bottom-to-top order of frame colors as a single-column grid.

Key insight:
The hidden parts of each frame do not need to be seen directly; the visible pixels reveal the full frame bbox, and overlap cells reveal the layer constraints.

annotation.src: overlaid one-cell-thick rectangular frames on the background
annotation.dst: single-column list of frame colors ordered from bottom layer to top layer
annotation.transform: reconstruct each frame from its visible-pixel bbox; at each frame intersection the visible color is above the other frames covering that pixel, then output the unique layer order
annotation.grid_shape: HxW input -> N x 1 output, one row per frame

references.docstring:
Project the framed periodic stripe pattern across the canvas and erase the unused frame cells.

Input structure
- A bg canvas with a one-cell-thick rectangular frame of one color.
- Inside the frame are two parallel full-interior marker bars of another color.
- A third color fills the region between the marker bars on periodically spaced rows or columns.

Rule
- Infer the periodic row or column mask from the third-color stripes inside the frame.
- Paint the frame color along those full rows or columns, extended to the grid boundary.
- Extend the marker bars across the full canvas and repaint the source-color stripe cells between them.

Key insight
- The outer frame is not preserved as a border; it supplies the color for the periodic stripes selected by the inner source pattern.

annotation.src: one-color rectangular frame, two parallel full-interior marker bars, and periodic source-color stripes between the bars
annotation.dst: same-size bg canvas with marker bars extended and the periodic stripe mask projected across the full grid
annotation.transform: infer the source stripe period along the axis perpendicular to the marker bars; paint those whole rows or columns with the frame color, extend the marker bars across the canvas, and repaint source-color cells between the bars

references.docstring:
Extend the edge-touching green start bar through the corridor, turning at each teal blocker until the path leaves the grid.

Input structure:
- The background is the most common color.
- Exactly two foreground colors are present: a 2-pixel 4-connected start bar and many blocker pixels.
- Exactly one pixel of the start bar lies on the grid border.

Rule:
- Start from the border pixel of the bar and move through the other bar pixel into the grid.
- Paint every traversed non-blocker pixel with the start color.
- When the next cell is a blocker, turn to the unique perpendicular non-blocker neighbor; when the next cell is outside the grid, stop.

Key insight: The blocker pixels define a one-cell-wide corridor, so every interior collision has exactly one valid 90-degree turn.

annotation.src: 2-pixel start bar with one endpoint on the grid border
annotation.path: continue from the border endpoint through the other endpoint; move straight through non-blocker cells, turn at each blocker to the unique perpendicular non-blocker neighbor, and stop when the next step would leave the grid
annotation.trajectory: paint every visited non-blocker pixel with the start-bar color
annotation.transform: keep blocker pixels and existing start pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Drop every large foreground object straight down to the bottom while leaving small marker objects fixed.

Input structure:
- The grid has a dominant background color and exactly one foreground color.
- The foreground is split into separated 4-connected objects.
- Objects of area at most three are stationary markers; larger objects are moving sprites.

Rule:
- Clear each moving sprite from its original position.
- Translate each moving sprite vertically downward until its bbox bottom reaches the grid bottom.
- Repaint each translated sprite in its original color; small markers stay unchanged.

Key insight:
- Object area separates the active falling sprites from the small fixed markers, and all active sprites follow the same vertical path.

annotation.src: 4-connected foreground objects with area greater than three pixels
annotation.path: vertical downward ray in the object's original columns until its bbox bottom touches the grid bottom
annotation.trajectory: translate the whole object once without changing shape or color
annotation.transform: clear moved objects at their original positions; leave foreground objects of area at most three pixels fixed

references.docstring:
Rebuild the foreground rectangles as a largest-to-smallest lower-left nesting.

Input structure
- A periodic wallpaper background is overlaid by foreground colors that each form a rectangular frame or solid rectangle.
- The largest foreground rectangle is the output frame; smaller foreground rectangles are the objects to nest inside it.
- A frame may be partially hidden by a smaller rectangle, but its visible pixels still determine its bbox.

Rule
- Ignore the wallpaper and crop the result to the largest foreground rectangle's bbox size.
- Sort foreground rectangles by bbox area from largest to smallest.
- Reconstruct each frame or solid rectangle, placing every next smaller rectangle in the lower-left of the current rectangle's usable region.

Key insight
- The scattered background colors are not objects; the meaningful order is the unique descending rectangle size chain, and each step nests into the previous rectangle's lower-left interior.

annotation.src: foreground rectangular frames and solid rectangles over periodic wallpaper
annotation.dst: nested lower-left inside the largest foreground rectangle
annotation.transform: discard the wallpaper; sort rectangles by bbox area descending; rebuild each frame or solid rectangle, placing each next smaller rectangle at the lower-left of the current frame interior or solid bbox
annotation.grid_shape: crop to the largest foreground rectangle bbox

references.docstring:
Remove the left control column and roll the remaining image downward by the red marker's row.

Input structure
- The input is a rectangular grid with a one-cell-wide control column on the left.
- That control column is all pink except for exactly one red marker pixel.
- The columns to the right are the image that remains in the output.

Rule
- Delete the left control column.
- Let r be the row index of the red marker in that column.
- Cyclically shift the remaining image downward by r rows.

Key insight
- The red marker's vertical position encodes the row-roll amount; the pink
  column is only a control strip and is removed after reading it.

annotation.src: image rows to the right of a pink control column with one red marker
annotation.dst: same-height output with rows cyclically ordered by the marker row
annotation.transform: delete the control column; cyclically roll the remaining rows downward by the red marker's row index
annotation.symbol_instructions: pink control column encodes a cyclic row shift; the red marker row gives the shift offset
annotation.grid_shape: height preserved, width minus one

references.docstring:
Cast yellow horizontal and vertical rays from the teal rectangle until blue blockers stop them.

Input structure:
- A black-background grid containing one solid teal rectangle.
- Blue objects are blockers; other non-background objects may lie in the ray paths.
- Yellow is absent from the input and is the output paint color.

Rule:
- From every row of the teal rectangle, cast rays left and right to the grid edge.
- From every column of the teal rectangle, cast rays up and down to the grid edge.
- A ray stops before a blue pixel; all crossed non-blue, non-teal pixels become yellow.

Key insight:
The teal rectangle defines a full cross-shaped projection, while blue objects are walls and red/background cells are simply paintable space.

annotation.src: the solid teal rectangular object
annotation.path: cast horizontal rays from each source row and vertical rays from each source column; stop at a blue object or the grid edge
annotation.trajectory: paint every crossed non-blue, non-teal pixel yellow
annotation.transform: preserve the teal source and blue blockers; leave all off-ray pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Fill the small background compartments bounded by the long contour color.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color and two foreground colors.
- The more frequent foreground color forms long 8-connected contour fragments.
- The other foreground color is a fixed distractor/obstacle color that partitions
  the background but is never recolored.

Rule:
- Split the background into 4-connected regions using all foreground pixels as
  barriers.
- Keep the two largest background regions as the outside of the contour drawing.
- Recolor every other background region that touches a long contour component
  to the contour color; leave all foreground pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
The apparent area fill is exactly a component-level fill of bounded background
compartments, not a row-wise interpolation between individual contour pixels.

annotation.src: 4-connected background regions partitioned by long 8-connected contour-color components and obstacle-color pixels
annotation.transform: recolor each non-exterior background region touching a long contour component to the contour color; keep the two largest background regions and all foreground pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Advance short marker bars away from the full edge bar, turning completed two-pixel markers into edge-color marks at the opposite side.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One non-background color forms a complete one-cell-thick bar on exactly one outer edge.
- The other foreground color appears only in the first two cells inward from that bar, lane by lane.

Rule
- In each lane perpendicular to the edge bar, a one-pixel marker adjacent to the bar grows one more cell inward.
- A two-pixel marker in those first two inward cells is cleared back to background.
- The cleared two-pixel marker is replaced by a two-pixel mark of the edge-bar color at the opposite side of the same lane.

Key insight
- The full edge bar defines both the orientation and the direction of the local two-step marker cycle.

annotation.src: one-pixel and two-pixel marker bars in lanes perpendicular to a complete edge bar
annotation.transform: extend one-pixel markers one cell inward; clear two-pixel markers to bg and write a two-pixel edge-color mark at the opposite side of the same lane

references.docstring:
Recolor the row-wise passage indicated by wall pixels with the singleton marker color.

Input structure:
- A dominant background contains one singleton marker pixel and one wall color.
- Wall pixels lie on several rows and form left/right limits around the marker column.
- Empty rows between the top and bottom wall rows are open horizontal passages.

Rule:
- On a wall row, paint background pixels between the nearest wall strictly
  left of the marker column and the nearest wall at or right of it; if only
  one side is present, paint from that wall to the opposite grid edge.
- On empty rows between the top and bottom wall rows, paint the whole row.
- On empty rows outside the wall-row band, reuse the nearest end wall-row interval.
- Preserve wall pixels and the original marker pixel.

Key insight:
- The wall color defines scanline limits relative to the marker column; the
  marker color fills those implied horizontal spans rather than flood-filling
  through connected background.

annotation.src: one singleton marker pixel and rows of wall-color pixels on a dominant background

references.docstring:
Draw a blue folded corner-to-corner route through the lone marker's column.

Input structure:
- A rectangular grid filled with one background color.
- Exactly one non-background marker pixel; blue is absent from the input.

references.docstring:
Extract the color of each noisy block in a row/column lattice and mirror the coarse grid horizontally.

Input structure:
- A background surrounds a rectangular lattice of monochrome foreground blocks.

- Consecutive columns in a lattice band share the same set of visible foreground colors.

references.docstring:
Drop the moving-color objects downward until they rest above a one-row cushion before the obstacle or bottom edge.

references.docstring:
Translate the colored objects into the most balanced complete rectangular frame.

references.docstring:
Crop the largest object and overlay each smaller sprite where its shared marker pattern matches.

references.docstring:

- A vertical bar's height is also the width it occupies after rotation, so the chain follows immediate horizontal contact after each rotated bar.

references.docstring:

moving left, then moving upward. For each block, send its top-left,

Keep the largest 8-connected motif and replace the corner/control pixels with a solid corner triangle.

- Count the non-corner control pixels; that count is the triangle side.

references.docstring:
Extend each colored domino marker into a full row or column bar, with horizontal bars covering vertical bars at crossings.

- Paint each marked row entirely with the color of its horizontal domino marker.

- The two-pixel orientation is the instruction: horizontal markers emit row bars, vertical markers emit column bars, and the only layering cue is row-over-column.

references.docstring:
Recolor the sparse foreground pixels in scan order along their longer spread, cycling red, teal, and grey.

Rule:

- If the foreground bbox is at least as tall as it is wide, order foreground pixels row-major; otherwise order them column-major.
- Recolor the ordered pixels by repeating red, teal, grey from the first pixel onward.

Key insight:
- The original foreground colors are only markers; the output color depends on each marker's ordinal position in the dominant scan direction.

references.docstring:

- Stop a ray when it reaches an existing interior foreground pixel; keep the frame and all original colored pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The diamond frame defines a strict interior, while the side markers are column or row emitters whose color fills the visible interior interval until blocked.

annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel strictly inside the diamond along the ray with the marker color

references.docstring:
Drop the columns of the top marker downward, stopping blue-ended columns on grey obstacles and letting maroon-ended columns pass to the bottom.

- The background is the dominant color.
- The most numerous non-background color forms stationary grey obstacle pixels.
- The other two colors form a single 3x3 top-edge marker whose top two rows
  are maroon and whose bottom row contains maroon or blue control pixels.

- Erase the top marker.
- Treat each marker column as a vertical drop retaining its three colors.
- A column whose bottom control pixel is blue stops immediately above the
  first grey pixel below that column, or bottom-aligns if none exists.

  through the cycle green, yellow, black, grey, red, teal, maroon, pink, blue.
- Fill every pixel of the original grid by this distance-indexed cycle.

Key insight: The output is not copied from existing objects; it is the
distance field around the single marker, colored by a cyclic palette that
excludes the orange background.

annotation.dst: entire grid as concentric Manhattan-distance rings centered on the marker
annotation.transform: use the marker color at distance 0, then advance one step per Manhattan distance through the fixed cycle green, yellow, black, grey, red, teal, maroon, pink, blue

references.docstring:
Recover the repeating background pattern hidden under the largest solid rectangle.

Input structure:
- The grid is covered by a small row/column periodic pattern.
- Several non-pattern colors form solid rectangular foreground objects that
  overwrite the pattern.
- The requested output region is the largest of those solid rectangles.

Rule:
- Find every 4-connected monochromatic object whose bounding box is a filled
  rectangle with both dimensions greater than one.
- Treat those rectangles as masks, infer the smallest repeating tile that is
  consistent with all remaining visible pixels, and repaint the largest
  rectangle's coordinates with that tile.

Key insight: The rectangle colors are occluders; the visible pixels outside
them are enough to reconstruct the original periodic background underneath.

annotation.dst: region covered by the largest solid rectangular occluder
annotation.transform: infer the minimal repeating tile from unoccluded pixels and output the tile values that would occupy the largest rectangle's coordinates
annotation.grid_shape: same shape as the largest rectangle

references.docstring:
Fill each centered square ring with the color of the marker at that ring distance.

Input structure
The input is an odd square grid with a dominant background color and one
non-background marker for every Chebyshev distance from the grid center.
Rule
The output replaces the background with concentric square rings centered on
the middle cell; every cell at distance d from the center takes the color of
the unique marker whose distance from the center is d.
Key insight
The scattered markers are not objects to move; their Chebyshev distances
form a palette for the centered square rings.

annotation.dst: centered square ring region d
annotation.match_cond: s.chebyshev_distance_to_grid_center == d.ring_radius
annotation.transform: fill every pixel in d with s.color

references.docstring:
Summarize the enclosed table slots by the single object color inside each slot, using the slot background color for empty slots.

Input structure
- The most common color forms the outer background and all enclosed slot
  backgrounds.
- The enclosed background components form a complete rectangular array of
  slots, ordered by their positions.
- Each slot contains either no other color or exactly one object color.

Rule
- Find all 4-connected components of the most common color that do not touch
  the input edge.
- Sort their bounding boxes into row and column order to define the output
  table.
- For each slot, output its unique non-background color if present; otherwise
  output the background color.

Key insight
- The large grid is an expanded table: the enclosed background components are
  the cells, and any colored object drawn inside a cell is that cell's summary
  value.

annotation.transform: collapse each slot to one output pixel in row/column order: use the contained object color if present, otherwise use the background color
annotation.grid_shape: number of slot rows x number of slot columns

references.docstring:
Recolor each framed interior mask with the color from the next red frame clockwise around the blue connector cycle.

Input structure
- The grid contains hollow red square frames connected pairwise by blue line components.
- The blue components connect the frames into one cycle, with every frame touching exactly two blue components.
- Each frame interior contains background plus exactly one non-background color mask.

Rule
- Sort the red frames clockwise by their centers around the cycle.
- Keep each frame's interior mask shape in place, but recolor it with the interior color from the next clockwise frame.
- Leave the red frames, blue connectors, background, and interior background holes unchanged.

Key insight
- The colored masks do not move; the blue cycle gives the order in which their colors rotate.

annotation.dst: the interior foreground mask of each red frame in the same clockwise frame order
annotation.match_cond: source color at clockwise rank k recolors destination mask at rank k-1, wrapping around the cycle
annotation.transform: recolor each destination mask in place; keep mask shapes, frame borders, blue connectors, and background unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor each placeholder object according to its normalized shape while leaving the background fixed.

Input structure
A same-size grid with one dominant background color and one foreground
placeholder color forming separated 4-connected objects.

Rule
Replace every placeholder object by the color assigned to its exact
translation-normalized mask; all background pixels remain unchanged.

Key insight
The input objects are a shape legend with repeated instances: identical
masks always receive identical colors, independent of their position.

annotation.src: 4-connected placeholder-color foreground objects on a dominant background
annotation.transform: recolor each object by exact translation-normalized mask: right-elbow triomino -> yellow, stair tetromino -> teal, plus pentomino -> green, 3-vertical bar -> red, 2-vertical bar -> maroon, 2x3 rectangle -> grey; leave background unchanged

references.docstring:
Mirror the smallest non-axis foreground color across the full straight axis.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One foreground color forms exactly one full row, column, main diagonal, or anti-diagonal reflection axis.
- The remaining foreground colors include a unique least-populated color to copy.

Rule
- Preserve the input grid.
- Select every pixel of the unique smallest non-axis foreground color.
- Reflect those pixels across the full straight axis and paint the reflected positions with the same color.

Key insight
- The axis color marks the mirror line, while the color population chooses which set of objects is duplicated.

annotation.dst: same canvas with the least-populated non-axis color mask completed across the axis
annotation.transform: mirror every pixel of the unique least-populated non-axis color across the row, column, main-diagonal, or anti-diagonal axis; leave all original pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Grow an alternating pink/orange triangular trace downward from the horizontal orange seed row.

Input structure:
- The grid has a green background and one horizontal row containing all orange foreground pixels.
- The seed row may contain isolated orange pixels and adjacent orange runs.
- Pink is absent from the input and is used for the first generated row.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- Two rows below the current active row, place a child pixel between each active pair
  whose middle cell in the current row is background.
- Alternate generated row colors between pink and orange, stopping when no children
  can be generated or the next row would leave the grid.

Key insight:
- Only an active-background-active triplet in the current row reproduces; contiguous
  active runs do not produce children through occupied middle cells.

annotation.src: horizontal orange seed row on green background
annotation.transform: copy the input; every two rows downward, fill each green midpoint of an active-background-active triplet in the previous active row, alternating new rows pink then orange until no triplet remains

references.docstring:
Convert each hollow 3x3 symbol to one pixel and slide the pixels clockwise from the marked edge.

Input structure
- The grid has a background, one full-edge marker line, and monochrome hollow 3x3 foreground symbols.
- The symbols lie on a coarse row/column lattice; fully empty lattice rows or columns are absent from the output.

Rule
- Replace each hollow 3x3 symbol with one pixel of its color in the corresponding coarse-grid cell.
- The marker edge gives the compaction direction by clockwise border travel: top -> right, right -> down, bottom -> left, left -> up.
- Preserve the order of non-background pixels while sliding them as far as possible in that direction.

Key insight
- The large picture is a scaled symbolic grid, and the blue edge marker acts as a gravity direction rather than as output content.

annotation.src: hollow 3x3 foreground symbols collapsed to one coarse-grid pixel each; the full-edge blue marker selects the path direction
annotation.path: straight along each coarse row or column in clockwise border direction from the marker edge: top->right, right->down, bottom->left, left->up; stop when packed against the boundary or previous pixel
annotation.trajectory: stably compact all non-background coarse pixels in each parallel line, preserving their order
annotation.transform: discard the blue marker and fully empty coarse rows or columns; replace each hollow 3x3 symbol by its color
annotation.grid_shape: occupied coarse lattice after empty rows or columns are dropped

references.docstring:
Render the filled-square object counts as compact nested stacks ordered by count rank.

Input structure
A large noisy grid has a dominant background, scattered non-square noise, and
filled monochrome square objects. Each square side length has exactly one
object color, and side lengths form consecutive sizes.

Rule
Ignore non-square components. If the lowest square in the scene is of the
smallest side length, treat that one smallest square as a distractor and do
not count it. For count rank k from left to right, create one block from all
square sizes with at least k remaining objects; draw larger squares first and
smaller squares over their upper-left corner, then append one background
separator column.

Key insight
The output is a count histogram of square side lengths, but each histogram
slot is rendered as nested upper-left square masks using the side colors.

annotation.src: filled monochrome square objects s, grouped by side length after ignoring non-square noise and the lowest square when it is smallest
annotation.dst: left-to-right count-rank stack slots d
annotation.match_cond: a side group s contributes to slot d_k iff count(s) >= k
annotation.transform: draw each slot as nested upper-left square masks, larger sides first; append one bg separator column after every slot
annotation.grid_shape: height is largest side + 1; width is sum of slot widths plus one separator per slot

references.docstring:
Slide each black border rectangle to the opposite border, recoloring its swept stripe orange and leaving the rectangle black at the far edge.

Input structure
- The grid contains black rectangular 4-connected masks, each touching exactly one outer border.
- Grey cells form incidental pattern content; orange is the trail color used when a black mask slides.

Rule
- Treat all black rectangles as moving simultaneously.
- A rectangle touching the top or bottom edge moves vertically to the opposite edge in the same columns.
- A rectangle touching the left or right edge moves horizontally to the opposite edge in the same rows.
- Recolor the complete swept row or column stripe to orange, then stamp every destination rectangle in black.

Key insight
- Edge contact gives the slide direction; the output is the set of opposite-edge black rectangles plus their orange trails.

annotation.src: black rectangular mask s touching exactly one outer border
annotation.path: straight slide from s to the opposite border along its row band or column band, determined by the touched border
annotation.trajectory: recolor the complete swept row/column stripe orange, then place s at the opposite edge
annotation.transform: all black masks move simultaneously; destination black masks overwrite orange trails and any grey cells, while cells outside swept stripes remain unchanged

references.docstring:
Move every object above the solid bottom stripe upward by its own pixel count.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, exactly one full-width non-background row
that acts as a fixed stripe, and one or more 4-connected monochrome objects
above that stripe.

Rule
Clear each object from its original cells, then translate it straight upward
by the number of pixels in that object, preserving its shape and color. Leave
the full-width stripe unchanged.

Key insight
Each object's area is also its vertical displacement; the full-width row is a
fixed baseline, not a moving object.

annotation.src: each 4-connected monochrome foreground object s above the full-width bottom stripe
annotation.path: straight upward by s.area rows
annotation.trajectory: move only s to the endpoint, preserving its shape and color
annotation.transform: clear s.old cells to background; keep the bottom stripe unchanged

references.docstring:
Fill the background under a top-row red/grey span with a shrinking diagonal pattern that alternates red and grey.

Input structure:
- The grid has an orange background.
- All foreground pixels are red or grey and lie on the top row.
- The first and last top-row foreground pixels define an odd-width span.

Rule:
- Copy the input grid.
- For row r below the top, fill columns span_left + r through span_right - r.
- Each filled cell takes the top-row color r columns up-left, flipped red<->grey once per row step.

Key insight:
- The output is the top-row span propagated down-right along diagonals, while the allowable region shrinks inward from both ends each row.

annotation.src: red/grey foreground pixels on the top row; first and last foreground pixels define the span
annotation.transform: copy the input; fill row r inside span_left+r..span_right-r by copying the top-row color r columns up-left with red/grey flipped each step

references.docstring:
Extract the hidden two-color image by compacting the rows and columns of its complete mask.

Input structure
The grid contains one pair of colors whose pixels occupy every cell in the
cross product of their active rows and active columns; all other colors form
the surrounding filler or separators.
Rule
Find that unique color pair, keep exactly the rows and columns touched by
the pair, and return the induced subgrid.
Key insight
The target image is not chosen by color id; it is the only two-color mask
whose occupied pixels form a full rectangular row/column product after
deleting unused rows and columns.

annotation.src: unique two-color mask whose pixels fill the cross product of its active rows and active columns
annotation.transform: delete every row and column not touched by that mask, preserving the induced two-color subgrid
annotation.grid_shape: active mask rows x active mask columns

references.docstring:
Transfer each colored marker to its adjacent neutral mask component, then erase the markers.

Input structure
- The background is the most common color.
- The neutral mask color is the unique most frequent foreground color.
- Other foreground colors are marker pixels that may touch neutral 4-connected mask components.
Rule
- Remove every marker pixel by recoloring it to the background.
- For each 4-connected neutral mask component, find marker colors touching it by edge adjacency.
- If a component touches one marker color, recolor the whole neutral component to that marker color.
- If a component touches no marker color, leave it neutral.
Key insight
- Marker pixels label neighboring neutral regions but are not part of the final colored objects.

annotation.src: neutral 4-connected mask components plus non-neutral marker pixels on the background
annotation.transform: erase all marker pixels to bg; recolor each neutral component by the unique marker color touching it by edge adjacency; preserve unlabeled neutral components

references.docstring:
Expand each 3-pixel L marker into a same-color corner L on an empty background.

Input structure
- The grid is an odd square with one dominant background color.
- Every foreground object is a monochromatic 4-connected 3-pixel L inside a
  2x2 box.

Rule
- Clear the grid to the background.
- For each marker, map its L orientation to the corresponding outer corner
  and draw that corner L in the marker color with arm length half the grid.

Key insight
- The small marker is a miniature corner; its orientation, not its position,
  chooses which outer corner receives the expanded L.

annotation.src: 3-pixel L marker object s in a 2x2 bbox
annotation.dst: outer corner L region d with half-grid arm length
annotation.match_cond: s.orientation == d.corner_orientation
annotation.transform: clear grid to bg and paint d with s.color

references.docstring:
Swap each 5x5 sprite with its corner marker color and stamp same-marker composite masks into the matching corner.

Input structure:
- A 30x30 grid has one dominant background color.
- Non-background corner pixels are marker labels.
- Every other foreground color is the body of one 5x5 sprite containing exactly one pixel of a corner marker color.

Rule:
- For each sprite, recolor body pixels to the sprite marker color and recolor the marker pixel back to its body color.
- If a marker lies on the side facing its matching corner and another same-marker sprite has a body pixel at that same local cell, use that visible body color for the marker pixel.
- For each corner marker, overlay the masks of all sprites with that marker color into the corner 5x5 block and paint the visible composite with the marker color.

Key insight:
The corner pixels are labels that group 5x5 sprites by their embedded marker color; each labeled corner shows the grouped sprite silhouette.

annotation.src: 5x5 sprite s with one body color and one corner-marker control pixel
annotation.dst: corner 5x5 block d marked by a corner control pixel
annotation.match_cond: s.control_color == d.corner_marker_color
annotation.transform: swap s.body_color and s.control_color in place; paint d with the visible overlay of all matched s.foreground masks using d.marker_color
annotation.multi_step: side control-pixel collisions take the visible matched body color at the same local cell; one-sprite vertical tails hidden between other matched masks are omitted from the corner overlay

references.docstring:
Replace gray plus-shaped damage masks with the hidden colors of the rectilinear mosaic.

Input structure:
- Color 8 appears only as isolated 3x3 plus masks.
- The non-mask pixels are visible parts of a clean grid made from horizontal
  and vertical color regions.

Rule:
- Treat every color-8 pixel as unknown damage and leave all other pixels fixed.
- First copy unknown pixels from exact matching parallel rows or columns.
- Then fill any remaining mask cells from opposite-side continuations and the
  better-supported local straight edge.

Key insight:
- The gray pluses are occluders, not objects; the underlying colors are
  determined by repeated line templates and nearby axis-aligned boundaries.

annotation.src: color-8 3x3 plus masks over a rectilinear color mosaic
annotation.transform: treat color-8 pixels as hidden cells; restore each mask from matching parallel rows or columns and local straight-edge continuation, leaving all visible pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Extrapolate the moving sprite from a horizontal sequence of shared-border frames into the next standalone frame.

Input structure
- The grid is a row of equal-width framed panels sharing their vertical border columns.
- Each panel has the same fill color and one identical interior sprite at the same local columns.
- The sprite's top row changes by a constant amount from panel to panel.

Rule
- Build one output panel with the same height, frame color, fill color, and sprite.
- Continue the sprite's diagonal motion one more panel to the right.
- Because the output is a standalone panel, advance by the full panel width, not the shared-border spacing.

Key insight
- The panels are consecutive frames of motion; the output is the next frame after the sequence.

annotation.src: identical interior sprite instances inside the shared-border framed panels
annotation.path: constant diagonal motion from panel to panel, continued one more standalone panel to the right; vertical offset is scaled from shared-border spacing to full panel width and rounded to the nearest row
annotation.trajectory: stamp one copy of the sprite in the next framed panel at the extrapolated row and the same local columns
annotation.transform: discard the previous panels; draw only the new single frame with the same frame and fill colors
annotation.grid_shape: same height, width of one standalone panel

references.docstring:
Erase the top palette row and redraw it below as a widening wedge centered on its missing cell.

Input structure
- The top row is a palette row with exactly one background gap.
- Below it, the only foreground is one vertical marker bar of a single color.
- The marker bar is either in the gap column or immediately beside it.

Rule
- Clear the grid to background.
- Starting at the top of the marker bar, each next row copies one more
  column of the top-row palette on both sides of the gap.
- Fill the gap column with the marker color, and keep the vertical marker bar.

Key insight
- The lone background cell in the top row is the center of the expanding
  copy; the lower vertical bar provides the center color and the row where
  the expansion begins.

annotation.src: top palette row with one bg gap and a lower single-color marker bar
annotation.dst: widening wedge rows below the marker bar, centered on the top-row gap
annotation.transform: erase the top row; in each row from the marker top downward, copy the top-row colors within the current centered interval, replace the gap column with the marker color, and keep the marker bar

references.docstring:
Copy each foreground object anchored in a true grid corner clockwise into the next corner.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the background.
- Foreground objects are monochromatic 4-connected components.
- Relevant objects are exactly those whose bounding box touches two adjacent borders at one grid corner.

Rule
- Start from the input unchanged.
- For each corner object, copy its pixel mask and color to the next corner clockwise: top-left to top-right, top-right to bottom-right, bottom-right to bottom-left, and bottom-left to top-left.
- Preserve each object's orientation by aligning its bounding box to the destination corner; stamps may overwrite existing pixels at the destination, but source pixels are not cleared.

Key insight
- Interior and side-only objects are distractors; only components actually anchored to a corner participate in the clockwise perimeter copy.

annotation.src: corner-anchored monochromatic object s
annotation.dst: next clockwise grid-corner slot d
annotation.match_cond: d.corner is the next clockwise corner after s.corner
annotation.transform: stamp s.mask with s.color aligned to d.corner, preserving orientation and leaving source pixels unless overwritten

references.docstring:
Pack all pixels into color-frequency runs along bottom-up columns.

Input structure
The input is a rectangular grid whose colors are all foreground material;
only the number of pixels of each color matters. In the observed task
instances, every present color has a distinct pixel count.

Rule
Count the pixels of each color and order the colors from most frequent to
least frequent. Rewrite a same-size grid by placing each color's full count
as one contiguous run while scanning columns from left to right and, within
each column, from bottom to top.

Key insight
The output preserves the multiset of colors but discards all original
positions, turning the grid into a frequency-sorted column packing.

annotation.src: input colors ordered from most frequent to least frequent by pixel count
annotation.dst: contiguous runs in a same-size grid scanned column-major left-to-right and bottom-to-top within each column
annotation.match_cond: the k-th ranked color fills the k-th scan-order run, with run length equal to its input pixel count
annotation.transform: discard original positions and preserve the exact pixel count of each color

references.docstring:
Rewrite a corner L block into two nested L borders and a diagonal trace.

Input structure
A rectangular grid has exactly two colors: one color forms a one-cell-thick
L on two adjacent outer edges, and the other color fills the remaining
rectangle.

Rule
Normalize the L to the top-left corner. Paint the outer top-left L with the
fill color, the next inner L with the original border color, and the main
diagonal of the remaining inner rectangle with the fill color. All other
cells become color 8, then the original orientation is restored.

Key insight
The corner of the input L determines the orientation; after flipping to a
canonical top-left L, the output is the same nested-layer pattern for every
example.
