annotation.src: two-color grid where one color forms a one-pixel L on two adjacent outer edges and the other color fills the opposite rectangle
annotation.transform: use the L corner as orientation; recolor the outer L to the fill color, draw the next inner L in the original L color, keep the fill color only on the main diagonal of the remaining inner rectangle, and recolor all other pixels to gray

references.docstring:
Recolor each side-marked multicolor object embedded in a monochrome panel to its marker color.

Input structure:
- Same-color 4-connected components form monochrome panel regions.
- The bounding box of a panel may contain 4-connected non-panel-color objects.
- A target object touches exactly one side of its panel bbox, and all of its
  pixels on that side have one marker color.

Rule:
- For every target object, fill any panel-colored holes enclosed by the object.
- Recolor the object and filled holes to the side marker color.
- Leave all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight:
- A multicolor object's single contact side identifies both which object should
  be normalized and which color should replace it.

annotation.src: 4-connected multicolor objects inside a monochrome panel bbox that touch exactly one bbox side with a single marker color
annotation.transform: fill any holes in each such object and recolor the object to its side marker color; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Fill each vertical foreground band's background cells with the color of the next band to its right.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the background.
- Each other color occupies a separate vertical band defined by that color's
  minimum and maximum columns.
- Within a band, all cells are either that band's color or background.

Rule
- Order the bands from left to right.
- In each band, replace background pixels with the color of the next band in
  that order, wrapping from the rightmost band back to the leftmost.
- Preserve all existing foreground pixels and all background pixels outside
  the bands.

Key insight
- The column bands form a cyclic palette legend: a band's gaps are completed
  by borrowing the color from its right-hand neighbor, not by changing the
  band's existing pixels.

annotation.src: foreground band colors s, one per vertical non-bg column span, ordered left-to-right
annotation.dst: background gap masks d inside the same vertical band spans, ordered left-to-right
annotation.match_cond: d_i receives color s_{i+1}; the rightmost d receives s_0
annotation.transform: paint only the matched background gaps; preserve existing foreground pixels and background separator columns

references.docstring:
Swap a connector segment with repeated marker sprites by connecting the marker anchors and stamping the sprite at the segment endpoints.

Input structure
The grid has one background color and exactly two foreground colors. One foreground color forms a single straight 8-connected segment. The other foreground color forms two or more identical centered sprites.

Rule
Build a background canvas of the same size. Draw straight connector-color segments between every pair of original sprite anchors. Then stamp the marker sprite, using its centered anchor, onto the two endpoints of the original connector segment.

Key insight
The original segment endpoints are the destinations for the repeated sprite, while the original sprite centers become the vertices of the new connector-color complete graph.

annotation.src: single straight connector segment c and repeated centered marker sprites s
annotation.path: for every pair of s.center anchors, the row/column/45-degree segment between them
annotation.trajectory: paint each full path with c.color on a background canvas
annotation.transform: erase original foreground; stamp one copy of s centered on each endpoint of c

references.docstring:
Flatten the interior object into a centered line and move the guide bars inward to bracket it.

Input structure:
- The dominant color is the background.
- One non-background guide color touches the boundary and forms exactly two full parallel bars plus a split perpendicular center bar.
- The other non-background color is a single 8-connected interior object whose area determines the flattened line length.

Rule:
- If the guide pair is vertical, make a vertical object-colored line centered between those bars; otherwise use the analogous horizontal line.
- The line length equals the number of interior object pixels and is centered on the split perpendicular guide bar.
- Rebuild the guide color as the perpendicular center bar plus two full bars immediately beside the flattened object line.

Key insight:
- The guide bars supply only the orientation and center; the interior object's pixel count supplies the length of the final one-cell-thick line.

annotation.src: same-shape grid with a boundary-touching guide color forming two full parallel bars plus a split perpendicular center bar, and one 8-connected interior object color
annotation.transform: replace the scene with the guide color as the perpendicular center bar and two adjacent bars bracketing a one-cell object-colored line; orient the line parallel to the full guide-bar pair, center it on the perpendicular bar, and set its length to the interior object area

references.docstring:
Expand the second mask into a block grid by stamping the first mask with the two payload colors.

Input structure
- A background grid has four panels separated by three full-height separator columns.
- The first two panels contain same-size binary masks; the last two contain solid same-size color squares.
Rule
- Use the second mask as an outer layout. For each foreground cell in that outer mask, place a tile equal to the first mask, coloring its foreground with the first solid-square color and its background with the second solid-square color; outer background cells become all second solid-square color.
Key insight
- The output is the Kronecker product of the two binary masks, with the two right-hand panel colors providing the palette.

annotation.src: four separator-delimited sections: inner mask, outer mask, and two solid color swatches
annotation.transform: crop both masks to their non-bg bboxes; build an N x N grid of N x N tiles where outer-mask foreground cells use the inner mask recolored with swatch1 on foreground and swatch2 on background, and outer-mask background cells are solid swatch2
annotation.grid_shape: N^2 x N^2

references.docstring:
Untangle overlapping colored rectangular frames into concentric square frames ordered by their visible crossings.

Input structure
- The background contains several one-cell-thick axis-aligned rectangular frames, one color per frame.
- Frames overlap, and the visible color at an overlap records a directed crossing from the hidden frame to the visible frame.
- Each foreground color still has visible pixels on the perimeter of its full rectangular bounding box.

Rule
- Infer each color's full rectangular frame from the bounding box of its visible pixels.
- Add a directed edge A -> B when B is visible at a crossing of A and B's frame perimeters.
- Find the unique path that visits every frame color once, then render those colors as one-pixel-thick concentric square frames from outside to inside.

Key insight
- The output is not a crop of the input; the crossing graph gives a single frame order, and that order is redrawn as nested rings.

annotation.src: overlapping one-cell-thick rectangular frames on the background
annotation.dst: concentric square frame layers from outermost to innermost
annotation.match_cond: rank(s.color in the unique directed crossing path) == rank(d from outermost to innermost)
annotation.transform: reconstruct each frame from its visible-pixel bbox; add A->B when B is visible at a crossing of the two frame perimeters; redraw each ordered color as one nested one-cell-thick ring
annotation.grid_shape: square of side 2N-1, where N is the number of frame colors

references.docstring:
Move each mirrored bottom source pixel to the far end of its trail and redraw the top half as its reflection.

Input structure
- A solid non-background row separates equal-height top and bottom halves.
- The top half has one marker color on the background.
- In the bottom half, exactly one color has positions that mirror the top markers across the separator, and the other color forms trails touching those source pixels.

Rule
- Identify the bottom source color by reflecting each bottom color into the top half and matching the top marker set.
- For every bottom source pixel, follow its unique 4-connected trail of the other bottom color to the trail endpoint.
- Clear the old top markers, bottom sources, and trails; place the source color at each endpoint and place the top marker color at the reflected endpoint.

Key insight
- The top half is only a mirror display of the bottom moving sources; the actual motion is encoded by the trail attached to each bottom source pixel.

annotation.src: bottom-half source pixels s, identified as the color whose positions reflect to the top marker mask across the separator row
annotation.path: from each s, follow its unique 4-connected trail of the other bottom color to the trail endpoint
annotation.trajectory: move s to that endpoint; clear the old source pixel and all trail pixels
annotation.transform: redraw the top marker color at the reflection of each moved source endpoint; keep the separator and background unchanged

references.docstring:
Recolor the unique safe route between the two maroon endpoints from teal to maroon.

Input structure
- A black background contains a teal 4-connected track, exactly two maroon endpoint pixels, and one or more orange blocker pixels embedded near the track.

Rule
- Treat each orange blocker and its 8-neighborhood as forbidden.
- In the remaining teal/maroon track graph, there is exactly one simple
  4-connected path between the maroon endpoints.
- Recolor teal pixels on that path to maroon; leave endpoints, blockers, and all other cells unchanged.

Key insight
- The orange pixels block nearby teal cells diagonally as well as orthogonally, which removes shorter decoy routes and makes the intended endpoint-to-endpoint path unique.

annotation.src: two maroon endpoint pixels on the teal track
annotation.path: unique shortest 4-connected route between the endpoints through teal/maroon cells after treating every orange blocker and its 8-neighborhood as forbidden
annotation.trajectory: paint the teal cells on the route maroon
annotation.transform: keep the endpoints, orange blockers, black background, and off-route teal cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Build a four-quadrant rotational tiling of the input square.

Input structure
- The input is a square grid treated as one complete sprite.

Rule
- Each output quadrant is a 2x2 repetition of a rotated copy of the whole input.
- The quadrant rotations are upper-left 180 degrees, upper-right 90 degrees
  clockwise, lower-left 90 degrees counterclockwise, and lower-right unchanged.

Key insight
- The output is a 4x4 grid of original-size blocks, not a per-pixel scale-up.

annotation.src: entire square input grid used as a sprite
annotation.dst: 4x4 grid of original-size blocks
annotation.transform: fill each 2x2 quadrant of blocks with one repeated rotation: upper-left 180 degrees, upper-right 90 degrees clockwise, lower-left 90 degrees counterclockwise, lower-right unchanged
annotation.grid_shape: input height and width multiplied by 4

tags: condition:四象限各不同旋转, quadrant_rotation

references.docstring:
Move the patterned edge band to the opposite edge along every row or column whose band slice contains the trail color.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the background.
- The two foreground colors are a frequent trail color and a rarer marker color.
- All marker pixels lie nearest to one grid edge, and that edge contains trail-color runs that define the source-band thickness.

Rule
- Choose the source edge identified by the marker pixels.
- A row or column perpendicular to that edge moves if its source-band slice contains the trail color.
- Copy that slice unchanged to the opposite edge, erase the remaining trail cells to background, and keep marker-only lines fixed.

Key insight
- The marker color identifies the active edge, while the trail color identifies which parallel rows or columns carry an edge-band slice across the grid.

annotation.src: source-edge band on the side containing all marker pixels; moving slices are rows/columns where the band contains the trail color
annotation.path: straight perpendicular path from that source edge to the opposite edge, stopping at the boundary
annotation.trajectory: copy each moving band slice unchanged to the opposite edge, preserving its order
annotation.transform: clear the old trail cells to background; rows/columns whose source slice has only marker/background remain unchanged

tags: condition:含轨迹色行列移动, trail_color_move

references.docstring:
Complete each partial marker mask by stamping the matching multicolor sprite over it.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains one or more 8-connected multicolor sprites.
- Separate target masks use colors that already occur inside one of those sprites.
- A target mask may contain only one marker pixel or several same-alignment marker pixels.

Rule
- For each multicolor sprite, test every translation that aligns a target pixel with a
  same-color sprite pixel.
- Keep the translations with maximal exact overlap against the existing target pixels,
  rejecting translations that conflict with other foreground or overlap a source sprite.
- Stamp the whole sprite at those translations; if a non-marker sprite color occurs as
  a single source pixel, consume that source-only marker back to background.

Key insight
The scattered target pixels are partial copies: their same-color overlap with a sprite
determines where the full sprite must be completed.

annotation.src: 8-connected multicolor sprite s
annotation.dst: partial target mask d of same-color marker pixels outside source sprites
annotation.match_cond: d is the maximal exact same-color overlap of s under one translation
annotation.transform: stamp full s onto d; erase any single-pixel source color not used by the matched marker mask

tags: condition:最大重叠确定位置, max_overlap_pos

references.docstring:
Move each maroon marker toward the blue rectangle and recolor the rectangle red.

Input structure
A background canvas contains one solid blue rectangular object and several isolated
maroon marker pixels. Each marker is horizontally or vertically aligned with the
rectangle and lies outside it.

Rule
Start with a background canvas, repaint the blue rectangle red, and move each
maroon marker straight toward the rectangle along its row or column. Exactly one
marker is strictly closer to the rectangle than all others and enters the
rectangle boundary; every other marker lands in the adjacent exterior cell just
outside its aligned side.

Key insight
The single entering marker is the unique global nearest marker to the rectangle,
not the nearest marker on each of the four sides.

annotation.src: isolated maroon marker pixels aligned by row or column with the solid blue rectangle
annotation.path: straight cardinal path from each marker toward its aligned rectangle side; stop on the side cell if the marker is closer than that side's span, otherwise stop in the adjacent exterior cell
annotation.trajectory: move only the marker pixel to the path endpoint
annotation.dst: blue rectangle side cell or adjacent exterior halo cell selected by the stopping rule
annotation.transform: erase the original markers and recolor the blue rectangle red

references.docstring:
Pack each solid foreground rectangle twice: wide across the top and tall from the bottom.

Input structure
The grid has one background color and one foreground color; the foreground forms
separate solid rectangles, ordered from left to right.

Rule
Build a 10-row background canvas whose width is the packed width of the wide
versions of the rectangles. For each source rectangle, paint a top-aligned
rectangle of shape min(h,w) by max(h,w), with one background column between
consecutive rectangles. Then, starting again from the left edge, paint a
bottom-aligned rectangle of shape max(h,w) by min(h,w) for each source rectangle,
again separated by one background column.

Key insight
The input rectangles are not copied in their original orientations; each object
contributes one horizontal-facing and one vertical-facing normalized rectangle,
preserving left-to-right object order.

annotation.src: solid monochromatic foreground rectangles ordered left-to-right
annotation.dst: packed upper wide slots and lower tall slots in the same left-to-right order
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d) for both the upper and lower slot sequences
annotation.transform: paint each rectangle twice: min(h,w) by max(h,w) top-aligned in the upper band, and max(h,w) by min(h,w) bottom-aligned in the lower band, with one background column between slots
annotation.grid_shape: height 10; width is the sum of max(h,w) over source rectangles plus one separator column between consecutive rectangles

tags: condition:每个矩形产生两份, each_rect_doubled

references.docstring:
Red diamond outlines contract by one layer and gray diamond outlines expand by one layer while other objects stay fixed.

Input structure
- A 16x16 orange-background grid contains one-cell-thick Manhattan-diamond outlines.
- Red and gray outlines are the changing objects; other colored diamond outlines are static.
- Some outlines may be clipped by the grid boundary, but their visible pixels still fit a clipped Manhattan-distance contour.
Rule
- Clear all red and gray pixels.
- Red objects are redrawn with the same diamond center and radius minus one.
- Gray objects are redrawn with radius plus one; an ambiguous edge-clipped growing arc continues away from the nearest perpendicular edge.
Key insight
- The task is not about moving whole objects: each changing object is a contour of a diamond, and the visible operation is one step of contour contraction or expansion.

annotation.src: red and grey 8-connected one-cell-thick Manhattan-diamond outline objects on an orange background
annotation.transform: clear each red/grey outline and redraw it from its own clipped diamond contour: red radius decreases by 1, grey radius increases by 1; preserve other colors

references.docstring:
Move each gray bar into its adjacent orange rectangle as full stripes from the contacted edge.

Input structure
- The scene uses black outside space, yellow fill, gray one-cell-thick bars, and solid orange rectangles.
- Each gray bar 4-touches exactly one orange rectangle; some orange rectangles have no touching gray bar.
- Gray bars touching the same orange rectangle all have the same orientation.

Rule
- Recolor every original gray cell to yellow.
- For each orange rectangle touched by gray bars, count the gray cells assigned to that rectangle.
- Horizontal gray bars repaint that many cells as complete orange rows starting from the contacted top or bottom row.
- Vertical gray bars repaint that many cells as complete orange columns starting from the contacted left or right column.
- Orange rectangles with no touching gray bar remain unchanged.

Key insight
- The gray pixels are not copied by shape; their count is transferred into the neighboring orange rectangle as edge-aligned row or column stripes.

annotation.src: gray one-cell-thick bars s
annotation.dst: 4-adjacent solid orange rectangles d
annotation.match_cond: s 4-touches d
annotation.transform: erase s to yellow; in each matched d, repaint |matched s cells| orange cells gray as complete rows for horizontal bars or complete columns for vertical bars from the touched edge

references.docstring:
Extend each of two aligned rectangular marker objects toward the other, filling half of the gap across the full perpendicular span.

Input structure
- A dominant background contains exactly two solid, same-sized monochromatic rectangles.
- The rectangles share either the same row span or the same column span, with a background gap between their facing edges.

Rule
- If the rectangles are side-by-side, color the left half of the inter-object gap across every row with the left object's color, and the right half with the right object's color.
- If one rectangle is above the other, color the upper half of the gap across every column with the upper object's color, and the lower half with the lower object's color.
- When the gap length is odd, leave the center row/column as background.

Key insight
- The marker objects are endpoints of an axial corridor; their own size identifies the facing edge, while the filled corridor spans the whole grid perpendicular to that axis.

annotation.src: two solid same-sized rectangular marker objects s sharing either a row span or a column span
annotation.path: straight cardinal ray from each s facing edge toward the other marker, stopping after half of the background gap; an odd middle line stays background
annotation.trajectory: paint the traversed gap rows/columns with s.color across the full grid span perpendicular to the path
annotation.transform: keep the original marker rectangles and unpainted background cells unchanged

references.docstring:
Extract the central object from the marker cluster whose markers have the same color.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background and several clusters; each cluster has four
same-color corner marker objects around one central monochromatic object.
Rule
Find every central object enclosed by four aligned corner markers of one color,
then choose the unique one whose object color equals the marker color.
Key insight
The answer is not the largest or most frequent object; it is the center of the
self-colored cluster, cropped to that object's bounding box with background kept.

annotation.src: 8-connected monochromatic central object s
annotation.dst: cluster d of four aligned same-color corner marker objects
annotation.match_cond: s is centered inside d and s.color == d.marker_color
annotation.transform: crop to s.bbox, preserving background pixels inside the bbox
annotation.grid_shape: crop to matched object bbox

tags: condition:标记色与对象同色, marker_obj_same_color

references.docstring:
Normalize the framed input motif into a 5x5 icon and stamp two copies on a 15x15 canvas.

Input structure
The input is a rounded rectangular frame: the four corners are the background
color, and every other outer-border pixel has one frame color. Non-background
pixels inside that frame are the motif to preserve.

Rule
Make a 5x5 version of the rounded frame with a 3x3 interior. Crop the input
interior motif to its bounding box, center that crop in the 3x3 interior, and
paste the resulting 5x5 icon at upper-left positions (2, 2) and (8, 8) in a
15x15 background canvas.

Key insight
The variable-size frame is only a carrier; the meaningful object is the
compact interior motif, which is normalized to the fixed 3x3 icon interior.

annotation.src: rounded rectangular outer frame with a non-background interior motif
annotation.transform: build a 5x5 rounded-frame icon from the frame color, center the interior motif bbox in its 3x3 interior, and paste two copies at fixed diagonal positions on a background canvas

tags: relation:归一化到固定尺寸, normalize_size

references.docstring:
Thicken the sparse frame and stamp the external sparse sprites into it in positional order.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background color, a regular lattice color, one large
sparse rectangular frame, and one or more external monochrome sprites whose
pixels also sit on a two-step lattice.

Rule
Use the largest sparse rectangular perimeter as the frame. Clear that frame
region and the external sprite pixels to background, draw a solid one-pixel
border in the frame color, solidify each sparse sprite into its contiguous
two-step mask, and place the sprites inside the frame with equal gaps.
Wide frames receive sprites left-to-right by source position; tall frames
receive them top-to-bottom by source position.

Key insight
The frame supplies ordered slots: the sprite-to-slot assignment is by visible
source order, not by numeric color or by matching individual cells.

annotation.src: external sparse monochrome sprites s on the two-step lattice, ordered left-to-right for a wide frame or top-to-bottom for a tall frame
annotation.dst: equal-gap interior slots d inside the large sparse rectangular frame, ordered along the frame long axis
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d)
annotation.transform: clear the original sprite pixels; replace the sparse frame by a solid one-pixel border; expand each sprite's two-step mask to a contiguous mask before stamping

references.docstring:
Drop the singleton marker into the matching red U-shaped container, or make a bottom-row puddle if no closed container is hit.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background, one singleton marker pixel on the top row,
  and one other foreground color forming vertical bars and bottom segments.
- A closed container is a U shape: two vertical side bars with a continuous
  bottom segment between them and an empty rectangular interior above the bottom.

Rule
- Remove the top marker from its original cell.
- If exactly one closed U-shaped container has the marker column within its
  horizontal footprint, fill that container's empty interior with the marker color.
- If no closed container is under the marker column, fill the whole bottom row
  with the marker color.

Key insight
- The marker does not identify a color by value; it identifies a vertical drop
  column, and only a structurally closed U shape can catch and contain the fill.

annotation.src: singleton top-row marker pixel
annotation.path: vertical drop down the marker column; a closed U-shaped wall container catches the drop when the marker column lies within its horizontal footprint, otherwise the path reaches the bottom edge
annotation.dst: closed U-shaped container interior, or the bottom row if no closed container catches the drop
annotation.trajectory: fill the caught container's background interior with the marker color; if uncaught, fill the whole bottom row
annotation.transform: erase the original marker pixel and keep all wall pixels unchanged

tags: condition:无容器则铺满底行, no_container_floor

references.docstring:
Move the lower sprite and its pink guide into the upper panel, aligning the sprite to the guide's lower-left branch.

Input structure
- The grid has one dominant background color and one full-width separator row.
- Below the separator are exactly two foreground roles: a five-pixel guide marker and one monochrome sprite.
- The guide marker has normalized shape {(0,2), (1,2), (2,0), (2,2), (3,1)} and starts immediately below the separator.

Rule
- Clear the canvas to the background, preserving the separator row.
- Translate the guide marker upward so its top row becomes row 0.
- Move the sprite, preserving its color and shape, so the sprite bbox bottom-right aligns to the translated guide's lower-left branch.

Key insight
- The marker supplies the destination anchor: its lower-left branch cell is where the moved sprite's bbox bottom-right must land.

annotation.src: monochrome sprite s below the separator
annotation.dst: translated guide marker branch anchor d in the upper panel
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox bottom-right aligns to d, the guide marker's lower-left branch after the marker shifts upward
annotation.transform: clear the lower panel; shift the five-pixel guide marker to the top; stamp s without rotation or recolor
annotation.multi_step: paint the shifted guide marker first, then stamp s so sprite pixels overwrite guide pixels on overlap

references.docstring:
Straighten the single foreground mask into a centered horizontal segment of the same color and length.

Input structure:
- The grid has one dominant background color.
- All non-background pixels share one foreground color.
- The number of foreground pixels fits in one centered row of the grid.

Rule:
- Erase the original foreground mask.
- Count its pixels, keep its color, and paint that many pixels as a horizontal segment.
- Place the segment on the middle row with equal background margin on the left and right.

Key insight:
- The original foreground shape is irrelevant except for its color and area; the output is the area normalized into the grid's central horizontal line.

annotation.src: single-color foreground mask on a dominant background
annotation.transform: erase the mask and redraw the same number of pixels in the same color as a horizontally centered segment on the middle row

references.docstring:
Let the largest center-pointing object grow outward while every other object loses its inward tip.

Input structure
- The grid has a single dominant background color and four 8-connected monochromatic foreground objects.
- The objects surround a central background gap and point toward it from cardinal directions.
- Exactly one object has the largest area.

Rule
- Find the central background gap by minimizing aggregate distance to the four objects.
- Recolor the nearest-to-center pixel of each non-largest object to background.
- Add a three-pixel cap in the largest object's color on the side away from the center, centered on the shared row or column.

Key insight
- The edit is a transfer of prominence around a common center: losers retract at their tips, and the unique largest object extends outward from the center.

annotation.src: four 8-connected monochromatic objects pointing toward a shared central bg pixel
annotation.transform: identify the unique largest object; recolor each other object's nearest-to-center tip pixel to bg and add a 3-pixel cap in the largest object's color on its side away from the center

references.docstring:
Move the colored object from the lower bracket lane to the upper bracket lane and drop it to the bottom edge.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- One frame color forms exactly two 4-connected bracket objects: a top-edge bracket open downward and a bottom-edge bracket open upward.
- One other 4-connected foreground object sits in the lower bracket's interior column span.

Rule
- Remove the movable object from its original cells.
- Keep its shape and color unchanged.
- Paste it with its bbox columns aligned to the top bracket's interior columns and with its bbox bottom aligned to the grid bottom.

Key insight
- The lower bracket identifies the object's source lane; the upper bracket provides the target lane, and the final vertical placement is bottom-aligned.

annotation.src: monochromatic foreground object s whose bbox columns match the lower bracket interior
annotation.dst: bottom-aligned slot d in the upper bracket interior column span
annotation.match_cond: s.width == d.width; lower bracket gives the source lane and upper bracket gives d.columns
annotation.transform: clear s; translate it unchanged into d with s.bbox.bottom aligned to the grid bottom

references.docstring:
Add a quantity-color label in the top marker column for each horizontal bar.

Input structure
- The grid has a black background and one non-background marker pixel in the top row.
- Below the marker row, every non-empty source row contains one solid monochrome horizontal bar to the left of the marker column.
- Source rows are staggered every other row.

Rule
- Copy the input grid.
- For each source bar, read its quantity as the bar length.
- Paint the quantity color in the marker column on the same row as the bar:
  2->1, 3->4, 4->9, 5->6.

Key insight
- The grey marker supplies the result column, while each bar supplies a small quantity with a fixed color code.

annotation.src: grey top-row marker column and lower monochrome horizontal bars on black background
annotation.transform: for each bar row, add one pixel in the marker column; its color is (n*n) mod 10 where n = min(bar length minus one, first bar row plus zero-based order among the every-other source rows)

references.docstring:
Project maroon markers into adjacent grey or pink 3x3 squares, erasing grey squares afterward.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background, solid 3x3 grey and/or pink squares, and maroon marker pixels or segments directly touching one side of exactly one square.
Rule
Grey squares are erased; their adjacent maroon markers stay in place and stamp the nearest edge cell inside the grey square. Pink squares stay pink; their adjacent maroon markers disappear and stamp the corresponding cell on the square's middle row or middle column.
Key insight
The side touched by a marker determines the projection: grey uses the near edge, while pink uses the centerline, preserving the marker's coordinate along that side.

annotation.src: maroon marker pixels or segments adjacent to solid grey or pink 3x3 square objects
annotation.transform: erase grey squares after stamping maroon into each touched near-edge cell; keep grey-adjacent markers in place; keep pink squares, remove pink-adjacent markers, and stamp their maroon cells onto the matching middle row or column of the pink square

tags: condition:颜色决定投影深度, color_det_depth

references.docstring:
Replace a corner L with a same-color right-triangle outline in the corresponding corner of an enlarged canvas.

Input structure:
- The input is a square grid with one background color and one foreground color.
- The foreground is a one-pixel-thick L inside a square bbox.
- The L touches exactly one horizontal grid edge and one vertical grid edge, identifying a corner.

Rule:
- Fill a square output canvas of side 3n-2, where n is the input side length, with the background color.
- Double the L leg length to get the triangle side length.
- Draw the two perpendicular triangle legs on the same output corner edges and connect their free endpoints with the diagonal.

Key insight:
- The input L encodes the corner, color, and side length of the triangle outline; the missing side is the diagonal between the L's two free endpoints.

annotation.src: single-color one-cell-thick L object touching one input corner
annotation.transform: replace the L with a same-color right-triangle outline in the same corner; double the L leg length and draw the missing diagonal between its free endpoints
annotation.grid_shape: square canvas of side 3n-2 (16x16 for the 6x6 inputs)

references.docstring:
Fill the one blank in each corner region so all four regions have the same color multiset.

Input structure:
- The dominant background color forms one solid separator row and one solid
  separator column.
- The separator cross splits the grid into four equal rectangular corner regions.
- Each corner region contains exactly one background-colored blank pixel.

Rule:
- Count the non-background colors in each corner region.
- The completed region multiset is defined by the maximum observed count of
  each color across the four regions.
- Replace each region's blank pixel with the single color needed to match that
  completed multiset.

Key insight:
- The separator color inside a corner region is a missing value marker; comparing
  the four regions reveals the shared multiset without using numeric color order.

annotation.src: four equal corner regions divided by a solid background cross, each with one background-colored blank pixel
annotation.transform: fill each blank with the color needed so every corner region has the same color multiset, using the maximum observed count of each color across the regions

references.docstring:
Mark the shallowest and deepest columns of a solid terrain boundary with vertical colored guide lines.

Input structure:
- The first row is a solid empty separator.
- Below it, each column consists of upper fill cells followed by a contiguous suffix of terrain cells.
- The bottom row is all terrain, so every column has a well-defined first terrain row.

Rule:
- Find the column whose first terrain row is latest; it is unique and its upper fill run becomes maroon.
- Find the rightmost column whose first terrain row is earliest; its upper fill run becomes yellow.
- Preserve the empty separator, terrain cells, and all other upper fill cells.

Key insight:
- The task is a column-height summary of the terrain profile: color the deepest upper run and the highest terrain peak.

annotation.src: columns below a solid empty top row, each with upper fill above a contiguous terrain suffix
annotation.transform: recolor the upper-fill run in the unique column with the latest terrain start to maroon; recolor the upper-fill run in the rightmost column with the earliest terrain start to yellow; preserve all other pixels

tags: condition:最深与最浅列唯一, unique_deep_shallow

references.docstring:
Recolor every target pixel by following the ordered two-column substitution legend.

Input structure
- A dominant background surrounds one multicolor vertical legend: a connected,
  fully filled two-column block with one color pair per row.
- Other non-background pixels or objects are the targets; divider or frame
  pixels are ordinary target-side structure that remain unchanged unless their
  color is rewritten by the legend.

Rule
- Read the legend rows from top to bottom as substitutions from the left
  column color to the right column color.
- For each non-background pixel outside the legend, scan those rows in order;
  whenever the current color equals the row's left color, replace it with the
  row's right color and keep scanning lower rows.
- Leave the legend itself and background pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The same color may be rewritten multiple times, but only by substitutions
  that appear later in the vertical legend, so the row order is part of the
  symbol instruction.

annotation.summary: Use the two-column legend as ordered color substitutions and recolor every non-background target pixel outside the legend.
annotation.src: non-background pixels outside the unique fully filled two-column legend
annotation.transform: replace each target pixel color with the final color reached by the ordered substitutions; keep the legend and background unchanged
annotation.symbol_instructions: the two-column legend maps each row's left color to that row's right color
annotation.multi_step: for each target pixel, scan legend rows top-to-bottom while carrying the current color, so later rows can rewrite earlier substitution results

tags: relation:图例行序决定替换, legend_row_order
condition:逐行顺序链式替换, chain_replace

references.docstring:
Move red into teal's top marker position, then move teal to the bottom outside corner of the grey rectangle.

Input structure
- The dominant background surrounds one filled rectangular non-background block.
- There is exactly one red marker and one teal marker, both in the row immediately above the rectangle.
- Both markers are horizontally aligned over columns inside the rectangle.

Rule
- Clear the original red marker.
- Recolor the original teal marker cell red.
- Place the teal marker beside the rectangle's bottom row, on the side indicated by the horizontal direction from red to teal.

Key insight
- The red-to-teal horizontal order chooses the rectangle side where teal exits at the bottom.

annotation.src: teal marker s above a filled rectangle, with a red marker on the same row
annotation.path: from s toward the rectangle side away from the red marker, then down to the background cell beside the rectangle's bottom row
annotation.dst: place s at that bottom-side endpoint
annotation.trajectory: paint only the endpoint teal
annotation.transform: clear the original red marker to background; recolor s.old cell red; keep the rectangle and other background unchanged

tags: condition:相对顺序决定出口, order_determines_exit

references.docstring:
Complete the scene by adding the point-reflected copy of the colored object across the central marker.

Input structure
- The grid has odd dimensions, a dominant background, and a center-row marker color appearing only at the left edge, center, and right edge.
- A single divider color fills the center column except for the center marker.
- All remaining foreground pixels form the object to copy, entirely on the left side of the divider.
Rule
- Keep the input unchanged.
- For every object pixel, paint the pixel rotated 180 degrees around the center marker with the same color.
Key insight
- The center marker is the rotation center; the yellow-looking divider is not mirrored, it only separates the source from the empty target side.

annotation.src: colored foreground object pixels excluding the center-column divider and center-row markers
annotation.transform: copy each source pixel to its 180-degree point-reflection through the center marker, preserving the original pixels, divider, and markers

tags: relation:绕中心点旋转对称, center_rotational

references.docstring:
Copy the unique colored sprite tile into every tiled cell marked by an internal separator-colored pixel.

Input structure
- Full same-color separator rows and columns partition the grid into equal rectangular tiles.
- One tile contains the only non-background, non-separator colored sprite.
- Target tiles are otherwise background-colored but contain at least one internal pixel of the separator color.

Rule
- Keep the separator lines and the source sprite tile unchanged.
- Replace each marked target tile with an exact copy of the source tile.
- Unmarked background-only tiles remain unchanged.

Key insight
- The internal separator-colored pixels are placement markers; the single colored tile is the template to stamp into those marked cells.

annotation.src: unique colored sprite tile s in the separator grid
annotation.dst: marked background tile d containing an internal separator-colored marker pixel
annotation.match_cond: every marked d receives the same unique s
annotation.transform: replace d with an exact copy of s, erasing the marker

tags: relation:标记指定放置位置, marker_position

references.docstring:
Reconstruct the repeated tile from its separated copies and mark the missing pixels in the damaged copy blue.

Input structure:
- The input is a lattice of equal-size blocks separated by one-cell solid rows
  and columns of the same separator color.
- All blocks are copies of one motif except exactly one block, where some
  motif pixels have been overwritten by the motif background color.
- Blue is absent from the input and is reserved as the output marker color.

Rule:
- Recover the motif by taking the unique majority color at each local block
  coordinate across all block copies.
- Find the single block that differs from this consensus motif.
- Return the consensus motif, recoloring the differing local coordinates blue.

Key insight:
- The repeated copies provide redundancy: the damaged positions are exactly
  the coordinates where the lone nonconforming copy has background instead of
  the consensus motif color.

annotation.src: lattice of equal-size tile copies separated by solid separator rows and columns, with exactly one copy damaged by background overwrites
annotation.transform: recover the tile by unique per-coordinate majority across copies; find the lone nonmatching copy; output the recovered tile with the nonmatching coordinates recolored blue
annotation.grid_shape: one tile block, omitting separator rows and columns

references.docstring:
Assemble the foreground objects by docking equal-colored boundary markers edge-to-edge.

Input structure
The grid has a dominant background color and several 4-connected multicolor foreground
objects.  One foreground color is the body color; the less frequent foreground colors are
boundary connector markers, and each marker color appears once as a free end or twice as a
matched docking pair.

Rule
Crop each foreground object to its bounding box and translate the objects so that the two
occurrences of every paired connector color touch on their exposed boundary sides.  Preserve
each object's orientation and colors, then return the tight crop around the assembled
foreground on the original background color.

Key insight
The colored marker pixels are ports: matching colors specify which objects must touch, and
the marker's side of its object determines the direction of the translation.

annotation.src: 4-connected foreground object sprite s with boundary connector markers
annotation.dst: matching boundary connector marker d on another sprite
annotation.match_cond: s.marker.color == d.marker.color and the two marker pixels have opposite exposed sides
annotation.transform: translate sprites so each paired marker touches edge-to-edge; preserve sprite colors and orientation
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop of the assembled foreground on the original background color

tags: relation:同色标记对齐对接, same_color_dock
condition:标记侧面决定方向, marker_side_dir

references.docstring:
Recolor the grey diagonal-chain regions in an orange field to teal.

Input structure
The input contains only grey pixels and orange pixels.  Grey pixels form
several 8-connected regions embedded in the orange field.

Rule
Decompose each grey 8-connected region into 4-connected lobes.  Recolor the
whole region teal only when it contains a straight diagonal run of at least
three pixels and those lobes meet only by diagonal corner contacts in a
non-branching diagonal chain or cycle; a single 4-connected region is
recolored only when it is a square diagonal staircase.

Key insight
The teal regions are not selected by size or position; they are the grey
regions whose internal connectivity depends on diagonal corner joins, while
same-edge cracks, rectangles, bars, and branching/noisy regions remain grey.

annotation.src: 8-connected grey regions in an orange field, classified by their 4-connected lobe structure
annotation.transform: recolor to teal each grey region whose 4-connected lobes form a non-branching diagonal-corner chain or whose single lobe is a square diagonal staircase; preserve all other pixels

references.docstring:
Keep only the lower-panel colors named by the top markers and expand each marker into an object-count bar.

Input structure
A black instruction strip sits above a non-black rectangular scene panel.  The strip contains one-cell markers
in the first column, and each marker color is a candidate object color in the lower panel.  The lower panel has
a unique dominant background color and scattered 4-connected foreground objects.

Rule
In the lower panel, preserve objects whose colors appear as top markers and recolor every other foreground
object to the panel background.  In the instruction strip, replace each marker by a horizontal run from column 0
whose length is the number of 4-connected lower-panel objects of that marker color; erase markers with count 0.

Key insight
The top strip is a color filter plus a compact count summary: marker colors select which lower-panel objects
survive, and their bars report the number of surviving objects by color.

annotation.src: lower-panel 4-connected foreground object s
annotation.dst: top-strip pixel d in the same-color marker row
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.row_marker_color
annotation.transform: s -> one pixel; unmatched lower-panel foreground -> panel background

tags: condition:条长等于物体计数, bar_equals_count

references.docstring:
Slide each inner colored object horizontally into the same-colored vertical wall until it touches an obstacle.

Input structure
- The background is the dominant color.
- The only foreground colors are two non-background colors.
- One foreground color fills the left column and the other fills the right column.
- Extra 8-connected objects of each wall color appear away from that color's wall.

Rule
- Clear the extra objects from their original positions.
- For each wall color, process its 8-connected extra objects from nearest to farthest from the matching wall.
- Slide each object horizontally toward its matching wall as far as possible without overlapping the wall or an already settled object of the same color.
- Keep the two vertical wall columns fixed.

Key insight
- The side columns act like color-specific gravity walls: same-colored objects compact sideways against their own wall while preserving each object's shape.

annotation.src: 8-connected objects away from the full-height side wall of the same color
annotation.path: horizontal slide toward the matching side wall, stopping just before the wall or an already settled same-color object would overlap
annotation.trajectory: translate each object rigidly to its final unobstructed position
annotation.transform: clear original object positions, keep both side walls fixed, and preserve each moved object's color and shape
annotation.multi_step: For each wall color, settle objects from nearest to farthest from that wall so later objects can stop against earlier same-color objects.

tags: relation:同色物体朝同色墙, same_color_wall

references.docstring:
Rotate every foreground bar 90 degrees around its own center on the same canvas.

Input structure
The background is the dominant color, and all foreground pixels share one color.
Each 4-connected foreground object is a solid one-cell-thick horizontal or vertical
bar with odd length, with single-pixel bars allowed.

Rule
Clear the canvas to the background, then redraw every bar with its midpoint, length,
and color preserved while swapping horizontal and vertical orientation.

Key insight
The bars are independent objects: their centers and lengths identify the output
placement, so no matching, ordering, or global symmetry is needed.

annotation.src: 4-connected monochromatic foreground bars on a dominant background
annotation.transform: rotate each odd-length horizontal or vertical bar 90 degrees about its midpoint; preserve its color and length, with single-pixel bars unchanged

tags: condition:朝向交换长度保持, orient_swap_keep

references.docstring:
Reorder the vertical color-major blocks while preserving every block's internal pixels.

Input structure
The grid is divided into vertical blocks, each with a unique dominant color.
Small marker pixels from other block colors may appear inside the blocks.

Rule
If adjacent shared-color marker rows read exactly as the current block order
from right to left, reverse the blocks. Otherwise move the leftmost block to
the far right and shift the remaining blocks left.

Key insight
The transformation acts on whole vertical blocks, so marker pixels move with
their source block instead of being recolored or independently rearranged.

annotation.src: vertical color-major blocks s, including their internal marker pixels
annotation.dst: left-to-right output block slots d with the same widths as the ordered source blocks
annotation.match_cond: rank(s) == rank(d) after applying the block-order rule
annotation.transform: copy each whole source block unchanged into its assigned output slot
annotation.multi_step: default order is a one-block left shift; if adjacent shared-color marker rows read the current block colors right-to-left, use reverse order

tags: condition:整块移动保持内容, block_move_intact

references.docstring:
Paint the top-connected middle channel between two orange path components teal.

Input structure
- The background is black.
- One foreground color forms exactly two 4-connected one-pixel-wide path components.
- Optional non-background control pixels may sit in the channel between the two paths.

Rule
- Dilate each path component by one cell in the 8-neighborhood and intersect the two dilations; this gives the one-cell-wide middle channel.
- A control pixel in that channel is a blocker only when its 4-neighbors touch fewer than both path components; otherwise it is part of the channel and is repainted.
- After removing blockers, paint the channel component connected to the top edge teal and keep all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The desired pixels are not found by region filling; they are the geometric overlap of the two paths' one-cell halos, with weakly attached control pixels splitting the channel.

annotation.src: middle-channel mask formed by intersecting the 8-neighborhood halos of the two orange 4-connected path objects
annotation.transform: recolor the top-connected passable channel to teal; a non-bg control pixel blocks the channel only if it is not 4-adjacent to both orange path objects, otherwise it is recolored too

tags: relation:两路径间隙重叠区, path_gap_overlap
condition:连通至边缘的部分, connected_to_edge

references.docstring:
Compress each colored ray pixel inward until it touches that color's 3x3 anchor block.
Input structure
- A uniform background grid with non-background colors.
- Each foreground color contains one solid 3x3 anchor block; all other pixels of that color lie on straight 8-neighbor rays aimed at that block.
Rule
- Keep anchor blocks fixed, erase loose foreground pixels, and for each ray pack its pixels into consecutive cells adjacent to the anchor along the same ray.
Key insight
- The scattered pixels are displaced pixels on visible row, column, or diagonal sightlines back to their same-colored 3x3 block.

annotation.src: loose non-background pixels outside each same-colored solid 3x3 anchor block
annotation.path: straight horizontal, vertical, or diagonal ray from each loose pixel toward its anchor block, stopping at the cell just before the ray enters the anchor
annotation.trajectory: pack all loose pixels on the same ray into consecutive cells adjacent to the anchor, preserving their order by distance from the anchor
annotation.transform: keep the 3x3 anchor blocks fixed, erase the original loose pixels, and preserve each color's pixel count

tags: relation:同色射线归属锚块, ray_belongs_anchor
condition:射线像素紧缩至锚, compact_to_anchor

references.docstring:
Reorient each two-pixel blue/pink segment so it reads pink then blue when viewed from its border marker.

Input structure
- The background is dominant, with one border-only marker color and blue/pink foreground segments.
- Every marker lies on the outer border and points inward along its row or column.
- Along exactly one inward ray from each marker is a single adjacent two-pixel blue/pink segment.

Rule
- For each marker, look inward perpendicular to the border side containing the marker.
- Rewrite the two blue/pink pixels on that ray so the nearer one is pink and the farther one is blue.
- Keep marker pixels, background pixels, and all other pixels unchanged.

Key insight
- The marker gives a local viewing direction; the segment's required order is relative to that marker, not to global row or column order.

annotation.src: border marker pixel s
annotation.dst: adjacent blue/pink segment d on an inward row or column ray
annotation.match_cond: d lies on the unique inward ray from s
annotation.transform: rewrite d so the pixel nearer s is pink and the farther pixel is blue

tags: relation:标记指定观察方向, marker_view_dir

references.docstring:
Build the woven rectangle determined by the two marked cells on each crossed bar.

Input structure
A black-background grid contains one long horizontal bar and one long vertical bar.
Each bar has a dominant base color and exactly two same-colored marker pixels.

Rule
The horizontal marker pair gives the output column span.  From the horizontal bar
row, walk toward the farther vertical marker; rows and columns alternate every
other cell.  Even step/even offset cells use the horizontal marker color until
the nearer vertical marker is reached, then use the vertical marker color.
Odd row steps use the horizontal base on marker columns and the original
crossing color on spacer columns.  Spacer columns on even row steps use the
vertical base, except at the switch row where they use the crossing color.

Key insight
The original cross cell records which base color wins at base/base lattice
crossings; the nearer vertical marker is the color-switch boundary.

annotation.src: one horizontal bar and one vertical bar crossing on the background; each bar has a dominant base color and exactly two same-colored marker pixels
annotation.transform: replace the scene with the woven rectangle whose columns span the horizontal marker pair and whose rows run from the horizontal bar to the farther vertical marker; alternate rows and columns every other cell, switch marker color at the nearer vertical marker, and use the original crossing color at base/base lattice intersections

references.docstring:
Complete every colored sprite by applying the union of all aligned partial sprite masks.

Input structure:
- The dominant color is the background.
- Each non-background color appears as a separated partial copy of one common sprite mask.
- The copies share a top-left-aligned sprite window; some copies may be missing lower or right edge pixels.

Rule:
- Crop each same-color mask to its bounding box.
- Pad the crops to the maximum observed height and width, aligned at the top-left, and OR them into one complete template.
- Fill that template at every sprite location using the sprite's own color.

Key insight:
- No single input sprite is complete, but their missing cells are complementary, so the aligned union reveals the full mask.

annotation.src: same-color partial sprite masks, one per foreground color, sharing a top-left-aligned window
annotation.transform: pad smaller masks down/right to the largest observed window, recover the complete sprite as the union of all aligned masks, then fill that mask in each sprite window using that window's color

references.docstring:
Connect same-colored foreground components with one-cell-wide orthogonal paths around teal wall segments.

Input structure
- The dominant color is the background.
- Teal cells are fixed wall segments and are never source connectors.
- Other foreground colors appear as one or more 4-connected components; colors with a single component stay unchanged.

Rule
- For each non-background, non-teal color, read its 4-connected components in row-major order.
- Connect each consecutive pair by the shortest clear L-shaped path between the two components.
- Clear paths may pass only through background or the same color, and they preserve the previous travel axis when both bends are possible.

Key insight
- The output is not a global recolor: each color traces a routed chain through its own components while teal cells and other colors act as blockers.

annotation.src: non-background, non-teal colors with multiple 4-connected components
annotation.path: from each component to the next same-colored component in row-major order, take a shortest clear one-bend horizontal/vertical path through background or same color; teal wall segments and other colors block the path
annotation.dst: next same-colored component in the ordered chain
annotation.trajectory: paint every background pixel on each connector path with the source color
annotation.transform: keep teal wall segments, single-component colors, and all original foreground pixels unchanged
annotation.multi_step: process each color's components in row-major order; when both bends are clear, preserve the previous travel axis, otherwise use the longer-axis-first clear bend

tags: relation:同色分量依序连接, same_color_chain

references.docstring:
Crop out the grid half containing the two aligned marker pixels, then erase the markers to background.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color and one non-background marker color
  that appears as exactly two cells.
- The marker cells are aligned either in one row or one column and both lie
  in the same half along that direction.
- Other non-background pixels are content inside one or both halves.

Rule
- If the markers share a row, keep the left or right half whose columns
  contain them.
- If the markers share a column, keep the top or bottom half whose rows
  contain them.
- In the kept half, recolor the marker pixels to the background color.

Key insight
- The two marker pixels are not part of the picture; their alignment and
  half-position identify which half of the doubled canvas is the answer.

annotation.src: half-grid region containing the two aligned marker pixels
annotation.transform: crop to that half; use row-aligned markers to choose left/right and column-aligned markers to choose top/bottom, then recolor marker pixels to bg
annotation.grid_shape: same height and half width for row-aligned markers; half height and same width for column-aligned markers

tags: relation:标记对齐指定半区, marker_selects_half

references.docstring:
Move the orange rectangle onto the maroon rectangle and mark gated corridor crossings in red.

Input structure
- The dominant background contains black obstacle segments.
- There is one solid orange rectangle and one solid maroon rectangle of the same size.
- The two rectangles share either their row span or their column span, so the move is straight and axis-aligned.

Rule
- Erase the original orange rectangle to the background.
- Replace the maroon rectangle with the orange rectangle.
- Between the two rectangles, paint red across the moving rectangle's width or height only at corridor cells flanked by black obstacle segments perpendicular to the movement.

Key insight
- The black segments define gates in the straight corridor; only those gated openings, not every swept background cell, become red.

annotation.src: solid orange rectangle s
annotation.path: straight horizontal or vertical corridor from s to the aligned same-sized maroon rectangle d
annotation.dst: same-sized maroon rectangle d aligned with s on one axis
annotation.trajectory: paint red only at corridor openings flanked by black segments perpendicular to the path
annotation.transform: erase old s to background; replace d with orange; keep black segments and all other cells unchanged

tags: relation:同轴对齐的矩形对, coaxial_rect_pair
condition:障碍门处标记通道, barrier_gate_mark

references.docstring:
Split the two-color object horizontally, swap its colors, and slide the upper half to the right.

Input structure:
- The grid has one background color and exactly two foreground colors.
- All foreground pixels form one 4-connected object with an even-height bbox.
- The object has foreground pixels on both rows adjacent to its horizontal midpoint.

Rule:
- Split the object into upper and lower halves at the midpoint of its bbox.
- Swap the two foreground colors in both halves.
- Keep the lower half in place and shift the upper half right until its lower-left
  boundary pixel is diagonally adjacent to the lower half's upper-right boundary pixel.

Key insight:
- The object is not copied or reflected; it is broken at the horizontal waist,
  recolored by exchanging the two visible object colors, then rejoined diagonally.

annotation.src: upper half s of the single two-color foreground object split at its horizontal midpoint
annotation.path: translate s right until its bottom-row leftmost foreground pixel is diagonally adjacent to the lower half's top-row rightmost foreground pixel
annotation.trajectory: place only the final translated upper-half sprite; leave no trail
annotation.dst: endpoint beside the fixed lower half
annotation.transform: exchange the two foreground colors in both halves; keep the lower half in place and clear the original upper-half cells

references.docstring:
Replace each colored corner marker with its corner-specific inward stencil in the same color.

Input structure
- The grid is 8x8 with a single dominant background color.
- Foreground pixels are marker pixels, each located at one of the four corners.
- A marker's color is carried to the stencil selected by its corner position.

Rule
- Erase each corner marker back to the background.
- Top corner markers become an inward 2x2 block one cell away from the top and side edges.
- Bottom corner markers become the mirrored three-pixel inward bent stencil shown by the bottom-corner examples.

Key insight
- The marker position selects the fixed stencil; the marker color only supplies the paint color, so multiple corners apply independently.

annotation.src: colored marker pixels at the four corners of the 8x8 grid
annotation.transform: erase each marker and stamp its color into the fixed inward stencil for that corner: top corners become 2x2 blocks, bottom corners become mirrored three-pixel bent stencils

tags: condition:标记色传递给模板, marker_color_pass

references.docstring:
Move the left-edge fragment into its same-colored anchor fragment to complete a solid rectangle.

Input structure
- The grid has a dominant background color.
- Exactly one foreground color is split into two 4-connected objects: one
  touches the left edge, and the other is an anchor away from the left edge.
- The translated left-edge object and the anchor can form one filled rectangle.
Rule
- Find the unique split color whose left-edge object can be translated onto
  background cells beside the other same-colored object so their union is a
  solid axis-aligned rectangle.
- Clear the left-edge object's original cells to the background.
- Paint that object at the unique completing offset, preserving all other cells.
Key insight
- The active color is identified by object structure and rectangle completion,
  not by a fixed color id; the same-colored anchor object stays in place.

annotation.src: left-edge 4-connected object s of the split foreground color
annotation.dst: same-colored anchor object d away from the left edge
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color and a translation of s plus d forms a filled axis-aligned rectangle
annotation.transform: erase s from its original cells and translate it to the unique completing offset; preserve d and all other cells

tags: relation:同色碎片拼成矩形, same_color_join
condition:碎片触边锚不触边, frag_edge_anchor

references.docstring:
Select the majority interior marker color, then redraw the framed board as that color's frame plus its bounding-box outline.

Input structure:
- The top row is a copied palette made from adjacent equal color pairs.
- Below it is a one-cell-thick rectangular frame around a black interior.
- Non-black, non-frame interior pixels are marker colors; one marker color has
  the unique highest count.

Rule:
- Keep the palette row unchanged.
- Pick the uniquely most frequent interior marker color.
- Clear the lower board to black, recolor its outer frame with the picked color,
  and draw the picked color's interior bounding-box border.

Key insight:
- The noisy marker cloud is not preserved as pixels; only the majority marker
  color and its spatial extent define the output.

annotation.src: framed lower region with black background and colored interior marker pixels
annotation.transform: copy the palette row; select the unique most frequent marker color, clear the lower region to black, recolor the outer frame, and draw that color's bbox border

tags: relation:众数颜色决定输出, majority_color_out
condition:仅保留边框包围盒, keep_frame_bbox

references.docstring:
Reveal the rectangular patch hidden by the solid marker using the grid's reflection symmetries.

Input structure:
- A square colored pattern with one solid rectangular marker color occluding a patch.
- The visible pattern has horizontal and vertical reflection symmetry on a large lower/right strip.
- The top and left outer strips also expose transpose counterparts for cells not recoverable by those reflections.

Rule:
- Find the unique color whose full extent is a solid rectangle; this rectangle is the output region.
- Infer the reflected strip start as the smallest row/column offset whose lower/right strips are mirror-consistent, ignoring marker pixels.
- For each marker pixel, copy the unique non-marker value in its horizontal/vertical reflection orbit; if that orbit is entirely hidden in the outer strip, use the transposed top/left-strip counterpart.

Key insight:
The marker is not part of the pattern; it covers a missing rectangle whose cells are still determined by the visible mirror or transpose copies elsewhere in the grid.

annotation.src: solid rectangular marker over a mirrored color pattern
annotation.dst: hidden marker-sized rectangle
annotation.transform: replace each marker pixel by the matching pixel from its horizontal/vertical reflection orbit; use the transposed top/left-strip counterpart when that orbit is also hidden
annotation.grid_shape: crop to marker bbox

references.docstring:
Repair noisy periodic patterns inside frame-delimited grid regions.

Input structure:
- Frame color (most common) forms full rows/cols, dividing the grid into rectangular regions.
- bg (second most common) fills empty space; each region contains a small colored tile repeated periodically with a few corrupted pixels.

Rule:
- For each region, find the bounding box of non-bg content.
- Infer the smallest repeating tile that explains the pattern (majority vote per residue position), requiring it repeat at least 2x per axis.
- Replace the region with the clean tiled version.

Key insight: Tile dimensions are unknown and must be inferred; prefer the smallest tile with genuine repetition over one that memorizes the entire region.

Draw a polyline by decoding 3x3 glyph instructions read across a divided grid.

Input structure:
- Left of a full-height vertical divider: 3x3 colored glyphs on bg.
- Right of divider: a single gray (5) start pixel.

Rule:
- Remove the divider; shift the gray start into the left canvas.
- Read glyphs in column-major order (left→right, top→bottom).
- Each glyph's shape (pixel area) encodes a segment: area 4 → down 2, area 5 → right 3, area 6 → left 4, area 7 → left 2.
- Append segments sequentially, stepping down one cell between each.

Key insight: Glyph pixel count (area) uniquely determines both segment length and direction — the shape itself is the instruction.

annotation.src: 3x3 glyphs left of a vertical divider, plus a gray start marker on the right
annotation.dst: a single polyline in the left canvas starting at the shifted gray marker
annotation.match_cond: glyphs ordered by tile column (left→right), then tile row (top→bottom)
annotation.transform: remove divider, shift gray into the left canvas, then append one segment per glyph while moving downward; segment length+orientation are determined by glyph type (area 4→vertical len2; area 5→horizontal len3 right; area 6→horizontal len4 left; area 7→horizontal len2 left)

references.docstring:
Fill partitioned regions with concentric colored bands derived from marker pixels.

Input structure:
- Grid partitioned into regions by wall-colored lines.
- Each region has a dominant base color and a few isolated marker pixels of other colors at varying depths from the region boundary.

Rule:
- For each region, read marker colors ordered by their Chebyshev distance from the boundary to build a color palette.
- If no marker sits on the boundary itself, the base color leads the palette.
- Paint every cell with palette[distance mod palette_length], producing repeating concentric rectangular frames that radiate inward.

Key insight: Each marker's depth from the boundary defines its position in the cyclic palette; the pattern then tiles inward automatically.

annotation.summary: Isolated colored pixels in each region expand by drawing alternating concentric rectangular frames parallel to region boundaries until the entire region is filled.
annotation.src: isolated single colored pixels within each partitioned region s
annotation.path: draw rectangular frame parallel to region boundary, then shrink inward by 1 pixel and repeat alternating s.color with background until region is filled
annotation.trajectory: paint s.color on current frame, alternate with region background color on next frame, continue inward

references.docstring:
Trace diagonal rays from triangular arrows, reflecting off colored wall pixels.

Input structure:
- bg grid with monochrome 3-pixel L-shaped "arrows" (2x2 bbox missing one corner) and scattered colored wall pixels.

Rule:
- Each arrow fires a ray diagonally away from its missing corner, painting bg cells in its color.
- A head-on wall hit reverses both axes; a side-touch wall hit flips the touched axis only.
- On any bounce the ray adopts the wall's color and recolors the contact cell.
- Ray stops when it exits the grid or reaches another arrow.

Key insight: Two distinct reflection types (corner vs side-touch) plus color inheritance at each bounce drive the path geometry.

annotation.src: triangular arrow
annotation.path: along the diagonal line pointed by the arrow then reflected by the wall
annotation.trajectory: continuous; ray color changes to wall color on each reflection
annotation.dst: out of grid
annotation.multi_step: reflected by all reachable walls one by one

references.docstring:
Assemble colored sprites into a central bar's notches, chaining successive pieces along fixed-width strips.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Largest monochrome component is a solid "bar" with boundary notches (bg holes opening to its bbox edge).
- Several smaller colored sprites scattered around the bar.

Rule:
- Each bar notch is filled by a root piece whose shape exactly covers the hole.
- The root defines a strip (column-span or row-span) for its chain.
- Successive pieces fill the bg cells inside the previous piece's bbox, locked to the same strip width.
- Multiple chains grow independently from different bar notches.

Key insight: The root piece's extent perpendicular to the chain direction locks the strip width for all subsequent pieces in that chain.

annotation.src: dangling monochrome sprite s
annotation.dst: plug into central bar or previously plugged sprite d
annotation.match_cond: s.shape fits into d.notch.shape
annotation.multi_step: place sprites one into the notch of another until no notches remain; multiple chains grow from different bar notches

references.docstring:
Fill periodic progressions that shoot from a unique grid edge.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.  Sparse non-bg dots of several colors.
- All repeating colors originate from the same grid edge (top, bottom,
  left, or right — the one with the most non-bg dots).
- Each repeating color has exactly 2 dots per shooting-direction line;
  their gap defines the step.
- Every non-bg dot lies on a shooting-direction line that contains a
  repeating color.

Rule:
- Determine the unique shooting edge; left/right → rows, top/bottom → columns.
- For each shooting-direction line, the repeating color has exactly 2 dots;
  step = gap between them, offset = first position mod step.
- A different-colored dot aligned to the same beat (pos % step == offset) is
  a companion: it absorbs the ray and becomes the fill color, limiting the
  fill range to the span between repeating and companion dots.
- An unaligned dot is a bystander and left untouched.
- Without a companion the repeating color fills the entire line.

Key insight: the shooting edge is identified by counting boundary dots;
the gap between the two marker dots is the period; a companion sharing the
modular class acts as a wall that stops the ray and dictates the paint color.

annotation.src: sparse colored dots
annotation.path: within each affected row/col, step size = gcd of gaps between repeated dots; traverse indices congruent to the first dot modulo step
annotation.trajectory: paint with the aligned companion color if present on the same modulo-class; otherwise paint with the dot color
annotation.dst: fill the line segment between extreme occurrences (or whole line if no companion color)
annotation.transform: fill background/marker cells on that path with the trajectory color; ties apply both row and column rules

references.docstring:
Detect thin '+' shapes in a single foreground color and recolor them to teal.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- One foreground color (e.g. yellow) forms various shapes on the bg, some of which are small '+' crosses.

Rule:
- A '+' center is any foreground pixel whose 4 orthogonal neighbors are also foreground.
- Recolor each such center and its 4 neighbors to teal (8).
- All other pixels remain unchanged.

Key insight: Only compact 5-cell crosses qualify — a pixel embedded in a larger filled region also satisfies the neighbor check, so the rule highlights every local '+' motif, not just isolated ones.

annotation.src: yellow plus sprites s
annotation.transform: s.color -> teal

references.docstring:
Simulate particles along a path with alternating turn direction at collisions.

Input structure:
- Top-left: 2x2 monochrome blocks define a repeating color cycle (left-to-right).
- Isolated single pixels of a cycle color: start markers adjacent to the path.
- A 2x2 monochrome block of a distinct color: end marker.

Rule:
- Each start marker launches a particle moving straight, painting cycle colors in order.
- On hitting a boundary, paint that cell with the end color and turn 90°.
- Turn direction alternates: odd collisions → left (CCW), even → right (CW).
- If the scheduled turn is blocked, the particle stops.

Key insight: The alternating left/right turn rule is the core mechanism; without it the path would be trivial.

annotation.src: start markers: isolated single pixels whose colors belong to a template cycle shown as 2x2 monochrome blocks in the top-left
annotation.path: enter the main path region (the most frequent non-template color) and move one cell per step; keep heading until a collision with non-path

references.docstring:
Extend row bars periodically across the opposite side of a separator column.

Input structure:
- bg = background. A near-solid vertical separator divides the grid into two sides.
- One side contains horizontal colored bars; the other side is blank target space.
- Bars may be stacked by row and may sit at different distances from the separator.

Rule:
- Identify the separator as the column whose non-bg cells are one color.
- Treat the denser side as the bar side and collect each contiguous row run.
- Process bars from nearest to farthest from the separator; for each bar, paint its
  color every bar-length cells into the blank side without overwriting earlier paint.

Key insight: Each bar's length is the period for its extension, and nearer bars claim target cells first.

annotation.summary: Horizontal monochrome color bars to the left of a vertical separator bar extend rightward with periodic intervals equal to their pixel count.

annotation.path: straight line from separator bar to the opposite grid edge, perpendicular to separator (rightward)
annotation.trajectory: paint s.color at intervals where interval = s.pixel_count
annotation.multi_step: Process multiple bars by distance from separator: start with the bar closest to the separator, then proceed outward; do not overwrite previously painted colors

references.docstring:
Connect two sprites using matching connector pixels, then tight-crop.

Input structure:
- Background color `bg`, sprite color `obj`, connector color `ctrl` (small, 2 components).
- Two main foreground sprites, plus possibly tiny detached pixels belonging to one sprite.

Rule:
- Identify the **base** sprite (closest to grid top-left).
- Translate the other sprite so its connector sits one cell above the base's connector.
- Stamp the plug onto the base; remove connectors (recolor `ctrl` to `obj`).
- Output is the tight crop around all non-background pixels.

Key insight: The connector pixels define the unique docking point and direction.
