annotation.dst: plug into base sprite d in top-left corner with a connector
annotation.match_cond: s.connector.color/shape == d.connector.color/shape and s.connector above d.connector
annotation.src2: s.connector and d.connector
annotation.transform2: recolor connector pixels to body color
annotation.grid_shape: expand if needed then tight crop

references.docstring:
Repaint regions from T-shaped control markers, erase the markers, and optionally rotate based on a color-9 L-marker.

Input structure:
- The grid is a mosaic of monochrome regions.
- Color 1 forms T-shaped control markers on region boundaries.
- Some controls use three singleton color-1 pixels around a colored center; that center is a literal replacement color.
- An optional 5-cell L-shaped color-9 marker triggers 90-degree rotation of the output.

Rule:
- For a color-1 T marker, the single stem points at the destination region to repaint.
- The two diagonal cells behind the stem identify the source region; the destination gets that source region's original color.
- For a colored-center T marker, the same stem identifies the destination, but the center color is the replacement.
- All marker cells are filled with the final color of the source-side region.
- A 5-cell L-shaped color-9 marker controls rotation: ┐ (corner top-right) → CCW 90°, ┌ (corner top-left) → CW 90°.

Key insight:
- The stem chooses what changes, while the two diagonals behind the stem choose where the marker itself belongs.

annotation.src: monochrome regions with T-shaped color-1 control markers
annotation.transform: recolor the region pointed to by each T stem using the original color from the two diagonal source cells behind the stem; colored-center T markers use the center color instead; erase marker cells into the source-side region
annotation.grid_shape: same, except rotate 90 degrees when indicated by the colored-center control orientation
annotation.notes: small non-rectangular colored scraps are absorbed into the neighboring region

tags: condition:标记形状决定操作, marker_shape_determines_operation

references.docstring:
Propagate a repeating striped pattern from a yellow border segment toward the opposite edge, recoloring foreground objects on certain stripes.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Foreground blobs of another color scattered in the interior.
- A short yellow (4) segment sits on one border edge.

Rule:
- From the yellow segment, march toward the opposite edge in steps of 2 cells, cycling colors Y, Y, G (4, 4, 3). The 1-cell gap between stripes is forced to bg.
- Yellow stripes paint only within the segment's span.
- Green stripes additionally recolor all non-bg pixels across the entire row/column to green.

Key insight: Green stripes act as a "flood" that recolors existing objects on the full row/column, while yellow stripes are confined to the segment span.

annotation.src: yellow line on edge
annotation.path: straight line
annotation.trajectory: YYGYYG...
annotation.dst: the opposite edge
annotation.src2: green line
annotation.path2: foreground pixels in the same row/col

references.docstring:
Move colored sprites from the left strip into a framed area at marker-defined targets.

Input structure:
- bg background; rectangular frame on right with colored markers on its edges; sprites in a narrow left strip separated by a constant-color divider column.

Rule:
- For each color, target rows/cols are where both opposite frame edges share that color. Targets are the Cartesian product.
- Erase each sprite from the left and stamp it centered at every target. Higher sprites cover lower ones.

Key insight: One sprite replicates to a grid of row × column marker intersections.

annotation.src: sprite s in the left area whose color appears on the right frame
annotation.dst: center at positions d in the right frame
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.same_row_frame_edges.color and s.color == d.same_col_frame_edges.color
annotation.multi_step: move sprites from bottom to top, with new covering old

references.docstring:
Complete a visible crop into the shared 20x20 binary motif in its matching orientation.

Input structure:
- The grid is a two-color rectangular crop of one rotation/reflection of the same 20x20 motif.
- One color is the motif foreground and the other color is the motif background.

Rule:
- Try each input color as the foreground mask.
- Match that mask against every possible window in every dihedral orientation of the motif.
- Repaint the uniquely matched full 20x20 motif with the matched foreground/background colors.

Key insight:
- The examples are partial windows of one canonical binary pattern; the local crop is distinctive enough to identify the full orientation and offset.

annotation.src: visible two-color crop of a 20x20 binary motif
annotation.dst: the full 20x20 motif in the matching rotation/reflection and window position
annotation.transform: repaint the completed motif with the crop foreground color and background color

references.docstring:
Move bordered containers toward same-colored destination markers, charging gray cells to orange.

Input structure:
- bg = 6 (magenta). Black-bordered (0) rectangles with gray (5) / orange (7) interiors.
- A head sprite (9) sits adjacent to one container edge; a matching destination sprite lies along the movement axis.

Rule:
- Each container translates toward its destination along the head-to-dest axis.
- Steps = min(head-to-dest distance, number of gray interior cells).
- Gray cells become orange from the head-facing side inward, one per step.

Key insight: Gray cell count caps movement — a container stops short if it runs out of gray cells to charge.

annotation.path: head forward
annotation.dst: reach the destination line or move_distance == s.inner_gey_pixels.num
annotation.src2: inner grey pixels whose num == move_distance
annotation.transform: change color to orange
annotation.multi_step: grey pixels change color in order

references.docstring:
Simulate water pixels falling under gravity into basins formed by colored obstacles.

Input structure:
- bg = 0. Water pixels = color 1 (blue).
- Other colors form static solid structures (walls, steps, containers).
- Water starts in unstable positions above or beside basins.

Rule:
- Each water pixel falls straight down through bg cells.
- When blocked below, it slides diagonally through the unique open side cell.
- When resting on a surface, it slides horizontally toward the nearest gap where it can fall again.
- Process repeats until no water pixel moves.

Key insight: Water seeks the deepest reachable basin via diagonal and horizontal sliding, not just vertical fall.

annotation.src: blue pixels
annotation.path: flow along neighboring bg cells to left/right/down (like water)
annotation.dst: lowest postion possible (into basin)
annotation.multi_step: iteratively move blue pixels whose left or right side is bg

references.docstring:
Reorder and stack rectangles by proximity to two colored edge lines.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Two edge lines (h + v) meet at a corner marked by a unique color.
- "Blue" line is color 1 if present, else the longer line; other is "red."
- Solid rectangles in the interior.

Rule:
- Sort rectangles by (distance to blue edge, distance to red edge).
- If the blue edge is vertical, rotate each rectangle 90° CCW.
- Stack top-to-bottom, centered horizontally.

Key insight: Edge-line colors encode a coordinate system; proximity to each axis determines stacking order and rotation.

annotation.src: rectangles
annotation.dst: into slot center aligned
annotation.match_cond: (distance(s, blue_edge), distance(s, red_edge)).order == d.pos.row.order
annotation.transform: rot90 if blue edge is vertical
annotation.multi_step: move rectangles in order, one below another

references.docstring:
Simulate tokens falling through a pipe network after gates rotate open.

Input structure:
- Wall (0), bg (pipe fill), gate (horizontal 1×3 bars), token (small edge pixels).

Rule:
- Rotate each gate into a vertical blocker; gate cells become bg.
- Tokens drop downward through bg, choosing the extreme column for their side (left→min, right→max).
- Tokens settle at true pipe ends (adjacent to wall/boundary), packing inward.

Key insight: Tokens select drop columns by entry side and land at wall-bounded endpoints, ignoring blocker-bounded ones.

annotation.transform: rot90, orange bar change to magenta
annotation.src2: green pixel
annotation.dst2: endpoint of path next to grid edge
annotation.multi_step: rotate_in_place then move_along_path

references.docstring:
Sort scattered 4×4 squares into two columns by type: frames left, solids right.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Multiple 4×4 objects on bg.
- Frames: colored 1px border, bg-filled 2×2 interior.
- Solids: entirely filled with one non-bg color.

Rule:
- Classify each 4×4 object as frame or solid by its interior.
- Sort each group top-to-bottom by input row.
- Stack frames in left column (cols 0–3), solids in right (cols 4–7).
- Output is 8 wide; height = 4 × max(#frames, #solids), bg-padded.

Key insight: Frame vs solid is determined solely by whether the 2×2 interior matches bg.

annotation.dst: into left slot
annotation.match_cond: s.pos.row.order == d.pos.row.order
annotation.src2: solid square
annotation.multi_step: move squares from top to bottom, then from left to right

references.docstring:
Attach monochrome sprites to the matching sides of a central hollow square.

Input structure:
- bg = background. A hollow NxN square (hub) with bg corners/interior and four differently-colored edges (top, bottom, left, right).
- 2-4 monochrome sprites scattered on the grid, each matching one hub edge color.

Rule:
- For each hub edge color, find the matching sprite outside the hub.
- Rotate the sprite (0/90/180/270°) so its contact edge has exactly N-2 contiguous cells aligned with the hub side, and the rotated sprite is mirror-symmetric along the contact-edge axis (UD for left/right, LR for top/bottom).
- Translate it to adjoin that hub side. 
- Clear everything else to bg; output is hub + attached sprites only.

Key insight: Each edge color uniquely pairs a sprite to a side; symmetry along the contact-edge axis disambiguates the correct rotation.

annotation.src: solid monochrome sprite s
annotation.dst: attach to an edge of hollow polychrome sprite d with bg corners and 4 differently-colored side edges
annotation.match_cond: s.head.color == d.edge.color and s.head.length == d.edge.length
annotation.transform: rotate s to align matching edge with d.side

references.docstring:
Convert a rough nested line drawing into a clean canonical frame-and-dot diagram.

Input structure:
- The grid has one background color and one foreground color.
- Foreground 4-connected objects are rough closed frames or small filled blobs.
- Frames may contain other frames/blobs; blobs outside a frame remain outside it.

Rule:
- Detect the containment tree of foreground objects using holes of each frame object.
- Replace every blob with one foreground pixel.
- Replace every frame with a rectangular border padded two cells around its direct children.
- Place siblings by their original row/column overlap and order, with one empty cell between canonical objects.

Key insight: The exact wobbly geometry is irrelevant; only enclosure plus relative sibling positions define the output.

annotation.src: rough two-color nested foreground drawing: closed frame objects and small blob objects
annotation.dst: canonical frame-and-dot diagram preserving containment and sibling row/column order
annotation.transform: replace each blob by one pixel; replace each frame by a rectangular border padded around its direct children; keep outside blobs outside the enclosing frame
annotation.grid_shape: canonical crop; root-level outside blobs occupy a 3x3 bg slot

references.docstring:
Sort vertical bars by height and redistribute them across fixed colored slots.

Input structure:
- bg background; a horizontal base line of a single color spans the full grid width.
- Several monochrome vertical bars of distinct colors rise upward from the base line.

Rule:
- Rank bar shapes by height (shortest to tallest).
- Rank original x-positions (slots) left to right.
- Place the i-th shortest shape into the i-th leftmost slot, recoloring it to that slot's original color.
- The base line is preserved unchanged.

Key insight: Each slot keeps its x-position and color identity; only the bar silhouettes are redistributed among slots by height order.

annotation.dst: replace vertical bar d
annotation.match_cond: s.size.order == d.pos.col.order
annotation.transform: s.color -> d.color

references.docstring:
Slide a solid square through a winding channel to reach a same-sized target square.

Input structure:
- bg (most common color). A river color forms a winding corridor.
- Two same-sized NxN solid squares on the river: mover and destination, each a distinct color.

Rule:
- The mover square travels along the river toward the destination.
- It can only pass through positions where the full NxN area is river.
- If reachable, the mover replaces the destination; otherwise it stops at the farthest reachable point.
- The mover's original position is filled with the river color.

Key insight: Chokepoints narrower than N pixels block the square, forcing it to stop short.

annotation.dst: reach same sized red square or "get stuck" on the way where the blue path is too narrow
annotation.transform: cover the red square if reaching it

references.docstring:
Complete outlined shapes and carry attached shadow pixels along their edges.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Each active color marks vertices of an 8-direction aligned outline.
- A start vertex can have adjacent non-bg, different-colored shadow pixels.
- Other colored pixels may be distractors unless they lie on valid drawable edges.

Rule:
- For each color, order its pixels by polar angle around their centroid to form a cycle.
- Draw only horizontal, vertical, or 45-degree edges whose interiors are clear.
- From the chosen start vertex, copy adjacent shadow offsets along each drawable edge
  when the parallel path is in bounds and clear.

Key insight: The main outline is reconstructed first, then the start vertex's neighbor offsets define parallel shadow strokes.

annotation.match_cond: s1.color == s2.color

annotation.trajectory: paint s.color along entire path between same-colored pixels
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify pairs of same-colored pixels that can connect via H/V/diagonal; Step 2: draw connecting line between them; Step 3: for each neighbor of starting pixel, draw parallel line with same offset

annotation.path2: parallel to primary path, offset by relative position of neighbor to starting pixel

references.docstring:
Simulate water falling from top-edge sources, pooling on shelves, and cascading off edges.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color; water = rarest non-bg; shelf = other non-bg.
- Sources: water clusters touching top row. Shelves: horizontal segments.

Rule:
- Water falls down from sources, painting bg cells as water.
- On hitting a shelf, it spreads across the shelf span plus one cell past each end.
- From those overflow positions, water resumes falling independently.

Key insight: Each shelf splits a stream into two at its edges, creating a branching waterfall tree.

annotation.path: through orange bg (air), vertical down or horizontal to both sides when landing on red horizontal bar
annotation.dst: bottom edge of grid
annotation.trajectory: continuous
annotation.multi_step: alternate vertical and horizontal movements until reaching bottom edge

references.docstring:
Extract the unique cell from each lattice row into a single-column lattice.

Input structure:
- Grid divided into equal square cells by uniform gridlines of color L.
- Cell interiors filled with bg; each cell has an inner sprite pattern.
- Each row of cells has exactly one cell with a unique pattern; the rest are copies.

Rule:
- For each lattice row, find the cell whose inner pattern appears exactly once (the "odd one out").
- Construct a single-column lattice preserving the original row heights, containing only the unique cells.

Key insight: The task is per-row "odd one out" — every cell in a row is identical except one oddball, which must be extracted.

annotation.dst: place into slot d in a column of slots
annotation.match_cond: s.pos.row == d.pos.row
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop

references.docstring:
Fill holes in a target object with colors from a source object's subsprites, then tight-crop.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Two similar 8-connected objects share an outline color.
- Source has colored subsprites in cavities; target has empty cavities.

Rule:
- Find the two 8-connected objects.
- Target = object with more hole area. Align subsprites to holes (rotation/flip if needed).
- Fill each hole with its matched subsprite color; tight-crop.

Key insight: Hole centers in the target are matched to source subsprite centers under the best rotation/flip transform.

annotation.dst: merge with sprite d with holes
annotation.match_cond: s.subsprites.arrangement == d.holes.arrangement

annotation.grid_shape: tight crop

references.docstring:
Eject content pixels from cup-shaped frames outward along each cup's tail direction.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Hollow cup/Y/funnel frames, each a unique border color.
- Each cup has a convergent tail spike on one side and an open mouth on the opposite side.
- Content pixels (a single non-border color per cup) sit inside the cup's mouth interior.

Rule:
- For each cup, identify its tail spike and tail direction.
- Erase all content pixels from the mouth interior.
- Draw a straight line of content-colored pixels from the spike outward in the tail direction,
  one pixel per erased content pixel; cells beyond the grid edge are dropped.

Key insight: The tail spike is the unique convergent point whose outward direction is opposite
the mouth opening where the content lives.

annotation.dst: stack onto tail or onto other colored pixels already stacked
annotation.trajectory: ignore colored pixels stacked out of grid

references.docstring:
Connect framed squares via colored bridges following a control-pixel sequence.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Border color forms equal-sized framed squares with unique inner fill colors.
- Control row below squares: colored pixels read left-to-right encode visitation order.

Rule:
- Start at the square matching first control color c0.
- For each consecutive pair (ci, ci+1), find the ci+1-colored square aligned in the same row or column band, preferring nearest.
- Draw a bridge colored ci between the pair, spanning the gap with inner-square thickness.

Key insight: Row/column-band alignment plus proximity resolves ambiguity when inner colors repeat.

annotation.trajectory: keep src
annotation.dst: merge with adjacent square pair d in an array of squares with colored inner square in main area

annotation.transform: connect d.inner_squares with s[0].color
annotation.multi_step: process control pairs from left to right
annotation.symbol_instructions: control pixels indicates connection path

references.docstring:
Fire projectiles from 3-pixel triangle sprites; mark collisions with maroon or blue.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Non-bg 3-pixel sprites shaped as axis-aligned L's or diagonal V's.

Rule:
- Each triangle has an apex and an emission direction determined by its shape: L-shapes fire diagonally away from the missing corner; V-shapes fire along the axis away from the open side.
- A projectile lands exactly 5 cells from the apex in the emission direction.
- If it hits an existing sprite, that entire sprite is recolored to maroon (9).
- If two projectiles land on the same empty cell, that cell becomes blue (1); a lone projectile on empty bg paints maroon (9).

Key insight: The triangle's orientation encodes both direction and target; dual-projectile collisions on open bg produce blue, not maroon.

annotation.path: L-shaped sprites emit along diagonal from apex; V-shaped sprites emit along axis from apex; collision at 5 cells from apex
annotation.trajectory: paint maroon at collision point
annotation.transform: if projectile hits opposing sprite, recolor entire sprite to maroon; if two projectiles collide, paint blue at intersection
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify sprite orientation (axis-aligned vs diagonal) by checking pixel arrangement; Step 2: determine emission direction from apex; Step 3: cast ray from position 4 cells beyond apex; Step 4: on collision with another projectile path paint blue, on collision with opposing sprite recolor sprite to maroon

references.docstring:
Assemble scattered rectangular pieces into a rectangle at an L-marker corner.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Non-bg rectangular pieces scattered on the grid.
- 3-pixel L-marker (2x2 minus one cell) tags the corner; the gap is the corner cell.

Rule:
- rect_col = most common color across all piece pixels; all outer rectangle edges must be rect_col.
- Translate pieces (no rotation) to tile the rectangle; touching edges must match, with rect_col as wildcard.

Key insight: rect_col acts as wildcard during edge matching — only non-rect_col pixels at shared boundaries must agree.

annotation.dst: fit against the matching edge d of a jigsaw growing from a corner square tagged by a marker
annotation.match_cond: s.edge.colors == d.colors, i.e. pixels with same postion on edge have same color
annotation.multi_step: attach pieces one onto another
annotation.notes: hidden rules: 1) the final jigsaw must be a rectangle with two edges established by the tagger corner; 2) the edges of the final rectangle must **all** be the same color, which is the "backgroud" color of the final rectangle.

references.docstring:
Build nested square frames from a stack of horizontal color stripes.

Input structure:
- Full-width horizontal stripes of distinct non-bg colors, stacked vertically.
- Each stripe has uniform color and variable height (1-4 rows).

Rule:
- Read stripes bottom to top.
- Bottom stripe becomes the center solid square with side length = stripe height.
- Each subsequent stripe wraps the current shape with a square frame of thickness = stripe height, in that stripe's color.

Key insight: Stripe height doubles as both frame thickness and (for the innermost) center-square side length; output dimensions are fully determined by the stripe heights.

annotation.transform: build nested square frames: bottom stripe -> center solid square (side=stripe_height); then for each higher stripe -> wrap with a square frame (thickness=stripe_height, color=stripe color)

annotation.notes: stripes are read bottom-to-top; frame colors/heights come from stripe colors/heights

references.docstring:
Cut a sprite along border-control rays and slide pieces to grid corners.

Input structure:
- bg, fg (main object, ~centered), ctrl (1-2 pixels on grid edges).

Rule:
- Draw rays inward from each ctrl pixel along its row/col, painting only bg cells up to the farthest fg pixel (intermittent).
- Rays partition the grid; fg on the cut line stays in place.
- Cut pieces in regions touching a control edge slide to that corner; others vanish.

Key insight: Only regions sharing a border edge with a control pixel keep their piece; the ray skips fg cells.

references.docstring:
Fit a grey bar into a grey frame by aligning projections with colored columns, then stack colors above.

Input structure:
- bg, a grey structural color forming two components: a large rectangular frame (slot) and a smaller bar with upward projections.
- Colored pixels inside the slot mark target columns.

Rule:
- Move the bar upward into the slot so its bottom edge sits one cell above the slot's interior bottom.
- Shift it horizontally so the bar's upward projections align column-wise with the colored pixels in the slot.
- Stack the colored pixels immediately above the bar projections in each column.

Key insight: The bar's projections act as keys that must align with the colored-column "locks" in the slot.

annotation.notes: The key geometric constraint: projections of the bar must align column-wise with the colored projections in the slot; movement distance varies based on projection lengths to achieve final alignment with 1-cell gap at bottom

annotation.path2: move(c, direction='up') such that c.projections align vertically with s.projections and s.bottom_edge is 1 cell above slot.bottom_edge

references.docstring:
Replicate a pre-drawn corner pattern to every other marker-bearing corner.

Input structure:
- bg = most frequent color. Hollow 0-frames (possibly partial L-shapes); each
  frame-corner cell is either 0 or a painted (non-bg, non-0) color.
- >= 1 'source' corner: the pattern is already drawn (one color, both outward
  cells and an inward-diagonal trail).
- Other corners: a single colored pixel on the inward diagonal at the pattern's
  deepest (k,k) offset; the pixel's color is that corner's target color.

Rule:
- Extract the canonical (TL-oriented) pattern from any source.
- For each non-source corner whose marker cell is colored, paint the same
  pattern rotated to that corner's orientation, using the marker's color.

Key insight: the pattern is symmetric about the corner's inward-diagonal axis
(canonical dr == dc), so it reflects cleanly across all four corner orientations.
Painting uses each target's OWN marker color, not the source color.

annotation.summary: Colored sprites inside black hollow square frames move to match destination sprites inside other frames via various mirror/diagonal symmetries, with colors transferred
annotation.src: colored sprites s inside black hollow square frames, where anchor is defined as: 1) the sprite's inner pixel, and 2) the black pixel at the minimum corner of the square that overlaps with the sprite's inner pixel
annotation.dst: single colored sprites d only inside black hollow square frames
annotation.match_cond: symmetry(s.anchor) == d (various mirror and diagonal symmetries)
annotation.trajectory: keep source
annotation.transform: s.color -> d.color
annotation.notes: Definition of anchor point: the relationship between sprite's inner pixel and the black pixel at minimum corner of square containing that pixel

references.docstring:
Learn a transformation rule from a training pair of framed sprites, then apply it to a test sprite.

Input structure:
- Grid contains several colored square frames (hollow borders of a single color).
- Each frame's interior holds a small pattern sprite; one frame's interior is blank (all black).
- Two frames form a training pair (their interiors share the same color palette); one remaining frame is the test case.

Rule:
- Identify the training pair by matching interior color sets; the other non-blank frame is the test input.
- Infer the rule mapping source→destination (e.g. reflection, color inversion, gap filling, endpoint extraction, or checkerboard complement).
- Apply that same rule to the test sprite; output the transformed interior.

Key insight: The puzzle is an analogy — "A is to B as C is to ?" — where you must discover the visual rule from one example pair and generalize it.

annotation.summary: Learn transformation rule from sprite pair in first frame, apply to sprite in second frame.
annotation.src: two non-black sprites (s1.s, s1.d) in first frame showing source-destination pattern; single non-black sprite (s2) in second frame as test case
annotation.dst: block square d representing the transformed output
annotation.match_cond: d = apply(s2, rule_from(s1.s → s1.d))
annotation.symbol_instructions: First frame contains two small pattern grids serving as training example (source pattern s1.s and transformed pattern s1.d); second frame contains test pattern s2 to which learned rule is applied
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop
annotation.notes: First frame contains training pair (s1.s, s1.d), second frame contains test case (s2); must infer transformation rule from training pair and apply to test case

references.docstring:
Extend marker tiles outward from '+' shapes by repeating them to the grid edge.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- A dominant non-bg color forms several '+'-shaped objects.
- Small colored patches (1–few cells) sit adjacent to each arm of a '+'.

Rule:
- For each marker tile touching a '+', determine which side of the '+' it sits on.
- Project the tile away from the '+' in that direction, repeating the tile pattern periodically until the grid boundary.
- '+' pixels are never overwritten.

Key insight: Each marker's attachment side determines its extension direction; the pattern repeats periodically, not as a single copy.

annotation.src: marker tile (non-bg patch) attached to a '+' sprite
annotation.path: straight ray starting from the marker tile, going away from the '+' attachment side until boundary
annotation.trajectory: repeat the marker tile periodically along the ray (tile repeats every tile width/height)
annotation.dst: grid edge
annotation.transform: copy the repeated marker pattern into background; keep the '+' pixels unchanged

references.docstring:
Move a triangular sprite across the grid, consuming aligned marker pixels.

Input structure:
- Frames concatenated horizontally with solid divider columns; bg is most common color.
- Each frame: a triangular arrow-shaped sprite and scattered single-pixel markers, all one color.

Rule:
- Start from the rightmost frame.
- At each step, exactly one cardinal direction from the head has reachable
  markers (on a half-line: same row or column); the sprite advances to the
  nearest one.
- On reaching a marker, consume it; sprite re-faces that direction.
- Repeat until no markers remain; output the final sprite position on a clean bg.

Key insight: The triangle's tip encodes facing direction, which sets marker-consumption priority.

annotation.summary: A triangular sprite moves through the grid consuming scattered marker pixels that match its head orientation, turning only when matching a marker, until all markers are consumed.
annotation.src: triangular sprite with distinct head orientation s
annotation.dst: scattered single-pixel markers of same color d
annotation.match_cond: s.head.direction aligns with ray to d position (d lies along s.head axis)
annotation.path: move(s, s.head.direction) until s.head.position == d.position; consume d; may turn 90° if new d aligns with perpendicular axis
annotation.trajectory: s moves without trail; d disappears when consumed
annotation.grid_shape: input is horizontally concatenated frames separated by divider; output is single frame of same cell dimensions
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify triangular sprite and all scattered markers in each frame; Step 2: sprite moves toward marker aligned with head direction; Step 3: consume marker and optionally turn 90° toward next aligned marker; Step 4: repeat until all markers consumed; Step 5: output shows sprite at final position with remaining markers removed

references.docstring:
Slide multi-color sprites to align their marker pixels with matching isolated border anchors.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Multi-color sprites in the interior; each has a minority-color "marker" pixel.
- Isolated border pixels (non-bg with all 4-neighbors bg) act as anchors.

Rule:
- Match each sprite to the border anchor sharing its marker color.
- Top/bottom-edge anchor (non-corner): slide sprite horizontally so marker column = anchor column.
- Left/right-edge anchor (or corner): slide sprite vertically so marker row = anchor row.

Key insight: The anchor's edge position determines the slide axis — top/bottom means horizontal, left/right (or corner) means vertical.

annotation.src: multi-color sprite s with a unique marker color (minority color inside s)
annotation.dst: align to isolated border pixel d (same marker color)
annotation.match_cond: s.marker.color == d.color
annotation.transform: translate s: if d on top/bottom edge → align col(s.marker) to col(d); else → align row(s.marker) to row(d); clip out-of-bounds pixels

references.docstring:
Count colored objects and record tallies inside a legend box.

Input structure:
- A black rectangular legend box with key-color pixels in its leftmost non-black column.
- Outside the box, distinct objects of each key color are scattered across the grid.

Rule:
- For each key color, count separate same-colored objects outside the legend box.
- Output the legend box repainted: each key row gets one dot per object, spaced every other cell rightward from the key pixel.

Key insight: The legend is both the color index and the output canvas — object counts become dot sequences on the matching row.

annotation.src: colored sprites s outside the black legend bbox
annotation.dst: follow pixels d inside the black legend bbox (one per key color)
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color
annotation.transform: s reduces to 1 dot placed left-to-right starting at pos(d) with 1 bg pixel gap, replacing d

references.docstring:
Carve color-matched motifs into solid blocks and pack them into a compact grid.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Several solid 5×5 monochrome blocks, each a distinct non-bg color.
- For each block color, a small same-colored motif sprite elsewhere on the grid.

Rule:
- Match each motif to its same-colored 5×5 block.
- Center the motif within the block and recolor those cells to bg (punching holes).
- Pack all carved blocks into an output grid preserving their original row/column order, separated by 1-cell gaps and a 1-cell outer border.

Key insight: The motif acts as a stencil — it's not stamped onto the block but carved out of it as background holes.

annotation.src: motif sprites s (small components)
annotation.dst: center on solid 5x5 block sprites d
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color
annotation.transform: s.color -> bg
annotation.grid_shape: packed grid of carved blocks (1px border + 1px gaps, row/col order preserved)

references.docstring:
Build a red ray network by activating blue blobs via directional green ports.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Large blue blobs with adjacent green pixels marking port directions.
- Start marker: yellow pixel atop a short red segment at grid bottom.

Rule:
- Extend a ray upward from start; on hitting a blue blob, recolor it red.
- Activated blobs emit thick rays through green ports until boundary or another blob.
- Cascade until no new blobs are reached.

Key insight: Green pixels encode ray direction and width; the network activates as a chain reaction from one start point.

annotation.src: port pixels s (start cap pixel; green pixels adjacent to blobs)
annotation.dst: extend rays d to activate blobs
annotation.path: cast a straight ray from the start port; when a blob is hit, recolor it and emit straight thick rays from its port side through the green pixels; newly hit blobs activate and emit (BFS) until no new hits
annotation.transform: activated blob -> red; ray path -> red

references.docstring:
Fill rectangular cavities in a template shape by placing source sprites into matching holes.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. A dominant "base" color forms a large frame/template with rectangular gaps.
- Small colored sprites sit outside the template region.

Rule:
- The base color (largest connected component excluding bg) defines the template bbox.
- Each rectangular hole inside the template matches exactly one outside sprite by size.
- Place each sprite into its matching cavity; output is the filled template bbox.

Key insight: Sprite bounding boxes match cavity dimensions exactly — it's a jigsaw-fit puzzle where each piece has a unique slot.

annotation.src: source sprites s outside the template bbox
annotation.dst: rectangular cavities d inside the template bbox
annotation.match_cond: s.bbox == d.rect (d is an all-hole rectangle)
annotation.transform: paste s into d (s.bg -> base); output = tight-crop to template bbox
annotation.grid_shape: tight-crop to template bbox

references.docstring:
Sort objects to top or bottom edge by whether their shape (up to rotation/flip) is shared.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Several multicolor connected components (8-connected) scattered across the grid.

Rule:
- Compute each object's canonical shape (binary mask, invariant to rotation and flip).
- Objects whose shape appears in two or more components → translate to TOP edge (row 0).
- Objects whose shape is unique → translate to BOTTOM edge (row H−h).
- Horizontal position (left column) is preserved; only vertical translation changes.

Key insight: The sorting criterion is shape frequency (rotation-invariant), not area — duplicated shapes go up, unique shapes go down.

annotation.src: all connected components (objects) on the background
annotation.dst: translate each object d vertically to an edge (x preserved)
annotation.match_cond: group objects by their pixel-count (area). If an area value occurs >=2 times, those objects go to the TOP edge; if the area is unique, that object goes to the BOTTOM edge
annotation.transform: duplicated-size -> top; singleton-size -> bottom

references.docstring:
Copy colored control-ray ports from one rectangular sprite orientation to every matching transformed sprite.

Input structure:
- bg is the most common color.
- Several dense 2-by-N or N-by-2 rectangular sprites are dihedral transforms of one template.
- Isolated single-pixel control markers sit on rays projected outward from the dominant long edge of some sprites.

Rule:
- For each sprite, the active edge is the long side whose cells have the strongest same-color majority.
- A control marker seen first along an outward ray from an active-edge cell assigns its color to that template cell.
- On every transformed sprite, draw that assigned color outward from the corresponding active-edge cell through bg cells until blocked or out of bounds.

Key insight:
- The marker positions are not absolute; they label cells of a shared rectangular template, then the labels follow each sprite's rotation/reflection.

annotation.src: single-pixel control markers labeling active-edge cells of rectangular sprites
annotation.path: outward normal ray from the corresponding active-edge cell of every transformed sprite
annotation.trajectory: continuous through bg cells
annotation.dst: grid edge or first foreground blocker
annotation.transform: copy marker labels by dihedral template position across all matching rectangular sprites

references.docstring:
Decode a stamp map: read templates, markers, and palette from a tiled grid, then render stamps.

Input structure:
- Grid divided into K tile columns (each N wide) separated by 1-col dashed separators.
- Top band (rows 0..N-1): K template masks, one per tile column.
- Middle band (rows N+1..2N): marker pixels whose color picks a template.
- Bottom band (rows 2N+2..): K palette swatches giving the output color per template.
- Separator rows at rows N and 2N+1 (dashed pattern of sep color).

Rule:
- Each marker's local position (lr, lc) within its tile column determines which N×N output block to stamp.
- The marker's color identifies which template to use; the palette recolors the template.

Key insight: Marker color encodes template index; local position within tile column encodes stamp block.

annotation.src: template-color marker pixels s in the middle band (between top templates and bottom palette)
annotation.dst: stamp slots d in an N×N grid of N×N tiles
annotation.match_cond: s.color == template_color[j]; d.pos == (s.r mod N, s.c mod N)
annotation.transform: replace d with template_mask[j] recolored to palette_color[j] (palette read from bottom band, left→right aligned to template columns)

references.docstring:
Fill holes inside a large template frame using shape-matched outside sprites.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. One large monochrome frame object (template).
- Inside the frame: holes of various shapes (non-frame-color regions).
- Outside the frame: small monochrome sprites scattered on bg.

Rule:
- Crop to the frame's bounding box; fill entirely with frame color.
- For each hole, find an outside sprite whose shape matches (rotation/flip allowed).
- Fill the hole with the matched sprite's color. If multiple sprites match, use the most frequent color.

Key insight: Sprites act as shape-coded color keys — their shape identifies which hole they fill, their color determines the fill color.

annotation.src: outside monochrome sprites s (connected components) on the background
annotation.dst: fill holes d (4-connected components of non-frame pixels) inside the largest frame sprite; output is cropped to the frame bbox
annotation.match_cond: s.shape == d.shape (allow rotation/flip); if multiple s match, prefer the most frequent s.color

references.docstring:
Slide black shapes rightward to a grey separator, then shoot red rays from enclosed holes.

Input structure:
- A vertical grey (5) separator column divides the grid into left and right halves.
- Black shapes sit on the left side against a background color (bg).

Rule:
- Translate each black connected component rightward until its right edge is flush with the separator.
- After sliding, find enclosed bg regions (holes) within the black shapes that touch the column just left of the separator.
- For each row spanned by such a hole, emit a red ray across the entire right half of the grid.

Key insight: Only holes adjacent to the separator trigger rays — the sliding creates enclosures that act as "nozzles" projecting rightward.

annotation.summary: Black objects on left side attract toward grey vertical separator line; enclosed magenta regions adjacent to separator emit red rays rightward to grid edge.
annotation.src: black connected sprites on left side of grey separator s
annotation.path: translate s rightward until s.rightmost_column is adjacent to grey separator
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: translate black sprites rightward to be adjacent to grey separator; Step 2: identify enclosed magenta regions that touch separator; Step 3: emit red horizontal rays from those rows rightward to grid edge
annotation.src2: magenta pixels enclosed by black sprites that are exactly 1 cell left of grey separator s
annotation.path2: draw horizontal line rightward from corresponding position on right side of separator until grid.right_edge
annotation.trajectory2: paint red along entire horizontal line

references.docstring:
Dock train sprites onto station groups by matching coupler count, then orient via divider-color markers.

Input structure:
- bg; colored stripes (edge + internal) partition grid into rectangular regions.
- Color 8 forms train bodies; color 9 marks both isolated stations and train-attached couplers.
- Stripe-colored pixels on trains are orientation markers.

Rule:
- Stations = 8-connected 9-clusters not adjacent to any 8. Trains = components containing 8.
- Match train to station group where |couplers| == |station size|.
- Rotate/flip train so marker pixels face the same-color boundary stripe of the target region.
- Translate so couplers align exactly onto station cells; erase original position.

Key insight: Coupler count selects the docking target; marker color encodes which boundary stripe to face, fixing the unique orientation.

annotation.src: train sprite s (cc containing 8) with attached coupler-9s and divider-color markers
annotation.dst: dock onto station group d (8-connected isolated 9s; no adjacent 8 in 8-neighborhood)
annotation.match_cond: |s.coupler9s| == |d|
annotation.transform: erase s; rotate/flip then translate so s.coupler9s == d; do not paint 9s (stations stay)
annotation.rotation_rule: orient s so its divider-color markers face the boundary stripes of d’s region (relative to coupler centroid)

references.docstring:
Crop a board cluster and rotate its color layers based on outside cue sprites.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- A main multi-color board cluster (largest foreground region).
- Small monochrome cue sprites outside the board for the colors that rotate.

Rule:
- Tight-crop around the board cluster.
- For each color layer inside the crop, find its same-color cue outside.
- Rotate that layer clockwise by (cue pixel count mod 4) × 90°.
- No outside cue → no rotation.

Key insight: Cue sprite size mod 4 encodes rotation amount for its matching color layer.

annotation.src: outside cue sprites s (components outside the main board cluster)
annotation.dst: color layers d inside the tight-cropped board
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color
annotation.transform: np.rot90(d, -s.size) (clockwise)
annotation.grid_shape: tight-crop of the main board cluster

references.docstring:
Highlight black defects in blue foreground by surrounding them with orange.

Input structure:
- Blue (1) foreground on black (0) bg; small black holes or protrusions within blue regions; occasional thin blue spurs into black areas.

Rule:
- Thin blue pixels mostly surrounded by black are absorbed into the background.
- Small black components (≤3 cells) and leaf pixels of larger black components are "defects."
- Each defect gets an orange (7) 8-neighbor halo; the defect pixels themselves stay black.

Key insight: Only structural anomalies—tiny isolated patches and dangling endpoints—are marked, not bulk black regions.

annotation.src: small black sprite s in and on edge of blue foreground regions
annotation.transform: surround s with orange
annotation.src2: small blue sprite s2 in and on edge of black bg regions

references.docstring:
Composite two pattern tiles into a fourth panel using flood-fill from an indicator pixel.

Input structure:
- Four 5×5 panels in one row, border-separated.
- Panel 0: cue pixels = wall boundary (8-connected, edge-to-edge, through center)
           + one 8-isolated indicator pixel.
- Panels 1–2: source patterns. Panel 3: blank (to fill).

Rule:
- Flood-fill (4-conn) from indicator, blocked by wall → inside region.
- Inside → non-bg from panel 1; outside → non-bg from panel 2.
- Wall → panel 1 if non-bg; panel 2 fallback when wall is 4-connected.

Key insight: The cue panel's isolated indicator and wall partition the tile into inside/outside masks that select between the two source panels.

annotation.src: cue line sprite s in tile0 + two pattern tiles (tile1, tile2)
annotation.dst: tile4 d (the blank 5x5 tile)
annotation.match_cond: s defines a line (row/col/diag/anti) and a side (chosen by the farthest off-line pixel)
annotation.transform: fill d: inside the region choose pixels from tile1; outside choose pixels from tile2; for row/col boundaries, allow tile2 pixels on the boundary line
annotation.grid_shape: same canvas (only tile4 changes)

references.docstring:
Fill the parallelogram-shaped region between parallel anti-diagonal line segments with red.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- One non-bg color forms short diagonal segments, each lying on a single anti-diagonal (r+c = const).
- Segments come in parallel pairs bounding a region to be filled.

Rule:
- For each main-diagonal axis (r−c = const), collect anti-diagonal segments whose span covers that axis.
- Sort those segments by their anti-diagonal index (r+c).
- Fill all bg cells lying strictly between consecutive segment pairs along that axis with red (color 2).

Key insight: The two diagonal directions decouple — segments sit on anti-diagonals, and filling sweeps along main diagonals between them, forming parallelogram regions.

annotation.summary: Fill the region between two parallel diagonal lines with red, connecting endpoints of the right diagonal to their left diagonal projection points
annotation.src: both endpoints s of the right diagonal line
annotation.dst: left diagonal projection point d (or midpoint between two points) on the other parallel line
annotation.match_cond: s.left_projection_point == d
annotation.path: left diagonal red block
annotation.trajectory: fill red inside the area bounded by the right diagonal line and the left projection path (continuous red region), keep the source pixels
annotation.notes: The key challenge is identifying two parallel diagonal lines and filling the parallelogram-like region between them with red while preserving the original colored diagonal pixels

references.docstring:
Reorder 5×5 blocks into a connected strip by matching edge foreground pixels.

Input structure:
- bg = background; sep = divider color (full row/column lines).
- Several 5×5 sprite blocks in a grid, separated by sep lines.

Rule:
- Two blocks "connect" when their facing edges share foreground pixels at the same offset (e.g., A's right edge ∩ B's left edge).
- Chain all blocks in the orientation (horizontal or vertical) that admits a complete sequence.
- Output is a 1×N strip of blocks in chain order, separated by sep lines.

Key insight: Edge-contact overlap determines both block ordering and output orientation.

annotation.src: 5x5 block sprites s separated by full-row/full-col magenta dividers
annotation.dst: paste s into strip slots d (a 1×N strip with magenta dividers)
annotation.match_cond: s.right-edge fg rows == d.left-edge fg rows (horizontal chain) OR s.bottom-edge fg cols == d.top-edge fg cols (vertical chain); choose the orientation where a full chain exists
annotation.transform: translate s into the matched slot d (no rotation)

references.docstring:
Recolor the shortest path between two terminal squares in a square-and-track graph.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Two non-bg colors form solid NxN squares (N>=2): one color marks exactly 2 terminals, the other marks stations.
- A third non-bg color forms 1-cell-wide track segments connecting pairs of squares (graph edges).

Rule:
- Find the shortest path (fewest edges) between the two terminal squares.
- Recolor every station square on that path to green.
- Recolor every track segment along that path to grey.
- Everything else unchanged.

Key insight: The grid encodes a graph where squares are nodes and tracks are edges; the task is graph shortest-path, not spatial proximity.

annotation.src: small square with minority color
annotation.dst: the other small square with minority color
annotation.path: shortest path along path pixels (not squares and bg)
annotation.trajectory: grey. recolor small squares with majority color on the way to green

references.docstring:
Assemble colored rectangular sprites into a single tiled rectangle, anchored by a marker pixel.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Several solid-colored rectangular sprites scattered on the grid.
- One sprite has a unique single-pixel marker (different color) at one corner — this is the anchor.

Rule:
- Identify the anchor sprite (contains the marker pixel) and the remaining pieces.
- Rotate the anchor so the marker pixel lands at position (0,0) of the output.
- Pack all remaining pieces (allowing 90° rotations) to tile a complete rectangle with no gaps.

Key insight: The lone marker pixel picks the anchor and fixes the output orientation — it must sit at the top-left corner.

annotation.summary: Assemble colored rectangular sprites like puzzle pieces using the grey-cornered orange block as the anchor, fitting other sprites by matching their edge positions.
annotation.src: colored rectangular sprites without grey corner marker s
annotation.dst: anchor sprite (orange block with grey corner pixel) or previously attached sprites d
annotation.match_cond: edge(s) aligns_with open_edge(d) such that union forms contiguous_tiled_rectangle
annotation.transform: rotate(anchor, until grey_pixel at top_left)
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop
annotation.multi_step: repeat merge until all sprites assembled into single rectangle
annotation.notes: The grey corner pixel identifies the anchor sprite and determines output orientation (grey stays at top-left corner). Each sprite is a solid colored rectangle; they tile together to form a complete rectangular output.

references.docstring:
Straighten a colored snake path into a single-column strip preserving pixel order.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Non-bg pixels form a single 4-connected path (snake) with exactly two endpoints.
- Each path pixel may be a different non-bg color.

Rule:
- Find the two endpoints (cells with only one path neighbor) of the snake.
- Begin at the top-left-most endpoint and trace the path cell by cell.
- Output an (N×1) column listing each cell's color in traversal order.

Key insight: The path is a simple chain with no branches; choosing the top-left-most endpoint fixes a unique reading direction.

annotation.src: snake-shaped polychrome sprite
annotation.transform: stretch vertically into a line
annotation.grid_shape: tight crop

references.docstring:
Remove diagonal staircase noise and complete broken straight lines.

Input structure:
- bg = background; one foreground color fg forming axis-aligned lines.
- Some fg pixels form 45° diagonal chains (8-connected but 4-disconnected from lines).

Rule:
- Delete all diagonal-only fg pixels (those with no orthogonal fg neighbor, only diagonal ones).
- Fill short gaps in horizontal/vertical lines where a deleted diagonal was nearby.
- Prune remaining diagonal-adjacent leaf pixels near former diagonal sites.

Key insight: Diagonal pixels are hints marking where a straight line is broken; their span sets the maximum gap size to fill.

annotation.src: foreground line sprites s + diagonal hint pixels s (45° staircase pixels)
annotation.transform: delete diagonal-only hint pixels; fill short gaps in straight lines when a hint is adjacent; delete any remaining diagonal-adjacent leaf pixels near the hints

references.docstring:
Dock two-tone sprites into color-matched horizontal bars with a color swap.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Top area: small two-tone sprites (outer color + inner color).
- Below: horizontal bars spanning most of the row, each with a fill color and border color on edges.

Rule:
- Match each sprite to the bar whose fill color equals the sprite's outer color.
- Place the sprite at its original x-position, aligned to the bar's bottom.
- Recolor: sprite outer → bar border, sprite inner → bar fill.
- Erase original sprites from the top area.

Key insight: Color matching is inverted — the sprite's dominant color identifies its target bar, then gets swapped to the bar's accent color.

annotation.src: two-tone sprite s (outer color + inner color)
annotation.dst: dock into horizontal bar sprite d (fill + border)
annotation.match_cond: s.outer_color == d.fill_color
annotation.transform: place at same x near bottom of d; swap: s.outer→d.border, s.inner→d.fill

references.docstring:
Mirror colored sprites using red (2) markers as reflection axes.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Red (2) = marker color.
- Colored sprites appear near red markers.

Rule:
- Red line within a sprite (vertical or horizontal) → mirror payload across that axis.
- Single red pixel in a mixed sprite → point-reflect payload around it.
- Isolated red pixel (alone, no payload) → point-reflect each adjacent 8-connected color component.
- Originals remain; mirrored pixels overlay.

Key insight: Red marker geometry (line vs single pixel) determines reflection type; isolated vs embedded red determines what gets reflected.

annotation.src: colored sprites s + red marker pixels
annotation.transform: mirror s across the red marker axis (vertical/horizontal red line) or point-reflect around an isolated red pixel; paint the mirrored pixels onto bg

references.docstring:
Recolor a path-network by adjacent seed regions.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Path color P forms a thin orthogonal network with a solid square hub (NxN).
- Seed colors appear in colored regions (non-bg, non-P) adjacent to path branches.

Rule:
- Infer P as the non-bg color whose largest component is most network-like.
- Find the largest solid k×k all-P square (the hub); exclude it from recoloring.
- Recolor each path branch to the seed-region color it touches most.
- Recolor the hub center pixel to the seed whose branches touch the hub most.

Key insight: The hub stays uncolored; branches inherit color from adjacent seed regions by adjacency count.

annotation.src: path-network pixels s (thin largest component) + seed regions s (non-bg, non-path)
annotation.transform: recolor each path branch (connected component of s excluding the hub square) to the majority color of the seed region it touches; keep the hub square, but recolor its center to the seed color that touches the hub most

references.docstring:
Extend diagonal rays outward from outer-border segments adjacent to diamond shapes on a checkerboard.

Input structure:
- Checkerboard bg (two most common colors).
- Hollow diamond outlines (8-pixel) in a non-bg color (inner border).
- Short diagonal line segments in another non-bg color adjacent to each diamond edge (outer border).

Rule:
- For each outer-border segment, determine the outward direction (perpendicular to the segment, away from the diamond).
- From each endpoint of the segment, cast a diagonal ray outward, painting over bg pixels with the segment's color until hitting a non-bg pixel or the grid edge.

Key insight: Rays emit only from the two endpoints of each outer-border segment, not every pixel, and travel diagonally away from the diamond.

annotation.summary: Diamond-shaped objects with inner and outer borders of different colors emit hollow diagonal rays in the outer border color from the edge where both borders exist.
annotation.src: edge of diamond s where outer border pixel and inner border pixel both exist with different colors
annotation.path: diagonal direction extending outward from s perpendicular to diamond edge until grid boundary
annotation.trajectory: paint hollow pattern (every other pixel) with s.outer_border.color

references.docstring:
Match sprites to frames by connected-hole count, then nest each sprite inside its frame.

Input structure:
- bg = azure (8). Large hollow squares (frames) arranged in a grid; smaller filled squares (sprites) placed elsewhere.
- Each frame and sprite has a distinct color. Sprites may contain holes (non-sprite-color pixels).

Rule:
- Frames form a regular grid; some may be bg-colored (invisible).
- Count connected hole regions inside each frame's interior and each sprite.
- Pair each frame with the sprite sharing the same hole count.
- Place the matched sprite inside the frame border; recolor sprite holes to the frame's color.

Key insight: The matching key is the number of connected hole components, not hole area or color.

annotation.src: sprites (small filled squares with holes) outside the frame grid
annotation.dst: place into frames d (large hollow squares) forming a grid
annotation.match_cond: count of connected hole regions (using scipy.ndimage.label)
annotation.transform: sprite holes become frame color when placed inside
annotation.notes: frames may include background-colored (invisible) frames; sprite fill ratio can be low due to holes

references.docstring:
Swing an irregular line segment around a nearby obstacle sprite, preserving its pixel count.

Input structure:
- bg, bar color (straight lines perpendicular to the grid edge, one end on the border), segment color (irregular stroke attached to bar's inner endpoint), obstacle color (sprite near the bar terminal).

Rule:
- Each bar is perpendicular to the edge it touches; its inner (terminal) endpoint has an attached irregular segment.
- The segment detaches and re-routes: it travels from the terminal toward the nearest obstacle, hugs the obstacle's boundary, then exits at a 45° diagonal.
- Total painted pixels equal the original segment length.

Key insight: The segment behaves like a rope swung around the obstacle — attach at the nearest point, trace the skin, exit diagonally, conserving length.

annotation.summary: An irregular line segment connected to the terminal of a vertical/horizontal bar perpendicular to grid edge wraps around a nearby obstacle sprite and repositions while preserving total pixel count.
annotation.src: irregular line segment attached to terminal of edge-perpendicular bar s
annotation.dst: wrap around nearest obstacle sprite d
annotation.match_cond: nearest(s.terminal, d.boundary) by manhattan_distance
annotation.path: connect s.bar_terminal to d.nearest_pixel, traverse d.boundary pixels, exit at d.farthest_corner with 45-degree diagonal extension
annotation.trajectory: paint s.color along path; total painted pixels == len(s.original_segment)
annotation.transform: s.original_segment -> disappear; repaint along new wrapped path
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify bar perpendicular to grid edge and its attached irregular segment s; Step 2: identify obstacle sprite d nearest to bar terminal; Step 3: compute shortest path from bar terminal to d; Step 4: traverse d boundary clockwise/counterclockwise; Step 5: exit at far corner with 45-degree diagonal; Step 6: repaint s pixels along new path preserving count
annotation.notes: Key insight: the irregular segment 'swings' around the obstacle like a rope, connecting to nearest point, hugging the obstacle boundary, then exiting diagonally. Total segment length (pixel count) is conserved.

references.docstring:
Slide yellow pixels inside walled regions in the direction dictated by border-legend arrows.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color; yellow pixels sit inside enclosed regions bounded by colored walls.
- Border legends: small rectangles on the grid edge whose fill color C matches a region's border color. Each legend contains a center dot and an indicator dot encoding a direction.

Rule:
- For each enclosed region, identify its border color C and look up the legend with fill color C.
- The direction from the legend's center dot to its indicator dot gives the slide direction.
- All yellow pixels in that region slide in that direction, stacking against the far wall.

Key insight: Legend fill color links to region border color; the center→indicator offset encodes the movement vector.

annotation.summary: Yellow pixels inside colored-border regions move in the direction indicated by the red pixel in the legend with matching background color, stopping at region boundary.
annotation.src: yellow pixels inside colored-border regions s
annotation.path: move(s, direction=legend.red_pixel_offset) where legend.background_color == s.containing_region.border_color until s.touches(region_boundary)
annotation.symbol_instructions: legend on grid edge with background color C and red pixel indicates: yellow pixels in regions with border color C move in direction from blue center to red pixel

references.docstring:
Convert each colored partitioned frame into a horizontal bar whose length is its number of enclosed regions.

Input structure:
- Black background with several axis-aligned colored line drawings.
- The line drawings are damaged by scattered pixels of one non-background noise color and by overlaps with other drawings.
- Each real drawing is a rectangular partitioned frame enclosing one or more background regions.

Rule:
- For each non-background color, reconstruct its horizontal and vertical wall segments from dense row/column evidence.
- Count the 4-connected background regions fully enclosed by those reconstructed walls.
- The color with no enclosed region is the noise/pad color.
- Sort drawing colors by enclosed-region count; equal counts are ordered by which reconstructed frame covers the other.

Key insight:
- The scattered color is not an object; it only pads the histogram, while each true object's room count is stable after rectilinear wall reconstruction.

annotation.src: colored partitioned frame line drawings; ignore scattered pad-color pixels
annotation.dst: stack one horizontal bar per frame, ordered by count of enclosed background regions then color id
annotation.transform: bar length = number of enclosed 4-connected background regions; pad right with the scattered color
annotation.grid_shape: height = number of frame colors, width = maximum enclosed-region count

references.docstring:
Inflate a frame's hole-layout and fill each hole with its matching piece.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Largest component is a monochrome frame enclosing bg holes.
- Outside pieces composed of k×k blocks; k = side of smallest solid square piece.

Rule:
- Extract connected hole regions inside the frame as slots.
- Match each piece to a slot by comparing block-level shapes under rotation/flip.
- Output the layout scaled by k, with pieces placed in slots; frame color as background.

Key insight: Pieces are k×k-block-scaled versions of holes; downsampling reveals shape matches under all 8 orientations.

annotation.src: sprite s outside the rectangle with holes
annotation.dst: fill hole d in the rectangle with holes
annotation.match_cond: s.shape matches enlarged_d.shape up to rotation/flip
annotation.transform: enlarge the rectangle to let s fit into its hole
annotation.grid_shape: crop to only retain the enlarged rectangle

references.docstring:
Fill enclosed regions along a line seeded by unique border pixels.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Colored lines/drawings on the grid.
- Unique single-pixel colors on the grid border mark seed endpoints of each line.

Rule:
- Each border seed pixel connects (8-connected) to a line drawing.
- Find closed bg cavities whose boundary touches that line.
- Flood-fill each such cavity with the seed pixel's color.

Key insight: Only cavities reachable through the seed's own line get filled; the seed's unique color acts as a per-line fill label.

annotation.summary: Find single pixels on grid edges that are endpoints of lines, trace along the line to find connected closed regions, and fill those regions with the edge pixel's color.
annotation.src: single colored pixels s on grid edge that are endpoints of a line
annotation.dst: closed regions d connected to the line
annotation.match_cond: d is reachable by following the line from s
annotation.path: trace along the continuous line from edge pixel s
annotation.trajectory: fill interior of each closed region d encountered along path with s.color
annotation.transform: d.interior.color = s.color
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify single pixels on grid edge; Step 2: trace the line connected to each edge pixel; Step 3: for each closed region touching the line, flood-fill its interior with edge pixel color

references.docstring:
Insert red components into interior sockets of large structures, leaving a black trail.

Input structure:
- bg = most common. Large non-bg, non-red structures with interior cavities.
- Red components outside structures.

Rule:
- Interior sockets: bg cells inside a structure's bbox, adjacent to structure pixels.
- For each structure, find the direction where rays from sockets hit a red component.
- Slide that component into the socket; paint traversed cells black.
- Unmatched reds vanish.

Key insight: Docking direction is inferred by ray-casting from interior sockets to the nearest red component.

annotation.src: red block s
annotation.dst: translate into interior socket cells d of each large structure
annotation.match_cond: s.col/row == d.col/row
annotation.trajectory: paint the traversed cells black
annotation.src2: red block without matching socket cell

references.docstring:
Clean each color layer by enforcing vertical mirror symmetry.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Several non-bg colors, each forming a nearly-symmetric pattern about some vertical axis.
- Some pixels in each color are "noise" that breaks the symmetry.

Rule:
- For each non-bg color, find the vertical axis that best explains its pixel layout.
- Remove any pixel that lacks a same-color mirror counterpart across that axis.

Key insight: Each color has its own independent symmetry axis; the task is per-color denoising, not whole-grid symmetry.

annotation.src: nearly symmetric sprite s
annotation.transform: delete pixels without a mirror counterpart to make s symmetric

references.docstring:
Count same-color patterns per frame and represent the tally as dots inside.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Hollow rectangular frames in various colors.
- Small monochrome pattern sprites scattered outside frames.

Rule:
- Remove all small patterns from the grid.
- For each frame of color C, count how many patterns share color C.
- Draw that many dots along the frame's center row, spaced by 2, starting from the right.

Key insight: Frames act as tally displays — scattered same-color patterns are "absorbed" and their count is shown as interior dots.

annotation.src: pattern sprites s outside frame sprites
annotation.dst: fill hollow rectangular frame sprites d
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color
annotation.transform: for each frame d: N = #{s | s.color == d.color}; draw N dots on mid-row(d), spaced by 2 from the right side

references.docstring:
Paint an inner border around the region reachable from a corner marker pixel.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color; wall color (blue) forms barriers dividing the grid.
- A unique single pixel (magenta) sits on one corner — the start marker.
- Some wall-colored pixels are structural (border-touching, enclosing regions); others are decorations.

Rule:
- Flood-fill from the marker corner to find all reachable bg cells, blocked by structural walls.
- Erase wall-colored decorations hidden behind structural walls (not reachable from marker side).
- Paint orange (color 7) on every reachable bg cell adjacent to a wall or grid edge — forming a 1-cell inner border.

Key insight: Only border-connected wall components act as real barriers; interior wall fragments are decorations to be removed.

annotation.summary: Starting from the magenta pixel at corner, draw orange inner border around teal regions enclosed by blue pixels.
annotation.src: magenta pixel at corner s
annotation.path: trace inner boundary of teal regions that are enclosed by blue pixels, starting from s position
annotation.trajectory: paint orange on teal pixels that are adjacent to blue boundary pixels

tags: condition:边界连通区分结构, border_connected_distinguishes_structural

references.docstring:
Fill rectangles between diagonal marker pairs using a color legend.

Input structure:
- bg grid with a vertical legend at the bottom-left: each row is a (marker_color, fill_color) pair.
- Scattered L-shaped corner markers of each marker color define opposite corners of axis-aligned rectangles.
- Some markers are solid 2×2 blocks instead of corner pairs.

Rule:
- Read legend bottom-to-top; for each entry find all pixels of that marker color.
- Determine which two bbox corners carry L-shaped anchors — the *other* diagonal defines the fill region.
- Fill the diamond (all shortest-path cells between those two corners) with the legend's fill color.
- Solid 2×2 marker blocks are simply recolored to the fill color.
- Later legend entries are protected from earlier fills.

Key insight: The L-shaped anchors sit on the marker diagonal; the fill goes on the opposite diagonal of the bounding box.

annotation.summary: Use a color legend at bottom-left to find diagonal marker pairs of matching color, then fill the rectangle between them with the adjacent legend color.
annotation.src: diagonal pixel pair s with same color forming opposite corners of a rectangle (upper corner pixel)
annotation.dst: diagonal pixel pair d with same color forming opposite corners of a rectangle (lower corner pixel)
annotation.match_cond: s.color == d.color && s and d are diagonally opposite
annotation.transform: fill rectangle bounded by s and d with color from legend where legend.left == s.color gives fill_color = legend.right
annotation.symbol_instructions: legend is vertical stack of color pairs at bottom-left, each pair (left-right only) has marker color on left and fill color on right
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify legend as vertically stacked color pairs at bottom-left corner; Step 2: process legend entries from bottom to top; Step 3: for each legend entry (marker_color on left, fill_color on right), find all diagonal pairs of marker_color pixels; Step 4: fill rectangle between each diagonal pair with fill_color
annotation.notes: sometimes as 2x2 squares which count as two diagonal triangles; processing order matters for overlapping regions

references.docstring:
Recolor vertical bars by legend-driven rank selection.

Input structure:
- bg = background. Top-left: monochrome blocks touching row 0; each has color K and height k.
- Main grid: vertical bars capped top and bottom by a single color, with solid-color interiors.

Rule:
- For each legend entry (K, k), find vertical bars capped by K.
- Rank bars by interior length (longest = rank 1).
- Recolor the rank-k bar's interior to K.

Key insight: Legend height is a rank index into length-sorted bars, not a literal size.

annotation.summary: Vertical bars with colored endpoints are grouped by endpoint colors, then bars within each group are recolored based on matching their length-rank to the count of colored blocks in the top-left legend.
annotation.src: vertical bars with colored pixels at both ends s, grouped by their endpoint colors
annotation.dst: legend entries in top-left corner showing colored blocks d
annotation.match_cond: s.endpoint_colors == d.color_group AND s.length_rank_in_group == d.block_count
annotation.transform: recolor entire bar s with d.legend_color
annotation.symbol_instructions: legend in top-left: each colored entry indicates target color; block count in legend determines which bar (by length rank) in matching endpoint-color group gets recolored
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify legend entries in top-left corner by color and count blocks; Step 2: identify vertical bars by their endpoint colors and group them; Step 3: within each group, rank bars by length; Step 4: match bar with length-rank equal to legend block count; Step 5: recolor matched bar entirely with legend color
annotation.notes: correspondence between rank and count

references.docstring:
Reconstruct a 4-way symmetric mosaic by filling missing (black) pixels.

Input structure:
- A colored grid exhibiting bilateral symmetry along both a vertical and a horizontal axis.
- Some pixels are erased to color 0 (black), creating gaps in the pattern.

Rule:
- Infer the vertical and horizontal reflection axes from the visible (non-zero) pixels.
- For each black pixel, recover its color from the mirrored position across either axis or both.
- When multiple mirrors yield candidates, use the majority color.

Key insight: The reflection axes are not given — they must be deduced from the surviving pixels by finding the axes that best preserve the existing symmetry.

Transfer sprites from red-marked lanes to green-marked lanes, recoloring and stacking.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color. Red (2) and green (3) thin bars define vertical lanes.
- Each lane contains repeated identical monochrome sprites in an evenly spaced vertical grid.

Rule:
- Each red lane's sprites turn grey (5); their count transfers to the nearest green lane.
- New sprites fill empty lattice slots bottom-up, using the source shape recolored to the destination lane's sprite color.
- All marker bars are removed.

Key insight: Sprite count is conserved across lanes — red sprites become grey, and equally many new sprites stack into the green lane's regular grid.

annotation.summary: Move sprite from red marker region to green marker region, recoloring it to match the green region's original sprite color, while turning the source sprite location grey and removing both markers.
annotation.src: sprite sitting on red marker pixel region s
annotation.dst: position of sprite sitting on green marker pixel region d
annotation.match_cond: s.marker_color == red && d.marker_color == green
annotation.transform: s.color -> d.original_sprite.color; s.original_location -> grey; markers -> disappear
annotation.symbol_instructions: red pixel marks source sprite to move; green pixel marks destination where sprite transfers with color change
annotation.multi_step: Step 1: identify red and green marker pixels; Step 2: move sprite above red marker to position above green marker; Step 3: recolor moved sprite to match original sprite color at destination; Step 4: turn original source sprite location to grey; Step 5: remove both marker pixels

references.docstring:
Move magenta particles along corridors formed by parallel colored bars.

Input structure:
- bg=7. Particles=6 in col 0. Colored bars on even rows form corridors on odd rows.

Rule:
- Particle goes straight through bg cells.
- When blocked by a colored cell, turns 90° into the perpendicular direction
  that has a bg cell flanked by same-color bars. Stops at grid edge or full blockage.

Key insight: Same-color parallel bars define the only valid corridors, so each particle follows a deterministic local trace.

annotation.src: magenta particle pixel in leftmost column at valid corridor entrances
annotation.path: corridor, i.e. empty space between two parallel bars of same color, with inertia principle
annotation.trajectory: none
annotation.dst: grid edge
annotation.notes: inertia principle: particle maintains direction until forced to change by obstacle or available turn

references.docstring:
Stamp source sprites into a destination frame via color-matched singleton markers.

Input structure:
- Two bordered rectangles: source (multi-cell sprites) and destination (singleton markers).
- Each sprite has an anchor pixel — its least-frequent color. Markers share these colors.

Rule:
- Match each destination marker to the source sprite with the same anchor color.
- Translate the sprite so its anchor overlaps the marker position.
- Output is the destination rectangle, interior cleared before stamping.

Key insight: The rarest color per sprite doubles as a template key and positioning anchor.

annotation.src: sprite s with anchor pixel inside the source framed rectangle
annotation.dst: anchored on singleton marker pixel d inside the destination framed rectangle
annotation.match_cond: s.anchor_color == d.color
annotation.transform: overlap s.anchor with d
annotation.grid_shape: crop to only retain the destination rectangle

references.docstring:
Dock movable tools into border-anchored frames by filling cavities.

Input structure:
- bg = most common color.
- Border-touching components cluster into anchor frames with interior bg cavities.
- Non-border 2-color components are movable tools.

Rule:
- Match each tool to a frame whose cavity size equals one of its color-region counts.
- Rotate/flip the tool so one color fills the cavity exactly; the other stays outside.
- If the docking orientation uses a reflection, swap the tool's two colors.

Key insight: Cavity size determines tool–frame pairing; reflection triggers color swap.

annotation.src: sprite s not touching the edges
annotation.dst: dock into frames d on edge
annotation.match_cond: s.component.shape == d.notch.shape with rotation/flip
annotation.transform: swap colors of the two components of s if flip is used

references.docstring:
Assemble and place enlarged sprites on a canvas using legend-panel instructions.

Input structure:
- Color-6 separators divide the grid into a left legend column and a main canvas.
- Each legend panel has (top to bottom): a unit sprite, a frame template, a 5x5 bordered square with a position-marker pixel, and a 3x3 rotation clock-hand.

Rule:
- Tile the unit sprite into each active cell of the frame to build an enlarged composite.
- Rotate the composite per the clock-hand direction (up=0, right=90, down=180, left=270 degrees).
